maxNumActDrbCatM.fullName: Max number act DRB for Cat-M

maxNumQci1DrbCatM.description:
This parameter specifies threshold for the maximum number of established Cat-M VoLTE DRBs including QCI1 and operator specific QCI in the cell.
The parameter is always relevant independent if "actEnhAcAndGbrServices"" is set to 'false' or to 'true'.
QCI1-DRBs for CAT-M UEs are special data radio bearers in the cell and are also checked against the threshold maxNumActDrb. 
In case "actEnhAcAndGbrServices"" is set to 'false' there is no interdependency to the counter/threshold for legacy VoLTE connections (maxNumQci1Drb) that means maxNumQci1Drb and maxNumQci1DrbCatM are independent from each other.
maxNumQci1DrbCatM.fullName: Max number QCI1 DRBs (GBRs) for Cat-M

maxNumQci1DrbEmergCatM.description:
This parameter specifies threshold for the maximum number of established Cat-M QCI1-GBR-DRBs for Emergency Sessions in the cell.
QCI1-DRBs for Emergency CAT-M UEs are VoLTE data radio bearers. Each VoLTE DRB admission increases the number of CAT-M DRBs and a check against the threshold maxNumQci1DrbCatM in addition.
maxNumQci1DrbEmergCatM.fullName: Max number QCI1 DRBs (GBRs) for Cat-M emergency session

maxNumRrcCatM.description: This parameter defines the threshold for the maximum number of Cat-M UEs in the cell which may establish a RRC connection.
maxNumRrcCatM.fullName: Maximum number of Cat-M RRC Connections

maxNumRrcEmergencyCatM.description:
This parameter define the threshold for the maximum number of Cat-M UEs in the cell which may establish a RRC connection, used to admit RRC connections for emergency calls.
In order to give emergency sessions more chance to be established than normal traffic maxNumRrcEmergency should be greater than maxNumRrcCatM.
maxNumRrcEmergencyCatM.fullName: Maximum number of Cat-M RRC Connections for Emergency Session

mibRepEnabledCatM.description: This parameter enables the repetitions of Master Information Block (MIB) for Cat-M.

minNumRrcCatM.description:
This parameter defines minimum allocated number of Cat-M UEs in the cell which may establish a RRC connection.
This is needed for AirScale where resources may be shifted from one cell to the other where needed. This parameter is only used by AirScale regardless dynamic PUCCH features activated or deactivated.
minNumRrcCatM.fullName: Minimum number of Cat-M RRC connections

mpdcchMaxNumRepCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum numbers of repetitions for M-PDCCH for DL and UL grants of Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 

Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 9.1.5-3. 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE mpdcch-NumRepetition-r13.
mpdcchMaxNumRepCatM.fullName: Maximum number of repetition for MPDCCH(UE-SS) for Cat-M CE Level 1

mpdcchMaxNumRepPagCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum number of repetitions for MPDCCH for Cat-M paging messages.
This parameter has range and step defined using letter 'n', which is equivalent to 3GPP nomenclature with letter 'r'.

Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 9.1.5-4.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE mpdcch-NumRepetition-Paging-r13.
mpdcchMaxNumRepPagCatM.fullName: Maximum number of repetition for MPDCCH(Paging) for Cat-M

mpdcchMaxNumRepRaCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum number of repetitions for MPDCCH  for RAR, HARQ of Msg3 and Msg4 of Cat-M UEs.
This parameter is applicable for both CE Level 0 and CE Level 1, i.e., CE Level 0 and CE Level 1 have same MPDCCH Rmax for Cat-M RAR, HARQ of Msg3 and Msg4 grant.
This parameter has range and step defined using letter 'n', which is equivalent to 3GPP nomenclature with letter 'r'.

Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 9.1.5-3. 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.211 and TS 36.331 and IE mpdcch-NumRepetition-RA-r13.
mpdcchMaxNumRepRaCatM.fullName: Maximum number of repetition for MPDCCH(Random Access) for Cat-M

mpdcchRepLevCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the repetition level of M-PDCCH to determine the repetition number of M-PDCCH for the DL and UL grants for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 

This parameter is used to set the ‘DCI subframe repetition number’ field of the DCI Format 6-1A or DCI Format 6-0A.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.212 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 9.1.5-3.
mpdcchRepLevCatM.fullName: Repetition level of M-PDCCH(UE-SS) for Cat-M CE Level 1

mpdcchRepLevPagCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the repetition level of paging message on M-PDCCH for Cat-M UEs mapping to paging CE Level 1.
This parameter is used to set the ‘DCI subframe repetition number’ field of the DCI Format 6-2.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.212 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 9.1.5-4 and Table 7.1.11-3.
mpdcchRepLevPagCatM.fullName: Repetition level of M-PDCCH(Paging) for Cat-M CE Level 1

mpdcchRepLevRaCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the repetition level of M-PDCCH to determine the repetition number of M-PDCCH for random access messages(Msg2, HARQ for Msg3, Msg4) for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 

This parameter is used to set the ‘DCI subframe repetition number’ field of the DCI Format 6-1A or DCI Format 6-0A.

Refer to 3GPP TS 36.212 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 9.1.5-3.
mpdcchRepLevRaCatM.fullName: Repetition level of M-PDCCH(Random Access) for Cat-M CE Level 1

mpdcchRepNumTaThres.description: This parameter determines the threshold of MPDCCH repetition number for dedicated TA command. The dedicated TA command can only be triggered if the MPDCCH repetition number is no more than this threshold.
mpdcchRepNumTaThres.fullName: The threshold of MPDCCH repetition number for dedicated TA

mpdcchStartSfCssCatM.description:
This parameters controls the starting subframe configuration for M-PDCCH common search space for RAR, Msg3 retransmission, PDSCH with contention resolution(Msg4) and PDSCH with RRCConnectionSetup for Cat-M UEs.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.321, TS 36.213 and TS 36.331 and IE mpdcch-startSF-CSS-RA-r13.
mpdcchStartSfCssCatM.fullName: MPDCCH Start SF for MPDCCH common search space for Cat-M

mpdcchStartSfUessCatM.description:
This parameters specifies the starting subframe configuration for M-PDCCH UE-specific Search Space UESS for Cat-M UEs. 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.321, TS 36.213, 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE mpdcch-StartSF-UESS-r13.
mpdcchStartSfUessCatM.fullName: MPDCCH Start SF for MPDCCH UE specific search space for Cat-M

mpdschRepNumTaThres.description: This parameter determines the threshold of MPDSCH repetition number for dedicated TA command. The dedicated TA command can only be triggered if the MPDSCH repetition number is no more than this threshold.
mpdschRepNumTaThres.fullName: The threshold of MPDSCH repetition number for dedicated TA

n310CatM.description:
Constant for 'out of sync' of Cat-M UEs indications n310CatM.
This parameter defines the maximum number of consecutive "out of sync" indications received from lower layers for Cat-M.
n1 corresponds to 1 and so on.
Refer to TS36.331 IE UE-TimersAndConstants: n310
n310CatM.fullName: Maximum number of out-of-sync indications for Cat-M

n311CatM.description:
Constant for 'in-sync' of Cat-M UEs indications n311CatM.
This parameter defines the maximum number of consecutive "in-sync" indications received from lower layers for Cat-M.
n1 corresponds to 1 and so on.

Refer to TS36.331 IE UE-TimersAndConstants: n311
n311CatM.fullName: Maximum number of in-sync indications for Cat-M

numRepPerPreambAttemptCECatM.description:
This parameter defines the number of PRACH repetitions per preamble attempts for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 

Refer to TS 36.321 and TS 36.331 and IE numRepetitionPerPreambleAttempt-r13
numRepPerPreambAttemptCECatM.fullName: Number of PRACH repetitions per attempt for Cat-M CE Level 1

numRepSib1BRCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the number of SIB1-BR repetitions in terms of 80ms period.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE schedulingInfoSIB1-BR-r13.

pagAreaScopeCheckCatM.description:
This parameter specifies whether S1AP:PAGING Next Paging Area Scope IE is checked or not for Paging algorithm optimization.

If pagAreaScopeCheckCatM is set to
- 'False': eNB does not check the S1AP:PAGING Next Paging Area Scope IE – which means that the first paging on proper ECGI is always sent regardless of the S1AP:PAGING Next Paging Area Scope IE.
- 'True': eNB checks the S1AP:PAGING Next Paging Area Scope IE – which means that the first paging on ECGI is only sent when S1AP:PAGING Next Paging Area Scope IE is same.
- if it is not configured, eNB does not check the S1AP:PAGING Next Paging Area Scope IE – which means that the first paging per TAC (Tracking Area Code) is always sent regardless of the S1AP:PAGING Next Paging Area Scope IE.
pagAreaScopeCheckCatM.fullName: Paging Area Scope Check for Cat-M

pagAttCeIncreaseModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the unsuccessful Paging Attempt threshold for Cat-M CE ModeA capable UEs. eNB should apply the higher configured paging CE level parameters for MPDCCH and PDSCH in case of unsuccessful Paging Attempt greater than or equal to this.

It is recommended to set to value ‘1’.
pagAttCeIncreaseModeACatM.fullName: Maximum attempt number for paging message within current coverage level for Cat-M CE ModeA

pagingNbCatM.description:
This parameter defines the number of possible paging occasions per radio frame for Cat-M UEs. 
Paging nB defines the number of possible paging occasions per radio frame, i.e. the density of paging occasions. This parameter is used to calculate the number of paging occasions within one paging DRX duration, which in turn is used to calculate the paging occasion.

Refer to TS 36.331 and IE nB-v1310: in case nB-v1310 is signalled, the UE shall ignore nB (that is to say nB without suffix). The eNB does not broadcast nB-v1310 in SIB2 but in SIB2-BR.
pagingNbCatM.officialRange:
4: quarterT 
5: oneEighthT 
6: oneSixteenthT 
7: oneThirtySecondT 
8: one64thT 
9: one128thT 
10: one256thT

pdschMaxNumRepModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum number of repetitions for PDSCH of Cat-M UEs in CE modeA. 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 7.1.11-1. 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and the optional IE pdsch-maxNumRepetitionCEmodeA-r13.

Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.
pdschMaxNumRepModeACatM.fullName: Maximum numbers of repetition for PDSCH of Cat-M in CE modeA

pdschRepLevModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the repetition level of PDSCH to determine the repetition number of PDSCH messages for Cat-M UEs in CE modeA Level 1. 

This parameter is used to set the 'Repetition Number' field of the DCI Format 6-1A.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.212
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 7.1.11-1.
pdschRepLevModeACatM.fullName: Repetition level for PDSCH of Cat-M in CE modeA Level 1

pdschRepLevMsg4ModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the Msg4 repetition level on PDSCH to determine the repetition number of random access Msg4 for Cat-M UEs in CE modeA Level 1. 

This parameter is used to set the 'Repetition Number' field of the DCI Format 6-1A.

Refer to 3GPP TS 36.212
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 7.1.11-1.
pdschRepLevMsg4ModeACatM.fullName: Repetition level for Msg4 on PDSCH of Cat-M in CE modeA Level 1

pdschRepLevPagCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the repetition level of paging message on PDSCH for Cat-M UEs mapping to paging CE Level 1.
This parameter is used to set the 'Repetition Number' field of the DCI Format 6-2.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.212 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213
Table 7.1.11-3.
pdschRepLevPagCatM.fullName: Repetition level of PDSCH(Paging) for Cat-M CE Level 1

pollPdu.description:
The parameter Poll PDU defines the number of RLC PDUs that are sent on a logical channel before the RLC polling bit is set.
This parameter specifies the parameter pollPDU of [36.331]

prachStartSFCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the PRACH starting subframe for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE prach-StartingSubframe-r13.
If it is set to '0', the optional IE "prach-StartingSubframe-r13" will be dropped in SIB2-BR message for Cat-M UE.
prachStartSFCatM.fullName: PRACH Starting subframe for Cat-M CE Level 1

preambMaxNumAttemptCECatM.description:
This parameter defines the maximum number of preamble transmission attempts for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 
Refer to TS 36.321 and TS 36.331 and IE maxNumPreambleAttemptCE-r13.
preambMaxNumAttemptCECatM.fullName: Maximum number of PRACH preamble transmission attempts for Cat-M CE Level 1

preambTxMaxCatM.description:
This parameter defines the maximum number of Random Access transmissions for Cat-M UEs, regardless of CE Levels. 

Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and 3GPP TS 36.321, IE preambleTransMax-CE-r13. 

For example, if the preambMaxNumAttemptCECatM for CE Level 0 and 1 are set to n3, and preambTxMaxCatM is set to n5, then an UE initiating RACH procedure at CE Level 0 would perform up to 3 preamble attempts at CE Level 0 and 2 preamble attempts at CE Level 1.  If another UE starts RACH procedure at CE Level 1, then up to 5 preamble attempts would be done at CE Level 1.

pucchF1NumRepModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the repetition number of the PUCCH Format 1 for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE pucch-NumRepetitionCE-format1-r13.
pucchF1NumRepModeACatM.fullName: Repetition number of PUCCH for Cat-M CE Level 1

pucchNumRepMsg4ModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the number of PUCCH repetitions of the HARQ feedback in response to the Msg4 for Cat-M in CE Level 1 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 RRC IE ‘pucch-NumRepetitionCE-Msg4-Level1-r13’.
pucchNumRepMsg4ModeACatM.fullName: Repetition number of PUCCH for HARQ feedback to Msg4 in Cat-M CE Level 1

puschMaxNumRepModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum number of repetitions for PUSCH of Cat-M UEs in CE modeA. 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE pusch-maxNumRepetitionCEmodeA-r13.

Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.
puschMaxNumRepModeACatM.fullName: Maximum numbers of repetition for PUSCH of Cat-M in CE modeA

puschRepLevModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the repetition level of PUSCH to determine the repetition number of PUSCH messages for Cat-M UEs in CE modeA Level 1. 

This parameter is used to set the 'Repetition Number' field of the DCI Format 6-0A and RAR for Msg3.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.212 
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.213 Table 8.2b.
puschRepLevModeACatM.fullName: Repetition level for PUSCH of Cat-M in CE modeA Level 1

qci1ProtectionTimerCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum time between Cat-M QCI1 bearer establishment and the release of the Cat-M UE to RRC idle mode. 
Cat-M QCI1 establishment starts a configurable timer which keeps the Cat-M UE in RRC connected mode even if there is no activity (e.g. during ringtone) until timer expiry.

qciForVoLTECatM.description:
This parameter specifies operator specific QCI for Cat-M VoLTE. 
If this parameter is set to the value within 128~254, it means operator specific QCI will be handled as well as QCI1 for Cat-M VoLTE.
Default value '255' means no operator specific QCI defined for Cat-M VoLTE.
qciForVoLTECatM.fullName: Operator specific QCI for Cat-M VoLTE

raContResoTmrCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum contention resolution timer for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 
Refer to TS 36.321 and TS 36.331 and IE mac-ContentionResolutionTimer-r13

This parameter is defined per CE Level (1...maxCE-Level-r13) of rach-CE-LevelInfoList-r13.
raContResoTmrCatM.fullName: Maximum contention resolution timer for Cat-M CE Level 1

raPreGrCSizeCatM.description:
This parameter specifies the number of RA preambles per cell that are reserved for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1.
Refer to TS 36.321 and TS 36.331 and IEs RadioResourceConfigCommon, RACH-ConfigCommon, firstPreamble-r13, lastPreamble-r13.

This parameter is defined per CE Level (1...maxCE-Level-r13) of rach-CE-LevelInfoList-r13.
raPreGrCSizeCatM.fullName: Number of random access preambles for Cat-M CE Level 1

raRespWinSizeCatM.description:
This parameter defines the random access response window size for Cat-M UEs in CE Level 1. 
Refer to TS 36.321 and TS 36.331 and IEs RadioResourceConfigCommon, RACH-ConfigCommon, RA-ResponseWindowSize-r13.

This parameter is defined per CE Level (1...maxCE-Level-r13) of rach-CE-LevelInfoList-r13.
raRespWinSizeCatM.fullName: Random access response window size for Cat-M CE Level 1

rrcGuardTimerCatM.description: This timer is started when an RRC message for setup, modification or release of a radio bearer is sent to the Cat-M UE. When the timer expires, the corresponding procedure is aborted.
rrcGuardTimerCatM.fullName: RRC guard timer radio bearer management for Cat-M

siRepPatternCatM.description:
The parameter SI Repetition Pattern defines the common System Information scheduling repetition pattern for all SIs of Cat-M UEs.
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331 and IE si-RepetitionPattern-r13.
Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.

siValidityTimeCatM.description:
This parameter indicates UE whether to delete any stored system information after 24 hours or 3 hours. If set to TRUE, the timer is set to 3h, otherwise the timer is set to 24h. 
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331 and IE si-ValidityTime-r13.

siWindowLenCatM.description:
The parameter SI Window Length defines the common System Information scheduling window for all SIs of Cat-M UEs.
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331 and IE si-WindowLength-BR-r13.
Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.

sib16PeriodicityCatM.description:
This parameter indicates the periodicity of CatM SI-Message which contains SIB16-BR.
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331 and IE si-Periodicity.
Note: If SIB16 is configured in this cell, all Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode may be released when this parameter is online modified.

sib2PeriodicityCatM.description:
This parameter indicates the periodicity of CatM SI-Message which contains SIB2-BR.
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331 and IE si-Periodicity.
Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.

sib3sib4PeriodicityCatM.description:
This parameter indicates the periodicity of CatM SI-Message which contains SIB3-BR and SIB4-BR. SIB3-BR and SIB4-BR are sent in one SI-BR message.
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331.
Note: If SIB4 is configured in this cell, all Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.
sib3sib4PeriodicityCatM.fullName: SIB3-BR and SIB4-BR periodicity for Cat-M

sib5PeriodicityCatM.description:
This parameter indicates the periodicity of CatM SI-Message which contains SIB5-BR.
This is broadcasted in SIB1-BR.
Refer to 3GPP 36.331 and IE si-Periodicity.
Note: If SIB5 is configured in this cell, all Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode may be released when this parameter is online modified.

srProhibitTimerCatM.description: This parameter controls the minimum separation in time between consecutive Scheduling Request transmissions by the UE (refer to 36.321 sec.5.4.4). It can be used to prevent unwanted repetitions of SRs. The parameter is expressed in number of SR periods. It is sent to the UE in the RRC IE sr-ProhibitTimer-r9. It applies to Cat-M UEs. srProhibitTimerCatM = 0 means no minimum interval (SRs can be sent at every SR period).

srbInactivityTimerCatM.description: The parameter defines the time period for the indication of the UE inactivity on signalling radio bearer in both DL and UL directions.

t300ModeACatM.description:
Timer T300 for Cat-M supervises the RRC connection establishment procedure of Cat-M UEs in CE modeA.
Timer T300 supervises the RRC connection establishment procedure. 
Start: Transmission of RRCConnectionRequest
Stop: Reception of RRCConnectionSetup or RRCConnectionReject message, cell re-selection and upon abortion of connection establishment by upper layers

At expiry: Perform the actions as specified in 36.331, 5.3.3.6 

Refer to TS36.331 IE UE-TimersAndConstants: t300
t300ModeACatM.fullName: Timer T300 for Cat-M in CE modeA

t301ModeACatM.description:
Timer T301 for Cat-M supervises the RRC connection re-establishment procedure of Cat-M UEs in CE modeA.
Timer T301 supervises the RRC connection re-establishment procedure. 
Start: Transmission of RRCConnectionReestabilshmentRequest
Stop: Reception of RRCConnectionReestablishment or RRCConnectionReestablishmentReject message as well as when the selected cell becomes unsuitable

At expiry: Go to RRC_IDLE

Refer to TS36.331 IE UE-TimersAndConstants: t301
t301ModeACatM.fullName: Timer T301 for Cat-M in CE modeA

t304IntraLteCatM.description:
Timer T304 supervises the successful completion of a handover or cell change for Cat-M.
The timer is started in the UE in connected mode upon reception of RRCConnectionReconfiguration message including the MobilityControl Information. At timer expiry the UE initiates the RRC connection re-establishment procedure. See TS 36.331.

t310CatM.description:
Timer T310 for Cat-M supervises the recovery from physical layer problems(Radio Link Failure).
Refer to TS36.331 IE UE-TimersAndConstants: t310

t311CatM.description:
Timer T311 supervises the RRC connection re-establishment for Cat-M UEs. 
The timer is started upon initiating the RRC connection re-establishment procedure and is stopped when a suitable cell has been selected. 

Refer to TS36.331 IE UE-TimersAndConstants: t311

tDiscardPdcpCatM.description:
This parameter indicates the delay before a PDCP PDU along with the corresponding PDCP SDU is discarded from the buffer. This timer shall be set in a way that the packet delay defined by the QCI characteristics is kept. The timer can be disabled by setting the parameter to infinity.
This parameter specifies the parameter discardTimer of [36.331]
tDiscardPdcpCatM.fullName: PDCP PDU Timer Discard for DRB Cat-M

tDiscardPdcpQci1CatM.description:
This parameter indicates the delay before a PDCP PDU along with the corresponding PDCP SDU is discarded from the buffer. 
The timer can be disabled by setting the parameter to infinity.
This timer is specific defined for Cat-M QCI1-DRB, other PDCP properties should be set in a way followed as wideband LTE PDCP profile configuration.
tDiscardPdcpQci1CatM.fullName: Timer discard for Cat-M QCI1 DRB PDCP SDU

tDiscardPdcpQci5CatM.description:
This parameter indicates the delay before a PDCP PDU along with the corresponding PDCP SDU is discarded from the buffer. 
The timer can be disabled by setting the parameter to infinity.
This timer is specific defined for Cat-M QCI5-DRB, other PDCP properties should be set in a way followed as wideband LTE PDCP profile configuration.
tDiscardPdcpQci5CatM.fullName: Timer discard for Cat-M QCI5 DRB PDCP SDU

tHalfRrcConCatM.description: The minimal time period that the eNB waits for an RRC CONNECTION SETUP COMPLETE message after sending a RRC CONNECTION SETUP message for Cat-M UEs.
tHalfRrcConCatM.fullName: Timer min lifetime of half-open RRC connection for Cat-M

tL2AckRrcRelCatM.description: The maximum time period  indicates the time after which the RRC L3 releases the RRC connection for Cat-M call only, if no positive ack is received from L2 to the RRC CONNECTION RELEASE message.  This timer has to absorb the potential preceding NAS transmission, which can be approximated via rrcGuardTimerCatM.  This timer is reset to 1.25 second upon reception of L1 HARQ ACK of RRC Connection Release, as per 3GPP R2-169034.
tL2AckRrcRelCatM.fullName: Timer missing L2 ack for Cat-M RRC connection release

tPeriodicBsrCatM.description: Likely a timer/duration setting related to "t Periodic Bsr category (e.g. Cat-M / LTE-M device category) M" on the CATMPR object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

tPeriodicPhrModeACatM.description: This parameter specifies sending periodic power headroom reports for Cat-M UE in CE modeA.
tPeriodicPhrModeACatM.fullName: Periodic PHR timer for Cat-M in CE modeA

tPollRetrDrb.description:
This timer is used by the transmitting side of an AM RLC entity in order to retransmit a poll.
This parameter specifies the parameter t-pollRetransmit of [36.331]
tPollRetrDrb.fullName: Timer Poll Retransmit for DRB Cat-M

tPollRetrSrb.description:
This timer is used by the transmitting side of an AM RLC entity in order to retransmit a poll.
This parameter specifies the parameter t-pollRetransmit of [36.331]
tPollRetrSrb.fullName: Timer Poll Retransmit for SRB Cat-M

tProhibDrb.description:
This timer is used by the receiving side of an AM RLC entity in order to prohibit transmission of a STATUS PDU.
This parameter specifies the parameter t-StatusProhibit of [36.331]
tProhibDrb.fullName: Timer Status Prohibit for DRB Cat-M

tProhibSrb.description:
This timer is used by the receiving side of an AM RLC entity in order to prohibit transmission of a STATUS PDU.
This parameter specifies the parameter t-StatusProhibit of [36.331]
tProhibSrb.fullName: Timer Status Prohibit for SRB Cat-M

tProhibitPhrModeACatM.description: This parameter specifies minimum intermediate time between two consecutive Power Headroom Reports for Cat-M in CE modeA.
tProhibitPhrModeACatM.fullName: Prohibited PHR timer for Cat-M in CE modeA

tReTxBsrTimeCatM.description: This parameter defines the time period when the BSR is reported when the Cat-M UE has data available for transmission and no corresponding UL grant is received so far.

tReordDrb.description:
This timer is used by the receiving side of an AM RLC entity for reordering, PDU loss detection and delay of STATUS PDU transmission. This timer depends on HARQ RTT and number of HARQ retransmissions.
This parameter specifies the parameter t-Reordering of [36.331]

tReordDrbQci1.description:
This timer is used by the receiving side of an UM RLC entity for reordering, PDU loss detection and delay of STATUS PDU transmission. This timer depends on HARQ RTT and number of HARQ retransmissions.
This parameter specifies the parameter t-Reordering of [36.331]

tReordSrb.description:
This timer is used by the receiving side of an AM RLC entity for reordering, PDU loss detection and delay of STATUS PDU transmission. This timer depends on HARQ RTT and number of HARQ retransmissions.
This parameter specifies the parameter t-Reordering of [36.331]

taCmdProhibitTimerCatM.description: This parameter determines the interval between two times DL transmissions triggered by TA command transmission for a CatM UE. The timer is started/restarted every time DL scheduling triggered by TA command transmission, and DL scheduling can be triggered by TA command transmission only when the timer is not running.
taCmdProhibitTimerCatM.fullName: The prohibit timer of scheduling dedicated TA command for CatM UE

taMaxOffsetCatM.description: This parameter determines the maximum allowed Time Alignment offset for CatM UE. If the value is exceeded, TA command is sent to the Cat-M UE to adjust UL timing.
taMaxOffsetCatM.fullName: Time alignment maximum offset for CatM UE

taTimerCatM.description: This parameter determines the number of subframes after which a CatM UE assumes it is out-of-sync in UL if no Time Alignment command was received.
taTimerCatM.fullName: Time alignment Timer for CatM UE

taTimerMarginCatM.description:
This parameter defines lead with respect to the taTimer expiration time for starting to send the periodic Timing Advance Command for CatM UE.
This parameter is not used when taTimerCatM is set to infinity.
taTimerMarginCatM.fullName: Time alignment Timer margin for CatM UE

ulGrantTimerForTACatM.description: This parameter determines the frequency of UL Grant for TA measurement. The timer is started on receiving MSG3, and restarted every time there's UL transmission occur. When the timer expired, the UL grant for TA measurement will be sent to CatM UE. With a configured value infinity, UL Grant for TA measurement is disabled.
ulGrantTimerForTACatM.fullName: The timer of scheduling UL grant for TA measurement

ulMaxHarqTxQci1CatM.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum number of HARQ transmissions in UL for Cat-M QCI1-DRB.
Refer to 3GPP TS 36.331 and IE maxHARQ-Tx.
But due to asynchronized HARQ for Cat-M UEs, the RRC IE ‘maxHARQ-Tx’ will be ignored by Cat-M UEs, therefore this parameter configuration is only used by eNB internally.
ulMaxHarqTxQci1CatM.fullName: UL Maximum number of HARQ transmission for Cat-M QCI1-DRB

ulMcsThrMultiHarqMaxTbsCatM.description: Likely a threshold value used to trigger or gate behavior related to "uplink Modulation and Coding Scheme threshold Multi Harq maximum Tbs category (e.g. Cat-M / LTE-M device category) M" on the CATMPR object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

ulTargetBlerModeACatM.description: This parameter defines target Block Error Ratio (BLER) for uplink Link Adaptation in percents used for Cat-M UEs in CE modeA.
ulTargetBlerModeACatM.fullName: UL target BLER of Cat-M in CE modeA

ulsMinTbsModeACatM.description:
This parameter specifies the minimum UL TBS (segment size) during Cat-M CE mode A link adaptation.
The allowed value range is derived from Table 7.1.7.2.1-1 in 3GPP TS 36.213 (1&2 PRB case and MAC constraints).
ulsMinTbsModeACatM.fullName: Minimum UL transport block size for Cat-M CE mode A

catMPrSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC CATMPRSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an CATMPRSPARE instance.

name.description:
This is the name of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The content is filled by the BTS and cannot be changed.

The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

value.description:
This is the value of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The allowed parameter values are defined in the feature specification.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.

authorityKeyIdentifier.description:
This parameter specifies the identifier of the public key corresponding to the private key that is used to sign the certificate.

Note: This parameter is valid for AirScale hardware unit type only.

caType.description:

fccId.description:
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) certification identifier of the CBSD.

FCC ID = Grantee Code(G) + Product Code(P)
Current Grantee Code Process:
- Grantee code = 3 characters
- Product code = maximum of 14 characters
- AGGPPPPPPPPPPPPPP, where A = grantee code character limited to alphabetic character only

New Grantee Code Process:
- Grantee code = 5 characters
– Product code = maximum of 14 characters
– #GGGGPPPPPPPPPPPPPP, where # = grantee code character limited to numeric value only (no zeros or ones)

This parameter describes the center frequencies, in 10 MHz block increments, within the 3.5GHz spectrum (3550 – 3700 MHz) for which CBSD seeks information.
This parameter is encoded as a bitmap, where bit N is set to "0" if the corresponding center frequency is not in selection list, and set to "1" if the corresponding center frequency is within the selection list.

Bitmask with bits defined as follows: 
0 – center frequency 3555
1 - center frequency 3560
2 - center frequency 3570
3 - center frequency 3585
4 - center frequency 3595
5 - center frequency 3605
6 - center frequency 3615
7 - center frequency 3625
8 - center frequency 3635
9 - center frequency 3645
10 - center frequency 3655
11 - center frequency 3665
12 - center frequency 3675
13 - center frequency 3685
14 - center frequency 3695

acBarring0To9.description:
Access Class Barring - 0 to 9
Defines the 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) access class barring factor for access overload classes 0 through 9. This parameter is used to determine the value of the ac-Barring0to9-r9 field of the AC-BarringConfig1XRTT-r9 Information Element (IE) broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message. It is the parameter “PSIST” in C.S0004  for access overload classes 0 through 9
acBarring0To9.fullName: AC barring factor for overload classes 0 to 9

acBarring0To9Adapt.description:
The switch enable/disable the SIB8 acBarring0To9 adaption.
FALSE means that ac-Barring0to9-r9 field of SIB8 AC-BarringConfig1XRTT-r9 is set to the value of acBarring0To9 of CDFIM rttAcBar/rttAcBarOvl.  

TRUE means that ac-Barring0to9-r9 field of SIB8 AC-BarringConfig1XRTT-r9 is set to the value based on combination of both acBarring0To9 of CDFIM rttAcBar/rttAcBarOvl and ac-BarringFactor of SIB2 ac-BarringForMo-Data

The SIB8 acBarring0To9 adaption is applicable for:static AC Barring or automatic AC Barring for overload or RRC connection triggered AC Barring.

Access Class Barring - Emergency Calls and Emergency Message Transmissions  when automatic AC barring broadcast condition is met due to BTS C-plane overload.

This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message. It is the parameter “PSIST_EMG” in C.S0004.

acBarringMsgOvl.description:
Access Class Barring - Message Transmissions when automatic AC barring broadcast condition is met due to BTS C-plane overload.

acBarringReg.description:

acBarringReg.fullName: AC barring modification factor for registration

acBarringRegOvl.description:
Access Class Barring - Autonomous Registrations when automatic AC barring broadcast condition is met due to BTS C-plane overload.
Defines the 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) access class barring modification factor for autonomous registrations. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message. It is the parameter “REG_PSIST” in C.S0004.

cdfimId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of the MOC CDFIM.
It uniquely identifies a CDFIM instance.
cdfimId.fullName: CDMA2000 frequency idle mode configuration identifier

foreignNidReg.description: Defines whether the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) Network Identification (NID) roamer registration indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration is broadcast. Value TRUE is to enable foreign NID roamers for autonomous registration. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and is provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

foreignSidReg.description: Defines whether the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) System Identification (SID) roamer registration indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration is broadcast. Value TRUE is to enable foreign SID roamers for autonomous registration. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and is provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

homeReg.description: Defines whether the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) home registration indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration is broadcast. Value TRUE is to enable home (non-roaming) autonomous registration. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode only when the homeRegIncluded parameter is set to TRUE.

hrpResTiFHM.description:
CDMA2000 HRPD Cell Reselection Timer factor if the UE is in High Mobility state.
The field tResHrpd is multiplied with this factor if the UE is in High Mobility state as defined in 36.304
hrpResTiFHM.fullName: HRPD cell reselection timer factor high mobility

hrpResTiFMM.description:
CDMA2000 HRPD Cell Reselection Timer factor if the UE is in Medium Mobility state.
The field tResHrpd is multiplied with this factor if the UE is in Medium Mobility state as defined in 36.304.
hrpResTiFMM.fullName: HRPD cell reselection timer factor med mobility

hrpdArfcn.description:
HRPD carrier frequency within a CDMA2000 Band.
The parameter value is based on the absolute radio-frequency channel number “ARFCN”.

hrpdBdClBcl.description:
CDMA2000 HRPD Frequency Band (used in Band Class List).
Identifies the CDMA2000 HRPD Frequency Band in which the CDMA2000 Carrier can be found.

hrpdBdClNcl.description: Identifies the CDMA2000 Frequency Band in which the CDMA2000 Carrier can be found.

hrpdCResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the Bandclass of CDMA2000 HRPD
Absolute priority  (0 means: lowest priority).

Equal priorities between RATs are not supported according to [3GPP 36.304].

hrpdExSel.description:
Distributes Physical Cell Ids between 3GPP-R8 List and 3GPP-R9 Extension List.
"R8ListPartOnly" means, the related Physical Cell Id has to be placed in the 3GPP-R8 NCL.
"R9ExtensionPartPossible" means, the related Physical Cell Id can be placed in the 3GPP-R8 NCL, if  all Physical Cell Ids with "R8ListPartOnly" are already placed in the 3GPP-R8 NCL and there is space left (up to 16 IDs allowed). Otherwise they shall be placed in the 3GPP-R9 Extension-NCL (acc. to ASN.1 rules)

hrpdFrqThrH.description:
High threshold towards this Bandclass of CDMA2000 HRPD

hrpdFrqThrL.description:
Low threshold towards this Bandclass of  CDMA2000 HRPD
This specifies the low threshold used in reselection towards CDMA2000 HRPD

hrpdPreRegAllowed.description: Defines whether the UE is allowed to perform pre-registration when the UE does not have a valid / current pre-registration. A value of false indicates UE is not allowed to perform preregistration in this cell.

hrpdPreRegZoneId.description: Defines the evolved High Rate Packet Data (eHRPD) Pre-registration Information.  This parameter contains the primary Color Code of the eHRPD Access Network (AN) which this Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (EUTRA) cell overlays.  The UE uses this parameter to determine whether it should pre-register with the eHRPD network.

hrpdSecPreRegZoneId1.description: Defines the evolved High Rate Packet Data (eHRPD) secondary pre-registration Information.  This parameter contains the secondary Color Code of the eHRPD Access Network (AN) which this Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (EUTRA) cell overlays.  The UE uses this parameter to determine whether it should pre-register with the eHRPD network. This parameter defines the first instance of secondary Color Codes which can be assigned to an eHRPD cell.

hrpdSecPreRegZoneId2.description: Defines the evolved High Rate Packet Data (eHRPD) secondary pre-registration Information.  This parameter contains the secondary Color Code of the eHRPD Access Network (AN) which this Evolved Universal Terrestrial Radio Access (EUTRA) cell overlays.  The UE uses this parameter to determine whether it should pre-register with the eHRPD network. This parameter defines the second instance of secondary Color Codes which can be assigned to an eHRPD cell.

idleLBHrpdCelResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the CDMA2000 HRPD band class used for idle mode load balancing.
For this parameter, 6 is the highest priority and 0 the lowest.

Note:
According to 3GPP 36.304, carriers in different RATs must have different Cell Reselection Priorities.
idleLBHrpdCelResPrio.fullName: CDMA HRPD band priority for idle mode load balancing

idleLBHrpdCelResWeight.description:
Weight factor of CDMA HRPD band used by round robin algorithm for idle mode load balancing.
When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in selecting main target for IdleModeMobilityControlInfo for load balancing. Weighted round robin algorithm shall select always one target frequency for idle mode load balancing, which is matching UE capabilities, to be used as main target for idle mode load balancing and this target will have always highest  priority assigned in RRC Release message.  All other target frequency for idle mode load balancing matching UE capabilities and configured in LNCEL, IRFIM, UFFIM, CDFIM and GNFL will be added as well, but with lowered priorities as configured for SIB with kept hierarchy of priorities.  The algorithm shall calculate proportional weights corresponding to configured values. There is no check about the sum of weights configured by the user.
idleLBHrpdCelResWeight.fullName: CDMA HRPD band weight factor idle mode load balancing

idleLBRttCelResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the CDMA2000 1xRTT band class used for idle mode load balancing.
For this parameter, 6 is the highest priority and 0 the lowest.
When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in IdleModeMobilityControlInfo for load balancing.

Note:
According to 3GPP 36.304, carriers in different RATs must have different Cell Reselection Priorities.
idleLBRttCelResPrio.fullName: CDMA 1xRTT band priority for idle mode load balancing

idleLBRttCelResWeight.description:
Weight factor of CDMA 1xRTT band used by round robin algorithm for idle mode load balancing.
When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in selecting main target for IdleModeMobilityControlInfo for load balancing. Weighted round robin algorithm shall select always one target frequency for idle mode load balancing, which is matching UE capabilities, to be used as main target for idle mode load balancing and this target will have always highest  priority assigned in RRC Release message.  All other target frequency for idle mode load balancing matching UE capabilities and configured in LNCEL, IRFIM, UFFIM, CDFIM and GNFL will be added as well, but with lowered priorities as configured for SIB with kept hierarchy of priorities.  The algorithm shall calculate proportional weights corresponding to configured values. There is no check about the sum of weights configured by the user.
idleLBRttCelResWeight.fullName: CDMA 1xRTT band weight factor idle mode load balancing

multiNid.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) multiple Network Identification (NID) storage indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration. When this parameter is set to TRUE, the UE may store entries in SID_NID_LIST for each SID.  This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and is provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

multiSid.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) multiple System Identification (SID) storage indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration. When this parameter is set to TRUE, the UE may store entries in SID_NID_LIST having different SIDs.  This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and is provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

nid.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) Network Identification (NID) associated with this cell for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and is provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

paramReg.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) parameter-change registration indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration. When this parameter is set to TRUE, the UE should register on parameter change events. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and is provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

powerDownReg.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) power down registration indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration. Set this parameter to TRUE for the UE to register immediately before powering down. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC CONNECTED mode.

powerUpReg.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) power up registration indicator for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration. regZone.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) registration zone number associated with this cell for Circuit Switched Fallback (CSFB) pre-registration. This parameter is broadcast in the RRC: SystemInformationBlockType8 (SIB8) message and is provided in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

CRLDP Contained in Certificate extension

CRLDistributionPoint.description: URI of the defined CRL distribution point.

CRLDownloadStatus.description: The status of the last download of CRL

CRLIssuer.description: This parameter holds the name of the issuing instance of the current certificate revocation list.
CRLIssuer.fullName: Issuer of the current certificate revocation list

CRLNextUpdate.description:
Time of next update of CRL 

The format is:
YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.SSS[+-]hh:mm
where hh:mm is the offset from GMT.

CRLNumOfRevCert.description: The number of revoked certificates in CRL

The format is:

where hh:mm is the offset from GMT.

CRLUpdateFailureReason.description:
The failure reason could be the following:
List (CRL) for one of the following reasons:
- The LDAP binding fails. 
- The LDAP search is emtpy (no CRL found). / The LDAP search contains more
than one entry. 
- The CRL signature validation fails. 
- The CRL file exceeds the BTS storage limit.

autoCertDelete.description: Enables automatic deletion of expired or superseded certificates from the certificate handler's store.

This parameter defines domain of Subject Alternative Names to be added to BTS EE operator certificate to be used as alternative IKE identities. It will be ignored if btsNumberOfSubjectAltNames is set to zero (or not set at all).
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
The default value is empty string.
btsDomainOfSubjectAltNames.fullName: Domain of alternative BTS identities in Subject Alternative Name

btsNumberOfSubjectAltNames.description:
This parameter defines number of Subject Alternative Names to be added to BTS EE operator certificate to be used as alternative IKE identities.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
The default value is 0.
btsNumberOfSubjectAltNames.fullName: Number of alternative BTS identities in Subject Alternative Name

caCertificateUpdateTime.description: This parameter is the number of days in advance prior to BTS own trust anchor certificate(s) or any of the peer trust anchor certificate(s) is expired or due to expire, that BTS shall raise an alarm.
caCertificateUpdateTime.fullName: Update time for CA certificate renewal

caSubjectName.description: This parameter is the subject name of the CMP server. It may either be detected by DHCP upon autoconnection or configured by the management system.

certhId.description: This parameter identifies the certificate handler configuration. The value is always 1.

certificateFingerprint.description:
Certificate Fingerprint
It should be in “Hex Ascii” format with “FF:EE:DD”.

certificateType.description:
Certificate Type
The Certificate type could be TA (Trust Anchor)/RA(Registration authority)/CA (Certificate Authority) .

cmpDirectory.description: This is the operator configured CMP Directory to be used for addressing the Certificate Management Protocol server.

cmpPollingTimeout.description: This is the maximum time in seconds BTS will wait for a CMP Polling cycle before timeout

cmpServerIpAddress.description:
This is the IP address of the Certificate Management Protocol server. 
If feature LTE955 is activated for private backhaul, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.
If public backhaul is enabled, an address of either IPv4 or IPv6 may be provided.
Note: The above rule can be ignored for Small Cell if LTE3978 is activated.
Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC 4291.

cmpServerPort.description: This is the port number to be used for addressing the Certificate Management Protocol server.

cmpState.description: This is the state of CMP operation when BTS is performing certificate enrollment.
cmpState.officialRange:
0: not_started 
1: started 
2: accepted 
3: rejected 
4: polling 
5: failed 
6: start 
7: completed

crlUpdatePeriod.description: This parameter specifies the period for executing a periodical update of the Certificate Revocation List. The value is given in hours. Value 0 means "no periodical update".

secCaSubjectName.description: This parameter identifies the Secondary CMP server by its subject name. It may either be detected by DHCP upon autoconnection or configured by the management system.

secCmpDirectory.description:
This is the operator configured Secondary CMP Directory to be used for addressing the Certificate Management Protocol server.
Default value is pkix.

secCmpServerIpAddress.description:
This is the IP address of the Secondary Certificate Management Protocol server. 

If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC4291.

secCmpServerPort.description:
This is the port number to be used for addressing the Secondary Certificate Management Protocol server.
The default value is 1024.

cmpCrlSrcIpv4AddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the IPADDRESSV4 object instance which holds the IPv4 address that BTS uses as source IP address in all communications with CMP/CRL servers.
If this parameter is not configured, BTS uses the M-plane IP address to communicate with CMP/CRL servers.
If CMP/CRL traffic shall not pass through IPsec tunnels an appropriate IPsec bypass rules has to be defined.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-1
cmpCrlSrcIpv4AddressDN.fullName: Source IP address used for CMP/CRL Servers

cmpCrlSrcIpv6AddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the IPADDRESSV6 object instance which holds the IPv6 address that BTS uses as source IP address in all communications with CMP/CRL servers.
If this parameter is not configured, BTS uses the M-plane IP address to communicate with CMP/CRL servers.
If CMP/CRL traffic shall not pass through IPsec tunnels an appropriate IPsec bypass rules has to be defined.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV6-1
cmpCrlSrcIpv6AddressDN.fullName: Source IP address used for CMP/CRL Servers

antlDN.description: Distinguished name of object ANTL or ASIANTL

channelId.description: Instance identifier of the object CHANNEL.

direction.description: States the direction of the channel of the related antenna line.

iqStreamId.description:
For CHANNELGROUP with multiple CHANNEL objects of the same direction (Tx or Rx), this parameter defines I/Q data stream which eNB shall assign to the CHANNEL.
As a part of LTE3639 feature, this parameter can be used to switch I/Q data streams between antenna lines to compensate sub-optimal cabling.

In TX direction, I/Q data streams are generated by DSP as composition of 3GPP antenna port signals. 2TX cell generates two I/Q data streams (0 & 1), 4TX cell generates four I/Q data streams (0, 1, 2, 3) and so on. 

I/Q data streams are associated with Cell-specific Reference Signals so that:
CHANNEL with iqStreamId = 0 carries I/Q data stream with CRS-R0
CHANNEL with iqStreamId = 1 carries I/Q data stream with CRS-R1
CHANNEL with iqStreamId = 2 carries I/Q data stream with CRS-R2
CHANNEL with iqStreamId = 3 carries I/Q data stream with CRS-R3

In RX direction, I/Q data streams are input for combining algorithms in DSP receiver.

resourceDN.description: Distinguished name of object resource that belongs to this CHANNEL. This parameter is only valid for LTE cells (LCELL object).

channelGroupId.description:
Instance identifier of the object CHANNELGROUP. In case the cell is a  "Super Cell" or "Liquid Cell" the CHANNELGROUP contains the related CHANNEL objects of the subcell, otherwise it contains the CHANNEL objects of the cell.
For Lean GSM/CMST, it can be upto 36 instance id.

mainCarrierId.description:
This parameter will indicate the main carrier id under which all replica carriers are defined for a single logical carrier. 
It will increase in sequential order for each logical main carrier.

Note: This parameter is only applicable for LCELC.

replicaId.description:
This parameter defines the Replica ID for either Lean GSM or CMST feature.
In Lean GSM, it should be considered as Beam ID.
In Composited Multi Site Transmission (CMST), it should be considered as Node ID.

Note: This parameter is only applicable for LCELC.

clockId.description: This is the instance identifier of the CLOCK object.

holdOverModeUsed.description: This parameter defines whether System Module fan speed is optimized by oscillator temperature or noise level.

inputConfigBiDiMode.description: Configures whether the synchronisation reference input (e.g. 1PPS/10MHz timing input) operates in bidirectional mode rather than input-only mode.

outputConfigBiDiMode.description: Configures whether the synchronisation reference output operates in bidirectional mode rather than output-only mode.

outputConfiguration1Pps.description:
This parameter controls the output of the 1PPS/ToD signals at the SYNC OUT connector. Additionally, a user can select if the 1PPS/ToD signals are kept enabled in holdover mode. 

The possible settings are:
- Disabled = The 1PPS/ToD output signals are disabled (default).
- EnabledWithBtsInputReference = The 1PPS/ToD output signals are enabled in normal mode but will be disabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.
- EnabledWithoutBtsInputReference = The 1PPS/ToD output signals are enabled in normal mode and are kept enabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.

outputConfiguration1PpsBackplane.description: Configures whether the 1PPS timing signal is output onto the equipment backplane (for distribution to other modules in the cabinet), and whether it is qualified by the BTS's input timing reference.

outputConfiguration1PpsFHS.description:
This parameter controls the output of the 1PPS/ToD signals on the sync-out port of the Fronthaul Switches.  Additionally, a user can select, if the 1PPS/ToD signals are kept enabled, when BTS operates in holdover mode. 

The possible settings are:
- Disabled = The 1PPS/ToD output signals are disabled (default).
- EnabledWithBtsInputReference = The 1PPS/ToD output signals are enabled in normal mode on the sync-out port of the Fronthaul Switch, but ToD signal will be disabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.
- EnabledWithoutBtsInputReference = The 1PPS/ToD output signals are enabled in normal mode on the sync-out port of the Fronthaul Switch, and will be kept enabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.
outputConfiguration1PpsFHS.fullName: Output configuration of Fronthaul Switch 1PPS/ToD clock signals

outputConfiguration2M048.description:
This parameter controls the output of the 2.048MHz signal at the SYNC OUT connector.  

The possible settings are:
- Disabled = The 2.048MHz output signal is disabled (default).
- EnabledWithBtsInputReference = The 2.048MHz output signal is enabled in normal mode but will be disabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.
- EnabledWithoutBtsInputReference = The 2.048MHz output signal is enabled in normal mode and is kept enabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.

outputConfigurationFCLK.description:
This parameter controls the output of the GSM Fclk/Fn signals at the SYNC OUT connector. Additionally, a user can select if the GSM Fclk/Fn signals are kept enabled in holdover mode. 

The possible settings are:
- Disabled = The  GSM Fclk/Fn output signals are disabled (default).
- EnabledWithBtsInputReference = The  GSM Fclk/Fn output signals are enabled in normal mode but will be disabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.
- EnabledWithoutBtsInputReference = The  GSM Fclk/Fn output signals are enabled in normal mode and are kept enabled when the BTS is operating in holdover mode.
outputConfigurationFCLK.fullName: Output configuration of GSM Fclk/Fn clock signal

outputConfigurationPdh.description:
This parameter defines if the PDH output interfaces are usable as synchronization reference or not. Additionally, an user can select if the PDH signal shall be usable as synchronization reference also in holdover mode. 

The possible settings are:
- Disabled = The PDH output signal isn’t usable as synchronization reference (default).
- EnabledWithBtsInputReference = The PDH output signal is usable as synchronization reference in normal mode but isn’t usable when the BTS is switching to holdover mode.
- EnabledWithoutBtsInputReference = The PDH output signal is usable as synchronization reference in normal mode and is kept usable when the BTS is running in holdover mode.

Note:
When the PDH outputs are useable as synchronization reference, the output signal is traceable to BTS system clock.
outputConfigurationPdh.fullName: Output configuration of PDH clock signal

sModDN.description:
This parameter defines the System Module SMOD to which the Synchronization related configurations are assigned to.
It has to be defined in the format: MRBTS-<id>/EQM-<id>/APEQM-<id>/CABINET-<id>/SMOD-<id>.
Example: MRBTS-1/EQM-1/APEQM-50/CABINET-1/SMOD-1.

syncInputPrio.description:
This parameter defines the priority of the selected sync input at the core system module.

ulCoMpMaxCandidateRequesters.description:
Maximum number of serving cells which can select a single (candidate) cell as an UL CoMP candidate cell. (Solution may impose additional restrictions.)  This parameter enables the operator to specify an upper limit on the parameter used. Decreasing this parameter will reduce the maximum number of SINR query requests received by a single candidate cell, and will also decrease the number of different serving cells which can simultaneously retrieve helper data from the same single helper cell.

If there is the wish to reduce the amount of processing and/or network traffic loading resulting from SINR queries, then this parameter may be reduced. By reducing this parameter the amount of (SINR) messaging overhead traveling over the system can be reduced. This might be done for example, if the GbE statistics or the on-time arrival rates for helper data indicate there is a problematic amount of network congestion.
If there is the wish to allow each helper cell to receive queries from a larger number of different serving cells, then this parameter may be increased. 
This parameter impacts to candidate set selector functionality, and it is calculated in some intervals, maybe every 15mins. Thus, even it is online modifiable, it is applied with some delay.

ulCoMpMaxCandidateSetLimit.description:
Maximum number of cells that a serving cell will include in the UL CoMP candidate set in any TTI. (Solution may impose additional restrictions.  This parameter enables the operator to specify an upper limit on the parameter used.)

Each serving cell can request SINR measurements from a group of candidate cells. This parameter limits the maximum number of such candidates, which can be queried by a single serving cell.  The list of candidates is provided to each cell by a candidate selector function, which uses this parameter. If the operator wishes to reduce the amount of processing and/or network traffic loading resulting from SINR queries, then this parameter may be reduced. If the operator wishes to allow each serving cell to query a larger number of candidate cells for SINR measurements, then this parameter may be increased.
- This parameter impacts to candidate set selector functionality, and it is calculated in some intervals, maybe every 15mins. Thus, even it is online modifiable, it is applied with some delay.
ulCoMpMaxCandidateSetLimit.fullName: UL CoMP Max Candidate Set Limit

ulCoMpMaxHelperEgress.description:
For a 2 Rx cell, the allowed egress traffic as percentage of the maximum possible resource blocks that a single cell could provide if it provided all of its Rx of help, across its entire BW, to each of 4 different cells.   Used to limit the amount of helper data sent by a helper cell. (Solution may impose additional restrictions.  This parameter enables the operator to specify an upper limit on the parameter used.)  For example, if the cell is a 2Rx 20MHhz cell, and parameter is set to 50%, then (on average across those cells)  50 PRBs on each of the 2 Rx may transmitted for each of the different requesting/serving cells, for a total of 4* 2* 50 = 400 RBs.
For a 4 Rx cells, the allowed egress traffic as percentage of the maximum possible resource blocks that a single cell could provide if it provided all of its Rx of help, across its entire BW, to each of 2 different cells.   Used to limit the amount of helper data sent by a helper cell. (Solution may impose additional restrictions.  This parameter enables the operator to specify an upper limit on the parameter used.)  For example, if the cell is a 4 Rx 20MHhz cell, and parameter is set to 50%, then (on average across those cells) 50 PRBs for each of the 4 Rx may transmitted to each of the different requesting/serving cells, for a total of 2 * 4* 50 = 400 RBs.

Each UL CoMP "helper cell" receives requests for helper data from different serving cells. This parameter places limit on the total amount of helper data which the helper cell can provide in each TTI. If the operator wishes to reduce the amount of UL CoMP traffic provided by this cell over the gigabit ethernet network, then operator can decrease this parameter.

ulCoMpMaxHelperIngress.description:
Allowed ingress traffic as percentage of the maximum possible resource blocks that the cell could receive if the cell requests the entire BW of that cell, from the maimum number of cells, i.e. supporting eight Rx IRC with a total of 6Rx received if it is a 2 Rx cell, or total of 4Rx receivedif it is a 4 Rx cell. This is used to limit the amount of helper data sent by a single helper cell.  (Solution may impose additional restrictions.  This parameter enables the operator to specify an upper limit on the parameter used.) For example, a) if the cell is a 2Rx 20MHhz cell, and parameter is set to 50%, then 50 PRBs on each of the 6 different Rx may received for a total of 6 * 50 = 300 RBs, b) if the cell is a 4Rx 20MHhz cell, and parameter is set to 50%, then 50 PRBs on each of the 4 different Rx may received for a total of 4 * 50 = 200 RBs.

Each UL CoMP transmits requests for helper data from one or more different helper cells. This parameter places a limit on the total amount of helper data which the serving cell can request during each TTI. If the operator wishes to reduce the amount of UL CoMP traffic provided by this cell over the gigabit ethernet network, then operator can decrease this parameter.

ulCoMpSinrAlpha.description:
The parameter determines the filtering coefficient of the UL CoMP SINR measurements for averaging both serving cell and helper cell.  As alpha decreases, the existing average given greater importance, and the most recent instantaneous observation is given less importance, i.e. filtering time constant increases (more filtering).

The long term average SINR is calculated for a specific UE. At a high level, this is done based upon the instantaneous SINR observations, where the avgSINR is the current average SINR estimate for that UE, i.e. along the lines of avgSINR = alpha*SINR + (1-alpha)* avgSINR.

ulCoMpSinrThreshold.description:
The received uplink signal from a neighbor cell is combined to the serving cell signal if its SINR is less than ulCoMPSinrThreshold below the SINR of the serving cell signal.

The recommended default value is for:
- 2RX CoMP: 10 dB
- 4RX CoMP: 15 dB

iqCompression.description:
This parameter describes if IQ compression is used for related port. Parameter can be set only for CPRI links.
None means IQ Compression function is not enabled, 15bits for I or Q; 12bits means 15-12bits algorithm. 9bits means 15-9 bits algorithm. 10bits means 15-10 bits algorithm.

- iqCompression can be set only for specific ports:
- For SMOD (FSIH):
o iqCompression can be configured to ports 7, 9, and/or 11 only. When port n (7, 9, 11) is configured, port n+1(8, 10, 12) is not used by the BTS.
- For BBMOD (FBIH or ABIA):
o iqCompression can be configured in CABLINKs with portID of the BBMOD to ports 1, 3, and/or 5 for FBIH, and ports 1, 2, and/or 3 for ABIA only. When port n is configured with iqCompression, the corresponding port n+1(2, 4, 6) for FBIH or n+3(4, 5, 6) for ABIA cannot process IQ data by the BTS.

linkSpeed.description:
This parameter defines the optical port speed.

1:Obsai3Gbps - When this value is configured, BTS enables the RP3-01 link speed at 4x line rate and always remain at that speed. 
2:Obsai6Gbps - When this value is configured, BTS enables the RP3-01 link speed at 8x line rate and always remain at that speed.
3:Cpri2 - When this value is configured, BTS enables the CPRI rate option 2 (link speed at 1228.8 Mbps) line rate and always remain at that speed.
4:Cpri3 - When this value is configured, BTS enables the CPRI rate option 3 (link speed at 2457.6 Mbps) line rate and always remain at that speed.
5:Cpri5 - When this value is configured, BTS enables the CPRI rate option 5 (link speed at 4915.2 Mbps) line rate and always remain at that speed.
6:Cpri6 - When this value is configured, BTS enables the CPRI rate option 6 (link speed at 6144.0 Mbps) line rate and always remain at that speed.
7:Cpri7 - When this value is configured, BTS enables the CPRI rate option 7 (link speed at 9830.4 Mbps) line rate and always remain at that speed. 

In FSIH System Module 9.8Gbps is allowed only on ports 7,9 and 11. If port n (7,9,11) is configured to 9.8Gbps, the adjacent ports n+1( 8,10 or 12) will become not applicable and is ignored by the BTS software. 
 
BTS will dynamically decide if BTS restart or dropping of cells is needed.

cranGain.description:
This parameter configures the CRAN gain, i.e., from which cells the RX-IQ data shall be used.

When configured to 'ON', the RX data of all internal as well as external helper cells are used. The CRAN gain is maximal.
When configured to 'OFF', only the RX data of the own cell is used. In this case there is no CRAN gain. In this case 2RX IRC combining is used an the application for all cells of the CRAN node.

IMPORTANT:
For maximal CRAN gain it is recommended to configure the value 'off' only temporary for test purposes.

Note:
CRAN-gain switching is supported only for FDD.

cranNodeId.description:

The value assigned shall be unique within the cluster.

Note: For LTE2662, the value shall be assigned to value '1'.

ulCoMpSinrThreshold.description:

The received uplink signal from a neighbor cell is combined to the serving cell signal if its SINR is less than ulCoMPSinrThreshold below the SINR of the serving cell signal.

The recommended default value is 15 dB for 8RX CoMP.

The value '0' means disabling subframe skipping.

defaultPlmnGroupId.description:
Group which is used if there is no explicit assignment.

Online modification is performed if the profile is not assigned to any LNCEL or if the feature is deactivated in all assigned cells, i.e. if cellResourceSharingMode is equal to 'none'.
If a cell contains PLMN IDs which are not part of the assigned cell resource group profile (CRGPR) instance, the PLMN IDs are considered as part of the default PLMN group.

All UEs/traffic not being associated with a PLMN ID (no usual scenario known) is considered as belonging to the default PLMN group.

plmnGroupId.description: The parameter assigns the PLMN Id to a PLMN group.

plmnGroupShare.description:
Specifies the share of the cell resource group on a percentage basis.

IMPORTANT:
Because TDD has less DL and UL TTIs per frame, so in order to have enough chances to be scheduled, TDD's value range shall be within 25 % and 75 %.
Lower bound 25% is decided based on uplink scheduling. There are 4 UL TTIs per frame, it is expected that each CRG will be scheduled at least once per frame for both downlink and uplink, so CRG share is set to start from 25%.

Then upper bound is 100%-25%=75%.

a3OffsetCsBIA.description:
Margin for intra-frequency better cell CSBIA.
Used in CSBIA measurement event type A3 where the event is triggered when the neighbor cell becomes better than the serving cell by the value of the A3 offset. The IE value is multiplied by 2.

a3ReportIntervalCsBIA.description:
Defines the interval with which measurement reports are sent as long as the specific criteria for the CSBIA measurement event A3 are met (Intra-Frequency).
This parameter defines the interval with which measurement reports are repeatedly sent as long as the specific criteria for the CSBIA measurement event A3 are met. Value definitions as stated in 3GPP

a3TimeToTriggerCsBIA.description:
Time for which the specific criteria for the CSBIA measurement event A3 must be met in order to trigger a measurement report (Intra-Frequency).
Value definitions as stated in 3GPP TS36.331: value MS0 corresponds to 0 ms, MS40 to 40 ms and so on.
a3TimeToTriggerCsBIA.fullName: A3 time to trigger for CSBIA

bwRatioCsBIA.description:
Ratio of (PRB number of CSBIA region / all PRBs eligible for PDSCH transmission)
Configuration rules:
All PRBs eligible for PDSCH scheduling will be divided into two parts, one is CSBIA (Coordinate Scheduling for Beamforming Interference Avoidance) region, the other is none-CSBIA region. This parameter represents the ratio of (PRB number of CSBIA region / all PRBs eligible for PDSCH transmission)
- The realistic ratio will not always equal to the O&M parameter for percentage of CSBIA region as this should be rounded up to RBG size.
For example, with 20M bandwidth tatal 100 PRB, if the percentage of CSBIA region is set to be 30%, the CSBIA PRB number is 30. RGB number is not interge 30/4=7.5.  Implementation will choose 7 or 8 in DL-S.

loggedTCEIP.description:
TCE IP address to corresponding TCE ID number {loggedTCEId} for MDT logged.
If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the address 0.0.0.0, the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).

Pv4 address ranges:

(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).

subscriberMDTObtainLocation.description:
This parameter controls whether the eNB requests the UE to attempt to provide detailed location information. It is only used for UEs which are requestred in Subscriber MDT configuration to provide GNSS location information in MDT Subscriber Trace session.
The UE is requested to attempt to have valid detailed location information available whenever sending a measurement report for which it is configured to include available detailed location information. The UE may not succeed e.g. because the user manually disabled the GPS hardware, due to no/poor satellite coverage. Further details, e.g. regarding when to activate GNSS, are up to UE implementation.

False - The eNB does not send the obtainLocationConfig-r11 field in RRC signaling to UE

True - The eNB sends the obtainLocationConfig-r11 field in RRC signaling to UEs which are GNSS capable, are 3GPP Release 11 (or higher) and are requestred in Subscriber MDT configuration to provide GNSS location information in MDT Subscriber Trace session.

dhcpClientIdentifier.description:
This is a unique string used in the DHCPv4 server of the BTS for identifying a DHCPv4 client that is assigned a fixed IP address. 
This may either be one of the predefined names "RET1" (Remote Electrical Tilt), "RET2", "BBU" and "LMU" or a user-defined name consisting of up to 20 digits [0-9] or letters [a-z] and [A-Z].

dhcpFixedIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the fixed IP address that is to be assigned to the DHCPv4 client if it requests a lease with the name specified in parameter dhcpClientIdentifier.
The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.

dhcpHardwareIdentifier.description: This is the unique hardware (MAC) address within the DHCPv4 server of the BTS by which a DHCPv4 client identifies itself at the BTS. The server will then assign the IP address of the parameter "DHCPv4 Fixed IP Address" to the client.

dhcpId.description: This parameter identifies the unique DHCPv4 Server object in the BTS. Its value is always 1.

dhcpRangeEnd.description:
This parameter specifies the final IP address of the DHCPv4 IP address range.
The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. 
However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.

dhcpRangeStart.description:
This parameter specifies the starting IP address of the DHCPv4 IP address range.
The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.

dhcpClientIdentifier.description:
This is a unique string used in the DHCPv6 server of the BTS for identifying a DHCPv6 client that is assigned a fixed IP address. 
This may either be one of the predefined names "RET1" (Remote Electrical Tilt), "RET2", "BBU" and "LMU" or a user-defined name consisting of up to 20 digits [0-9] or letters [a-z] and [A-Z].

dhcpFixedIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the fixed IP address that is to be assigned to the DHCPv6 client if it requests a lease with the name specified in parameter dhcpClientIdentifier.
The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789. The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not allowed.

dhcpHardwareIdentifier.description: This is the unique hardware (MAC) address within the DHCPv6 server of the BTS by which a DHCPv6 client identifies itself at the BTS. The server will then assign the IP address of the parameter "DHCPv6 Fixed IP Address" to the client.

dhcpRangeEnd.description:
This parameter specifies the final IP address of the DHCPv6 IP address range.
The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789. The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not allowed.

dhcpRangeStart.description:
This parameter specifies the starting IP address of the DHCPv6 IP address range.
The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789. The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not allowed.

dhcpv6Id.description: This parameter identifies the unique DHCPv6 Server object in the BTS. Its value is always 1.
