applyOutOfSyncState.description:
Determines which UEs shall no longer receive TA commands and thus shall be actively sent to UL out-of-sync state if taTimer is not set to 'infinity' provided that bearer combination and applied DRX profile allows for this.
extendedDrxOnly: only UEs being configured with extended settings for the long DRX cycle, i.e. long DRX cycle durations larger than 80ms
allDrx: all UEs being configured for DRX provided that applied DRX profile allows
allUEs: all UEs independently of DRX configuration provided that bearer combination allows.

drxApplyDeviceType.description:
This parameter determines whether the device type "noBenFromBatConsumpOpt" of the UE shall be considered for DRX configuration.
Such an UE does not foresee to particularly benefit from NW-based battery consumption optimisation.

If drxApplyDeviceType is set to "APPLY" and the device type is "noBenFromBatConsumpOpt", DRX will not be activated for this UE.

drxId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC DRX.
It uniquely identifies a DRX instance.

drxInactivityT.description:
Configures the Inactivity Timer for DRX.
The Inactivity Timer determines the number of consecutive PDCCH-subframes for which the UE monitors the PDCCH after decoding an UL or DL resource assignment on PDCCH for an initial data transmission.

Note: It is not recommended to set this timer to shorter values than the default value to allow for sufficient scheduling flexibility.

drxLongCycle.description:
Configures the long DRX cycle. 
The long DRX cycle determines the periodic repetition of the DRX On Duration.

drxOnDuratT.description:
Configures the On Duration Timer for DRX.
The On Duration determines the number of consecutive PDCCH-subframes at the beginning of a DRX cycle during which the UE monitors the PDCCH.

Note: It is not recommended to set this timer to shorter values than the default value to allow for sufficient scheduling flexibility.

drxProfileIndex.description:
DRX profile index.
Uniquely identifies a DRX profile.

drxProfilePriority.description:
DRX profile priority.

Applied to identify the DRX profile to be used if a UE has multiple bearers established.
Note: Modification of DRX profile priority is not recommended; preparation for future use.

drxRetransT.description:
Configures the Retransmission Timer for DRX.
The Retransmission Timer determines the maximum number of PDCCH-subframes a UE monitors the PDCCH as soon as a retransmission in DL is expected by the UE.

Note: It is not recommended to set this timer to shorter values than the recommended default value to allow for sufficient scheduling flexibility.

qci1DrxOffThreshold.description:
Threshold for the poor radio condition when DRX will be disabled for UEs using VoLTE (QCI1 bearer configured).
This threshold is defined in terms of CQI. If DRX is enabled for a VoLTE UE, and the VoLTE UE’s corrected CQI value remains below this threshold for a sufficient amount of time, then DRX will be disabled for the UE.

qci1DrxOnThreshold.description:
Threshold for the good radio condition when DRX will be enabled for UEs using VoLTE (QCI1 bearer configured).
This threshold is defined in terms of CQI. If DRX was disabled for a VoLTE UE that is not in TTI bundling due to poor RF conditions, and if the UE’s corrected CQI value remains above this threshold for a sufficient amount of time, then DRX will be re-enabled for the UE.

stInactFactor.description: Factor with which the DRX Inactivity Timer of the DRX profile as applied for a UE is multiplied in order to determine how long to keep a UE UL synchronized following last transmission of new data.

cancelDelay.description: Sets the cancellation delay for the alarm.

eacInId.description: Defines the external alarm input identifier.

inUse.description:
Defines if a particular EAC line is in use or not in use.
For RMODs only: If RMOD-cpriARfSharing is set to SECONDARY, RMOD/EAC_IN-inUse configuration is ignored.

polarity.description: Defines the used polarity of the external alarm line: normally open or normally closed. Normally_open: when the connector is open, there is no alarm. Normally_closed: when the connector is closed, there is no alarm.

portId.description:
Defines the external alarm lines port number. 

System module FSMr3:
There are 14 input signals and with EAC box 26. Lines 13 and 14 are reserved for the Power Module and cannot be assigned to other use. Values 1-26 are allowed. Maximum total number of input signals is 26. In FSM release 3 module, lines 7-12 are reserved for mixed lines (Input or Output). If any line 1-6 in EAC_OUT is configured to output lines then the corresponding line 7-12 in EAC_IN cannot be configured to input lines. E.g. Input line 7 corresponds to Output line 1. If input line 7 is configured, Output line 1 cannot be configured.

AirScale indoor:
There are 12 input signals and with EAC box 24. Values 1-24 are allowed. Maximum total number of input signals is 24. In AirScale module, lines 7-12 are reserved for mixed lines (Input or Output). If any line 1-6 in EAC_OUT is configured to output lines then the corresponding line 7-12 in EAC_IN cannot be configured to input lines. E.g. Input line 7 corresponds to Output line 1. If input line 7 is configured, Output line 1 cannot be configured.
Radio Module:
Varies depending on hardware type. The maximum is 8 input signals.

FHS Module:
There are 12 inputs signals. lines 7-12 are reserved for mixed lines (Input or Output). If any line 1-6 in EAC_OUT is configured to output lines then the corresponding line 7-12 in EAC_IN cannot be configured to input lines. E.g. Input line 7 corresponds to Output line 1. If input line 7 is configured, Output line 1 cannot be configured.

severity.description: Defines the seriousness of the external alarm condition in question. Minor = 1 Major = 2 Critical = 3

startDelay.description: Sets the activation delay for the alarm

eacOutId.description: Defines the external alarm output control identifier.

inUse.description: Defines if a particular EAC line is in use or not in use.

portId.description:
Defines the external alarm line port number.

FSMr3, Airscale System module, FHS:
There are 6 output signals. These output signals are mixed lines which use line numbers 1-6. If any line 1-6 in EAC_OUT is configured to output lines then the corresponding line 7-12 in EAC_IN cannot be configured to input lines.. E.g. Output line 1 corresponds to Input line 7. If Output line 1 is configured, Input line 7 cannot be configured

Radio Module:
Varies depending on hardware type. The maximum is 4 output controls.

state.description: Defines the state of the external control line. The options are "On" and "Off". If state is "On", voltage is applied.

direction.description: States the direction of the channel of the related antenna line.

eacRId.description: This parameter identifies an instance of an EAC.

lineState.description: This parameter indicates the line state ON/OFF of the EAC line when in used.

operationalState.description: Operational state of the eNB, the value is set by system.

productCode.description: Defines the product code of the unit.

Parameter to define the distribution mode of RRC PAGING with systemInfoModification_eDRX in case of essential SIB parameter modification. 

noPagStorm means that systemInfoModification_eDRX flag will be carried only in Paging Occasions within the next BCCH modification period, together with normal systemInfoModification flag.

partialPagStorm means that  systemInfoModification_eDRX flag will be carried in Paging Occasions within the next 2621.44 seconds  where there are RRC  PAGING messages for other purpose  to be sent. 

fullPagStorm means that  systemInfoModification_eDRX flag will be carried in every Paging Occasion within the next 2621.44 seconds no matter there are RRC PAGING messages for other purpose to be sent or not.

sibParameterSet.description:

MTService&CellCamp means that both SIB parameters related with mobile terminated service and  SIB parameters related with serving cell camp will be taken as essential SIB parameter set for eDRX.

actExtPIMCancellation.description:
This parameter activates the PIM Cancellation feature on External PIM Cancellation HW unit that resides between the Airscale System Module and Radio Units.
The PIM Cancellation feature is for the passive inter-modulation (PIM) interference cancellation in uplink signals.
The PIM Cancellation feature can be activated on the External PIM Cancellation HW unit if all of Radio Units connected to it, do not have another connection to an SMOD_EXT.
PIM performance counters and PIM performance threshold alarms remain active as long as this parameter is 'true'.

epimcId.description:
Defines the External Passive Inter-Modulation Cancellation object identifier.
EPMIC object can be created only if the hardware unit supports the EPIMC function.

extPIMCancellingEnabled.description:
This parameter enables or disables the cancelling of the passive inter-modulation (PIM) interference on External PIM Cancellation HW unit that has the PIM Cancellation feature activated.
The External PIM Cancellation algorithm removes the passive inter-modulation interference in uplink signal.
PIM performance counters and PIM performance threshold alarms remain active as long as the actExtPIMCancellation parameter is 'true'.
This parameter is ignored if actExtPIMCancellation parameter is 'false'.

extPIMPerformanceMajorThreshold.description: The parameter is used to determine when to trigger the ‘External PIM Performance Measurement Major Threshold Exceeded’ fault. The fault is issued if the level of  PIM performance measurement in the antenna line of RX path exceeds the level of external PIM performance major threshold value for a fixed raise fault delay. The fault is cancelled if the level of measured PIM performance in the antenna line is below the external PIM performance major threshold for a fixed clear fault delay.

extPIMPerformanceMinorThreshold.description: The parameter is used to determine when to trigger the ‘External PIM Performance Measurement Minor Threshold Exceeded’ fault. The fault is issued if the level of PIM performance measurement in the antenna line of RX path exceeds the level of  external PIM performance minor threshold value for a fixed raise fault delay. The fault is cancelled if the level of measured PIM performance in the antenna line is below the level of external PIM performance minor threshold for a fixed clear fault delay.

contributedTXEarfcn.description: This parameter contains E-UTRA absolute radio frequency channel number of downlink signal which contributes to unwanted products of passive intermodulation interference occurring on uplink signals.
contributedTXEarfcn.fullName: Contributed TX EUTRA absolute radio frequency channel number

epimcRId.description: Defines the External Passive Inter-Modulation Cancellation runtime object identifier

extPIMCOperationStatus.description:
This parameter describes the status of operation of External PIM Cancellation unit.
The 'inactive' status means the External PIM Cancellation feature activation flag is set to false. The feature is deactivated on the External PIM Cancellation HW unit. 
The 'active_disabled' status means the External PIM Cancellation feature activation flag is set to true (feature activated) and the PIM Cancellation enabling flag is set to false (function disabled) and there is no fault  on the External PIM Cancellation HW unit. The External PIM Cancellation feature is up and running with PIM Cancellation function disabled.
The 'active_enabled' status means the External PIM Cancellation feature activation flag is set to true (feature activated) and the PIM Cancellation enabling flag  is set to true (function enabled) and there is no fault on the PIM Cancellation HW unit. The External PIM Cancellation feature is up and running with PIM Cancellation function enabled.
The 'active_failure' status means the External PIM Cancellation feature activation flag is set to true and there is an active or internal fault that prevents the PIM Cancellation feature from functioning on the External PIM Cancellation HW unit.

supportForRadioModel.description: This parameter indicates if a model of targeted radio module is supported by External PIM Cancellation function.

targetedCellDN.description: This parameter contains DN of E-UTRA cell where its uplink signal is targeted for External PIM Cancellation or/and its downlink signal contributes to unwanted products of passive intermodulation interference occurring on uplink signals.

targetedRXEarfcn.description: This parameter contains E-UTRA absolute radio frequency channel number of uplink signal targeted for External PIM Cancellation.
targetedRXEarfcn.fullName: Targeted  RX EUTRA absolute radio frequency channel number

targetedRadioDN.description: This parameter contains DN of a radio module targeted for External PIM Cancellation.

detectedClock.description:
This parameter indicates the detected clock mode with an electrical Ethernet interface operating at 1000Base-T technology. The displayed value enables to determine whether the negotiated clock mode of a 1000Base-T interface, fits to the expected clock mode, when using Synchronous Ethernet.
NOT_APPLICABLE is the value with all Ethernet technologies different than 1000Base-T 
CONFIGURATION FAULT signifies that both peers at the Ethernet link could not succesfully negotiate the clock mode.
MASTER means that the Ethernet interface is operating at master clock mode, driving the Ethernet signal with the clock of the BTS.
SLAVE means that the Ethernet interface is operating at slave clock mode, allowing to use the recovered clock from the Ethernet signal as potential sync source for BTS synchronization.
detectedClock.fullName: Detected Clock mode with an electrical interface

detectedSpeedAndDuplex.description: This parameter indicates the actual link characteristics for bitrate and full/half duplex mode.
detectedSpeedAndDuplex.fullName: Detected interface bitrate and duplex mode

esideConnRId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the Ethernet sidehaul connection object (ESIDECONN_R). It uniquely identifies the object.

linkId.description: This parameter indicates Id of Ethernet sidehaul connection.

operationalState.description:
This parameter indicates whether the Ethernet link is currently able to transmit Ethernet frames (enabled) or not (disabled).

'enabled' is equivalent to 'up' or 'active'
'disabled' is equivalent to 'down ' or 'inactive'
operationalState.fullName: Operational state of the Ethernet sidehaul connection

ethAppId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the ethernet application object. It uniquely identifies the object.

optionalTlvReplyEnabled.description:
If this parameter is set to "true",  the optional TLV received in a Link Trace or Loopback message (LTM or LBM message) is sent back unchanged in the corresponding reply message (LTR, or LBR).
If this parameter is set to "false", the received optional TLV is ignored and not being sent back in the reply-message.

remoteMepMacAutoLearningEnabled.description: Likely a true/false switch that enables or disables a behavior related to "remote Mep Mac Auto Learning Enabled" on the ETHAPP object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

serviceOamEnabled.description: This parameter defines whether service OAM shall be enabled. When enabled the service OAM functionality is started and reacts on incoming OAM PDUs.

ethIfId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the Ethernet interface object. It uniquely identifies the object.

linkSelectorDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the internal (IBRGPRT), external bridgeport (BRGPRT) or an ethernet link (ETHLK) by giving the distinguished name.
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/ETHSVC-1/L2SWI-1/BRGPRT-1
linkSelectorDN.fullName: Reference to an external or internal bridgeport

sbsTotal.description: This parameter defines the burst size in bytes of the token bucket shaper at the output of the second-level scheduler (i.e. aggregating the traffic of the plain Ethernet interface and all related VLAN interfaces).

shapingOverhead.description:
This parameter defines whether the shaper accounts for the Ethernet frame or IP packet data for scheduling and shaping calculations, and ignores the corresponding overhead.

Ethernet frame:
Considers Ethernet protocol fields from destination MAC address to the frame check sequence (FCS) (including possible Ethernet padding), thus ignoring the overhead of Ethernet IPG, Preamble and SFD field.

IP packet:
Considers all IP protocol fields, thus ignoring the overhead of Ethernet encapsulation.

sirTotal.description:
This parameter defines the shaper rate in kbps at the output of the second-level scheduler (i.e. aggregating the traffic of the plain Ethernet interface and all related VLAN interfaces).
If the defined rate is exceeding the detected Ethernet link speed (ETHLK_R-detectedSpeedAndDuplex) , the value of the detected Ethernetlink speed will be used. This is applicable only in cases where the scheduler is directly associated with a physical interface.

txPriorityTagging.description:
This parameter defines whether the non-VLAN interface transmits all Ethernet frames untagged or priority-tagged.

Value "true" means transmitted frames are priority tagged.
Value "false" means transmitted frames are untagged.

userLabel.description: This parameter denotes the label that may be used, for example, for a usage description of this Ethernet interface.

ethIfRId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only Ethernet interface object. It uniquely identifies the object.
ethIfRId.fullName: Read only Ethernet interface object identifier

macAddr.description: This parameter indicates the MAC address of the Ethernet interface.

acceptableFrameTypes.description:
If the value of this parameter is "AdmitTagged", the device will discard untagged and Priority-tagged frames received on this interface. If the value is “AdmitAll”, tagged, untagged, and Priority-tagged frames received on this interface will be accepted. Untagged and Priority-tagged frames are assigned to the VLAN defined by the portDefaultVlanId parameter for this interface.
Notes:
1) Priority tagged" frames (IEEE 802.1Q tagged frames with VLAN ID=0) can be configured via the VLAN filter list of parameter l2VlanIdList.
2) Ethernet management frames (i.e. Synchronous Ethernet and Ethernet OAM frames) are always allowed to ingress and egress the Ethernet interface of the layer 2 switch independent of the status of the value of the discardUntagged parameter.

administrativeState.description:
Administrative state of the cell, the value is set by the operator.
Note: This parameter used for NB-IoT standalone cell.
administrativeState.fullName: Administrative state of the Ethernet link

clockMode.description:
This parameter defines whether the clock mode to be advertised during autonegotiation is automatically determined (autodetect) by the system or the value defined by the user. 
The parameter is only valid for interfaces of type 1000Base-T.
The values are:
AUTODETECT: If the Ethernet interface is part of the synchronization priority list (syncInputType==SYNCE-x), then "single port device" is advertised with auto-neg, else "multi port device".
MANUAL MASTER: The Ethernet interface advertises during auto-neg "manual master", forcing its own clock mode to the master and link partner to slave. The link is kept down if the link partner advertises "manual master" as well.
MANUAL SLAVE: The Ethernet interface advertises during auto-neg "manual slave", forcing its own clock mode to the slave and link partner to master. The link is kept down if the link partner advertises "manual slave" as well.

Hardware variants and supported ports:
FSMF: EIF1
FTIF: EIF3, EIF4
ASIA: EIF3, EIF4, EIF5
FTIH: EIF3, EIF4

Note: In case the parameter is defined for a port which actually is not supported, the parameter will be ignored by the BTS

connectorLabel.description:
This parameter defines which connector of the HW shall be used.
The supported connectors depend on the hardware.
FSMF:
1.) If the modDN is referencing to a SMOD of type FSMF or FSMFA:
- A maximum of two Ethernet interfaces can be taken into use
- The usage depends on the configuration of the parameter portMode, which defines whether the port EIF2 / RF/6 shall be used as a transport interface.
    I.) If the portMode is set to "Ethernet", the following connectors can be selected.
        a.) EIF1 (RJ45)
        b.) EIF2 (SFP)
    II.) If the portMode is set to "RF", the following connector can be selected.
        a.) EIF1 (RJ45)
2.) If the modDN is referencing to a TRMOD  of type FTIF:
- A maximum of two Ethernet interfaces can be taken into use
- The usage depends on the configuration of the parameter portMode, which defines whether the port EIF1/EIF3 on the FTIF can be used.
    I.) If the portMode is set to "Ethernet", the following connectors can be selected.
        a.) EIF2 (SFP) or EIF4 (RJ45). The usage is mutually exclusive
    II.) If the portMode is set to "RF", the following connectors can be selected.
        a.) EIF1 (SFP) or EIF3 (RJ45). The usage is mutually exclusive 
        b.) EIF2 (SFP) or EIF4 (RJ45). The usage is mutually exclusive

ASIA or ASIAA (AirScale system module - Indoor):
A maximum of five Ethernet interfaces can be taken into use.
The supported values are:
EIF1 (SFP+), EIF2 (SFP+), EIF3 (RJ45), EIF4 (RJ45), EIF5 (RJ45)

FSIH:
1.) If the modDN is referencing to a SMOD of type FSIH:
- A maximum of three Ethernet interfaces can be taken into use.
- The usage depends on the configuration of the parameter portMode, which defines whether the port EIF5 / RF/6 shall be used as a transport interface.
    I.) If the portMode is set to "Ethernet", the following connectors can be selected.
        a.) EIF5
        b.) EIF1 (SFP) or EIF3 (RJ45). The usage is mutually exclusive  
        c.) EIF2 (SFP) or EIF4 (RJ45). The usage is mutually exclusive 
    II.) If the portMode is set to "RF", the following connectors can be selected.
        a.) EIF1 (SFP) or EIF3 (RJ45). The usage is mutually exclusive  
        b.) EIF2 (SFP) or EIF4 (RJ45). The usage is mutually exclusive 

In addition to the above exactly one instance of ETHLK can be created with the connectorLabel set to LMP1.

EIFx refers to the connector number as used on the label on the front plate.
SFP/RJ45 refers to the type of the connector.
SFP  refers to a "Small Form-factor Pluggable".
RJ45 Registerd Jack which is commonly used in telecommunications.
connectorLabel.fullName: Label of the connector by the Ethernet link
connectorLabel.officialRange:
0: LMP1 
1: EIF1 
2: EIF2 
3: EIF3 
4: EIF4 
5: EIF5 
6: EIF6 
7: EIF7 
8: EIF8 
9: EIF9 
10: EIF10

ethBhType.description:
This parameter specifies the type of back haul in use.     

        Supported types are Copper, 1000BaseSX, 1000BaseLX,  1000BasePX, G984,  1000BaseBx, 10GbaseSR and 10GbaseLR.

ethLinkId.description:
For FSMF/FSMG (Flexi BTS Release 3 Outdoor System Module),
          slot#: 0 : This is always 0, since Transport is integrated into common system module.
          if#: 1..2 : Value range is 1..2 for EIF1..EIF2 on this unit
          Additionally, EIF2 can be configured as an RP3-01 port.

For FSIF/FSIG (Flexi BTS Release 3 Indoor System Module),
         slot#: 0 : This is always 0, since Transport is integrated into common system module.
         if#: 1..5 : Value range is 1..5 for EIF1..EIF5.
         Usage of EIF1 and EIF3 is mutually exclusive. Similarly for EIF2 and EIF4. Additionally, EIF5 can be configured as an RP3-01 port.

For FTIF (optional outdoor external Transport module),
          slot#: 1 : The slot number is '1', since this is an additional unit
          if#: 1..4 : Value range is 1..4 for EIF1..EIF4 on this unit
          Usage of EIF1 and EIF3 is mutually exclusive. Similarly for EIF2 and EIF4. Usage of EIF1/EIF3 on this unit and EIF2 on FSM is mutually exclusive.

For FIIF (optional indoor external Transport module),
          slot#: 1 : The slot number is '1', since this is an additional unit
          if#: 1..2 : Value range is 1..2 for EIF1..EIF2 on this unit
          Usage of EIF1 and EIF2 is mutually exclusive on this unit. Usage of EIF1/EIF2 on this unit and EIF5 on FSI unit is mutually exclusive.

For FSIH,
          slot#: 0 : This is always 0, since Transport is integrated into common system module. 
          if#: 1..5 : Value range is 1..5 for EIF1..EIF5.
          Usage of EIF1 and EIF3 is mutually exclusive. Also EIF2 and EIF4 is mutually exclusive. Additionally, EIF5 can be configured as an RP3-01 port.

          Examples:
          FSMF/FSMG/FSIF/FSIG:
          0-1: refers to the physical Ethernet interface 1 in slot 0. (EIF1)

FTIF/FIIF:
            1-1: refers to the physical Ethernet interface 1 in slot 1. (EIF1)

For Flexi zone micro, it is standalone device, box only has 1 slot.
           1-1: refers to the physical Ethernet interface EIF1 (port A);
           1-2: refers to the physical Ethernet interface EIF2 (port B);
           1-3: refers to the physical Ethernet interface EIF3 (port C) [Applicable only for FZMs which support at least 3 ports (e.g. FWHC, FWHE, FWHF, FW2EHB, FW2QC, etc.)]
           1-4: refers to the physical Ethernet interface EIF4 (port D) [Applicable only for FZMs which support 4 ports (e.g. FW2EHB, FW2QC, etc.)

For ASIA (AirScale System Module Indoor),
           slot#: 0 : This is always 0, since Transport is integrated into common system module.
           if#: 1..5 : Value range is 1..5 for EIF1..EIF5 on this unit.
           EIF1, EIF2 –> SFP+ 1G/10G
           EIF3, EIF4, EIF5 –> 1000Base-T

ethLkId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the Ethernet link object. It uniquely identifies the object.

flushFdbOnLos.description: If this parameter is set to "true", the dynamic MAC address entries in the Forwarding Database (FDB) will be purged when an Ethernet Layer Loss of Signal (LOS) is detected on one of its physical switch-ports.

highValue.description:
This parameter specifies the upper value of a range of VLAN identifiers.

VLAN id ‘1’ is reserved for un-tagged frames handling and should not be configured.
highValue.fullName: Upper value of VLAN identifier range

l2BurstSize.description:
This parameter defines the maximum burst size in byte(s) that can be transmitted in a single burst of the duration of 1s, in egress direction, for this Ethernet interface on the layer 2 switch.
The supported value range depends on the hardware.
For Flexi BTS applies: 
  - Range and Step: from 0 to 7500000 step 125
  - recommended value: 0
  - the maximum supported value is 6% of the actually configured l2ShaperRate * 1s
  - Value 0 means no bursts are allowed.
For AirScale BTS applies: 
  - only the values listed below must be defined
    32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16 384, 32 768, 65 536, 131 072, 262 144, 524 288, 1 048 576
  - recommended value: 1 048 576

l2IngressRate.description: This parameter defines the ingress rate limit, in kbps, for this Ethernet link.

l2ShaperBurstSize.description:
This parameter defines the maximum burst size in octets that can be transmitted in a single burst in egress direction on this Ethernet interface of layer 2 switch. 
The parameter is only valid for AirScale hardware unit type.
The default value is 15 (1M).

l2ShaperRate.description:
This parameter defines the configurable egress shaper rate, in Kbit/s, for this switch-port.
Note: When the configured shaper rate exceeds the actual available bandwidth of the physical Ethernet interface, then this physical limitation will be applied at the rate shaper so that packet discard happens in a controlled way at scheduler queues only.
Note for FlexiBTS variants: If the configured value is below 1600 Kbit/s, the actually applied shaper rate will be 1560 Kbit/s. If the configured value is above 1500 Kbit/s, the configured value will be applied for the shaper rate.
l2ShaperRate.fullName: Layer 2 switch member egress shaping rate

linkOAMDyingGaspEnabled.description:
This parameter enables the Link OAM Dying Gasp functionality for Link OAM.
The flag is disabled by default.
linkOAMDyingGaspEnabled.fullName: Link OAM Dying Gasp enabling flag

linkOAMEnabled.description:
Enables the Link OAM functionality for this ethernet link. In consequence:
- the values of all statistics counters of the Link OAM feature for this interface are set to 0
- the Link OAM alarms for this interface are cleared
- the Link OAM discovery process is started, either in active or in passive mode.
For FlexiZone Micro:
This parameter shall  be set to FALSE for ETHLK-1-3 in case of FWHC.

linkOAMProfile.description:
A reference to a Link OAM profile. This is a distinguished name referencing an instance of class OAMPRF.
Format: "FTM-1/OAMPRF-*"

where
FTM-1: = a parent instance of object class ETHLK, This is always 1 (static MO)
OAMPRF-#, # = an instance of object class OAMPRF

Example: FTM-1/OAMPRF-1

lowValue.description:
This parameter specifies either a single VLAN identifier or the lower value of a range of VLAN identifiers.

VLAN id ‘1’ is reserved for un-tagged frames handling and should not be configured.
lowValue.fullName: Low value of VLAN identifier range

macAddr.description: This parameter shows the MAC address of the Ethernet link.

modDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the HW module to which the Ethernet Link shall be assiged to.
The module can be either a System Module (SMOD) or a Transport Module (TRMOD).
In addition the port on the module has to be selected in the parameter connectorLabel.
Examples: 
MRBTS-1/EQM-1/APEQM-1/CABINET-1/SMOD-1
MRBTS-1/EQM-1/APEQM-1/CABINET-1/TRMOD-1

portDefaultPriority.description:
Default VLAN priority for untagged frames.

Every untagged ingress Ethernet frame at this interface gets assigned this Port Default Priority. If QoS classification mode is configured to VLAN-PCP, this priority is used for enqueing decision of the frame. If the frame egresses the switch tagged, this priority shall be used in the VLAN tag header.

portDefaultVlanId.description:
This parameter defines the VLAN identifier that is associated to untagged and priority-tagged frames received at this Ethernet interface (internal switch-port).

Furthermore this parameter determines, that frames associated to this VLAN identifier which are switched and transmitted at this switch-port will be transmitted untagged.

In order to achieve that a received untagged or priority-tagged frame is switched and transmitted via another (external) switch-port, the same VLAN identifier must be configured at the transmission port:
a) for VLAN-tagged transmission: in the VLAN identifier list of that transmit switch-port (see parameter l2VlanIdList) or
b) for untagged transmission: in the portDefaultVlanID of that transmit switch-port.
Else the frame will be discarded.
portDefaultVlanId.fullName: Default VLAN identifier for layer 2 switching

speedAndDuplex.description:
This parameter defines if auto-negotiation is enabled or disabled for an Ethernet Interface, and if auto-negotiation is enabled whether to restrict the speeds to be advertised.
AUTODETECT: Auto-negotiation is enabled and 100Base-Tx, 1000Base-T, full duplex are advertised. With 1000Base-X: Auto-negotiation is enabled and full duplex is advertised.
1000MBIT_FULL: Auto-negotiation is enabled and only 1000Base-T, full duplex is advertised. With 1000Base-X: Auto-negotiation is disabled and Ethernet interface is forced to 1000Base-X, full duplex.
100MBIT_FULL: Auto-negotiation is disabled and Ethernet interface is forced to 100Base-Tx, full duplex. Not applicable with 1000Base-X
For ASIA (AirScale system module - Indoor)
The optical 10 GE interface supports only 10GBIT_FULL.
The optical 1GE interface supports only AUTODETECT, 1000MBIT_FULL.
Note: 'AUTODETECT' setting for ASIA initiate the interface probe for 10G and if found, the speed and duplex is forced to 10GBIT_FULL since auto negotiation is not supported on 10 Gigabit Ethernet interface.
If the SFP type is 10GbaseSR or 10GbaseLR, then speedAndDuplex must be set to 10GBIT_FULL.

syncEAutoNegMode.description:
This parameter defines the Synchronous Ethernet autonegotiation mode for the electrical 1GE port to either automatic or forced.

Note: The decision whether the electrical 1GE port is SyncE master or slave depends only on the synchronization reference source selection.

This parameter is relevant only for electrical 1GE interfaces.
The default value is 0 (automatic)

userLabel.description: The label that can be used for a usage description of the BFD session.

detectedClock.description:
This parameter indicates the detected clock mode with an electrical Ethernet interface operating at 1000Base-T technology. The displayed value enables to determine whether the negotiated clock mode of a 1000Base-T interface, fits to the expected clock mode, when using Synchronous Ethernet.
NOT_APPLICABLE is the value with all Ethernet technologies different than 1000Base-T 
CONFIGURATION FAULT signifies that both peers at the Ethernet link could not succesfully negotiate the clock mode.
MASTER means that the Ethernet interface is operating at master clock mode, driving the Ethernet signal with the clock of the BTS.
SLAVE means that the Ethernet interface is operating at slave clock mode, allowing to use the recovered clock from the Ethernet signal as potential sync source for BTS synchronization.
detectedClock.fullName: Detected Clock mode with an electrical interface

detectedSpeedAndDuplex.description: This parameter indicates the actual link characteristics for bitrate and full/half duplex mode.
detectedSpeedAndDuplex.fullName: Detected interface bitrate and duplex mode

vmPortTypeAllocated.description: This parameter indicates the port type of the allocated port on the virtual machine.

portMirroringEnabled.description:
This parameter allows to enable/disable the port mirroring in the NE
When enabled all traffic will be mirrored according to the configurations in the mirror sets.

destinationDN.description:
This parameter defines to which port the traffic defined in source shall be mirrored.
The destination  is defined by giving the distinguished name (DN) to the ETHLK.
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/ETHSVC-1/ETHLK-1

ethMirrorSetId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the Ethernet mirror set object. It uniquely identifies the object.

sourceDN.description:
This parameter defines the traffic source which shall be mirrored.
The source can be either the internal bridge port (IBRGPRT) or an Ethernet link (ETHLK):

The source is defined by giving the distinguished name (DN).
Examples: 
 - Ethernet: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/ETHSVC-1/ETHLK-1
 - Internal bridge port: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/ETHSVC-1/L2SWI-1/IBRGPRT-1

Up to 4 sources can be defined.

sourceDirection.description: This parameter defines the direction of the traffic which shall be mirrored to the destination.

act1PpsFrequencyValidation.description: Activates validation of the 1PPS timing pulse's frequency accuracy, as an integrity check on the synchronization source.

actAldSharing.description: Activates sharing of the Antenna Line Device (RET/TMA) control bus between multiple basebands or operators.

actAldSwUpdate.description: This is a feature flag to enable or disable monitoring for ALD software management.

actAntennaPathDelayMeasurement.description: This parameter enables automatic measurement of antenna path roundtrip delay on the RF modules which support that functionality.

actAntiTheftProtectionSystem.description: Activates an anti-theft protection mechanism for the equipment (e.g. location-based lock or tamper response).

actApts.description: Activates Assisted Partial Timing Support (APTS), a synchronization mode combining a packet-based timing protocol (e.g. PTP) with a local reference (e.g. GNSS) for improved holdover accuracy.

actAsi.description:
This parameter allows the support of the ASi. With the feature enabled, the ASIRMODs are allowed to be created and operator is able to use ASiManager to manage the ASi. 

When the feature is disabled, operator is not able to use ASiManager to manage the ASi and all the cells using the ASIRMOD will be disabled.

actAutAntRecPwrAntBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on per-antenna received-power statistics.

actAutAntRecPwrBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on antenna received-power statistics: if received power patterns indicate a cell has silently failed, the system attempts automated recovery.

actAutAntRecPwrDiff2AntBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on the received-power difference between two antennas, catching faults that manifest as an imbalance rather than an absolute drop.

actAutAntTxPwrBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on abnormal antenna transmit-power readings.

actAutBBModParamUpdate.description: Activates automatic update/propagation of baseband module parameters, e.g. after a hardware replacement, to keep configuration consistent.

actAutNrRrcConStAtSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on RRC connection statistics.

actAutPrachBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on anomalies in PRACH (random access) activity.

actAutRachBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on RACH (random access) attempt statistics - an abnormal drop in RACH attempts can indicate a 'sleeping cell' that the system then tries to auto-recover.

actAutRrcAtmpBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on RRC connection attempt statistics.

actAutRrcBasedSlCellDetRec.description: This is a feature flag to enable or disable automatic sleeping cell detection and recovery based on RRC check. The cell will considered as sleeping when RRC successful rate calculated within  autRrcBasedSlCellDetHCheckFreq  is above threshold defined in autRrcBasedSlCellDetRrcSuccRateThr and RRC volume in  autRrcBasedSlCellDetHCheckFreq is bigger than defined in autRrcBasedSlCellDetRrcVolThr.
actAutRrcBasedSlCellDetRec.fullName: Activate automatic RRC based sleeping cell detection and recovery

actAutS1CommBasedSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery based on anomalies in S1 interface communication.

actAutoPwrOffDCPort.description: Activates automatic power-off of an unused or faulted DC output port to save energy or isolate a fault.

actBbReconfigImprovement.description: Activates an improved (faster, less service-impacting) baseband reconfiguration procedure.

actCellTimingOffset.description: Activates the ability to configure a deliberate frame-timing offset for a cell, used e.g. for interference coordination or staggered scheduling between cells.

actCellTimingOffsetCpriN.description: Activates the cell-timing-offset feature specifically for CPRI-based fronthaul links of a certain generation/variant ('CPRI-N').

actCertPartitionSynch.description: Activates synchronization of the certificate store partition between redundant/paired controller units, keeping trusted certificates consistent.

actCli.description: This is a feature flag to enable or disable usage of BTS CLI.

actCpriLinkRecovery.description: Activates automatic recovery procedures for a failed CPRI fronthaul link.

actCpriOTNRecovery.description: Likely a true/false switch that enables or disables a behavior related to "activate/enable Cpri OTN Recovery" on the FEATCADM object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

actDeploymentIdCalcEnhancement.description: Activates an enhanced calculation method for the deployment/site identifier used internally by planning-related algorithms (e.g. PCI or ANR).

actDetectionUnstableEcpriLinks.description: Activates detection of unstable eCPRI fronthaul links (e.g. intermittent errors/flapping) to flag them for attention.

actDhcp.description: This parameter enables or disables DHCP service

actDhcpIpContinuation.description: Activates retention of a previously-assigned DHCP IP address across a reboot, avoiding renegotiation of a new address.

actDiagnosticCheck.description: Activates general automated diagnostic self-check routines on the equipment.

actDisableEcpriUlScalingEnh.description: Controls (enables/disables) an uplink data-scaling enhancement used over eCPRI fronthaul, likely related to fronthaul bandwidth/compression efficiency.

actDistributedSite.description:
The parameter actDistributedSite allows usage of Distributed Site.
That is a site where there is a long distance (high latency) between the FSM and the antenna (i.e. a RF unit may lie up to 23 km distance from the system module).

actDtPim.description: This parameter enables the RF Interference Distance to PIM testing function in the BTS.

actDualCoreParallelReset.description: Activates resetting dual processor cores in parallel rather than sequentially, shortening reboot time.

actDualStackIpV4V6ForMplane.description:
This parameter defines the use of the feature "Dual Stack IPv4/IPv6 for M-plane".
If IPv6 addresses shall be used the feature must be enabled.

If dual stack  is disabled (FALSE): 

Only IPv4 addresses shall be configured.

If Dual Stack is enabled (TRUE):
All configured IP versions/addresses are operational.
actDualStackIpV4V6ForMplane.fullName: Feature activation flag for Dual Stack IPv4/IPv6 for M-plane

actEAPMode.description: Selects the EAP (Extensible Authentication Protocol) operating mode used for authentication (e.g. 802.1X/IPsec), such as whether the BTS acts as the authenticator that initiates the exchange.

actECPRITransportForORANAndTSN.description: Activates eCPRI transport support tailored for O-RAN fronthaul interoperability and Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) Ethernet features.

actEccMemoryErrorAlarm.description: Activates alarm generation when ECC (error-correcting-code) memory reports correctable/uncorrectable errors.

actEcpriDelayMeasurement.description: Activates the eCPRI delay-measurement procedure used to calibrate one-way/round-trip fronthaul latency.

actEcpriMPlaneResilience.description: Activates resilience mechanisms (e.g. redundant paths/failover) for the eCPRI Management-Plane connection to the Radio Unit.

actEcpriMacSecTraffic.description: Activates MACsec (Layer-2 encryption) protection for eCPRI fronthaul traffic.

actEcpriMplaneIPV6.description: Activates IPv6 addressing for eCPRI Management-Plane connectivity.

actEcpriRuMPlaneSecurity.description: Configures the security protection level applied to the Radio Unit's Management-Plane traffic carried over eCPRI.

actEcpriSyncMismatchAdjustment.description: Activates automatic adjustment when a timing/synchronization mismatch is detected over an eCPRI fronthaul link.

actFaultSignature.description: Activates the fault-signature analysis feature, which correlates recurring alarm/fault patterns to help automatically identify known hardware or software issues.

actFhNcOverTls.description: Activates carrying the fronthaul NETCONF (management) session over a TLS-secured transport.

actFhsDelayComp.description:
This parameter enables delay compensation realized by Fronthaul Switch (FHS) with or without an External PIM Cancellation (EPIMC) module to support compensation of fiber length differences (up to 23km) in case CPRI-A radios.
Notes:
- The parameter can be enabled only when all CPRI-A radio are connected to a FHS.

actFiberLinkLengthExt1.description:
The parameter enables support for up to 30km fiber length between AirScale System Module and CPRI-N or CPRI-A radio.

Notes: 
- if the parameter is enabled, radios other than CPRI-N or CPRI-A cannot be used
- if CPRI-A radio is used, actFhsDelayComp parameter has to be set to true and all CPRI-A radios have to be connected to AirScale SM via FHS
actFiberLinkLengthExt1.fullName: Activate support for fiber link length extension (phase 1)

actFipsMode.description: Activates FIPS 140-2/3 compliant cryptographic operation mode for regulated/government deployments.

actGnssJammingSpoofing.description: Activates detection of GNSS jamming or spoofing attacks against the timing receiver, raising an alarm/response if suspicious signal conditions are seen.

actHierarchyAutoFix.description: Activates automatic correction of managed-object hierarchy inconsistencies detected in the configuration.

actHybridSynch.description:
This parameter activates/deactivates the optional feature "Hybrid Synchronization". 
This feature is disabled by default.

actIntelligentSynceAssHoTime.description: Activates an intelligent SyncE-assisted holdover mode that uses SyncE frequency information to improve timing accuracy while a node is in holdover (without a live traceable reference).

actKpiAlarms.description: Activates alarms that are raised automatically when configured KPI thresholds are breached.

actL1FastAutoHealing.description: Activates fast automatic healing/recovery of Layer-1 (baseband/radio physical layer) faults, minimizing outage duration.

actL1ReconfigImprovement.description: Activates an improved Layer-1 (physical layer) reconfiguration procedure with reduced service impact.

actL2L3ReconfigImprovement.description: Activates an improved Layer-2/Layer-3 reconfiguration procedure with reduced service impact.

actLbmOnFronthaul.description: Activates Ethernet CFM Loopback Message (LBM) connectivity checking on the fronthaul link, used to verify link health.

actLocationLock.description: Activates a location-lock (anti-theft/anti-relocation) feature that uses GNSS position to detect if the equipment has been moved from its commissioned site and can trigger an alarm or restrict operation.

actLoginCredPartitionSync.description: Activates synchronization of login credentials between redundant controller partitions, keeping user accounts consistent across them.

actMhaAutoConfig.description:
This flag activates the MHA auto-configuration function when it's set to true.
When MHA auto-configuration is activated, there is no need to include manually MHAs to plan file. The BTS shall support auto-configurations of the MHAs with the following conditions:
- MHA supports AISG 2.0
- MHA does not have any LNA marked as external 
- MHA is single band
- MHA with 2 LNAs
- MHA connected to a shared radio and BTS is the master
- MHA is not a Nokia harmonized MHAs introduced in LTE2099

actMhaEnhancement.description: Activates an enhancement to Mast Head Amplifier (tower-mounted amplifier) control/monitoring.

actMplaneFronthaulFirewall.description: Activates a firewall protecting Management-Plane traffic on the fronthaul interface.

actMultiCablesForOTN.description: This parameter enables multi cables configuration in Optical Transport Network (OTN). This parameter is used to compensate length difference of optical links.

actMultipleDynamicIP.description:
This parameter  activates the support for dynamic assignment of IP addresses for multiple tunnels in case of public backhaul scenario. Both IPv6 or IPv4 inner IP addresses obtained for LTE M/C/U/S-planes through IPv4 IPSec tunnels are supported.
The default value is "false".
When this feature is activated the following IP addresses should be set to 0.0.0.0: IPNO-cPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-mPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-sPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-uPlaneIpAddress, IEIF-localIpAddr, IEIF-NetMask, IPRT-staticRoutes::gateway, IPSECC-securityPolicies::localTunnelEndpoint. Moreover, if operator creates VLAN (IVIF) object, then the operator should set the vlanId to 0 and the following IP addresses to 0.0.0.0: IEIF/IVIF-localIpAddr, IEIF/IVIF-netmask (the eNB shall send CCN to iOMS/NetAct to update the values for the above attributes).
actMultipleDynamicIP.fullName: Feature Activation Flag for multiple IPsec tunnels with dynamic IP assignment

actNonOperOwnedBhMode.description: Activates a mode tailored for backhaul connectivity that is not owned by the mobile operator (e.g. leased/wholesale backhaul), adjusting relevant handling.

actNonStationaryBts.description: Activates support for a non-stationary (mobile/vehicle-mounted) base station deployment.

actNrAutCntRachStpSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on RACH-attempt-count/step statistics.

actNrAutDegAdmCtrlSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on degraded admission-control statistics.

actNrAutNgCommSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on NG (core network) interface communication-failure statistics.

actNrAutPrachAccSltSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on PRACH access-slot statistics.

actNrAutRxPwrAntSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on per-antenna received-power statistics.

actNrAutRxPwrDiff2AntSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on the received-power difference between two antennas.

actNrAutRxPwrSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on received-power statistics.

actNrAutSgnbAddCplSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on secondary-gNB-addition (EN-DC) completion statistics.

actNrAutTxPwrSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on transmit-power statistics.

actNrAutUeCtxStpRtSlCellDetRec.description: Activates automatic sleeping-cell detection and recovery for NR cells based on UE-context-setup success-rate statistics.

actNrRrcSuccRateSlCellCuDetRec.description: Activates sleeping-cell detection for NR cells based on RRC success-rate statistics observed at the CU (Central Unit).

actNrRrcSuccRateSlCellDuDetRec.description: Activates sleeping-cell detection for NR cells based on RRC success-rate statistics observed at the DU (Distributed Unit).

actNspNe3s.description: A Nokia-internal feature activation flag; based on its class (FEATCADM) and naming it likely toggles a specific optional network-element software capability, but the precise function of 'NspNe3s' cannot be determined from the name alone.

actOPGEnergySaving.description: Activates an energy-saving mode related to the module's output power/gain stage.

actObsaiOTNRecovery.description: Activates automatic recovery of OBSAI/Optical Transport Network links after a fault, without requiring manual intervention.

actPfoe.description: Activates Power-and-Fiber-over-Ethernet support, allowing a single cable to carry both data and remote power to equipment such as a Radio Unit.

actPimTesting.description: This parameter enables the Passive Inter-Modulation (PIM) testing functions in the BTS.

actPowerMeter.description:
This parameter indicates if BTS Embedded Power Meter for Energy Efficiency Monitoring feature is activated in the BTS or not.
This parameter indicates if the BTS Embedded Power Meter for Energy Efficiency Monitoring feature is activated in the BTS or not. When the feature is activated, it monitors the energy consumption of the system modules, radio modules and entire BTS.
Note: This parameter is valid only for configurations with FSM-r3 or newer

actPrefBbBoard.description: Sets a preferred baseband board to be used for certain functions when multiple baseband boards are available.

actPreservingRFPortMapp.description: Activates preservation of the existing RF-port-to-antenna mapping across a reconfiguration or software upgrade, avoiding an unwanted remap of antenna connections.

actPtiAndSpectreV2KernelFlag.description: Activates kernel-level mitigations for the PTI (Page Table Isolation, Meltdown) and Spectre V2 CPU security vulnerabilities.

actPtpMasterClock.description: Activates the PTP (Precision Time Protocol) master/grandmaster clock function on this node, letting it distribute timing to other network elements.

actRadioDeepSleepTimeSchedule.description: Activates a scheduled deep-sleep mode for the radio during defined low-traffic time windows to save energy.

actRatResetEnhancement.description: Activates an enhanced reset procedure for the radio-access-technology module, reducing recovery time or impact.

actRecovFromSecondaryController.description: Activates the ability to recover system operation from a secondary (backup) controller unit if the primary fails.

actRemoteRfDiag.description:
This is a feature flag to enable or disable remote RF diagnostic test feature.
Depending on the type of radio being tested, some measurements may not be available. Additional information about these missing measurements may be found in the testOutcomeAdditionalInfo parameter.

actRfChaining.description:
The parameter actRfChaining allows RF units chaining. 
That is, an optical fiber from the system module is chained via a RF unit to another RF unit.

actRfiTesting.description: This parameter enables the RF Interference testing function in the BTS.

actRuResetResiliency.description: Activates resiliency improvements that limit service impact when a Radio Unit undergoes a reset.

actRxMonitoring.description:
This parameter activates monitor of RX signal.
When this flag is set to true and RX signal level is below threshold alarm will be activated. Alarm will be active since TL/FL16A only.

actSWRollbackReject.description:
This is a feature flag to enable or disable rejection of an operator requested SW Rollback operation.
When Activate SW Rollback Rejection is enabled the BTS will reject an operator requested SW Rollback operation.
This feature flag is automatically set to disabled upon SW Upgrade.

actSecurityForFHS.description: Activates additional security hardening for the Fronthaul Switch (FHS).

actShdfAutoDelaySetting.description: Activates automatic calibration of a holdover/frequency-related delay setting used by the synchronization subsystem.

actSoftSyncErrorRecovery.description: Activates a soft (non-service-disruptive) recovery procedure when a synchronization error is detected, avoiding a full reset where possible.

actSyncEGen.description:
This parameter enables/disables the optional feature "Synchronous Ethernet Generation" .
The feature is disabled by default.
actSyncEGen.fullName: Feature activation flag for Synchronous Ethernet Generation

actSyncLinkSwitchover.description: Activates automatic switchover to an alternate synchronization link/source when the active one fails.

actSysCriticalEventLogs.description: Activates logging of system-critical events for later diagnostic review.

actSystemModuleSanityChecker.description: Likely a true/false switch that enables or disables a behavior related to "activate/enable System Module Sanity Checker" on the FEATCADM object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

actTargetConfigPrep.description: Activates pre-staging/preparation of a target configuration ahead of a planned change (e.g. software upgrade), to shorten the change window.

actTempFhsPrimController.description: Activates temporary designation of this unit as the primary Fronthaul Switch controller, typically during a redundancy switchover or recovery scenario.

actTempRadioMaster.description: This parameter activates the slave BTS in RF Sharing to temporarily take over the radio master role upon the detection of the master failure.

actTemperatureReport.description: Activates periodic reporting of equipment temperature readings for monitoring/diagnostics.

actTimeErrorManagement.description: Activates monitoring/management of accumulated timing error against synchronization budget limits (e.g. per ITU-T G.8271 concepts).

actToppTruechimerSelection.description: Activates automatic selection among candidate timing sources ('truechimers' - sources deemed reliable) for the Timing-over-Packet Profile.

actTransceiverAlarmMonitoring.description: Enables monitoring and alarm generation for pluggable transceiver (SFP/optics) fault conditions.

actTransportConfigFallback.description: This parameter enables/disables the transport configuration fallback functionality in the BTS.

actTrsActivationFailureRecovery.description: Activates automatic recovery action when activation of the timing/reference synchronization (TRS) subsystem fails.

actValidationOnUpgrade.description: Activates configuration/compatibility validation checks performed automatically during a software upgrade.

actWifiLmp.description: Controls a Wi-Fi-related local management link/port feature; exact function unclear from the name alone.

antLineSupervisionEnabled.description: Likely a true/false switch that enables or disables a behavior related to "antenna Line Supervision Enabled" on the FEATCADM object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

btsHotelId.description: This parameter allows to the operator to define BTS association with the BTS hotel.

btsHotelInterconnectionType.description: This parameter indicates whether the Ethernet links to the others BTS hotel members are realized via external Ethernet switch or without (direct link(s)).

btsHotelMaxNumMembers.description:
This parameter defines maximum allowed number of members in the BTS hotel.
Note: In runtime, if the parameter value will differ from recognized number of neighbours in BTS hotel, the alarms will be raised.
btsHotelMaxNumMembers.fullName: Maximal expected number of members in BTS hotel

cntrldResetMplaneBreakTime.description: Expected duration of Management-plane (O&M) connectivity loss during a controlled/planned base station reset, used by network management to suppress false connectivity alarms during that window.

cntrldResetMplaneBreakTimeSite.description: Configured allowable break time in Management-Plane connectivity for the whole site during a controlled/planned reset.

enforcedRecovTimeWindow.description: Defines the time window within which an enforced automatic-recovery action is permitted to execute.

featCAdmId.description: Defines the feature common management adminstration identifier

intShutdownInUse.description: This parameter denotes if intelligent shutdown feature is enabled or disabled for WCDMA and LTE. Intelligent shutdown for GSM is controlled via parameters in BCF.

ipsecSHA1DigitalSignDisable.description: Security-hardening flag that disables use of SHA-1-based digital signatures within IPsec, forcing stronger signature algorithms.

ne3sOperationLogging.description: Enables operation logging for the NE3S northbound/O&M interface, recording management operations for audit purposes.

neighbourPrachConfigReportingPeriod.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "neighbour Physical Random Access Channel Config Reporting Period" on the FEATCADM object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

netRfScanningEnabled.description: Enables the network RF-scanning feature, which lets the radio scan the spectrum (e.g. for interference detection or automated commissioning) outside of normal traffic operation.

otnCpriRecoveryPeriod.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "otn Cpri Recovery Period" on the FEATCADM object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

otnObsaiRecoveryPeriod.description: Time period the system waits between automatic recovery attempts for a failed OBSAI/OTN transport link.

rfSharingEnabled.description:
This parameter enables RF sharing with GSM, UTRAN, or EUTRA (FDD or TDD) between BTSs.

The shared RF cannot  be chained.
The shared ASIRMODs can be chained.

When RP3-01 sync is used between LTE and 3G,
LTE-3G RF sharing can be configured only if the shared BTS does or will contain a 3G System Module. If the 3G System Module does not exist and the LTE-3G RF sharing has been configured, LTE BTS will stay in the initializing state because the 3G System Module is always the synchronization master in case of LTE-3G RF sharing. Initializing state in the LTE BTS SW prevents reconfiguration commissioning of the LTE BTS by the BTS Site Manager.

When Sync Hub Direct Forward is used, and the LTE is the sync slave,
LTE-3G or LTE-LTE RF sharing can be configured only if the shared BTS does or will contain another 3G/LTE System Module. If the 3G/ LTE System Module does not exist and the LTE-3G or LTE-LTE RF sharing has been configured, LTE BTS will stay in the initializing state when the shared 3G/LTE System Module is the synch hub master or it is disrupting the synchronization chain. Initializing state in the LTE BTS SW prevents reconfiguration commissioning of the LTE BTS by the BTS Site Manager.

When LTE-LTE + LTE-GSM is configured, Sync Hub Direct Forward must be used. The LTE sync slave can be configured only if the shared BTS does or will contain another LTE or GSM System Module which provides sync propagation. If the LTE or GSM System Module does not exist, the LTE-LTE + LTE-GSM RF sharing has been configured, and the position of the LTE BTS in the SHDF chain is after a module that does not exist, that is, forwarded synch not provided, the LTE BTS will stay in the initializing state. Initializing state in the LTE BTS SW prevents reconfiguration commissioning of the LTE BTS by the BTS Site Manager. 

When AirScale is used, Sync Hub Direct Forward must be used.

When operating in RF sharing mode, a single RF Module is connected to two modules (System or Baseband Extension) simultaneously.

Two technologies are connected to the one and the same Flexi Multiradio RF Module. The two technologies can be:
- Flexi EDGE System Module is operating in GSM/EDGE SW with Flexi Multimode System Module in LTE
- Flexi EDGE System Module is operating in GSM/EDGE SW with Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE
- Flexi Multimode System Module is operating in WCDMA SW with Flexi Multimode System Module in LTE
- Flexi Multimode System Module is operating in WCDMA SW with Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE
- Flexi Multimode System/Extension Module is operating in LTE SW with a Flexi Multimode System/Extension Module in the peer LTE (LTE-LTE RF sharing) 

Two technologies are connected to the one and the same ASIRMOD. The two technologies can be:
- Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE TDD with Flexi Baseband Extension Module in LTE FDD

When the parameter ""rfSharingEnabled"" is ""true"" and LTE-LTE RF sharing is configured with additional sharing with GSM, the following are the recommended Sync Hub configuration:
1st in chain - LTE
2nd in chain – LTE
3rd in chain - GSM
4th in chain – GSM
When the parameter ""rfSharingEnabled"" is ""true"" and LTE-LTE RF sharing is configured without additional sharing with GSM, the parameter ""BTSSCL-syncPropagationEnabled"" must be set to ""true"" in one BTS and ""false"" in the other BTS.

The BTS will dynamically decide if a BTS restart or dropping of cells is needed.

systemAcctPermEnable.description: This BTS LINUX System Account Permissions feature enable parameter determines whether or not the service account and root account access controls provided by the feature  are in effect or disabled. When the parameter is set to "disabled", no feature effects are present. Service  account and root account access works exactly as it did prior to the feature introducing release. When the parameter is set to  "enabled", the full effects of the feature are present which includes service account access and root  account access.

tempRadioMasterRecovTime.description:
This is the timer started in Temporary Radio Master state after it detects that configured Radio Master has recovered. This is done to ensure that peer tech BTS is stable enough to take over Radio Master role again.

SYNC (from Peer Technology BTS ) on RP3-01 ports and before releasing the shared radios. This is done to ensure that
peer tech BTS is stable enough to start taking sync from it.
Zero (0) value indicates that no waiting is desired.

tempRadioMasterTriggerTime.description:
This is the timer started in Radio Slave state after slave BTS detects loss of Radio Master, before it takes over Temporary Master Role and re-establishes cells for the slave. Wait time is used to allow Radio Master to recover from a reset.
If eNB shall be able to enter test dedicated state while it is in Temporary Master role, the parameter must be set to the min value (0), meaning no waiting is desired.

This is the timer started in Sync Slave state after slave BTS detects SYNC loss (from Peer Technology BTS ) on RP3-01 ports. This is done to rule out any maintenance activity planned for peer technology BTS.

climateControlProfiling.description:
Climate control Profiling parameter.
Fan speed will be controlled according to module temperature and desired BTS fan profile.
- Low Noise: Minimised noise for low and moderate ambient temperatures
- Optimized Cooling: Maximised unit MTBF (long life) by running fans with maximum speed already in
moderate ambient temperatures
- Linear: An intermediate profile which increases fan speed linearly as temperature increase.
 
It is possible to select fan control profiles independently for each module in the BTS.

If user does not want to define fan profiling or module does not support fan profiles, the BTS manager will not set a value to SCF.

Parameter values are: "Optimized Cooling", "Linear" and "Low Noise". Default value is "Optimized Cooling".
BTS property Fan.Control.Profiles.Supported is defined if module supports Fan control profiles (low noise, linear, Optimized cooling). RF variants from Rel. 2.x onwards and FSM3r3 with fans shall have "TRUE" value. RF variants without fans or older than Rel. 2.x shall have "FALSE" value.

radioProtSearchOrder.description:
This parameter allows the operator to define the starting protocol for radio detection between OBSAI and CPRI variants.  

When this parameter is set, the FHS will start the radio protocol detection algorithm with the specified protocol on first startup or following upgrade activation of that module.  The use of this parameter can reduce the radio detection time in configurations where the Operator knows the type of radio deployment. If this parameter is not specified, the FHS will still be able to automatically detect the type of radio protocols in use, although the time to detect the radios may be increased for certain exceptional cases.  In this scenario, the FHS will attempt to use prior radio detection information to select the starting point for protocol searches.

Since this parameter defines the starting point for the search algorithm, it can only decrease the detection time for radios that are attached to the FHS when the algorithm is started. If no radios are attached to the module, the time to detect to the radios will be dependent upon the radio protocol type and the current protocol being probed by the FHS.

Note that if the Operator sets this parameter incorrectly, the radio detection time can be increased following a BTS restart or upgrade activation.

In all scenarios, the BTS will be able to detect the radio protocol with or without the Operator’s use of this parameter.

actAlarmsInTestDedicatedState.description: Controls whether alarms continue to be raised for a unit while it is in a Test/Dedicated (maintenance) administrative state, rather than being suppressed.

actAutoBTSCommission.description: Activates automatic (zero-touch) commissioning behavior tied into the fault-management subsystem.

actCategoryAlarms.description:
When this parameter is set to true, the BTS raises category alarms (alarm range 7100-7198). The BTS reports the faulty or degraded cells in the alarm.
When this parameter is set to false, the BTS raises legacy alarms (alarms 76xx and 74xx). 
7662 alarm and transmission alarms (61xxx) are reported independent of the value of actCategoryAlarms.

actCellAutoRecalculation.description: Controls when the system automatically recalculates derived cell configuration parameters - never, or only on operator demand.

actECpriOutOfTimingWindowAlarm.description: Activates the alarm raised when eCPRI fronthaul timing falls outside its acceptable window.

actForceAutoReset.description:
If this parameter is set to false, the BTS initiates an autonomous BTS reset or RAT reset or Site reset or BTS secondary core reset or FHS for fault recovery, only if 1) the recovery reset does not disable any working cell and 2) the reset counter value for the BTS/RAT/Site/secondary core/FHS is lower than number of allowed resets.

If this parameter is set to true, the BTS initiates an autonomous BTS reset or RAT reset or Site reset or BTS secondary core or FHS reset for fault recovery, when the BTS/RAT/Site/secondary core/FHS reset counter value is lower than number of allowed resets, even if the recovery reset temporary disables working cell(s). If any of the affected working cell(s) is in a degraded state, the autonomous fault recovery reset is abandoned, as degraded cell setup is not yet supported in the BTS.
If this parameter is set to true, the recovery reset is performed only after a graceful shutdown of the affected working cell(s). It may happen that not all calls are handed over from the shutdown cell to another cell within the shutdown time window. In this case, the calls are terminated.

SBTS Exceptions: 
a. 3G RAT reset is executed regardless of actForceAutoReset value. 
b. 3G cells are not gracefully shutdown before 1) 3G RAT reset or 2) site reset.
c. If 3G RAT reset is escalated to site reset, but site reset is not allowed, for example because actForceAutoReset is set to false and there are other RAT's working cells in the SBTS, all 3G cells are shutdown.

RAT autonomous reset for fault recovery is only applicable for SBTS.
BTS autonomous reset for fault recovery is only applicable for eNB.

actForceUnitAutoReset.description:
If this parameter is set to false, the BTS initiates an autonomous DSP group or FSP or radio reset for fault recovery, only if 1) the recovery reset does not disable any working cell and 2) the reset counter value for the DSP group/FSP/radio is lower than number of allowed resets 3) the DSP group/FSP only supports LTE application (condition 3 valid for DSP group/FSP reset).
If this parameter is set to true, the BTS initiates an autonomous DSP group reset or FSP or radio reset for fault recovery, when the DSP group/FSP/radio reset counter value is lower than number of allowed resets and the DSP group/FSP only supports LTE application for DSP group/FSP resets, even if the recovery reset temporary disables working cell(s). If any of the affected working cell(s) is in a degraded state, the autonomous fault recovery reset is abandoned, as degraded cell setup is not yet supported in the BTS.
If this parameter is set to true, the recovery reset is performed only after a graceful shutdown of the affected working cell(s). It may happen that not all calls are handed over from the shutdown cell to another cell within the shutdown time window. In this case, the calls are terminated.

If a device/unit recovery reset is escalated to BTS/Site/RAT/secondary core recovery reset, actForceAutoReset is taken into account. It may happen actForceUnitAutoReset is set to true and actForceAutoReset is set to false and recovery reset escalated from device/unit reset to BTS/Site/RAT/secondary core reset is blocked due to working cells.

DSP group and FSP autonomous reset for fault recovery is only applicable for eNB.

faultName.description:
BTS Fault name. The same name can be found in the BTS alarm documentation. This parameter includes also alarming resource and fault ID. Syntax used in enums: hw_faultId_faultName. NOTE: There are some special marks indicating usually dynamic part in the fault name.

Eventhough category alarms report root faults directly instead of group faults, group faults are used in alarm toggling suppression rules even when category alarms are reported. When a group fault is selected for alarm toggling suppression and category alarms are reported, the alarm toggling suppression rule will be applied for all the root faults that map to the specified group fault.

sfnPort.description:
This parameter allows the user to specify the port number where the SFN Z3 Network can be connected.
The default value is "none".
