softwareReleaseVersion.description: This parameter shows the SW release version of the FTM.

systemTitle.description: This parameter holds the the name of the network element. The operator can freely define the value of this parameter.

userLabel.description: The label that can be used for a usage description of the BFD session.

gerResTiFHM.description: The field t-ReselectionGERAN is multiplied with this factor if the UE is in the high mobility state as defined in 36.304
gerResTiFHM.fullName: GERAN cell reselection timer factor high mobility

gerResTiFMM.description: The field t-ReselectionGERAN is multiplied with this factor if the UE is in the medium mobility state as defined in 36.304.
gerResTiFMM.fullName: GERAN cell reselection timer factor medium mobility

gfimId.description: This parameter uniquely identifies a GFIM (GERAN frequency Idle Mode Configuration) managed object.
gfimId.fullName: GERAN frequency idle mode configuration identifier

allSelectedBeams.description: This parameter defines whether all beams are selected for PS calls (or only selected beam is for PS calls). It is relevant only in Lean GSM feature

bcfId.description: This parameter identifies the BTS in Abis signalling. The value equals with BCF ID in BSC RNW. The value may need updating during rehosting.

bscId.description: This is the unique BSC identifier used in Abis signalling. The value needs to be updated during rehosting.

gnBCFId.description: This is the instance identifier of the GNBCF object. The GNBCF contains GSM-BTS-specific base station parameters.

iuaAckTimerOmuSig.description: This parameter specifies the acknowledge timer, in seconds, for the IUA configuration.

leanGsmOrCmst.description: This parameter activates Lean GSM or Composited Multi Site Transmission (CMST) in the BTS. The features must also be activated in the BSC.

mPlaneDscpOmuSig.description: This parameter specifies the Differentiated services code point (DSCP) value to be used for OMUSig's management of the plane traffic.

mPlaneLocalIpAddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the IPADDRESSV4 object instance which holds the IPv4 address to be used M-plane OMUSIG.

IP addresses must not be identical with BTS internal IP addresses falling in the range 192.168.254.XXX or 192.168.255.XXX.

Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-1
mPlaneLocalIpAddressDN.fullName: Management plane local IP address for OMUSIG

mPlaneRemoteIpAddressOmuSig.description: This parameter defines the OMUSIG management plane traffic IP Address in the primary BSC. The IP address is not identical with BTS internal IP addresses falling in the range 192.168.254.XXX or 192.168.255.XXX.
mPlaneRemoteIpAddressOmuSig.fullName: Management plane remote IP address for OMUSIG

mPlaneRemoteIpAddressOmuSig2.description: This parameter defines the OMUSIG management plane traffic IP Address in the backup BSC. The IP address is not identical with BTS internal IP addresses falling in the range 192.168.254.XXX or 192.168.255.XXX.
mPlaneRemoteIpAddressOmuSig2.fullName: Management plane backup remote IP address for OMUSIG

maxBscTimeError.description: The parameter configures  the total expected error contained in the BSC time as received at the BTS. Its value is composed of the maximum error in the time within the BSC with respect to global GPS time and the maximum one-way delay in the Abis transmission path between the BSC and the BTS. When using terrestrial transport, the estimated maximum one-way delay is about 34ms (adding NTP error estimated total is 134 ms ) . When using satellite transport, the delay may be in the order of 300…400 ms. If the transport delay contains a variable component, the worst case delay must be chosen.

maxBtsTimeError.description: This parameter configures the maximum allowed time error between BSC and BTS required for supporting features depending on Loose H-SFN Sync in GSM
maxBtsTimeError.fullName: Absolute Allowed Maximum Time Error for BTS

rxds.description: This parameter denotes the minimum number of samples required in an RSSI measurement.

sctpBundlingEnabledOmuSig.description: This parameter defines whether the SCTP chunk bundling is used or not.

sctpHbIntervalOmuSig.description: This parameter specifies the SCTP heartbeat interval in order to monitor each idle remote IP address (that is, those not transmitting data traffic). A heartbeat message shall be exchanged between the BTS and BSC at every heartbeat interval.

sctpMaxPayloadSize.description: This parameter defines the maximum number of octets in an SCTP packet available for chunks. The SCTP has built-in means to control the packet size, for example, by chunk bundling. Therefore, fragmentation on the IP layer is not advisable and should be avoided. The SCTP payload size can be used to adapt the size of the SCTP packets to the MTU of the underlying link. The value of this parameter is defined in octets.

sctpMaxRetransAssocOmuSig.description: This parameter specifies the maximum number of consecutive retransmissions to a destination before an endpoint considers that the destination is unreachable and closes the association. There can be multiple paths in a single association.

sctpMaxRetransPathOmuSig.description: This parameter specifies the maximum value of tried retransmissions per destination per path.

sctpPortOmuSig.description:
This parameter specifies the start of the local SCTP port space that can be used for each instance of the Abis interface. This SCTP port is used for OMUSIG and SCTP.
The ports for TRXSIG are in the following order:
TRXSIG1   minSctpPort+1
TRXSIG2   minSctpPort+2
TRXSIG3   minSctpPort+3

sctpRtoInitOmuSig.description: This parameter specifies the initial value for the retransmission timeout. The value needs to be configured considering the network delay.

sctpRtoMaxOmuSig.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum value for the retransmission timeout. 
The maxRTO value should always be greater than or equal to the minRTO value.

sctpRtoMinOmuSig.description:
This parameter specifies the minimum value for the retransmission timeout. 
The minRTO value should always be less than or equal to the maxRTO value.

sctpSackPeriodOmuSig.description: This parameter specifies the selective acknowledge period which allows the SCTP to acknowledge packets selectively.

switchoverFailTimer.description: This parameter defines how many minutes the BTS shall wait for the establishment of the OMUSIG connection to the backup BSC. When the timer expires, BTS switches to the primary BSC. The parameter is valid only when valid remote backup BSC address is configured.

switchoverStartTimer.description: This parameter defines how many minutes the BTS shall wait for the loss of OMUSIG and TRXSIG connection and the re-establishment of the OMUSIG connection to the primary BSC. When the timer expires, BTS switches to the backup BSC. The parameter is valid only when valid remote backup BSC address is configured.

txPowerPooling.description: This parameter defines if the transmit power can be overridden to the nominal limit.

ucsSupervisionPktTimerValue.description: This parameter provides the interval, in milliseconds, for sending dummy packets for the U-CS plane supervision. The special value "0" indicates that the dummy packets are not sent.

udpMaxDatagramSize.description: This parameter defines the maximum number of octets of an IP packet used for GSM U-plane. The BSC does not support IP reassembly of fragmented IP packets. Accordingly the BSC discards fragmented IP packets. To minimize the probability of IP fragmentation of GSM U-plane IP packets, therefore the BTS can limit the maximum datagram size of the GSM U-plane IP packet. The value of this parameter is defined in octets.

upsSupervisionPktTimerValue.description: This parameter provides the interval, in milliseconds, for sending dummy packets for U-PS plane supervision. The special value "0" indicates that the dummy packets are not sent.

leanGsmOrCmst.description: This parameter indicate that which feature is active. Lean GSM or Composited Multi Site Transmission (CMST).

gnBTSId.description: This is the instance identifier of the GNBTS object. The GNBTS contains GSM-BTS-specific base station parameters.

gncelId.description: This is the instance identifier of the GSM local sector object (GNCEL). A local sector consists of the HW resources required by one sector for transmission and receiving. In Abis signalling, the local sector is associated with the BTS ID in the BSC RNW.

lcelcId.description: This parameter maps to the corresponding local sector (LCELC) object.

gsmBtsId.description: This parameter equals with the unique BTS ID in BSC RNW.

bandInd.description:
This is an indicator to distinguish the GERAN frequency band in case of ARFCN values associated with either GSM 1800 or GSM 1900 carriers.
For ARFCN values not associated with one of those bands, the indicator is not relevant.

gCelResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the GERAN carrier frequency

Equal priorities between RATs are not supported according to [3GPP 36.304].
gCelResPrio.fullName: GERAN RAT carrier frequency absolute priority

gerFrqThrH.description: This specifies the threshold used by the UE when reselecting towards a higher priority frequency X than the currently serving frequency

gerFrqThrL.description: This specifies the threshold used in reselection towards frequency X priority from a higher priority frequency

gnflId.description: Identifies GNFL (GERAN Neighbour Frequency List Configuration) managed object

idleLBGeranCelResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the GERAN carrier frequency used for idle mode load balancing.
For this parameter, 6 is the highest priority and 0 the lowest.
Note:
According to 3GPP 36.304, carriers in different RATs must have different Cell Reselection Priorities.
idleLBGeranCelResPrio.fullName: GERAN carrier freq prio for idle mode load balancing

idleLBGeranCelResWeight.description:
Weight factor of GERAN carrier frequency used by round robin algorithm for idle mode load balancing.
When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in selecting main target for IdleModeMobilityControlInfo for load balancing. Weighted round robin algorithm shall select always one target frequency for idle mode load balancing, which is matching UE capabilities, to be used as main target for idle mode load balancing and this target will have always highest  priority assigned in RRC Release message.  All other target frequency for idle mode load balancing matching UE capabilities and configured in LNCEL, IRFIM, UFFIM, CDFIM and GNFL will be added as well, but with lowered priorities as configured for SIB with kept hierarchy of priorities.  The algorithm shall calculate proportional weights corresponding to configured values. There is no check about the sum of weights configured by the user.
idleLBGeranCelResWeight.fullName: GERAN carrier weight factor idle mode load balancing

nccperm.description:
This parameter restricts the permitted Network Colour Code (NCC) for idle mode mobility.
Using default settings, no network is permitted.

A field encoded as a bitmap, where bit N is set to "0" if a BCCH carrier with NCC = N-1 is not permitted for monitoring, and set to "1" if the BCCH carrier with NCC = N-1 is permitted for monitoring; N = 1 to 8; bit 1 of the bitmap is the leading bit of the bit string.
nccperm.officialRange:
Bit 0:NCC 7:0:N; Bit 1:NCC 6:0:N; Bit 2:NCC 5:0:N; Bit 3:NCC 4:0:N; 
Bit 4:NCC 3:0:N; Bit 5:NCC 2:0:N; Bit 6:NCC 1:0:N; Bit 7:NCC 0:0:N

pMaxGer.description:

actBeidou.description: Enables use of the Chinese BeiDou satellite constellation by the GNSS timing/positioning receiver.

actGalileo.description: Enables use of the European Galileo satellite constellation by the GNSS timing/positioning receiver.

actGalileoOsnma.description: Activates Galileo OSNMA (Open Service Navigation Message Authentication), an anti-spoofing signal-authentication feature.

actGlonass.description: Enables use of the Russian GLONASS satellite constellation by the GNSS receiver.

actGps.description: Enables use of the US GPS satellite constellation by the GNSS receiver.

actNavic.description: Enables use of the Indian NavIC satellite constellation by the GNSS receiver.

galileoOsnmaExtTimeEnabled.description: Enables an extended-time-validity mode for Galileo OSNMA authentication, allowing a longer window of offline signal authentication.

This parameter contains the altitude of the GNSS antenna configured by the user. 

The parameter must be determined against the  reference ellipsoid within the WGS-84 coordinate system, with an accuracy of +/- 30 m.
The parameter is used by the GNSS receiver when locationMode is configured to manual mode.

gnssControlMode.description:
This parameter sets the GNSS receiver operation mode.

This parameter specifies the GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System), the GNSS receiver can utilize. The GNSS receiver may receive RF signals from the GNSS set by this parameter.

Nokia recommends strongly to select a dual GNSS operation mode.

gnssLineDelay.description:

Note: When using Nokia 1pps/ToD sync cables, the delay can be calculated using the specific cable delay of 4.9 ns/m.

gnsseId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the GNSSE object.

intervalRepGnssAntPosiSpeed.description: Reporting interval at which the GNSS subsystem reports antenna position/speed measurements, useful for detecting unexpected equipment movement.

locationMode.description:
This parameter defines how the GNSS  receiver determines the antenna location:

When set to "automatic" mode (default), the GNSS receiver determines the coordinates from the received satellite signals.

When set to "manual" mode, the coordinates must be manually determined by the user and configured into the BTS. Manual mode may be used when the number of visible satellites is too low for the GNSS receiver to determine the position itself.
Manual mode needs to be used with caution, since any errors in the configured location data beyond the specified limits can result in significant timing errors or erratic GNSS receiver operation.
