gNBIpAddrList.description:
This parameter defines the list of en-gNB IP-Addresses (to be supervised). 

"Transport separation for RAN sharing" not applicable on X2 interface for  path supervision towards  en-gNB

Both IP address formats can be used.
Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals or IPv6 address parameter acc. to RFC 4291.

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the address 0.0.0.0, the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).
gNBIpAddrList.fullName: gNB IPv4/v6 addresses of neighbor gNB

gtpuId.description: This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC GTPU

gtpuN3Reqs.description: This parameter holds the number of unanswered GTP-U ECHO REQUESTs (within the time defined by parameter t3Response), after which a GTP-U path failure is declared. The parameter is only relevant in case GTPU path supervision is switched ON (parameter gtpuPathSupint has a non-zero value).
gtpuN3Reqs.fullName: Maximum number of unanswered N3 requests

gtpuPathSupint.description:
This parameter holds the time interval between sending GTP-U ECHO REQUESTs, used for GTP-U user data path supervision on the S1 and X2 interfaces. It defines also if data path supervision is ON or OFF. Path supervision supported on X2 interface towards en-gNB only.

The 3GPP recommend  GTP-U supervision interval  starts with a value 60s.

gtpuT3Resp.description: This parameter holds the maximum waiting time for GTP-U ECHO RESPONSE messages, used for GTP-U data path supervision on the S1 and X2 interfaces. This parameter is only relevant in case GTP-U path supervision is switched ON (parameter gtpuPathSupint has a non-zero value). Path supervision supported on X2 interface towards en-gNB only.
gtpuT3Resp.fullName: T3 maximum waiting time for GTP-U responses

sgwIpAddress.description:
Application IPv4/v6 address of the serving SAE gateway (S-GW) for which datapath supervision is switched on.
Both IP address formats can be used.
Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals or IPv6 address parameter acc. to RFC 4291.

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the address 0.0.0.0, the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).

transportNwId.description: This parameter holds the identifier for the transport network to which the S-GW belongs.

udpMaxDatagramSize.description: This parameter defines the maximum number of octets of a UDP datagram excluding the UDP header in the transport layer. This value is used to determine the MSS for clamping of end user TCP traffic. The maximum segment size due to clamping is udpMaxDatagramSize - 16 (GTP-U) - 20/40 (IPv4/v6) - 20 (TCP).

locationName.description: This parameter holds the description of the geographical location of the network element. The format can be freely decided by the operator. The parameter may also be empty.

userLabel.description: The label that can be used for a usage description of the BFD session.

vendorName.description: User defined inventory unit vendor name.

hwResetComment.description: Comment to the hardware reset command

hwResetReqId.description: Identifier of the hardware reset command

targetHwResetUDN.description:
Target Dist Name of the HW Unit to be resetted.

If the target HW unit is a radio module and the radio module is shared with CDMA (i.e. cpriARfSharing is set to SECONDARY), reset request will only iniitate an LTE session reset and not a reset of the entire radio.
targetHwResetUDN.fullName: Target HW reset unit distinguish name

hwResetResId.description: Identifier of the hardware reset result instance.

hwResetResult.description: Value defines result of the hardware reset command

hwTopRId.description: Defines the HW Topology Runtime identifier

iafimId.description: This parameter uniquely Identifies an IAFIM (Intra-Frequency Idle Mode configuration) managed object.
iafimId.fullName: Intra frequency idle mode configuration identifier

physCellIdNcl.description:
The Physical Cell Identifier is a unique cell identification in a neighboring cell list.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.
physCellIdNcl.fullName: Physical cell identifier in neighboring cell list

qOffsetCell.description:
The parameter defines a cell-specific offset (in dB) that is used in the cell reselection procedure.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

rangeIntraPci.description:
Indicates the number of PCIs in the range (including startPCI). Value n4 corresponds with 4, n12 corresponds with 12 and so on. The UE applies value 1 if the field is absent, in which case only the physical cell identity value indicated by start applies.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.
rangeIntraPci.fullName: Number of PCI in intra-frequency range

startIntraPci.description:
Indicates the lowest PCI in the range.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

IAFIMNB.officialFullName: Intra-frequency Idle Mode for NB-IoT configuration

iafimnbId.description: This parameter uniquely identifies an IAFIMNB (Intra-Frequency Idle Mode configuration for NB-IoT) managed object.
iafimnbId.fullName: Intra frequency idle mode configuration identifier for NB-IoT

physCellIdNcl.description: The Physical Cell Identifier is a unique cell identification in a neighboring cell list for NB-IoT.
physCellIdNcl.fullName: Physical cell identifier in neighboring cell list for NB-IoT

qOffsetCell.description: The parameter defines a cell-specific offset (in dB) that is used in the cell reselection procedure for NB-IoT.
qOffsetCell.fullName: Cell reselection procedure offset for NB-IoT

rangeIntraPci.description:
Indicates the number of PCIs in the range (including startPCI). Value n4 corresponds with 4, n12 corresponds with 12 and so on. The UE applies value 1 if the field is absent, in which case only the physical cell identity value indicated by start applies.

The setting is commonly valid for NB-IoT UE.
rangeIntraPci.fullName: Number of PCI in intra-frequency range  for NB-IoT

startIntraPci.description: Indicates the lowest PCI in the range for NB-IoT.
startIntraPci.fullName: Lowest PCI in intra-frequency range for NB-IoT

iBrgPrtId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the internal bridge port object. It uniquely identifies the object.

portDefaultVlanId.description:
This parameter defines the VLAN identifier that is associated to untagged and priority-tagged frames received at this Ethernet interface (internal switch-port).

Furthermore this parameter determines, that frames associated to this VLAN identifier which are switched and transmitted at this switch-port will be transmitted untagged.

In order to achieve that a received untagged or priority-tagged frame is switched and transmitted via another (external) switch-port, the same VLAN identifier must be configured at the transmission port:
a) for VLAN-tagged transmission: in the VLAN identifier list of that transmit switch-port (see parameter l2VlanIdList) or
b) for untagged transmission: in the portDefaultVlanID of that transmit switch-port.
Else the frame will be discarded.
portDefaultVlanId.fullName: Default VLAN identifier for layer 2 switching

portDefaultVlanPriority.description:
This parameter defines the default VLAN priority assigned to untagged Ethernet frames received at this Ethernet interface (external switch-port)

The priority is used:
- for QoS classification of the frame, depending on the selected qosClassificationCriteria and frame content,
- for L2 priority marking of the frame at egress when the frame is transmitted VLAN-tagged, depending on the transmit port VLAN configuration.

The priority level values range from zero (best effort) to seven (highest).

gtpFDscp.description: This parameter defines the differentiated services code point (DSCP) value assigned to the GTP-F traffic.

gtpFUdpPort.description: This parameter defines the UDP port to be used for the GTP-F traffic.

iComGwId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the ICOMGW object. It uniquely identifies the object.

ipV4AddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the IPADDRESSV4 object instance which holds the IPv4 address to be used for the ICOM gateway.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-2

ipV6AddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the IPADDRESSV6 object instance which holds the IPv6 address to be used for the ICOM gateway.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV6-2

sctpDscp.description: This parameter defines the differentiated services code point (DSCP) value assigned to the SCTP traffic.

sctpPort.description: This parameter defines the SCTP port.

userLabel.description:
The user label can be used freely to add a short description, e.g. the purpose of the configuration related to this managed object.
The following characters are supported:
a-z
A-Z
0-9
Special characters: !|#|$|%|(|)|*|+|,|-|.|/|:|;|=|?|@|[|\|]|^|_|`|{|||}|~

dnsAccessId.description: This parameter identifies the DNS Access configuration object. Value is always 1.

serverIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address of the primary DNS server. If the parameter has a valid value (not empty, not 0.0.0.0, not ::) this server is queried first for DNS resolution.

If feature LTE955 is activated, IPv6 address must be provided, otherwise an IPv4 address must be provided.
Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC 4291.
serverIpAddress.fullName: IP address of the primary DNS server

serverIpAddress2.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address of the secondary DNS server. The secondary DNS is queried if the IP address of the primary DNS server is not configured or if it is configured but a query for DNS resolution to the primary DNS server fails.

If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC 4291.
serverIpAddress2.fullName: IP address of the secondary DNS server

ieifId.description:
This parameter identifies the BTS transport Ethernet-based IP interface. 
The value is always 1.
ieifId.fullName: Identifier of the ethernet based IP interface

localIpAddr.description:
This parameter defines the IPv6 address. 
Format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. 
Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

The localIpAddr together with the parameter localIpPrefixLength define an IP subnet.
For virtual IP interfaces a subnet can't be defined.
localIpAddr.fullName: IP address of the plain Ethernet network interface

localIpv6Addr.description:
This is the IPv6 address of the VLAN Ethernet network interface towards the external transport network. 
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.
localIpv6Addr.fullName: Plain Ethernet Network Interface IPv6 Address

localIpv6PrefixLength.description:
This is the IPv6 prefix-length parameter of the plain Ethernet network interface towards the external transport network. 
Format: parameter acc. to RFC4291.

Note: Values 1 and 2 are not allowed.
localIpv6PrefixLength.fullName: Plain Ethernet Network Interface IPv6 Prefix-Length

mtu.description:
This is the maximum transfer unit of the Ethernet interface.

NOTE: For HW unit types FSM/FTIF, the supported range is '576..1644 octets'. For all HW FlexiZone Micro unit types, the supported range is '576..1644 octets'. For AirScale HW unit type ASIA, the supported range is '576..9978 octets'

netmask.description: Specifies the mask of the remote network. To be entered in dotted decimal format.
netmask.fullName: Subnet mask of the plain Ethernet network interface

overrideMTUSize.description:
This parameter is used to specify the override value that should be used for MTU size instead of the MTU size value obtained from DHCP server or when MTU value is not obtained from DHCP server.
(Note: When DHCPOFFER does not contain MTU value, eNB defaults to using a value of 1500 bytes for MTU size)
The parameter is only applicable if actACNonOpBackhaul or actDynamicIP is TRUE
The default value is 0.

qosEnabled.description: This parameter specifies if multiple PHB queues are used over this VLAN interface or only a single one. Multiple PHB queues allow DSCP based traffic prioritisation.

sbs.description:
This parameter defines the shaper burst size at the egress of the particular first level scheduler.
Note : The parameter shapingOverhead automatically applies also to all linked first level schedulers/shapers when enabled and it needs to be considered in all shaping and calculating packet length.

sbsTotal.description: This parameter defines the burst size in bytes of the token bucket shaper at the output of the second-level scheduler (i.e. aggregating the traffic of the plain Ethernet interface and all related VLAN interfaces).

sir.description:
This parameter defines the egress-shaping rate of this particular first level scheduler.
Note : The parameter shapingOverhead automatically applies also to all linked first level schedulers/shapers when enabled and this needs to be considered in all shaping and calculating packet length.

sirTotal.description:
This parameter defines the shaper rate in kbps at the output of the second-level scheduler (i.e. aggregating the traffic of the plain Ethernet interface and all related VLAN interfaces).
If the defined rate is exceeding the detected Ethernet link speed (ETHLK_R-detectedSpeedAndDuplex) , the value of the detected Ethernetlink speed will be used. This is applicable only in cases where the scheduler is directly associated with a physical interface.

trafficPathShapingEnable.description: This parameter decides on the type of shaping in case of VLANs.  When traffic path shaping is enabled, shaping at the level of each VLAN is enabled, else shaping at the WFQ aggregator level is enabled. Shaping may also be switched off entirely.

upperLayerShaping.description: This parameter decides if shaping takes the ethernet overhead into account. If the flag has value "true", the shaped bandwidth is the bandwidth on the IP layer only. If the flag has value "false", the ethernet header is counted also.
upperLayerShaping.fullName: Take ethernet overhead into account when shaping

wfqSchedQueueWeight.description: This is the weight value to be used in the WFQ aggregation scheduler for this interface.

algSelection.description:
This parameter defines the selection method of inter-frequencies in final frequency list 
The default value is "weighted probability randomization" which the weight of a frequency depends on number of neighbour cells and relations
algSelection.fullName: Selection method in default group profile
algSelection.officialRange:
1: fixed order within the group 
2: weighted probability randomization 
3: equal probability randomization

groupPrio.description: This parameter defines the group priority within the default group profile
groupPrio.fullName: Group priority in default group profile

groupSize.description:
This parameter defines the group size reserved in final frequency list
The default value is 0 which means the group is no place reserved in final list, the frequency within the group will be filled in the gaps without any reservation in final frequency list.
groupSize.fullName: Group Size in default group profile

ifGDPrId.description: This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC IFGDPR and it uniquely identifies an instance of the Inter-frequency Default Group Profile (IFGDPR)

algSelection.description:
This parameter defines the selection method of inter-frequencies in final frequency list 
The default value is "weighted probability randomization" which the weight of a frequency depends on number of neighbour cells and relations
algSelection.fullName: Selection method in dedicated group profile
algSelection.officialRange:
1: fixed order within the group 
2: weighted probability randomization 
3: equal probability randomization

groupPrio.description: This parameter defines the group priority within the default group profile
groupPrio.fullName: Group priority in dedicated group profile

groupSize.description:
This parameter defines the group size reserved in final frequency list
The default value is 0 which means the group is no place reserved in final list, the frequency within the group will be filled in the gaps without any reservation in final frequency list.
groupSize.fullName: Group Size in dedicated group profile

ifGPrId.description: This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC IFGPR and it uniquely identifies an instance of the Inter-frequency dedicated Group Profile (IFGPR).

ifGPrSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC IFGPRSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an IFGPRSPARE instance.

name.description:
This is the name of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The content is filled by the BTS and cannot be changed.

The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

value.description:
This is the value of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The allowed parameter values are defined in the feature specification.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.

dhcpAccessId.description:
This parameter identifies the unique DHCP Server object in the BTS. Its value is always 1.

Note:This is not applicable for FlexiZone Micro hardware.

dhcpClientIdentifier.description:
This is a unique string used in the DHCP server of the BTS for identifying a DHCP client that is assigned a fixed IP address. 
This may either be one of the predefined names "RET1" (Remote Electrical Tilt), "RET2", "BBU" and "LMU" or a user-defined name consisting of up to 20 digits [0-9] or letters [a-z] and [A-Z].

dhcpFixedIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the fixed IP address that is to be assigned to the DHCP client if it requests a lease with the name specified in parameter dhcpClientIdentifier.
The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.

dhcpHardwareIdentifier.description: This is the unique hardware (MAC) address within the DHCP server of the BTS by which a DHCP client identifies itself at the BTS. The server will then assign the IP address of the parameter "DHCP Fixed IP Address" to the client.

dhcpRangeEnd.description:
This parameter specifies the final IP address of the DHCP IP address range.

The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. 
However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.

dhcpRangeStart.description:
This parameter specifies the starting IP address of the DHCP IP address range.

The IP address must be within the public IP subnet of the BTS. However, neither the IP addresses of the BTS nor its subnet IP address must be used.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.

connectionEstablishmentMode.description: This parameter defines if the base station shall actively initiate a connection to the peer or if the base station should wait for the peer to establish the connection.

dpdDelay.description: This parameter defines the time delay after which the first empty INFORMATIONAL message is sent to the peer if no IKE messages are received in order to check if the peer is still alive (Dead Peer Detection). After that, further INFORMATIONAL messages are sent with increasing intervals (4, 7, 13, 24 and 42 seconds) so that six INFORMATIONAL messages are sent in one repetition cycle. After the sixth INFORMATIONAL message and 75 seconds waiting time the cycle starts again with dpddelay timer restart. The BTS raises the Dead Peer Detected (DPD) alarm after the fourth INFORMATIONAL message is sent in the cycle (dpddelay timer + (4 + 7 + 13) seconds). The dpddelay timer and thus the repetition cycle is restarted if an IKE message is received.

ikeAuthenticationMethod.description:
This parameter defines the authentication method used for the IKE protocol.
Please note that the supported values depend on the defined IKE authentication method.
ikeAuthenticationMethod.officialRange:
1: AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 
2: AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128 
3: AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_384_192 
4: AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_512_256 
5: AUTH_AES_XCBC_MAC_96 
6: AUTH_AES_GCM_ICV16_128 
7: AUTH_AES_GCM_ICV16_256

ikeDiffHellGrp.description: This parameter defines the DH group to be used for the establishment and rekeying of IKE SAs.

ikeEncryptionMethod.description:
This parameter defines the encryption method used for the IKE protocol.
Please note that the supported values depend on the defined authentication method.
ikeEncryptionMethod.officialRange:
0: ENC_AES_128_CBC 
1: ENC_3DES_192_CBC 
3: ENC_AES_192_CBC 
4: ENC_AES_256_CBC 
5: ENC_AES_GCM_ICV16_128 
6: ENC_AES_GCM_ICV16_256

ikeMaxLifeTime.description:
This parameter defines the maximum duration, in seconds, in the life time of the  IKE security associations. 
Before the timer expires for a security association, a new security association is negotiated.
Note: It is recommended to start negotiation of a new security association on BTS side. 
Therefore, the value has to be lower than the corresponding value configured at the remote end.

ikePId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IKE profile object. It uniquely identifies the object.
It is highly recommended to use for object creation the lowest free ikePId value within all IKEP instances of the BTS.
This will ensure that there will be no conflicts between manually configured IKEP instances and autonomously created IKEP instances by the BTS.
If enabled, the BTS can support the autonomous creation of IKEP instances. For this the BTS will always use the highest free ikePId value.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).

ipsecPerfForwSecEnabled.description: This parameter enables the use of the Perfect Forward Secrecy when establishing and re-keying IPsec SAs.

localTunnelEndpointDN.description:
This parameter defines the IPADDRESSV4 or IPADDRESSV6 object instance which holds the IPv4 or IPv6 address to be used as local endpoint of the IPsec tunnel.
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example:
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-1
localTunnelEndpointDN.fullName: Local IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

remoteTunnelEndpoint.description:
This parameter defines the remote endpoint of the IPsec tunnel as seen by the NE.
IPv4 address format: Dot-decimal notation (x.x.x.x). 
Example: 10.10.10.10.

IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. 
Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
remoteTunnelEndpoint.fullName: Remote IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

userLabel.description: This parameter denotes a label that can be used for a usage description of the object configuration.

ikePDN.description:
This parameter defines which IKE profile shall be used.
The IKE profile is defined by giving the distinguished name (DN):
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPAPP-1/IPSECC-1/IKEP-1

The IKE Profile DNs for primary and secondary must be different.

ikeProtGrpId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IKE protection group object. It uniquely identifies the object.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).

role.description:
This parameter defines whether the IKE profile shall be used as primary or secondary IKE profile.
The preferred IKE profile is to be defined as "PRIMARY".
The secondary IKE profile provides the backup configuration which is used if the primary IKE profile fails.
Within an IKEPROTGRP the role must be configured different for the IKE profiles.

switchBackMode.description:
This parameter defines whether the NE should automatically or manually (operator command) switchback to the primary IKE profile.
Only if set to MANUAL, the switch can be triggerd by management request.

switchTimeMax.description: This parameter defines the maximum time delay in seconds before switchover or switchback of the IKE profile. The NE will use random delay between minimum and maximum delay timers for switchover or switchback.

switchTimeMin.description: This parameter defines the minimum time delay in seconds before switchover or switchback of the IKE profile. The NE will use random delay between minimum and maximum delay timers for switchover or switchback.

ikeProtGrpRId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only IKE protection group object. It uniquely identifies the object.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA.
ikeProtGrpRId.fullName: Read only IKE protection group object identifier

ikeProtState.description: This parameter indicates whether the primary or secondary IKE profiles is active.

ikeSwitchReqId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IKE profile switch request object. It uniquely identifies the object.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).
ikeSwitchReqId.fullName: IKE profile switch request object identifier

switchRequest.description: This parameter requests a switch of the IKE profile.

ikeSwitchResId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IKE profile switch response object. It uniquely identifies the object.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A)
ikeSwitchResId.fullName: IKE profile switch response object identifier

switchResult.description: This parameter indicates whether the  IKE profile switch request has been successful (OK) ot not (FAIL).

ikePeerState.description:
This parameter indicates the state of the IKE peer.
Every connection could be in these states- 
CONNECTING or ESTABLISHED (IKE SA status),
NO_STATE (if the state is unknown)

ikepRId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only IKE profile object. It uniquely identifies the object.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).
ikepRId.fullName: Read only IKE profile object identifier

maxNtpTimeError.description: This parameter configures the maximum expected time error recovered from NTP source by the BTS, as measured against UTC/GPS time.
maxNtpTimeError.fullName: Maximum NTP time error at the BTS

ntpAccessId.description: This parameter identifies the unique NTP configuration entity of the BTS. The value is always 1. Exactly 1 NTP configuration entity always exists on the BTS.

ntpAlarmThreshold.description:
This parameter defines the amount of time in seconds the BTS will wait before raising the "NTP server is not accessible" fault when NTP server unavailability is detected.
The default value is 300 seconds.

ntpDscp.description: This parameter defines the differentiated services code point (DSCP) value to be used for NTP traffic.

ntpServers.description:
This parameter specifies the IP addresses of the NTP servers. 
All configured IP addresses shall be of the same version (IPv4 or IPv6).

Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC4291.
ntpServers.fullName: List of NTP server IP addresses

ntpSourceIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address to be used for the BTS NTP  client .
The BTS NTP client must collapse with either  U, C, M or S-plane.
This parameter supports both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
If this parameter is not configured or set to the default value "0.0.0.0" then mPlaneIpAddress is used for the BTS NTP client.
For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

ntpSyncPortMode.description:
This parameter specifies how the NTP client IP port number is assigned.
In the default setting (0:Standard) the NTP client assumes a port number of 123. In the 1:Asymmetric mode the NTP client assumes a port within the range 30001 to 30010.
ntpSyncPortMode.fullName: NTP Synchronization IP Port Selection Mode

ntpTimeLocalIpMapping.description:
This parameter specifies to which Plane IP address (M-Plane, C-Plane, U-Plane, S-Plane or as configured by the INTP-ntpSourceIpAddress parameter) the BTS NTP Time Synchronization client will be mapped.
When this parameter is configured to Plane supporting Dual Stack operation (C/U-Plane) then the NTP Time Synchronization client is mapped to the IP version (IPv4 or IPv6) of the IP addresses configured in the list of NTP time synchronization servers (INTP-ntpServers).
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM only.
By default, the NTP client used for setting BTS system time is mapped to the M-Plane BTS IP address.
ntpTimeLocalIpMapping.fullName: NTP time synchronization local IP mapping
ntpTimeLocalIpMapping.officialRange:
0: M-Plane 
1: C-Plane 1 
2: C-Plane 2 
3: U-Plane 1 
4: U-Plane 2 
5: S-Plane 
100: Set by INTP-ntpSourceIpAddress

utcGpsNtpOffsetAfter.description:
This parameter sets the offset (in seconds) between GPS time and UTC (without the timezone difference) valid after the date/time specified in utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate. It is dedicated to NTP time source.
Note: This parameter is used by Macro BTS only.
utcGpsNtpOffsetAfter.fullName: NTP UTC-GPS offset value after change date

utcGpsNtpOffsetBefore.description:
This parameter sets offset (in seconds) between GPS time and UTC (without the timezone difference) valid before the date/time specified in utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate. It is dedicated to NTP time source.

Note: This parameter is used for Macro BTS only.
utcGpsNtpOffsetBefore.fullName: NTP UTC-GPS offset value before change date

utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate.description:
This parameter describes the next date of change of utcGpsOffset, or the previous date if next has not been announced yet. It is dedicated to NTP time source.
The format is: YYYY-MM-DD
utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate.fullName: Next/last known NTP UTC-GPS offset change date

configDN.description: Distinguished name of paired configured managed object.
configDN.fullName: Distinguished name of paired configured managed object

parentDN.description: The Distinguished Name of the parent managed object in the equipment hierarchy for this inventory unit.

runtimeDN.description: Distinguished Name of the actual as-installed (runtime) managed-object instance corresponding to this inventory unit record, the runtime-side counterpart of configDN.

serialNumber.description: Serial number of inventory unit.

state.officialRange:
0: CMP_Unitialized 
1: CMP_InitializationRequested 
2: CMP_InitializationOngoing 
3: CMP_InitializationOK 
4: CMP_InitializationFailed 
5: CMP_KeyUpdateRequested 
6: CMP_KeyUpdateOngoing 
7: CMP_KeyUpdateOK 
8: CMP_KeyUpdateFailed 
9: CMP_InitializationWaiting 
10: CMP_UpdateWaiting 
99: CMP_Uninitialized

vendorName.description: User defined inventory unit vendor name.

versionNumber.description: The version information related to vendorUnitTypeNumber.

dateOfLastService.description: Date of last service or repair of inventory unit.

dateOfManufacture.description: Date of Manufacture of inventory unit.

invunitRId.description: Identifies the specific runtime inventory unit.

manufacturerData.description: Manufacturer specific data of inventory unit.

serialNumber.description: Serial number of inventory unit.

unitPosition.description: Position of inventory unit. When there is more than 1 instance of the same inventory unit is present, the unit position distiguishes the location of the unit. Depending on the unit type, it can be a slot number, a port number, etc. which can be used to identify the unit at the site.

vendorName.description: User defined inventory unit vendor name.

versionNumber.description: The version information related to vendorUnitTypeNumber.

ipAddressAllocationMethod.description:
This parameter defines how an IP address shall be allocated.
The following options are supported:
1.) MANUAL: it is mandatory to define the localIpAddr.
2.) DISCOVERED: the IP address shall be allocated by the environment.

The actually allocated IP address can be found from IPADDRESSV6_R-localIpAddrAllocated.

ipAddressV4Id.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IPv4 address object. It uniquely identifies the object.

localIpAddr.description:
This parameter defines the IPv6 address. 
Format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. 
Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

The localIpAddr together with the parameter localIpPrefixLength define an IP subnet.
For virtual IP interfaces a subnet can't be defined.

localIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter defines the prefix length.
Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-32
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-128

ipAddressV4RId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only IPv4 address object. It uniquely identifies the object.
ipAddressV4RId.fullName: Read only IPv4 address object identifier

localIpAddrAllocated.description:
This parameter indicates the successfully allocated IPv4 address. 
This can be either the manually configured IP address or a dynamically allocated IP address.

ipAddressAllocationMethod.description:
This parameter defines how an IP address shall be allocated.
The following options are supported:
1.) MANUAL: it is mandatory to define the localIpAddr.
2.) DISCOVERED: the IP address shall be allocated by the environment.

The actually allocated IP address can be found from IPADDRESSV6_R-localIpAddrAllocated.

ipAddressV6Id.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IPv6 address object. It uniquely identifies the object.

localIpAddr.description:
This parameter defines the IPv6 address. 
Format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. 
Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

The localIpAddr together with the parameter localIpPrefixLength define an IP subnet.
For virtual IP interfaces a subnet can't be defined.

localIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter defines the prefix length.
Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-32
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-128

ipAddressV6RId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only IPv6 address object. It uniquely identifies the object.
ipAddressV6RId.fullName: Read only IPv6 address object identifier

localIpAddrAllocated.description:
This parameter indicates the successfully allocated IPv6 address. 
This can be either the manually configured IP address or a dynamically allocated IP address.

ipAppId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IP application object. It uniquely identifies the object.

twampSenderMessageRate.description:
This parameter defines the overall rate at which the TWAMP sender of the NE sends the TWAMP test messages. The messages are evenly spread over the enabled TWAMP sessions at any given time.
The two message rates can be configured as: RATE_1 (0): 1 message per second; or RATE_10 (1): 10 messages per second.
twampSenderMessageRate.fullName: Rate at which TWAMP sender sends out messages

interfaceDN.description:
This parameter defines a reference to a Layer 2 interface. It can refer to an instance of either ETHIF, VLANIF, P3SL or P3ML.The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN):
Examples: 
- MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/ETHSVC-1/ETHIF-1
- MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/P3ML-1
This parameter must not be defined, if the interface shall be a virtual IP interface. Only one virtual IPIF can be created per BTS.

ipIfId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IP interface object. It uniquely identifies the object.

ipMtu.description:
This parameter defines the maximum IP packet size, in octets, transmitted through that IP interface.
The supported value range depends on the Layer 2 capabilities (Ethernet, VLAN, ML PPP, SL PPP).
For VLAN interfaces, the ipMtu must be minimum four octets smaller than the configured MTU of the underlying Ethernet interface.
The ipMtu must not be defined for the virtual IP interfaces. Virtual IP interfaces have no interfaceDN defined.
The ipMtu must not be defined for IP interfaces whose interfaceDN refers to an ETHIF instance which has the linkSelectorDN defined to match an ETHLK instance with the connectorLabel set to "LMP1".

The supported value range depends on the IP version. For IPv4: 200..9500; for IPv6: 1280..9500.

userLabel.description: The label that can be used for a usage description of the BFD session.

ipIfRId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only IP interface object. It uniquely identifies the object.
ipIfRId.fullName: Read only IP interface object identifier

linkLocalIpV6Address.description: This parameter indicates the Link-Local IPv6 address (specified acc. to RFC 4862) which has been set by the system based on the corresponding Ethernet MAC address.

actACNonOpBackhaul.description:
This parameter activates the support of auto-connection functionality when eNB is connected to a non-operator owned (untrusted) backhaul.

The default value is "false".
actACNonOpBackhaul.fullName: Activate Autoconnection in Non-Operator Owned Network

actDualUPlaneIpAddress.description: This parameter activates/deactivates the feature "Dual U-Plane Ip Addresses"
actDualUPlaneIpAddress.fullName: Activation Flag Dual U-Plane Ip Addresses

actDynamicFirewall.description: This parameter enables/disables the optional feature "Dynamic X2 and S1 firewall configuration".
actDynamicFirewall.fullName: Feature Activation Flag for dynamic X2 and S1 firewall configuration

actDynamicIP.description:
The parameter "actDynamicIP" activates the support for dynamic assignment of IP addresses for transport and M/C/U/S plane from DHCP server and/or Security gateway depending on the deployment scenario (private or public backhaul).
The default value is "false".
By default initial IP addresses obtained from DHCP server and/or Security gateway during autoconnection phase will be replaced after final configuration is received from NetAct.
actDynamicIP.fullName: Feature Activation Flag Dynamic IP assignment

actEnableTLSv13.description: Enables TLS protocol version 1.3 for securing management-plane (O&M) network connections.

actFastIpRerouting.description: This flag indicates whether the optional feature Fast IP Rerouting is in use or not.
actFastIpRerouting.fullName: Feature Activation Flag For Fast IP Re-Routing

actIPv6Mplane.description: This parameter activates IPv6 in M-plane. All related IP addresses shall be in IPv6 format if this flag is set. When this flag is not set, only IPv4 is supported in M-plane.

actIpTnlMeasure.description:
This flag enables/disables the optional feature IP Transport Network Measurement.
NOTE: The individual sessions creation and other related parameters configuration should be allowed irrespective of state of this flag.
By default, the parameter is set to 'false'
actIpTnlMeasure.fullName: Feature Activation Flag IPTransport Network Measurement

actIpv6.description: This parameter enables/disables the optional feature "Dual Stack IPv4/IPv6 for S1/X2".
actIpv6.fullName: Feature Activation Flag Dual Stack IPv4/IPv6 for S1/X2

actLoSPropagation.description: This parameter enables LoS propagation feature to troubleshoot connectivity problems downstream.

actMultipleDynamicIP.description:
This parameter  activates the support for dynamic assignment of IP addresses for multiple tunnels in case of public backhaul scenario. Both IPv6 or IPv4 inner IP addresses obtained for LTE M/C/U/S-planes through IPv4 IPSec tunnels are supported.
The default value is "false".
When this feature is activated the following IP addresses should be set to 0.0.0.0: IPNO-cPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-mPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-sPlaneIpAddress, IPNO-uPlaneIpAddress, IEIF-localIpAddr, IEIF-NetMask, IPRT-staticRoutes::gateway, IPSECC-securityPolicies::localTunnelEndpoint. Moreover, if operator creates VLAN (IVIF) object, then the operator should set the vlanId to 0 and the following IP addresses to 0.0.0.0: IEIF/IVIF-localIpAddr, IEIF/IVIF-netmask (the eNB shall send CCN to iOMS/NetAct to update the values for the above attributes).
actMultipleDynamicIP.fullName: Feature Activation Flag for multiple IPsec tunnels with dynamic IP assignment

actSeparationRanSharing.description:
This parameter activates/deactivates the feature "Transport Separation for RAN Sharing"
If IPsec is enabled and additional transport network is deleted or modified, then actSeparationRanSharing should be disabled first.
actSeparationRanSharing.fullName: Activation Flag  Transport Separation For RAN Sharing

addCPlaneIpAddressSec.description:
This parameter holds the secondary C-Plane IPv4 address of this  eNB for the additional transport network in case feature LTE648 and LTE505 are used.
Format: the format of this parameter allows for an IPv4  address in the dotted decimal form.
addCPlaneIpAddressSec.fullName: C-plane Ipv4 address secondary for additional network

addCPlaneIpv4Address.description:
This parameter holds the C-Plane IPv4 address of this  eNB for the additional transport network.
Format: the format of this parameter allows for an IPv4  address in the dotted decimal form.

addCPlaneIpv6Address.description:
This parameter holds the C-Plane IPv6 address of this  eNB for the additional transport network.
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.

addCPlaneIpv6AddressSec.description:
This parameter holds the secondary C-Plane IPv6 address of this  eNB for the additional transport network in case feature LTE648 and LTE505 are used.
Format: parameter acc. to RFC4291.
addCPlaneIpv6AddressSec.fullName: C-plane Ipv6 address secondary for additional network

addUPlaneIpv4Address.description:
This parameter holds the U-Plane IPv4 address of this  eNB for the additional transport network.
Format: the format of this parameter allows for an IPv4  address in the dotted decimal form.

addUPlaneIpv6Address.description:
This parameter holds the U-Plane IPv6 address of this  eNB for the additional transport network.
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.

addressCacheExpirationTime.description:
This parameter defines the mean time, in seconds, that the  (IPv4 ARP / IPv6 ND) cache entries persist in the cache before flushing.
Note: The configured value is used to initialize an internal timer. A fuzzy logic is used to prevent all entries to time out at the same time so the cache entry will remain in reachable state for: 
- Minimum: 0.5 *configured value 
- Maximum: 1.5 * configured value

bfdHoldUpTime.description: This parameter specifies the delay for re-installig routes as active ones after a BFD session has recovered from down to up state. Defining a delay can prevent from too heavy toggling of de-installing and re-installing routes for unstable BFD sessions.
bfdHoldUpTime.fullName: BFD Hold-Up time delay for re-installing the protection

btsId.description: This parameter identifies the base station in the transport network.

btsSubnetMacAddr.description: This parameter contains the MAC address used towards BTS subnet/LMP/SSE.

cPlaneIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address to be used for control plane traffic. The IP address may collapse with a network interface IP address. If it does not collapse with a network interface IP address, it is considered to be virtual.
The control plane IP address may also collapse with the uPlaneIpAddress, the mPlaneIpAddress and the sPlaneIpAddress.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.
The default value is "0.0.0.0" which means this parameter is not configured.

cPlaneIpAddressSec.description:
This parameter specifies the secondary IPv4 address to be used for control plane traffic in case feature LTE648 is used. 
To be entered in dotted decimal format.
The default value is "0.0.0.0" which means this parameter is not configured.

cPlaneIpv6Address.description:
This parameter holds the C-Plane IPv6 address of this  eNB.
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.
The default value is "::" which means this parameter is not configured.

cPlaneIpv6AddressSec.description:
This parameter specifies the secondary IPv6 address to be used for control plane traffic in case feature LTE648 is used. 
Format: parameter acc. to RFC4291.

enableSoam.description:
Enable/disable service OAM.

NOTE: Ethernet service OAM enabling flag cannot get value true in ATM Iub transport mode.

ftmBtsSubnetAddress.description:
This is the IP address for the BTS subnet. 

If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC 2460.

ftmBtsSubnetPrefixLength.description:
This is the prefix length for the BTS subnet.

Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-31
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-126
ftmBtsSubnetPrefixLength.fullName: Prefix length for the BTS subnet

icmpDscp.description: This parameter defines the DSCP value assigned to the ICMP traffic.

icmpResponseEnabled.description: This parameter defines if the BTS shall respond to the ICMP and traceroute requests. The value "true" means the response is enabled, while the value "false" means the response is disabled.

icmpv6RouterMessageResponseEnabled.description: Likely a true/false switch that enables or disables a behavior related to "icmpv 6 Router Message Response Enabled" on the IPNO object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

ipNoId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IP node object. It uniquely identifies the object.

ipNodeId.description:
This parameter identifies the BTS transport IP node configuration. 
The value is always 1.

ipReassemblyTimeout.description: This parameter defines the maximum period, in milliseconds, allowed until all packets of an IP fragment have to be received. If fragments are received later than this, the packet will be dropped.

mPlaneIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address to be used for management plane traffic. The IP address may collapse with a network interface IP address. If it does not collapse with a network interface IP address, it is considered to be virtual.
The management plane IP address may also collapse with the uPlaneIpAddress, the sPlaneIpAddress and the cPlaneIpAddress.

If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC4291.

mainTransportNwId.description: This parameter selects the transport network which shall be used as main transport network.

ndMldDscp.description: This parameter defines the DSCP value assigned to ICMPv6 Neighbour Discovery (ND) and Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) messages.

oamIpAddr.description:
This parameter holds the transport network IP address of the O&M system for the FTM. To be entered in dotted decimal format.

If only 1 OMS IP is configured, then a manual BTS reset after change of the IP address is needed so that BTS will take into use the new values.

If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.


Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC4291.
oamIpAddr.fullName: Transport network IP address of the O&M system

oamTlvReply.description:
If this parameter is set to "true",  the optional TLV received in  a Link Trace or Loopback message (LTM or LBM message) is sent back unchecked in the corresponding reply message (LTR, or LBR).
If this parameter is set to "false", the received optional TLV is ignored and not being sent in the reply-message.
NOTE: By default, the parameter is set to 'false'

omsTls.description:
This parameter specifies the usage of TLS between the eNB and the OPS system.
The usage of TLS requires that valid certificates are installed to the eNB.
omsTls.fullName: TLS usage towards the OPS system

planeMacAddr.description: This parameter contains the MAC address of the interface through which the U/C/M/S Plane is configured.

retransTimer.description: This parameter defines the interval, in milliseconds, between (re-) transmission of the neighbor solicitation messages from the BTS.

sPlaneIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address to be used for synchronization plane traffic. The IP address has to collapse with a network interface IP address. The synchronization plane IP address may collapse with the uPlaneIpAddress, the mPlaneIpAddress and the cPlaneIpAddress.
This parameter supports both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. 

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460. 
Note 1: " ToP feature (TOPF) is not supported for TDD release and only 0.0.0.0 address can be configured to S-plane IP address"
Note 2: Validation doesnot prevent from configuring virtual IP addresses.

secOmsIpAddr.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address of the OMS serving in secondary role. It is used for OMS resiliency.

If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC4291.

servingOms.description: This parameter shows  which OMS (primary or secondary) is the current serving OMS. This is a read-only parameter.

servingOmsAdminSetting.description: This parameter specifies the administrator preference for how the NE should select its serving OMS. Automatic selection (value "automatic") means that the NE autonomously selects its serving OMS based on availability of the configured primary or secondary OMS. The NE may also be administratively assigned/locked to either the configured primary or the configured secondary OMS (values "primaryForced" and "secondaryForced").

servingOmsSwoRequest.description: This parameter requests an administrative switch-over from current serving OMS (primary or secondary) to the other OMS. The parameter value specifies the OMS to which the switch-over is requested.

srcIpForCmpCrl.description:
This parameter represents the IPv4 or IPv6 address that eNB uses as source IP address in all communications with CMP/CRL servers.
If this parameter is left empty, eNB uses M-plane address to communicate with CMP/CRL servers.
If feature LTE955 is activated for private backhaul, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.
If public backhaul is enabled, an address of either IPv4 or IPv6 may be provided.
The srcIPForCmpCrl IP Version, if populated, must match the cmpServerIpAddress IP Version.
srcIpForCmpCrl.fullName: Source IP address used for CMP/CRL Servers

tls11Enabled.description: This parameter specifies whether TLS1.1 is supported  between the BTS and other systems

tls12Enabled.description: Enables TLS protocol version 1.2 for securing management-plane (O&M) network connections.

tlsRenegotiationInterval.description:
This parameter defines the time interval in seconds to trigger secure renegotiation of a TLS session, used in management connections, according to RFC 5746. If the parameter is set to non-zero, BTS triggers secure renegotiation on a TLS session if the session allows secure renegotiation and the session has been alive for a period defined by this timer after initial setup or last renegotiation, whichever occurs most recently. If the parameter is set to zero, BTS does not trigger time-based secure renegotiation.

Note: this parameter can only be set to 0, or between 300 and 86400.

transportNwId.description: This parameter holds the identifier for the additional transport network  in case "Transport Separation for RAN sharing"  feature is supported.

twampIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address to be used for the application or IP interface object. Each address specified in this structure for TWAMP usage must be identical with one of the configured eNB application or interface IP addresses.
Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals or IPv6 address parameter according to RFC 4291.
twampIpAddress.fullName: TWAMP application or IP interface address

twampMessageRate.description:
This parameter specifies the overall rate at which the BTS sends TWAMP initiator messages. The messages are evenly spread over the enabled TWAMP sessions at any given time.
NOTE: By default, the parameter is set to 'RATE_10'
twampMessageRate.fullName: TWAMP initiator rate for sending messages

twampReflFlag.description: This flag enables/disables the TWAMP reflector functionality for the application or IP interface object.

twampReflectorPort.description:
This parameter specifies the source port that is assigned to the TWAMP reflector. The sender on any measurement request packet shall use that port to reach the TWAMP reflector. 

Note: UDP ports 7 (standard UDP echo port) and port range 5001..5010 (UDP ports of TWAMP sender) shall not be used for UDP reflector port.

Note: When configuring TWAMP reflector service, it is important to configure a UDP port that is not in use by any other service (such as 500 for IKE/IPsec for example). Otherwise both TWAMP and the conflicting service will be impacted and not work as expected. As many of the ports 1..1023 are typically in use for various services, it is recommended to select a port starting from 1024 (in most of the cases the default setting should be appropriate).

uPlane2IpAddress.description: This parameter specifies the secondary U-Plane IPv4 Address.

uPlane2Ipv6Address.description: This parameter specifies the secondary U-Plane IPv6 Address.

uPlaneIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the IP address to be used for user plane traffic. The IP address may collapse with a network interface IP address. If it does not collapse with a network interface IP address, it is considered to be virtual.
The user plane IP address may also collapse with the mPlaneIpAddress, the sPlaneIpAddress and the cPlaneIpAddress.
To be entered in dotted decimal format.

uPlaneIpv6Address.description:
This parameter holds the U-Plane IPv6 address of this  eNB.
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.

udpEchoFlag.description: This flag enables/disables the UDP echo functionality for the application or IP interface object.

wfqSchedOamWeight.description: This parameter defined the weight value to be used in the WFQ aggregation scheduler for Service OAM messages.
wfqSchedOamWeight.fullName: WFQ aggregator queue weight for Service OAM messages

iprmId.description:
This parameter identifies the unique instance of class IPRM. The value is always 1.

Note:This is not applicable for FlexiZone Micro hardware.

sourceTwoDiscr.description:
With this parameter, the user can select the way how to define source two.
The possible values are: 
SINGLE: a single IP address
RANGE: a range of IP addresses given by an IP address and a subnet mask
WILDCARD: any IP adress is allowed

sourceTwoIpAddr.description:
This parameter is only meaningful if parameter sourceTwoDiscr has value SINGLE or RANGE.

If sourceTwoDisc has value SINGLE, this parameter specifies the only IP address from / towards which traffic is allowed.
If sourceTwoDisc has value RANGE, this parameter specifies the upper limit of a range of IP addresses from / towards which traffic is allowed.

If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

Format: IPv4 IP address in dotted decimal or IPv6 address acc to RFC4291.

sourceTwoPrefixLength.description:
This parameter is meaningful  only if source two is defined as RANGE; in all other cases it is ignored.
"SourceTwoPrefixLength" specifies a prefix length which, when applied to "IP address for source two", yields the allowed range of IP addresses for source two.
 
If feature LTE955 is activated, the operator must provide an IPv6 address, otherwise the operator must provide an IPv4 address.

Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-31
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-127
sourceTwoPrefixLength.fullName: Prefix length for source two IP address

userLabel.description:
An alphanumeric string assigned by the user to identify the Restricted Mode exception.
NOTE: This parameter is mandatory for exception and must be unique

bfdId.description:
This parameter identifies the Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) session that shall protect this route. The parameter value shall match one of the object instance identifiers of the BFD managed object class.
Value 0 means the route is not protected by any BFD session.

destIpAddr.description: This parameter defines the IP address for indirectly connected IP nodes (remote network). If a default gateway shall be defined, its value is to be set to 0.0.0.0.
destIpAddr.fullName: Destination IP address of the route

destinationIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter defines the destination's prefix length. The prefix length for IPv4 is 0..32.
This parameter along with destIpAddr defines an IPv4 subnet.

gateway.description: This parameter defines the IP address of the next hop through which the route destination IP address can be reached.
gateway.fullName: IP address of the next hop of the route

ipRoutingTableId.description:
This parameter identifies the IP routing table. 

Note 1: The maximum number of routing tables  is 1 for FSMr2 and 33  for FSMr3 and FlexiZone Micro.
ipRoutingTableId.fullName: Identifier of the IP routing table

ipRtId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IPv4 routing table object. It uniquely identifies the object.
It must be ensured that one instance is defined with the identifier set to "1".

netmask.description: Specifies the mask of the remote network. To be entered in dotted decimal format.

preSrcIpv4Addr.description:
This parameter defines the corresponding primary- or secondary- source IP address of SCTP related applications.
An example for such an application is SCTP multihoming for C-Plane.

preference.description: This parameter defines a cost value for this route. The lower preference value means lower cost. The BTS will use preference routes with a lower preference value.

routeIpMtu.description:
This parameter defines the IP MTU that applies towards the destination subnet of the route.
In case of IPSec tunneling enabled, this parameter is the length of the ciphered packet (including IPsec overhead) before the fragmentation process.
Fragmentation with IPsec can be selected between pre-frag and post-frag algorithm. 
See parameter description for ipFragmentationAlgorithm.

1. If routeIpMtu is not configured, the interface MTU is valid for this route entry. 
2. If routeIpMtu is configured the given value is applied for this route entry.

triggerDN.description:
This parameter defines the trigger that shall protect this route. The parameter value shall match one of the object instance identifiers of the Trigger managed object class. An empty value means the route is not protected by any Trigger. An actionTrigger state of TRUE will activate this route, otherwise, this route will be not applied.
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/TRIGGER-1

If the triggerDN is set other than value "" (empty value), the read only parameter actFastIpRerouting is "TRUE".
If the triggerDN has no value set (empty value) for all static routes, the read only parameter actFastIpRerouting is "FALSE".

userLabel.description: This parameter defines the label that can be used for a usage description of the IP routing table.

bfdId.description:
This parameter identifies the Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) session that shall protect this route. The parameter value shall match one of the object instance identifiers of the BFD managed object class.
Value 0 means the route is not protected by any BFD session.

destIpv6Addr.description:
This parameter defines the destination IPv6 address of the static route.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.
destIpv6Addr.fullName: Destination IPv6 address of the static route

destinationIpv6PrefixLength.description: This parameter defines the IPv6 prefix-length parameter of the destination IPv6 address. The format of this parameter is according to RFC4291.

gatewayIpv6Addr.description:
This parameter defines  the IPv6 address of the next IP hop through which a remote network can be reached.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

ipRtV6Id.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IPv6 routing table object. It uniquely identifies the object.
It must be ensured that one instance is defined with the identifier set to "1".

ipv6RoutingTableId.description:
This parameter identifies the IPv6 routing table. 

Note 1: The maximum number of routing tables  is  33  for FSMr3 and FlexiZone Micro.
ipv6RoutingTableId.fullName: Identifier Of The IPv6 Routing Table

preSrcIpv6Addr.description:
This parameter defines the preferred primary- or secondary- source IP address of SCTP related applications.
An example for such an application is SCTP multihoming for C-Plane.

IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

preference.description: This parameter defines a cost value for this route. The lower preference value means lower cost. The BTS will use preference routes with lower preference value.

routeIpMtu.description:
This parameter defines the IP MTU that applies towards the destination subnet of the route.
In case of IPSec tunneling enabled, this parameter is the length of the ciphered packet (including IPsec overhead) before the fragmentation process.
Fragmentation with IPsec can be selected between pre-frag and post-frag algorithm. 
See parameter description for ipFragmentationAlgorithm.

1. If routeIpMtu is not configured, the interface MTU is valid for this route entry. 
2. If routeIpMtu is configured the given value is applied for this route entry.

triggerDN.description:
This parameter defines the trigger that shall protect this route. The parameter value shall match one of the object instance identifiers of the Trigger managed object class. An empty value means the route is not protected. An actionTrigger state of TRUE will activate this route, otherwise, this route will be not applied.
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-TRIGGER-1

If the triggerDN is set other than value "" (empty value), the read only parameter actFastIpRerouting is "TRUE".
If the triggerDN has no value set (empty value) for all static routes, the read only parameter actFastIpRerouting is "FALSE".

userLabel.description: This parameter defines the label that can be used for a usage description of the IPv6 routing table.

destIpv6Addr.description: This parameter displays the IPv6 address for indirectly connected IP nodes (remote network) or the destination IP address of a route.
destIpv6Addr.fullName: Destination IPv6 address of the route

destinationIpv6PrefixLength.description:
This is the IPv6 prefix-length parameter of the destination IPv6 address.
Format: parameter acc. to RFC4291.

gatewayIpv6Addr.description:
This parameter displays the IPv6 address of the next IP hop via which a remote network can be reached.
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.

ipIfDN.description:
This parameter refers to the IP interface for this route. It is available for static direct routes only.

The value is an a distinguished name (DN).
Example:
MRBTS-1//TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-1

ipRtV6RId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only IPv6 routing table object. It uniquely identifies the object.
ipRtV6RId.fullName: Read only IPv6 routing table identifier

preSrcIpv6Addr.description:
This parameter defines the preferred source IP address for the route.
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.
Default Value is "::" which means the parameter is not used: a preferred source IPV6 address is not defined

preference.description: This parameter shows the cost value for this route. Lower preference value means lower cost.

routeIpMtu.description:
This parameter indicates the IP mtu that applies towards the destination subnet of the route.
NOTE: In case if IPSEC, this parameter is the length of raw IP packet i.e before IPSEC processing [Cleartext Fragmentation Limit (CFL)]

routeType.description:
This parameter displays the type of the route, It can have below values  
1) direct, meaning the route destination belongs to one of the NE directly connected subnets.
2) indirect, meaning the route destination does not belong to one of the NE directly connected subnets.

triggerDN.description:
This parameter indicates the trigger that is being used to protect this route. 
Empty value means the route is not protected.

destIpAddr.description:
This parameter together with netmask displays the destination IPv4 subnet of a forwarding entry.
The parameter has dotted decimal format.

destinationIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter together with destIpAddr displays the destination IP subnet of a forwarding entry.
The parameter has dotted decimal format.

gateway.description:
This parameter displays the IP address of the next hop via which the route destination IP address can be reached. This is available only in indirect routes.
The parameter has dotted decimal format.

ipIfDN.description:
This parameter refers to the IP interface for this route. It is available for static direct routes only.

The value is an a distinguished name (DN).
Example:
MRBTS-1//TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-1

actIpSecBkupTun.description: This flag indicates whether the optional feature IPsec backup tunnel is in use or not.

antiReplayEnabled.description: If this flag is true,anti replay checking for the IPsec connections of this policy is enabled, else it is switched off.

antiReplayWindowSize.description:
This is the size of the anti replay window to be used on the security policy.

The value range for FlexiZone Micro : 0:SIZE_64;1:SIZE_128 with default value as 1. FZM supports only 30 protect policies.
The value range for FSMr3 and AirScale: 0:SIZE_64;1:SIZE_128;2:SIZE_256 with default value as 2.
antiReplayWindowSize.fullName: Size of the anti replay window

authenticationMethod.description:
This parameter holds the ESP authentication algorithm to be applied to the traffic data packet for which the policy matches.
Values 1-9 are valid for macro eNodeB;
Values 1-2,5-9 are valid for FZM (with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later)
Default value is 1 (AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96).

authenticationScheme.description:
This parameter defines the authentication scheme.
It can be either preshared key (PSK) or certificate.

connectionEstablishmentMode.description:
This parameter defines if the base station shall actively initiate a connection to the peer or if the base station should wait for the peer to establish the connection.
Default value is 0 (INITIATOR_AND_RESPONDER).

dnsSrcIpSelection.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "dns source IP Selection" on the IPSECC object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

dpdOptimisationEnabled.description: Likely a true/false switch that enables or disables a behavior related to "dpd Optimisation Enabled" on the IPSECC object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

dpddelay.description:
This parameter specifies the delay between the sending of two consecutive DPS INFORMATIONAL messages by the BTS. The INFORMATIONAL message indicates the BTS is still alive.
For IKEv2, the BTS raises the Dead Peer Detected (DPD) alarm if the remote peer has not sent any INFORMATIONAL message to the BTS after the BTS has sent a fixed number of INFORMATIONAL messages. 
For IKEv1 the BTS raises the DPD alarm, if the remote peer has not sent back any INFORMATIONAL messages after the time defined in the parameter dpdtimeout has expired.

dpdtimeout.description:
This parameter specifies the time after which the BTS raises the Dead Peer Detected (DPD) alarm.
The parameter dpddelay specifies the delay between the sending of two consecutive DPS INFORMATIONAL messages by the BTS. The INFORMATIONAL message indicates that the BTS is still alive.
For IKEv1, the BTS raises the Dead Peer Detected (DPD) alarm if the remote peer has not sent back any INFORMATIONAL messages after the time defined in the parameter dpdtimeout has expired.
This parameter does not apply to Macro eNB or to FZM (with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later).
Default value is 120 seconds.

encryptionMethod.description:
This parameter holds the ESP encryption algorithm to be applied to the traffic data packet for which the policy matches.
Values 0, 1, 2, 3 are valid for FZM (without LTE739 i.e. before 17A); values 0, 1,2, 4-9 inclusive are valid for Macro eNB, and for FZM(with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later).
Default Value: 1 for Macro eNB; 3 for FZM

1: ENC_AES_128_CBC

3: ENC_AES_128_CBC_OR_3DES_192_CBC

6: ENC_AES_GCM_ICV16_128 
7: ENC_AES_GCM_ICV16_256 
8: ENC_AES_GMAC_128 
9: ENC_AES_GMAC_256

extendedSequenceNumberMode.description:
This parameter defines whether to support the normal sequence number (32 bit) or extended sequence number (64 bit).
Default value is 0 (NORMAL_SEQUENCE).

ikeAuthenticationMethod.description:
This parameter holds the authentication algorithm at the IKE layer to be applied to the traffic data packet for which the policy matches.
Values 1-7 are valid for Macro eNB;
Values 1-2,5-7 are valid for FZM (with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later)
Default value is 1 (AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96).
