ikeConfigRequest.description:
This parameter determines if the BTS shall request an internal IP address as part of IKEv2 Configuration Payload. 
If the parameter is set to "NO", then BTS shall not send CFG_REQUEST during IKE_AUTH exchange. 
If the parameter is set to "NON_ZERO_IP", then BTS shall send CFG_REQUEST during IKE_AUTH exchange and shall suggest a non-zero IP address. 
If the parameter is set to "ZERO_IP", then BTS shall send CFG_REQUEST during IKE_AUTH exchange but shall not suggest an IP address.

By default, the BTS shall not request for an internal IP address as part of IKEv2 configuration payload.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.

ikeDiffHellGrp.description:
This parameter selects the DH group to be used in the establishment and rekeying of IKE SAs.
Value 0, 1 are applicable for FZM (without LTE739 i.e. before 17A); value 0, 1, 2, 3 are applicable for Macro eNB, and for FZM(with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later).

ikeDscp.description: This parameter defines the DSCP value assigned to the IKE traffic.

ikeEncryptionMethod.description:
This parameter holds the encryption algorithm at the IKE layer to be applied to the traffic data packet for which the policy matches.
Values 1, 2, 3 are valid for FZM (without LTE739 i.e. before 17A); Value 1,2,4,5,6,7 are valid for Macro eNB, and for FZM(with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later)
Default value: 1 for Macro eNB and for FZM (with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later);
3 for FZM (without LTE739 i.e. before 17A)
ikeEncryptionMethod.officialRange:
1: ENC_AES_128_CBC 
2: ENC_3DES_192_CBC 
3: ENC_AES_128_CBC_OR_3DES_192_CBC 
4: ENC_AES_192_CBC 
5: ENC_AES_256_CBC 
6: ENC_AES_GCM_ICV16_128 
7: ENC_AES_GCM_ICV16_256

ikeIdentityIndex.description:
This parameter defines local IKE identity attribute for the IPSec tunnel. ikeIdentity shall be unique among all protect policies. If Flexi Zone Dynamic IP Assignment feature is deactivated or IPSec status is not Protect, parameter is ignored.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only and empty value is set by default.
ikeIdentityIndex.officialRange:
1: MainId 
2: Id1 
3: Id2 
4: Id3 
5: Id4 
6: Id5 
7: Id6 
8: Id7 
9: Id8

ikeMaxLifeTime.description:
This parameter defines the maximum duration, in seconds, in the life time of the IKE security associations. Before the timer expires for a security association, a new security association is negotiated.
Default value is 86400 seconds.

ikeProtocol.description:
This parameter holds the IKE protocol version of this association used for this policy.
This parameter does not apply to Macro eNB.
Default value is 1 (IKE_V2).
This parameter does not apply to Macro eNB or to FZM(with LTE739 i.e. 17A and later.

ipFragmentationAlgorithm.description:
This parameter defines whether the IP fragmentation shall take place before or after ESP encapsulation.

The supported values are :
Pre-fragmentation  - The IP fragmentation takes place before ESP encapsulation.
Post-fragmentation - The IP fragmentation takes place after ESP encapsulation.

NOTE: The reconfiguration of the IP fragmentation algorithm will cause an interruption of all IPsec traffic.
ipFragmentationAlgorithm.fullName: IP fragmentation algorithm selection for IPsec Tunnels

ipSecBkupRemoteTEPFQDN.description:
This parameter defines the FQDN for remote SEG endpoint of the secondary IPsec tunnel.
It is ignored when corresponding IP address parameter (remoteTEP) is set to non-default value.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
The default value is empty string.
ipSecBkupRemoteTEPFQDN.fullName: FQDN for IPsec Backup Tunnel remote endpoint

ipSecBkupTunCurrRemoteEndpoint.description:
This parameter holds the remote endpoint IPv4 or IPv6 IP Address of the current active IPsec tunnel.
Format:
For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.
ipSecBkupTunCurrRemoteEndpoint.fullName: IPSec Backup Tunnel current remote endpoint

ipSecBkupTunMaxSwitchTime.description: This parameter specifies maximum time delay before switchover or switchback of IPSec tunnel. NE will use random delay between minimum and maximum delay timers for switchover or switchback
ipSecBkupTunMaxSwitchTime.fullName: IPSec Backup Tunnel maximum switch time

ipSecBkupTunMinSwitchTime.description: This parameter specifies minimum time delay before switchover or switchback of IPSec tunnel. NE will use random delay between minimum and maximum delay timers for switchover or switchback
ipSecBkupTunMinSwitchTime.fullName: IPSec Backup Tunnel minimum switch time

ipSecBkupTunRemoteEndpoint.description:
This parameter holds the remote SEG endpoint IPv4 or IPv6 IP Address of the secondary IPsec tunnel.
It also enables backup tunnel feature for the primary tunnel associated with this policy.

Format:

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

ipSecBkupTunRemoteTEPCurrIp.description:
This parameter holds translated IP address from FQDN for remote SEG endpoint of the secondary IPsec tunnel. It is set only when corresponding FQDN parameter has been set.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
ipSecBkupTunRemoteTEPCurrIp.fullName: FQDN for IPsec Backup Tunnel remote endpoint

ipSecBkupTunState.description:
This parameter indicates the state of the IPsec Backup Tunnel.

Note: The value is valid only when parameter ipSecBkupTunCurrRemoteEndpoint is set (other than 0.0.0.0)

ipSecBkupTunSwitchbackMode.description: This parameter indicates whether BTS should automatically or manually (operator command) switchback to primary IPSec Tunnel

ipSecEmBypassCtrlIpAddr.description:
This parameter defines the IP address of the IPsec emergency bypass control server.
IPv4 address format: Dot-decimal notation (x.x.x.x). 
Example: 10.10.10.10.

IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. 
Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA.
ipSecEmBypassCtrlIpAddr.fullName: IPsec emergency bypass control server IP address

ipSecEmBypassEnabled.description: This parameter is used for enabling/disabling IPsec emergency bypass

ipSecEmBypassExit.description: This is action parameter to exit the active IPsec emergency bypass request state.
ipSecEmBypassExit.fullName: IPsec emergency bypass exit active state request

ipSecEmBypassPingTimer.description: This parameter defines the timer value in seconds for the ping request towards the IPsec emergency bypass control server in "Probing" state in order to allow entering "Active" state.

ipSecEmBypassState.description: This parameter indicates IPsec emergency bypass status

ipSecEnabled.description:
This parameter switches the IPsec globally on (value is "true") or off (value is "false").

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).

ipSecStatus.description:
This flag rules the basic treatment of a traffic data packet that applies to the selection criteria of this policy.
The values have the following meaning:
"DISCARD": the packet is discarded without any further action or notification, i.e. it is prevented from passing to its designated destination.
"BYPASS": the packet is delivered to its destination without any other processing, in particular without any further IPsec-related processing.
"PROTECT": the packet will be made subject to the settings of its security policy.

ipSeccId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IPSEC object. It uniquely identifies the object.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).

ipsecPerfForwSecEnabled.description:
This parameter enables the use of the Perfect Forward Secrecy when establishing and rekeying IPsec SAs.
Default is 0 (false).

localIpAddress.description:
This parameter holds the local IP address of the data traffic packet for this policy as seen by the FTM.

To be entered in dotted decimal format.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers and protocol are feasible:
- a single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- a single IP address, selected protocol/port
- an IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- an IP subnet, selected protocol/port.

Parameter value 0.0.0.0 means ""wildcard"" - all IP addresses are allowed.
Both IP address formats can be used.
Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals or IPv6 address parameter acc. to RFC 4291.
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM units only.

localIpPort.description:
This is the port number of the local IP address. If value -1 is configured, the IPSec policy is valid in the same way to and from all ports of the local IP address.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM units only.
localIpPort.fullName: Port number of the local IP address

localIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter specifies the length netmask to the parameter localIpPrefixLength.
Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-32
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-128
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM units only.

localTEP.description:
This parameter is the local tunnel endpoint IPv4 or IPv6 IP Address of the IPsec Tunnel(IKESA) whose related policies have  secondary remote tunnel endpoint set to a valid non-default IP Address and IPsec backup tunnel feature is enabled. 

Format:
For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

localTunnelEndpoint.description:
This parameter defines the local endpoint IPv4 or IPv6 address of the IPsec tunnel.
Format:

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.
localTunnelEndpoint.fullName: Local IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

localTunnelEndpointV4.description:
This parameter defines the local IPv4 tunnel endpoint of X2 IPSec tunnel.
Format:
The parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format and the default value is 0.0.0.0
Note: This parameter is valid for macro BTS only.
localTunnelEndpointV4.fullName: Local IPv4 X2 IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

localTunnelEndpointV6.description:
This parameter defines the local IPv6 tunnel endpoint of X2 IPSec tunnel.
Format:
The parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.
The default value is ::
Note: This parameter is valid for macro BTS only.
localTunnelEndpointV6.fullName: Local IPv6 X2 IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

mPlaneIpDynCfg.description:
This parameter defines which IPsec tunnel is used (based on assigned identity) for setting inner IP address for this plane. If DHCP is chosen, then IP address assigned by DHCP will be used for this application IP and this traffic will not be IPsec protected.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only and empty value is set by default.
mPlaneIpDynCfg.fullName: Dynamic configuration of management plane IP address

peerIkeIdVerificationMode.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "peer Ike Id Verification Mode" on the IPSECC object. peerIkeIdentity.description:
This parameter defines accepted peer IKE identity in FQDN format. It is ignored when LTE3978 (actMultipleDynamicIP) is disabled.

Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
Default value is empty string.

pfsDiffHellGrp.description:
This parameter selects the DH group to be used when the PFS is enabled during the establishment and rekeying of IPsec SA's.
Default value is 2 (DH14).

policyNumber.description:
This is the order number of the security policy. 
Only the lowest number of several equally matching policies is executed on a specific traffic data packet.

protocol.description:
This parameter holds the protocol information of the IP packet according to RFC791 (IPv4) or RFC1883 (IPv6).
If the parameter has value -1, the policy is valid for all protocols.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM units only.

relatedTrafficSelectorId.description:
This parameter identifies the list of comma seperated traffic selector list identifier(s) related to security policy. 
Note 1: Maximum 17 comma seperated entries should be allowed. For e.g. 1,2,500.
Note 2: This parameter is valid for macro BTS only.
relatedTrafficSelectorId.fullName: List of comma seperated IPsec policy traffic selector list identifiers

remoteIpAddress.description:
This parameter holds the remote IP address of the data traffic packet for this policy as seen by the FTM.

To be entered in dotted decimal format.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.

Parameter value 0.0.0.0 means "wildcard" - all IP addresses are allowed.
Both IP address formats can be used.
Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals or IPv6 address parameter acc. to RFC 4291.
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM units only.

remoteIpPort.description:
This is the port number of the remote IP address. If value -1 is configured, the IPSec policy is valid in the same way to and from all ports of the remote IP address.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM units only.
remoteIpPort.fullName: Port of the remote IP address

remoteIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter specifies the length netmask to the parameter remoteIpPrefixLength.
Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-32
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-128
Note: This parameter is applicable for FZM units only.

remoteTEP.description:
This parameter is the remote tunnel endpoint IPv4 or IPv6 IP Address of the IPsec Tunnel(IKESA) whose related policies have  secondary remote tunnel endpoint set to a valid non-default IP Address and IPsec backup tunnel feature is enabled.

Format:
For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

remoteTEPFQDN.description:
This parameter is the FQDN for remote tunnel endpoint in of the IPsec Tunnel(IKESA) whose related policies have secondary remote tunnel endpoint set to a valid non-default IP Address and IPsec backup tunnel feature is enabled.
It is ignored when corresponding IP address parameter (remoteTEP) is set to non-default value.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
The default value is empty string.
remoteTEPFQDN.fullName: FQDN for IPsec Tunnel remote tunnel endpoint

remoteTunnelEndpoint.description:
This parameter holds the remote endpoint IP Address (IPv4 or IPv6) of the IPsec tunnel as seen by the FTM.

Format:
For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.
remoteTunnelEndpoint.fullName: Remote IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

remoteTunnelEndpointCurrIp.description:
This parameter holds translated IP address from FQDN for remote endpoint of the IPsec tunnel as seen by the FTM. It is set only when corresponding FQDN parameter has been set.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
remoteTunnelEndpointCurrIp.fullName: FQDN for remote IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

remoteTunnelEndpointFQDN.description:
This parameter holds the FQDN for remote endpoint of the IPsec tunnel as seen by the FTM.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
Default value is empty string.
remoteTunnelEndpointFQDN.fullName: FQDN for remote IPsec tunnel endpoint IP address

sPlaneIpDynCfg.description:
This parameter defines which IPsec tunnel is used (based on assigned identity) for setting inner IP address for this plane. If DHCP is chosen, then IP address assigned by DHCP will be used for this application IP and this traffic will not be IPsec protected.
Note: This parameter is valid for Flexi Zone Micro only.
The default value is 100:DHCP. This value is assigned when whole structure exists.
sPlaneIpDynCfg.fullName: Dynamic configuration of synchronization plane application IP address

saMaxLifeTime.description:
This parameter holds the maximum lifetime of an IPSEC security association. The IPSEC SA will be rekeyed at a random time between 270 and 180 seconds before the maximum lifetime expires, i.e. between (saMaxLifetime – 270 seconds) and (saMaxLifetime – 180 seconds) after establishing the IPSEC SA.

Note:
IKE SAs with a fixed maximum lifetime of 86400 seconds (24 hours) will be rekeyed at a random time between 3870 and 180 seconds before the maximum lifetime expires, i.e. between 82530 and 86220 seconds after establishing the IKE SA

It indicates the range of packet sequence numbers which are tracked back by decryptor (receiving side) to provide anti-replay protection. Actual (instantaneous) range spans to highest received sequence number (X) from highest received sequence number minus window size (X-N+1). Any packet with the sequence number X-N or below is discarded.

ipSecpId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the IPsec profile object. It uniquely identifies the object.
It is highly recommended to use for object creation the lowest free ipSecpId value within all IPSECP instances of the BTS.
This will ensure that there will be no conflicts between manually configured IPSECP instances and autonomously created IPSECP instances by the BTS.
If enabled, the BTS can support the autonomous creation of IPSECP instances. For this the BTS will always use the highest free ipSecpId value.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).

Therefore, the value has to be lower than the corresponding value configured at the remote end.

dpdDelay.description: This parameter defines the time delay after which the first empty INFORMATIONAL message is sent to the peer if no IKE messages are received in order to check if the peer is still alive (Dead Peer Detection). After that, further INFORMATIONAL messages are sent with increasing intervals (4, 7, 13, 24 and 42 seconds) so that six INFORMATIONAL messages are sent in one repetition cycle. After the sixth INFORMATIONAL message and 75 seconds waiting time the cycle starts again with dpddelay timer restart. The BTS raises the Dead Peer Detected (DPD) alarm after the fourth INFORMATIONAL message is sent in the cycle (dpddelay timer + (4 + 7 + 13) seconds). The dpddelay timer and thus the repetition cycle is restarted if an IKE message is received.

idleLBEutCelResWeight.description:

When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in selecting main target for IdleModeMobilityControlInfo for load balancing. Weighted round robin algorithm shall select always one target frequency for idle mode load balancing, which is matching UE capabilities, to be used as main target for idle mode load balancing and this target will have always highest  priority assigned in RRC Release message.  All other target frequency for idle mode load balancing matching UE capabilities and configured in LNCEL, IRFIM, UFFIM, CDFIM and GNFL will be added as well, but with lowered priorities as configured for SIB with kept hierarchy of priorities.  The algorithm shall calculate proportional weights corresponding to configured values. There is no check about the sum of weights configured by the user.

mbmsNeighCellConfigInterF.description:
Provides information related to MBSFN configuration of neighbour cells of a non-serving frequency.
00: Not all neighbour cells of this frequency have the same MBSFN subframe allocation
01: No MBSFN subframes are present in all neighbour cells of this frequency
10: The MBSFN subframe allocations of all neighbour cells are identical to or subsets of this frequency
11: Different UL/DL allocation in neighbouring cells for TDD of this frequency.

Notes:
- Value 11 is not valid for FDD cells
- For TDD cells, 00, 10 and 01 are only used for same UL/DL allocation in neighbouring cells of this frequency.

measBdw.description:

carrier frequency. The values mbw6, mbw15, mbw25, mbw50, mbw75, mbw100 indicate 6, 15, 25, 50, 75 and 100 resource blocks respectively.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.
value.fullName: Inter frequency Idle Mode parameters spare

irSaiListId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC IRSAILIST.
It uniquely identifies a IRSAILIST instance.
irSaiListId.fullName: Inter frequency MBMS SAI  list (IRSAILIST) identifier

saiListEarfcnDl.description: Downlink carrier frequency the inter-frequency SAI list applies to
saiListEarfcnDl.fullName: Downlink earfcn of the MBMS service area identity list

saiListInterFreqNeighbors.description: List of MBMS service area identities (SAI) for inter-frequency neighbor cells
saiListInterFreqNeighbors.fullName: SAI list of inter-frequency neighbor cells

irSaiListSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC IRSAILISTSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an IRSAILISTSPARE instance.

name.description:
This is the name of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The content is filled by the BTS and cannot be changed.

The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

value.description:
This is the value of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The allowed parameter values are defined in the feature specification.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.

actFastIncreaseGbr.description: Activates the fast increase mechanisms of amount of preferred resources for new GBR bearer arriving into the system.
actFastIncreaseGbr.fullName: Activation of fast pref. resource inc. mech. for GBR

actFastIncreaseNonGbr.description: Activates the fast increase mechanisms of amount of preferred resources for new non-GBR bearer arriving into the system.
actFastIncreaseNonGbr.fullName: Act. of fast pref. resource inc. mech. for non-GBR

activationThreshold.description: Defines a fraction of the resources being available for UE scheduling on PDSCH. If average PDSCH utilization falls below this threshold, interference shaping functionality is applied.

blankingPosition.description:
Determines at which frequency edge the blanked resources should be allocated in a macro cell. A micro cell will use always the opposite edge.

Note: Used only for preferred alignment 'macro-micro'
blankingPosition.fullName: Freq. edge for blanked resources in macro cell

ishPrId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC ISHPR and it uniquely identifies an instance of the Downlink Interference Shaping Profile (ISHPR).

If the feature "Downlink Interference Shaping" is activated, a default ISHPR profile with ISHPR-ishPrId = 0 must exist.

limitHighLoadNeighbor.description: Load limit for considering a neighbor cell as highly loaded
limitHighLoadNeighbor.fullName: High load limit for neighbor cell

nCellsLoadExchange.description:
Determines the maximum amount of neighboring cells from which to request neighbor cell load information internally or via X2 interface for eICIC.

Note: Value '0' deactivates the neighbor cell load information exchange.
nCellsLoadExchange.fullName: Max. num. of cells for neighbor cell load info exch.

nHighLoadNeighbor.description: Minimum number of neighbor cells in high load in order to apply interference shaping.
nHighLoadNeighbor.fullName: Number of highly loaded neighbor cells

periodicityLoadExchange.description: Determines the periodicity with which neighbor cell load information is exchanged.
periodicityLoadExchange.fullName: Periodicity for neighbor cell load info exchange

prefAlignment.description:
Determines the alignment method being applied in DL interference shaping. Available options allow giving preference to alignment of neighbor cell interference by selecting for downlink resources preferred frequency domain area:
- either based on cell PCI number via module operation (pciModBased),
- or based on macro vs. micro cell type (macroMicro).
prefAlignment.fullName: Alignment method for DL interference shaping

prefResDecreaseThreshold.description: Lower utilization threshold of preferred resources. If exceeded downwards, the amount of preferred resource is decreased.
prefResDecreaseThreshold.fullName: Lower threshold to decrease preferred resources

prefResIncreaseThreshold.description: Upper utilization threshold of preferred resources. If exceeded upwards, the amount of preferred resource is increased.
prefResIncreaseThreshold.fullName: Upper threshold to increase preferred resources

prefResLowerLimit.description: Lower limit for preferred resources. Preferred resources are not decreased below this limit.

prefResStepSize.description: Determines the step size for increasing/decreasing the amount of preferred resources.
prefResStepSize.fullName: Step size for adjusting the amount of pref. resources

restartPeriodLoadExchange.description:
Determines a period with which to restart the neighbor cell load information exchange for eICIC.

The exact cells from which to ask neighbor cell load information will be updated only with such a restart.
restartPeriodLoadExchange.fullName: Restart period for neighbor cell load info exchange

updatePeriod.description: Determines the basic periodicity for interference shaping to perform measurements, update preferred resources, etc.
updatePeriod.fullName: Periodicity for interference shaping for update actions

ishPrSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC ISHPRSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an ISHPRSPARE instance.

The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

localIpAddr.description:
This parameter defines the IPv6 address. 
Format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. 
Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

The localIpAddr together with the parameter localIpPrefixLength define an IP subnet.
For virtual IP interfaces a subnet can't be defined.
localIpAddr.fullName: Local IP address of the VLAN interface

localIpv6Addr.description:
This is the IPv6 address of the VLAN Ethernet network interface towards the external transport network. 
Format: parameter with IPv6  address acc. to RFC4291.
localIpv6Addr.fullName: VLAN Ethernet Network Interface IPv6 Address

localIpv6PrefixLength.description:
This is the IPv6 prefix-length parameter of the plain Ethernet network interface towards the external transport network. 
Format: parameter acc. to RFC4291.

Note: Values 1 and 2 are not allowed.
localIpv6PrefixLength.fullName: VLAN Ethernet Network Interface IPv6 Prefix-Length

netmask.description: Specifies the mask of the remote network. To be entered in dotted decimal format.
netmask.fullName: Network mask of the local IP address

qosEnabled.description: This parameter specifies if multiple PHB queues are used over this VLAN interface or only a single one. Multiple PHB queues allow DSCP based traffic prioritisation.

sbs.description:
This parameter defines the shaper burst size at the egress of the particular first level scheduler.
Note : The parameter shapingOverhead automatically applies also to all linked first level schedulers/shapers when enabled and it needs to be considered in all shaping and calculating packet length.

sir.description:
This parameter defines the egress-shaping rate of this particular first level scheduler.
Note : The parameter shapingOverhead automatically applies also to all linked first level schedulers/shapers when enabled and this needs to be considered in all shaping and calculating packet length.

vlanId.description: This parameter defines the VLAN ID to be used at this VLAN interface.

vlanIfNetId.description:
This parameter identifies the VLAN interface object. Value is 1 to 9. Up to 9 VLANs can exist on the BTS.
BTS supports VLAN interfaces with one PHB queue or 6 PHB queues. 
Note: FZM supports only two 6 PHB queues.

The maximum number of VLAN interfaces  supported are as below: 
FSMr3=9, FZM=8.

wfqSchedQueueWeight.description: This is the weight value to be used in the WFQ aggregation scheduler for this interface.

l2PoolDistrReqId.description: Parameter is used for requesting the activation of L2 pool distribution in VNF

l2PoolDistrResId.description: Parameter is used by VNF when replying to the activation request of L2 pool distribution in VNF

l2PoolDistrResult.description: Parameter is used to inform operator about a result of L2 pool distribution in VNF

dscp.description: This parameter specifies a DSCP value.

enableLayer2Switching.description:
This parameter enables the layer 2 switching feature.
If the feature is switched off (false), the Ethernet switching between eNB and backhaul network remains operational, but all other Ethernet ports are inactive. eNBs connected to those ports are effectively disconnected from  the transport network.

For FZM hardware variants with integrated WiFi:
BTS Site Manager shall use enableLayer2Switching = TRUE as default setting for manual commissioning. User is allowed to change the value.

l2PriorityQueueWeight2.description: This parameter specifies the weight for the 1st weighted queue.
l2PriorityQueueWeight2.fullName: Layer 2 switch member weight for queue 2

l2PriorityQueueWeight3.description:
This parameter specifies the weight for the second weighted queue.

The default value of this parameter = 4 for FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
l2PriorityQueueWeight3.fullName: Layer 2 switch member weight for queue 3

l2PriorityQueueWeight4.description: This parameter specifies the weight for the third priority queue.
l2PriorityQueueWeight4.fullName: Layer 2 switch member weight for priority queue 4

l2PriorityQueueWeight5.description:
This parameter specifies the weight for the fourth weighted queue.
This parameter is only supported for the FSMr3 and FlexiZone Micro hardware unit types.
Default value 1 is supported in FSMr3 and FlexiZone Micro unit types.
l2PriorityQueueWeight5.fullName: Layer 2 switch member weight for queue 5

l2PriorityQueueWeight6.description:
This parameter specifies the weight for the fifth weighted queue.
This parameter is only supported for the FSMr3 and FlexiZone Micro hardware unit types.
Default value 1 is supported in  FSMr3 and FlexiZone Micro unit types.
l2PriorityQueueWeight6.fullName: Layer 2 switch member weight for queue 6

l2PriorityQueueWeight7.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "l 2 Priority Queue Weight 7" on the L2SWI object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

l2QoSEnabled.description: This parameter allows to enable/disable QoS awareness for Ethernet switching for all switch-ports.
l2QoSEnabled.fullName: Enable layer 2 QoS awareness per switch-port

l2SwiId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the L2 switch object. It uniquely identifies the object.

l2SwitchingEnabled.description:
This parameter defines whether Layer 2 Ethernet switching between the physical (external) switch-ports is enabled (true) or not.

When disabled (false), still traffic to and from the NE can be received and transmitted at all physical switch-ports, but switching between the physical switch-ports is blocked.
l2SwitchingEnabled.fullName: Enable layer 2 switching between physical ports

l2WeightAF1.description: This parameter defines the scheduler weight of the queue for AF1 traffic class, common for all switch-port schedulers of that switch.
l2WeightAF1.fullName: Switch-port scheduler weight for forwarding class AF1

l2WeightAF2.description: This parameter defines the scheduler weight of the queue for AF2 traffic class, common for all switch-port schedulers of that switch.
l2WeightAF2.fullName: Switch-port scheduler weight for forwarding class AF2

l2WeightAF3.description: This parameter defines the scheduler weight of the queue for AF3 traffic class, common for all switch-port schedulers of that switch.
l2WeightAF3.fullName: Switch-port scheduler weight for forwarding class AF3

l2WeightAF4.description: This parameter defines the scheduler weight of the queue for AF4 traffic class, common for all switch-port schedulers of that switch.
l2WeightAF4.fullName: Switch-port scheduler weight for forwarding class AF4

l2WeightBE.description: This parameter defines the scheduler weight of the queue for BE traffic class, common for all switch-port schedulers of that switch.
l2WeightBE.fullName: Switch-port scheduler weight for forwarding class BE

portDefaultPriority.description:
Default VLAN priority for untagged frames.

Every untagged ingress Ethernet frame at this interface gets assigned this Port Default Priority. If QoS classification mode is configured to VLAN-PCP, this priority is used for enqueing decision of the frame. If the frame egresses the switch tagged, this priority shall be used in the VLAN tag header.

portDefaultVlanId.description:
This parameter defines the VLAN identifier that is associated to untagged and priority-tagged frames received at this Ethernet interface (internal switch-port).

Furthermore this parameter determines, that frames associated to this VLAN identifier which are switched and transmitted at this switch-port will be transmitted untagged.

In order to achieve that a received untagged or priority-tagged frame is switched and transmitted via another (external) switch-port, the same VLAN identifier must be configured at the transmission port:
a) for VLAN-tagged transmission: in the VLAN identifier list of that transmit switch-port (see parameter l2VlanIdList) or
b) for untagged transmission: in the portDefaultVlanID of that transmit switch-port.
Else the frame will be discarded.
portDefaultVlanId.fullName: Default VLAN identifier for layer 2 switching

priorityQueue.description:
This parameter specifies a packet scheduling queue.

FlexiZone Micro hardware unit types:
Packet scheduling queue values range from 1 to 6 where 6 means lowest and 1 means highest priority. The default value of the parameter = 6.

priorityQueueNonClassified.description:
This parameter defines the priority queue for enqueuing of frames not matching the selected classification criteria (see parameter qosClassificationCriteria)

In DSCP classification:
queue for enqueuing all non-IP frames. (e.g. transmitted ARP- , Ethernet OAM- and Synchronous Ethernet messages).

When VLAN awareness for switching is disabled (see parameter 'vlanAwarenessEnabled') this parameter is furthermore used for enqueuing of all untagged 
non-IP frames in VLAN-ID and VLAN-PCP classification mode.
priorityQueueNonClassified.officialRange:
0: EF 
1: AF4 
2: AF3 
3: AF2 
4: AF1 
5: BE

priorityQueueNonIP.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for non-IP frames. Non-IP frames examples are ARP-, Ethernet OAM- and Synchronous Ethernet messages.
The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for the  FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 1 for all hardware unit types, this is the strict priority queue.

priorityQueuePcp0.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 0.

The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for FlexiZone Micro  hardware unit.
The default value of this parameter = 6 for the FlexiZone Micro hardware units, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
priorityQueuePcp0.fullName: L2 queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 0

priorityQueuePcp1.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 1.

The value range of this parameter = 1..4 for the FTIB hardware unit.
The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for the FTLB and FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 4 for the FTIB hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
The default value of this parameter = 4 for the FTLB hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
The default value of this parameter = 5 for the FlexiZone Micro hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
priorityQueuePcp1.fullName: L2 queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 1

priorityQueuePcp2.description: This parameter specifies which priority queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 2.
priorityQueuePcp2.fullName: Priority queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 2

priorityQueuePcp3.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 3.

The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for the FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 4 for FlexiZone Micro hardware units, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
priorityQueuePcp3.fullName: L2 queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 3

priorityQueuePcp4.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 4.

The value range of this parameter = 1..4 for the FTIB hardware unit.
The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for the FTLB and FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 2 for the FTIB hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
The default value of this parameter = 3 for the FTLB and FlexiZone Micro hardware units, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
priorityQueuePcp4.fullName: L2 queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 4

priorityQueuePcp5.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 5.

The value range of this parameter = 1..4 for the FTIB hardware unit.
The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for the FTLB and FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 2 for the FTIB hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
The default value of this parameter = 3 for the FTLB hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
The default value of this parameter = 2 for the FlexiZone Micro hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin queue.
priorityQueuePcp5.fullName: L2 queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 5

priorityQueuePcp6.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 6.
The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for  FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 1 for the FlexiZone Micro hardware unit, this is a Weighted Round Robin  queue.
priorityQueuePcp6.fullName: L2 queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 6

priorityQueuePcp7.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for frames with VLAN PCP bits value 7.

The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for the FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 1 for all hardware unit types, this is the strict priority queue.
priorityQueuePcp7.fullName: L2 queue for frames with VLAN PCP bits 7

priorityQueueUntagged.description:
This parameter specifies which queue shall be used for untagged frames.

The value range of this parameter = 1..6 for FlexiZone Micro hardware units.
The default value of this parameter = 1, this is the strict priority queue.

In case VLAN aware switching, this parameter is not taken into account. Untagged traffic will be enqueued according to the default priority configured for each interface separately.

qosClassification.description:
This parameter specifies if the layer 2 switching is based on DSCP to PHB mapping or on PCP to PHB mapping.
- In case it is DSCP to PHB mapping, the queue for egress traffic is taken from parameter dscpMap for IP frames and from parameter priorityQueueNonIP for non-IP frames.
- In case it is PCP to PHB mapping, the queue for egress traffic is taken from the parameters priorityQueuePcp0 to priorityQueuePcp7 for tagged frames and from parameter priorityQueueUntagged for untagged frames.

qosClassificationCriteria.description:
This parameter defines the criteria to be used for the egress QoS classification for all switch-ports (i.e. criteria for the enqueuing decision).

Options:
IP packet DSCP
Ethernet VLAN-PCP
Ethernet VLAN-ID

Depending on the criteria, the actual mapping of values must be defined in 
managed object classes PCP2QMAP and DSCPTOQMAP or the parameter vlanIdToQueueMap.

switchId.description: This parameter identifies the layer 2 switch. The value is always 1.
switchId.fullName: Identifier of the layer 2 switch object

vlanAwareSwitch.description:
This parameter controls the VLAN behavior of the Transport Ethernet switching. It is applicable when the switching feature is enabled. 
If set to "true", ethernet frames tagged with a VLAN ID shall be switched between two ethernet member ports of a layer 2 bridge only, if both ports are member of the same VLAN. Else the packet shall be dropped. The handling of untagged frames depends on the parameter acceptableFrameTypes.

If set to "false", any VLAN information is not considered when switching. The switching is purely based on MAC Destination address lookup result.
vlanAwareSwitch.fullName: Flag to decide if VLAN aware switching is used

vlanAwarenessEnabled.description:
This parameter defines whether VLAN based separation of Ethernet broadcast domains is enabled (true) or not (false).

When enabled, a frame's VLAN information is considered together with the VLAN configuration of the switch for VLAN ingress filtering, learning, switching decision and VLAN egress tagging/detagging.

When disabled, a frame's VLAN information together with the VLAN configuration of the switch is not considered for VLAN ingress filtering, learning VLAN egress tagging/detagging.
Instead, the switching decision is only based on MAC destination address lookup.

ccaThresholdXr.description: This parameter corresponds to the maximum energy detection threshold defined by regulatory requirements, i.e., to the “Xr” factor in the 3GPP TS 36.213 formula which defines “XThresh_max” when absence of any other technology sharing the carrier can be guaranteed on a long-term basis (see lteUWiFiCoexistence parameter for details).
ccaThresholdXr.fullName: CCA threshold for a specific country

evaluationDurationDpc.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "evaluation Duration Dpc" on the LAA object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

freqHoldoffTimer.description:
Frequency hold-off timer

This timer defines the minimum period of time between LTE-U /LAA cell carrier frequency changes.

Note: In high-load conditions, it is recommended to have a value greater than 20 minutes.

idcLaaScellReleaseTimer.description: A nonzero value for this parameter starts a supervision timer upon receiving InDeviceCoexIndication message with hardware sharing indication from the UE and stops it upon receiving InDeviceCoexIndication message that clears the hardware sharing problem. Upon timer expiry the eNB releases the LAA SCells of the UE. A value of 0 deactivates the supervision timer.
idcLaaScellReleaseTimer.fullName: LAA SCell release timer for LAA in-device coexistence

laaId.description: This parameter identifies the LAA instance.

laaKickdownDelayDpc.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "laa Kickdown Delay Dpc" on the LAA object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

lteUItuRegion.description: This parameter indicates the ITU region where LTE unlicensed has to operate. eNB will adapt the LBT and the transmission mode functionalities to the selected ITU region.

administrativeState.description:
Administrative state of the cell, the value is set by the operator.
Note: This parameter used for NB-IoT standalone cell.

operationalState.description: Operational state of the eNB, the value is set by system.
operationalState.officialRange:
0: initializing 
1: commissioned 
2: notCommisioned 
3: configured 
4: integrated to RAN 
5: onAir 
6: test

LBPUCCHRDPR.officialFullName: Load Based PUCCH Region Default PRofile

countdownPucchCompr.description:
This parameter specifies the countdown timer that defines how long it takes before any new SIB modification process may be triggered again by a PUCCH region compression.
It represents the minutes until the next compression possibility.

If no value in the LBPUCCHRPR is configured, the value from the default profile LBPUCCHRDPR is taken into use.
countdownPucchCompr.fullName: Countdown timer SIB modification by PUCCH compression

countdownPucchExp.description:
This parameter specifies the countdown timer that defines how long it takes before any new SIB modification process may be triggered again by a PUCCH region expansion.
It represents the minutes until the next expansion possibility.

If no value in the LBPUCCHRPR is configured, the value from the default profile LBPUCCHRDPR is taken into use.
countdownPucchExp.fullName: Countdown timer SIB modification by PUCCH expansion

lbPucchRDPrId.description:

It uniquely identifies a LBPUCCHRDPR instance.
lbPucchRDPrId.fullName: Load based PUCCH region default profile identifier

minNumUeIncrPucchExp.description:
The parameter defines the minimum number of additional UEs that should be supported in subsequent PUCCH configurations.

Note: A small configured value of the parameter will lead in case of UE attach requests simultaneously to RAC rejections.

Please note, the modification of the parameter value impacts all TDD cells using the default profile value.
minNumUeIncrPucchExp.fullName: Minimum number of additional UEs in PUCCH expansion

rrcConnectedLowerThresh.description:
This parameter specifies the lower threshold load for the number of UE in RRC_Connected mode where PUCCH compression will be triggered.

If no value in the LBPUCCHRPR is configured, the value from the default profile LBPUCCHRDPR is taken into use.
rrcConnectedLowerThresh.fullName: Lower threshold UEs in RRC connected

rrcConnectedUpperThresh.description:
This parameter specifies the upper threshold load for the number of UE in RRC_Connected mode where PUCCH expansion will be triggered.

If no value in the LBPUCCHRPR is configured, the value from the default profile LBPUCCHRDPR is taken into use.
rrcConnectedUpperThresh.fullName: Upper threshold UEs in RRC connected

lbPucchRPrId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC LBPUCCHRPR.
It uniquely identifies a LBPUCCHRPR instance.

The parameter of this class instance define specific settings in addition to the default profile LBPUCCHRDPR.

If the LBPUCCHRPR instance is not referenced by APUCCH-lbPucchRPrId, there is no need to delete it from the configuration. The configuration is not used by the application.

bandNumber.description: This parameter contains the GSM band number.

lCelcId.description: This is the instance identifier of the GSM local cell resource object (LCELC). A local cell resource consists of the HW required by one cell for transmission and receiving. The local cell resource is associated with the cell identifier (C-ID) in the radio interface. If the configuration is initialized at the BTS, the signalling related to a cell is addressed using C-ID instead of the local cell resource identifier.

actAsiDistMimo.description: Enables a distributed MIMO feature that combines antenna signals from separate physical radio locations into a single logical MIMO cell.

actDynamicSharedSpectrum.description: This parameter enables dynamic spectrum sharing

actWcdmaLteSharedSpectrum.description: Activates a feature allowing WCDMA and LTE to dynamically share the same spectrum/carrier, enabling spectrum refarming without a hard split.

bandNumber.description: This parameter contains the LTE band number.

dynamicSharedSpectrumGsmCellDN.description:
The Distinguished Name of the associated GSM cell used in dynamic shared spectrum.
e.g. MNL-1/MNLENT-1/CELLMAPPING-1/LCELC-1
dynamicSharedSpectrumGsmCellDN.fullName: Dynamic shared spectrum GSM cell distinguished name

intShutdownTimeout.description: This parameter denotes timeout for intelligent shutdown in minutes. The value of "0" means that cell is immediately shut down with high priority. If parameter isn't present in LCELL object, it means that cell remains operational until the batteries run out.

lCellId.description: The LTE local cell resource is an object that consists of the HW required by one cell for transmission and receiving. Local cell resource identifier is used to address one particular local cell resource at the BTS. The lCelId is unique within a BTS. With the Configuration Data message, the local cell resource can be associated to the cell identifier used at the radio interface. In cases when the configuration is initialized at the BTS, the signaling related to a cell is addressed using the cell identifier instead of the local cell resource identifier.

smodDN.description:
This parameter contains the Distinguished Name of the system module the cell shall be allocated to. This parameter is only valid for dual core configuration where Radio Module handling particular LTE cell is connected to both cores.

intShutdownTimeout.description: This parameter denotes timeout for intelligent shutdown in minutes. The value of "0" means that cell is immediately shut down with high priority. If parameter isn't present in LCELW object, it means that cell remains operational until the batteries run out.

lCelwId.description:
This is the instance identifier of the WCDMA local cell resource object (LCELW). A local cell resource consists of the HW required by one cell for transmission and receiving. The local cell resource is associated with the cell identifier (C-ID) in the radio interface. If the configuration is initialized at the BTS, the signalling related to a cell is addressed using C-ID instead of the local cell resource identifier. 

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

Please note that not all values in the range are actually defined in 3GPP.

antOperGain.description: The antenna gain for the band. Some devices may restrict overwriting device values.

Defines the gain of the mast-head amplifier.
This parameter is validated against HW capabilities for for known type of MHAs.

lnaId.description: Identifies the specific low noise amplifier unit.

subunitNumber.description: The ALD subunit number. For a single-unit device, the subunit number is always 1. For a multi-units device, the subunit  number starts at 1 and increases by 1 for each controlled subunit device, with no numbering gaps allowed.

adjEnbId.description: This is the unique ID of the neighbor eNB within PLMN, where adjEnbId and plmnId form the neighbor global eNB ID.
adjEnbId.fullName: Identity of neighbor eNB within PLMN

cPlaneIpAddr.description:
This parameter holds the C-Plane IPv4/v6 address of this adjacent eNB.
Both IP address formats can be used.
Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals or IPv6 address parameter acc. to RFC 4291.

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the address 0.0.0.0, the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).
cPlaneIpAddr.fullName: C-Plane IP address of neighbor eNB

cPlaneIpAddrCtrl.description:
The parameter determines whether the C-Plane IP address of the neighbor eNB (X2 link) is statically configured or whether eNB is allowed to update the address based on information provided by ANR procedures.

oamControlled X2 link:
It is the responsibility of the operator to configure the correct cPlaneIpAddr.

enbControlled X2 link:
The IP address will be maintained by ANR procedures. It is the default value for neighbor eNBs which have been learnt via ANR procedures.

lnAdjId.description:
This is the instance identifier of the object LNADJ. This parameter appears only in the distinguished name (DN) in the plan file and is used for O&M purposes.
It is highly recommended to use for object creation the lowest free lnAdjId value within all LNADJ instances of an eNB. This is to avoid rejection of plan file activation due to colliding lnAdjId values if an LNADJ instance is automatically created by eNB because of activated ANR features.

Please consider following hardware related information:
FSMr2 supports at maximum 128 LNADJ instances per LNCEL. 
FSMr3 supports at maximum 256 LNADJ instances per LNCEL.

uPlaneIpAddrList.description:
This parameter holds the list of X2 U-Plane IPv4/v6 addresses of this adjacent eNB.  It is used only when the LTE529 Dynamic X2 and S1 Firewall feature is enabled.

Both IP address formats are supported.

Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals and IPv6 address parameter acc. to RFC 4291.
This is used to open the firewall for the specified user plane addresses and will allow incoming packets from the specified IP addresses during X2 handover direct forwarding.

oamControlled X2 link:
It is the responsibility of the operator to configure the correct uPlaneIpAddrList.

enbControlled X2 link:
The IP addresses will be maintained by ANR procedures. It is the default value for neighbor eNBs which have been learnt via ANR procedures.

---------------------

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the address 0.0.0.0, the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).

bandIndicatorGeran.description:
Bandindicator Value of the GERAN neighbour cell
(Part of CarrierFrequency)
The IE BandIndicatorGERAN indicates how to interpret an associated GERAN carrier ARFCN, see TS 45.005 [20]. More specifically, the IE indicates the GERAN frequency band in case the ARFCN value can concern either a DCS 1800 or a PCS 1900 carrier frequency. For ARFCN values not associated with one of these bands, the indicator is not relevant.

rimStatus.description:
Provides the status of the RIM association to serving BSS.

Meaning of the values:

- disabled:
The GERAN neighbor cell is not RIM enabled, that is
the feature is not activated
or
PLMN of the GERAN cell is blacklisted for RIM
or
no RAC value is configured.

- unavailable:
The GERAN neighbor cell is RIM enabled but no valid system information from RIM procedure is available.

- available:
The GERAN neighbor cell is RIM enabled and valid system information from RIM procedure is available.

systemInfoListGeran.description:
This parameter contains the GERAN Systeminformation which is used when sending a UE to GSM by eNACC or UE Context Release with redirect.

At least one list entry must be configured if SystemInformationType has the value “si” or “psi”. 

The parameter is meaningless if:
- LTE498: RIM for GSM feature is activated AND
- the PLMN of the cell is not blacklisted for RIM AND
- parameter "gTargetRac" is configured

Constant value maxGERAN-SI is defined in 3GPP TS36.331 section 6.4

The 23 octet 3GPP parameter must be added as character string in hexadecimal notation with leading '0x', where for each octet two character must be configured, with a minimum length of one octet.

systemInfoType.description:
This parameter is set by Operator to indicate which type of GERAN Systeminformation (if any) is included in the RRC MOBILITYFROMEUTRANCOMMAND message.

The parameter is meaningless 
- if feature 'RIM for GSM (LTE498)' is activated and AND
- the PLMN of the cell is not blacklisted for RIM and AND
- parameter gTargetRac is configured.

Target C-ID
Uniquely identifies a neighbouring cell within the RNC. Required (together with the RNC ID) for the Source RNC To Target RNC Transparent Container IE in the S1AP: HANDOVER REQUIRED message during handover to UTRAN

uTargetFreq.description:

UtranTarget_FREQ provides the DL Carrier Frequency of the neighbouring UTRAN cell. Received from RRM-CMC in the TCL, which together with the primary scrambling code identifies a neighbouring UTRAN cell

uTargetLac.description:

UtranTarget_LAC provides the Location Area Code identifying the Location Area of a neighbouring UTRAN cell. Required for the S1AP: HANDOVER REQUIRED message during handover to UTRAN

uTargetRac.description:

srvccHoInd.description:
This parameter selects if SRVCC to a WCDMA target cell is performed as a combined PS and CS SRVCC or whether SRVCC is performed for the CS bearer only.
This parameter must be configured individually for every WCDMA cell that is used as target for SRVCC.

uTargetCid.description:
UTRAN Cell-ID which is part of the UTRAN Cell Global Identifier (CGI) of the related neighbor cell.
It uniquely identifies a neighbouring cell within the RNC and is required (together with the RNC ID) for the Source RNC To Target RNC Transparent Container IE in the S1AP: HANDOVER REQUIRED message during handover to UTRAN.

The UTRAN Cell Global Id is built as a 28 bit value. It consists either
- of a 12 bit RNC-ID (range 0..4095) and a 16 bit UTRAN Cell ID (range 0..65535) or
- of a 16 bit Extended RNC-Id (range 4096..65535) and a 12 bit UTRAN Cell ID (range 0..4095).

uTargetFreq.description:
Target Frequency
Target Frequency  provides the DL Carrier Frequency of the neighbouring UTRAN cell. Received from RRM-CMC in the TCL, which together with the primary scrambling code identifies a neighboring UTRAN cell

uTargetLac.description:
Target Location Area Code
UtranTarget_LAC provides the Location Area Code identifying the Location Area of a neighbouring UTRAN cell. Required for the S1AP: HANDOVER REQUIRED message during handover to UTRAN

uTargetRac.description:
Target Routing Area Code
UtranTarget_RAC provides the Routing Area Code identifying the Routing Area of a neighbouring UTRAN cell. Required for the S1AP: HANDOVER REQUIRED message during handover to UTRAN

uTargetRncId.description:
UTRAN RNC identifier which is part of the UTRAN Cell Global Identifier (CGI) of the related neighbor cell.

Values in the range of 4096 .. 65535 are considered as Extended RNC-ID.
It uniqely identifies a neighbouring UTRAN RNC within the primary PLMN and is required for the S1AP: HANDOVER REQUIRED message during handover to UTRAN.

The UTRAN Cell Global Id is built as a 28 bit value. It consists either
- of a 12 bit RNC-ID (range 0..4095) and a 16 bit UTRAN Cell ID (range 0..65535) or
- of a 16 bit Extended RNC-Id (range 4096..65535) and a 12 bit UTRAN Cell ID (range 0..4095).

uTargetScFdd.description:

UtranTarget_SC_FDD: The primary scrambling code (FDD) of the neighbouring UTRAN cell. Received from RRM-CMC in the TCL, which together with the cell frequency identifies a neighbouring UTRAN cell

actAcBarringCFR.description: This parameter activates LTE4175 'Connection failure rate based Access Class Barring'. The feature aggregates the number of RRC Connection Requests and the connection failure rate defined by the ratio between RRC connection setup rejections due to RAC at cell level and total RRC attempts over sliding window and if they are exceeding start thresholds it triggers step-wise access class barring parameters broadcast in SIB2.
actAcBarringCFR.fullName: Activate CFR based access class barring

actAcBarringPlmn.description: This parameter activates LTE2996 'PLMN Specific Access Class Barring'.
actAcBarringPlmn.fullName: Activate automatic access class barring per PLMN

actAcBarringRrcConn.description:
This parameter activates LTE2823 'RRC Connection triggered access class barring'.
The feature detects that number of RRC connections is near RAC limit on cell level and triggers access class barring parameters broadcast in SIB2.
The feature introduces ACB step-wise algorithm to broadcast access class barring parameters in SIB2.
If LTE4175 is activated, i.e. actAcBarringCFR is set to ‘true’ then LTE2823 does not detect that number of RRC connections is near RAC limit on cell level and does not  trigger access class barring parameters broadcast in SIB2. LTE2823 ACB step-wise algorithm is triggered by LTE4175, LTE2235 or LTE1788 if activated.
actAcBarringRrcConn.fullName: Activate RRC connection triggered access class barring

actAcBarringRrcReq.description:
This parameter activates  'RACH load triggered access class barring'. 
The feature aggregates the number of RRC Connection Requests over sliding window and if it's exceeding start threshold it triggers step-wise access class barring parameters broadcast in SIB2.
actAcBarringRrcReq.fullName: Activate RACH load triggered access class barring

actAcBarringSpecialClass.description: Enables Access Class Barring to also apply to the 'special' access classes (AC 11-15, normally reserved for high-priority users), allowing the network to bar them too under extreme congestion.

actAcSrvcc.description: This parameter activates the functionality to accept an E-RAB with QCI#1 by overbooking in RAC and/or TAC and immediately trigger SRVCC to WCDMA for respective UE.

actAddA3HoCheck.description:

Note: Currently, this functionality cannot be activated.

actAdvScellMeas.description: This parameter activates the feature for advanced SCell measurement handling for carrier aggregation.

actAdvStepwiseScellAdd.description:
Activate advanced step-wise SCell addition.
If this parameter is set to 'oneStepAdvanced', and step-wise cell addition is enabled (numTxWithHighNonGbr is not equal to '0'), one step SCell addition occurs when the UE enters the cell.
If this parameter is set to 'buffer-based', and step-wise cell addition is enabled, the eNB starts buffer measurements when the UE enters the cell. Upon buffer overflows, one step SCell addition occurs if no SCells are configured for this UE, otherwise step-wise addition is performed.
If this parameter is 'off', and step-wise cell addition is enabled, the eNB starts buffer measurements when the UE enters the cell, and step-wise cell addition is performed upon buffer overflows.
If numTxWithHighNonGbr is equal to '0', this parameter is ignored.

actAdvUlScellHandling.description:

- the PCell UL pathloss is checked for adding a DL+UL SCell and for downgrading a DL+UL SCell to a DL-only SCell.

When the feature is activated the cells handled by the individual nodes of the cluster need to be configured according to the CRAN feature description. There are no inter-BTS cross checks assuring correct cell definitions within the CRAN cluster. The CRAN configuration itself is checked for correctness.
For scalability information please refer to the configuration guidelines.

actCellTraceWithIMSI.description:
This parameter is used for enabling/disabling of the feature "Cell Trace with IMSI". It will be only utilized when cell trace is activated, i.e. actCellTrace is TRUE.
If the value is set to TRUE the eNB will send the CELL TRAFFIC TRACE message to MME for every call in every cell trace session.
This will allow the MME to map the Trace Reference/Trace Recording Session Reference to IMSI/IMEI.
If the parameter is set to FALSE the eNB will not send the CELL TRAFFIC TRACE message to MME for all calls in all Cell Trace Sessions.

actCoC2kWcdmaGsmMob.description: Enables a coordinated mobility feature that jointly considers CDMA2000, WCDMA, and GSM as inter-RAT mobility targets, aligning thresholds/decisions across them.

actCoMp.description:
Coordinated multipoint (CoMP) feature activation for the eNB. The parameter is used to configured CoMP features supported by the eNB for UL and /or DL CoMP.

For UL CoMP features LTE1402, LTE1691, LTE2104 and LTE2128 please configure the value to 'fixedULCoMp'.
For measurement based CoMP features LTE3102 (DL) and LTE3286 (UL) please configure the value to 'measBasedCoMp'.

For 'fixedULCoMP', SINR measurements are used, where for 'measBasedCoMp' A3 measuremets are used in addition to SINR.

The eNB will dynamically decide dependent on the current and newly required DSP deployment if eNB restart or dropping of all cells is needed.

Configuration rules for FDD:
Distributed sites are only supported if the distance between RRHs is less than 1 km.

Notes for TDD:
Recommendations for balancing increased TDD cell throughput and link level gain (not considered in validation) for LTE1402, LTE1691, LTE2104 or LTE2128 configurations:
If chBw is set to '20MHz' AND dlMimoMode is set to 'Closed Loop MIMO (4x4)', actCoMp is recommended to be configured to 'fixedULCoMp'.

Configuration rules for TDD:
Distributed sites are only supported if the distance between RRHs is less than 1 km, with a maximal Doppler shift of 250 Hz.
For 4 Rx UL-CoMP (LTE1691) only cells with 15 MHz and 20 MHz bandwidth are supported.
For 2 Rx, 4 Rx and 8 Rx UL-CoMP (LTE1402, LTE2104 and LTE2128) cells with 10 MHz, 15 MHz and 20 MHz bandwidth are supported.

actEnhAcAndGbrServices.description:
This parameter activates support of the following features
LTE534: ARP based Admission Control 
LTE497: Smart Admission Control, comprising RAC and TAC
LTE496: EPS bearers with QCI 2, 3 and 4
Feature LTE496 introduces support of QCI 2, 3, and 4 along with higher guaranteed bit rates and related congestion detection and handling mechanisms.

Admission control functionality (LTE497) is extended at the same time from a counter based solution to become load based and offer in addition congestion handling functionality to better address the needs being imposed by higher guaranteed bit rates.

Finally the ARP based admission control (LTE534) allows to consider the ARP priority in load-based admission and admission related pre-emption as well as in congestion handling as an additional more service-related dimension for differentiated treatment of bearers with guaranteed resources.

As those features are closely inter-related, they are activated via a common activation parameter.

Note:  actIPv6MBMS is only allowed to be set to "true" for AirScale eNBs.
actIPv6MBMS.fullName: Activate IPv6 MBMS M1 Interface Support

actIdleLB.description:
The parameter activates the feature Idle Mode Load Balancing
This flag also activates the following functionalities:
- inter-RAT IdleLB targets
- Load balancing for redirection (requires also the feature 'UE context release with redirect' actRedirect  and 'CS Fallback via Redirection' actCSFBRedir)
- IdleLB targets in Mobility profiles (requires also the feature 'Selective Mobility Profiles' actSelMobPrf)
- Support of special SPID values (requires also the feature 'Selective Mobility Profiles' actSelMobPrf)
- Load-triggered idle mode load balancing
- Support of dedicated idle mode mobility priorities
actIdleLB.fullName: Activation of idle mode load balancing (IdleLB)

actIdleLBCaAware.description:
The parameter activates the feature Idle Mode Load Balancing for CA capable UEs
This flag also activates the following functionalities:
- inter-RAT IdleLB targets
- IdleLB targets in Mobility profiles (requires also the feature 'Selective Mobility Profiles' actSelMobPrf)
- Load-triggered idle mode load balancing for CA capable UEs
- Support of dedicated idle mode mobility priorities for CA capable UEs
actIdleLBCaAware.fullName: Activation of idle mode load balancing for CA capable UEs

actIdleLBCaAwareAdv.description:
The parameter activates the feature Carrier aggregation aware idle mode load balancing - II (advanced).

If activated, not only the PCell CA capabilities of a UE but also its SCell CA capabilities are taken into account for idle mode load balancing.
actIdleLBCaAwareAdv.fullName: Activation of advanced CA aware idle mode load balancing

actIdleLBEnDcAware.description: Enables idle-mode load-balancing decisions to be aware of EN-DC capability/status, favouring redirect/reselection targets that support EN-DC for capable UEs.

actIdleLBNrAware.description: Enables idle-mode load-balancing decisions to consider NR (5G) coverage/availability when selecting redirection targets.

actIdleLBSupportedBands.description: This activates use of the supportedBandListEUTRA (from UE capabilities) to populate the secondary target frequencies from the idelLBEutCelResPrio parameters. Additionally, if activated, the serving cell is always included in the secondary target list.
actIdleLBSupportedBands.fullName: Activate idle mode load balancing supported band list

actIdleLBTM9aware.description: Enables idle-mode load-balancing decisions to consider whether target cells support Transmission Mode 9 capability.

actIfHo.description: This parameter enables the feature Inter Frequency Handover to FDD and TDD neighbor cells.

actImmHRPD.description: Activates "Idle mode mobility from LTE to CDMA/eHRPD".

actImmXrtt.description: Activates idle mode mobility from LTE to CDMA/1xRTT.

actIncCarrMonit.description: feature flag for increased carrier monitoring

actInterEnbDLCAggr.description: This parameter activates the features 'Inter-eNB DL carrier aggregation' and ‘Inter-site DL carrier aggregation’ for up to 4 macro or 2 FZM eNBs.

actInterEnbULCAggr.description: This parameter activates the functionality for 'Inter-eNB uplink carrier aggregation'.

actInterFreqMDTCellTrace.description: This parameter enables the activation of MDT inter-frequency UE periodic measurements.

actInterFreqRstdMeasSupp.description:
The parameter configures feature LTE1638 "Inter-frequency RSTD measurement support".
If the feature is activated (configured to 'true') the Flexi-BTS supports UE RSTD (reference signal time difference) inter-frequency measurements for OTDOA.
The UE may request the eNode B to start / stop measurements gaps via the RRC:InterFreqRSTDMeasurementIndication message (UEs with 3GPP Release 8 or 9 are not able to request this).

The timing of the measurement gap is derived from the IE measPRS-Offset. 

UE controlled inter-frequency RSTD measurements may help to improve the accuracy of OTDOA, without having the pre-requirement of activated OTDOA.

actIntraFreqPciSharing.description: Allows reuse (sharing) of the same Physical Cell Identity across intra-frequency cells at the site/cluster, easing PCI planning in dense deployments where full PCI separation isn't practical.

actL1PM.description:
This parameter activates/deactivates the following PM counters from feature Additional Layer 1 Performance Measurements:

Group 1: M8005C306-M8005C313, M8005C336-M8805C339, M8005C317-M8005C325, M8005C326-M8005C335, M8005C314, M8010C74, M8010C75
Group 3: M8031C0-M8031C259, M8031C520-M8031C539, M8031C260-M8031C519, M8031C540-M8031C559

Activation of the other counters from feature LTE1491 is controlled by parameter actServicePRButiL.
actL1PM.fullName: Feature Activation Flag Additional Layer 1 PM Group 1 and Group 3 Counters

actLBPowerSaving.description:
This parameter activates the feature LTE1103 'Load-Based Power Saving for Multi-Layered Networks'. When the feature is activated, intra-eNB cells that provide service to the same coverage area may be automatically switched off/on according to the aggregate load across the set of cells (Power Group).
LTE1103 Load-Based Power Saving is not meant to be used with eNBs that support RF Sharing (BTSSCL:rfSharingEnabled = 'true'). There is no coordination between the technologies that are configured for RF Sharing. However, LTE1103 Load-Based Power Saving can be used for LTE cells in frequencies that do not share power amplifiers across technologies.

actLBRTXPowerSaving.description:
This parameter activates the feature LTE1203 'Load-Based Power Saving with TX-Path Switch Off'. When the feature is activated, intra-eNB cells that provide service to the same coverage area may have TX-Paths automatically switched off/on according to the aggregate load across the set of cells (Power Group).

LTE1203 Load-Based Power Saving is not meant to be used with eNBs that support RF Sharing (BTSSCL-rfSharingEnabled = 'true'). There is no coordination between the technologies that are configured for RF Sharing. However, LTE1203 Load-Based Power Saving can be used for LTE cells in frequencies that do not share power amplifiers across technologies.
actLBRTXPowerSaving.fullName: Activate load-based reduced TX power saving

actLPPaEcid.fullName: Activate LPPa enhanced cell ID location service

actLPPaEcidNB.description: Enables LPPa (LTE Positioning Protocol Annex) support for Enhanced Cell-ID positioning specifically for NB-IoT UEs.

actLPPaOtdoa.description: Activates support of the LPPa OTDOA information request procedure via S1AP

actLTES1Ho.description: This parameter enables the feature Intra LTE Inter eNodeB Handover via S1

actLaaPrefOverEnDc.description: Enables giving LAA (Licensed Assisted Access) preference/priority over EN-DC when both could be used for a capable UE.

actLbpsCtrlLogicEnh.description: Activates an enhancement to the load-based power-saving (LBPS) control logic used to scale radio power/capacity down under low traffic.

actLoadPmCounter.description: Enables collection of additional load-related PM counters/statistics.

actLocRep.description: Activation/deactivation of Location Reporting (feature 'Support of cell based location service')

actLocRepNB.description: Enables UE location reporting for NB-IoT.

actLteNrDss.description: Activates Dynamic Spectrum Sharing (DSS) between LTE and NR at the BTS level, the master switch that enables sharing the same carrier spectrum between the two RATs.

actLteNrDualConnectivity.description: This parameter activates LTE-New Radio Dual Connectivity (EN-DC) functionality.

actLteNrFastNbrRelAdd.description: Enables faster/expedited addition of LTE-NR neighbor relations, speeding up ANR-style discovery of NR neighbor cells for EN-DC.

actMBMS.description:
Activates the feature 'Multimedia Broadcast/Multicast Service (MBMS)'

MBMS will be only activated if actOtdoa, sib2xTransmit and liquidCellConfigInfo-csiRsSubfr (if actLiquidCell equal to 'true') have the same value in all LNCEL instances with earfcnDL equal to mbsfnEarfcn and dlChBw equal to mbsfnDlChBw.

MBMS will be only activated if actOtdoa, LTE2085 activation status and csiRsConfigInfo-csiRsSubfrConf (if (dlMimoMode is set to ('Closed Loop MIMO (4x2)' OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (4x4)'  OR 'Closed Loop MIMO (8x2)' ) AND (activatedMimoTM is NOT set to 'TM4')) have the same value in all LNCEL instances with earfcnDL equal to mbsfnEarfcn and dlChBw equal to mbsfnDlChBw.

Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode may be released, when this parameter is online modified together with Cat-M are activated.

actMeasGapCoordEnDc.description: Enables coordination of measurement gaps between LTE and NR for EN-DC UEs, so LTE and NR gap patterns do not conflict and both links get needed measurement opportunities.

actMeasGapIfEnDc.description: Enables use of inter-frequency measurement gaps specifically when EN-DC is active.

actMfbiNr.description: Activates support for a Multi-Frequency-Band Indicator mechanism for NR, used in interworking/mobility signalling between LTE and NR bands.

If this parameter is set to “true”, then for UEs moving from 2G/3G to LTE, exclusion of MMEGI information in MME selection is possible, i.e. eNB is able to select the MME based on only the MME Code and selected PLMN-Identity.
actMmecPlmnIdMmeSelection.fullName: Activate MMEC PLMN ID based MME selection

actMobProfileDataVol.description: Enables selecting or adjusting a UE's mobility profile based on its observed data-volume/usage pattern.

actMroInterRatUtran.description:

Please note, the activation of the feature for functional usage does require to activate LTE56 "Inter RAT handover to WCDMA" or LTE898 "TDD inter-RAT handover to TD-SCDMA".

actMultBearers.description: This parameter activates the support of multiple EPS Bearers.

actMultGbrBearers.description: This parameter activates the support of multiple GBR EPS Bearers.

actMultiSCGSplit.description: Enables split-bearer support across Multiple Secondary Cell Groups (Multi-SCG), allowing bearer data to be split across more than one secondary node/cell group in advanced multi-connectivity configurations.

actMultiSCGSplitwoeLcId.description: Enables Multi-SCG split-bearer operation without extended Logical Channel ID signalling, a compatibility-mode variant of the general Multi-SCG split feature.

actMultipleCarrier.description:
This parameter activates multiple carrier operation.
When the parameter is set to value "false", the eNB is working in single carrier operation, when set to one of the other values, it is working in multi carrier operation. The parameter need to be configured always to the highest number of carriers transmitted over the same antenna line in the eNB.

An FDD eNB supports up to 6 carrier configurations at the same antenna line.
A TDD eNB supports up to 4 carrier configurations at the same antenna line.

eNB will dynamically decide dependent on the current and newly required DSP deployment if eNB restart or dropping of all cells is needed.

actNonGbrServiceDiff.description: This parameter activates the Service Differentiation for non-GBR Bearers.
