maxNtpTimeError.description: This parameter configures the maximum expected time error recovered from NTP source by the BTS, as measured against UTC/GPS time.
maxNtpTimeError.fullName: Maximum NTP time error at the BTS

ntpAlarmingThreshold.description: This parameter defines the amount of time the BTS will wait before raising the "NTP Server $IP unavailable" fault when NTP server unavailability is detected.

ntpDscp.description: This parameter defines the differentiated services code point (DSCP) value to be used for NTP traffic.

ntpId.description: This is the instance identifier of the NTP object.

ntpServerConfigSource.description: Nokia RAN configuration parameter related to "Network Time Protocol Server Config Source" on the NTP object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

ntpServerIpAddrList.description:
This parameter defines the IP address of the NTP server. It is to be entered in the dotted decimal format.
Although the NTP server configuration is optional due to the possibility that other time sources (e.g., GNSS) may be configured, it is recommended to define at least one NTP server as a backup time source in case the primary time source is lost.
At maximum 3 ntp server can be configured.
If more than one address is set, IP protocol versions must be the same. Mixed IPv4/IPv6 configurations are not supported.
The following IP addresses are not allowed:
1.) Loopback addresses 127.0.0.0 - 127.255.255.255.
2.) IP addresses 0.0.0.1 - 0.255.255.255.
 The format is an IPv4 defined in RFC 2373 or IPv6 defined in RFC4291.

ntpSourceIpAddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the IPADDRESS object instance which holds the IPv4 or IPv6 address to be used for the BTS NTP  client(s) .
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-1/IPADDRESSV4-1 (or MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-1/IPADDRESSV6-1)

utcGpsNtpOffsetAfter.description: This parameter sets the offset (in seconds) between GPS time and UTC (without the timezone difference) valid after the date/time specified in utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate. It is dedicated to NTP time source
utcGpsNtpOffsetAfter.fullName: NTP UTC-GPS offset value after change date

utcGpsNtpOffsetBefore.description: This parameter sets offset (in seconds) between GPS time and UTC (without the timezone difference) valid before the date/time specified in utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate. It is dedicated to NTP time source
utcGpsNtpOffsetBefore.fullName: NTP UTC-GPS offset value before change date

utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate.description:
This parameter describes the next date of change of utcGpsOffset, or the previous date if next has not been announced yet. It is dedicated to NTP time source.
The format is: YYYY-MM-DD
utcGpsNtpOffsetChangeDate.fullName: Next/last known NTP UTC-GPS offset change date

ntpSyncLocalIpMapping.description:
This parameter specifies to which Plane IP address the BTS NTP Frequency Synchronization clients will be mapped (M-Plane, C-Plane, U-Plane or S-Plane).
When this parameter is configured to Plane supporting Dual Stack operation (C/U-Plane) then the NTP Frequency Synchronization client is mapped to the IP version (IPv4 or IPv6) of the IP addresses configured in the list of NTP frequency synchronization servers (NTPS-ntpSyncServers).
ntpSyncLocalIpMapping.officialRange:
0: M-Plane 
1: C-Plane 1 
2: C-Plane 2 
3: U-Plane 1 
4: U-Plane 2 
5: S-Plane

ntpSyncPollingRate.description: This parameter defines the NTP frequency synchronization client/master polling rate in seconds.

ntpSyncServers.description:
This parameter specifies the IP addresses of the NTP servers to be used to synchronize the eNodeB system clock frequency.
All configured IP addresses shall be of the same version (IPv4 or IPv6).
For IPv4, the IP addresses have to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the IP addresses have to be entered according to formats specified in RFC4291.
ntpSyncServers.fullName: List of NTP frequency synchronization server IP address

ntpsId.description:
This parameter identifies the NTP frequency sync configuration of the FTM. The value is always 1.
NTP sync as a clockProtocol is supported only with FlexiZone micro FDD units.

ntpRId.description: This is the instance identifier of the read only NTP  object.
ntpRId.fullName: Network Time Protocol read only identifier

ntpServerIpAddr.description: This is the IP address of the NTP server. The IPv4 is in dotted decimal format  or IPv6 in format defined in RFC4291.
ntpServerIpAddr.fullName: IP address of the NTP server

ntpStatus.description:
This parameter shows the status of the NTP server.
Meaning:
 - InSync:          NTP server is available and used as synchronization source. (Only possible for one configured NTP server in the list at once)
 - Unavailable:  NTP server cannot be used for synchronization (e.g. not reachable)
 - Unknown:      Status unknown (e.g. during initialization)
 - Available:      NTP server as such is OK and available to provide its service but is not used as synchronization source

aisHandlingEnabled.description: This parameter defines whether a received AIS is used for alarm suppression.

assocId.description: This parameter identifies a Maintenance Association. Up to 15 associations may exist in the BTS.

ccmRemoteMacAddr.description:
This parameter defines the MAC address of the remote Maintenance Association End Point (MEP) to be addressed by the continuity check function..
Note:The MAC address must be a unicast MAC address.

ccmRemoteMepId.description: This parameter defines the MEP identifier of the remote Maintenance Association End Point (MEP) to be addressed by the continuity check function.

ccmSendingEnabled.description:
This parameter enables the sending of continuity check messages (ETH_CCM) towards the remote Maintenance Association Endpoints (MEPs).
Changing the parameter from false to true resets the CCM counters.
ccmSendingEnabled.fullName: Enable sending of continuity check messages

ccmTxPeriod.description: This parameter defines the period for sending continuity check messages (CCM).
ccmTxPeriod.officialRange:
0: CCM_3_33MS 
1: CCM_10MS 
2: CCM_100MS 
3: CCM_1SEC 
4: CCM_10SEC 
5: CCM_1MIN 
6: CCM_10MIN

ethIfDN.description:
This parameter defines to which Ethernet interface (ETHIF) the service OAM function shall be assigned to.
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/ETHSVC-1/ETHIF-1

localMepId.description: This parameter defines the local maintenance endpoint identifier to be used for this maintenance association.

maName.description: This parameter defines the maintenance association name.

oamMaId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the Ethernet OAM maintenance association.
oamMaId.fullName: Ethernet OAM maintenance association object identifier

oamMdDN.description:
This parameter defines the assignment of the maintenance association to a maintenance domain
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/ETHAPP-1/OAMMD-1

vlanEnabled.description: This parameter defines whether VLAN mapping is enabled for this maintenance association. In case VLAN mapping is not enabled, all messages on the maintenance association will be sent in plain format.

vlanId.description:
This parameter defines the VLAN identifier which shall be used for sending coninuity messages for this maintenance association.

In case there is a switch involved in the overall configuration it is to be ensured that the L2 switch is configured to handle the defined VLAN identifier appropriately.
Ethernet service OAM Down-MEP frames generated by the service OAM application are transmitted at a switch-port as selected by the service OAM application, irrespective of the configuration of VLAN awareness (VLAN list, PVID, Acceptable FrameTypes, etc.).
I.e. VLAN egress processing and tagging/detagging will not be applied.
vlanId.fullName: VLAN identifier of the maintenance association

vlanPrio.description: This parameter defines the VLAN priority (PCP bit value) to be used for service OAM messages for this maintenance endpoint (MEP).

domainId.description: This parameter identifies a Maintenance Domain. Up to 10 domains may exist on the BTS.

mdLevel.description: This parameter defines the maintenance domain level.

mdName.description: This parameter defines the maintenance domain name.

oamMdId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the Ethernet OAM maintenance domain.
oamMdId.fullName: Ethernet OAM maintenance domain object identifier

aisEnabled.description: This parameter specifies if the transmission of AIS messages is enabled.

enableCcm.description: This parameter allows sending continuity check messages (ETH_CCM) towards the remote Maintenance Association Endpoints (MEPs) of the End Point. Changing the parameter from false (not allowed) to true (allowed) resets the CCM counters and alarms of all remote MEPs.
enableCcm.fullName: Allow sending of CCM messages and reset CCM counters

ethernetPort.description:
This parameter specifies the ethernet link that the BTS uses for sending Service OAM messages. The parameter is a local managed object instance identifier (LMOID), i.e. a reference to an instance of object class ETHLK.
Format: "FTM-1/ETHLK-1-*"

where
FTM-#: # = a parent instance of object class ETHLK, This is always 1 (static MO)
ETHLK-#-#.# = an instance of object class ETHLK

 Example: FTM-1/ETHLK-1-1

For Flexizone Micro:
In case of FWHC, this parameter shall set values only to FTM-1/ETHLK-1-1 or FTM-1/ETHLK-1-2

macAddr.description:
This parameter specifies the MAC address of the Maintenance Association End Point (MEP).
Note:The MAC address must be a unicast MAC address.
macAddr.fullName: MAC address of the Maintenance Association End Point

mepId.description: This parameter identifies the Maintenance Association End Point (MEP).

oammepId.description: This parameter identifies the Maintenance association Endpoint (MEP).

vlanPrio.description: This parameter specifies the PCP bits value to be used for Service OAM messages for this Maintenance association Endpoint (MEP).

activeMode.description: This parameter specifies the Link OAM operational mode at the local peer. If false, the BTS will only respond to a remotely initiated discovery process, if active the BTS will itself initiate the process.
activeMode.fullName: Link OAM operational mode at local peer

alarmClearanceDelay.description: This parameter specifies for how long critical event flags must be cleared before the BTS  clears the corresponding Link OAM Critical Event alarm.
alarmClearanceDelay.fullName: Link OAM Link Critical Event Alarm clearance delay

efEventThreshold.description:
This parameter specifies the threshold value for counting the Errored Frame Event. If the number of errored frames detected within the measurement window specified by efEventWindow is exceeded, the BTS transmits an OAM PDU Event Notification message for that event.

The maximum value of efEventThreshold equals "32 bit value".

efEventWindow.description: This parameter specifies the measurement interval for counting the Errored Frame Event. If the number of errored frames detected within the measurement interval exceeds the threshold number specified in parameter efEventThreshold, the FTM transmits an OAM PDU Event Notification message for that event.

efpEventThreshold.description:
This parameter specifies the threshold value for counting the Errored Frame Period Event. If the number of received errored frames within the measurement window specified by efpEventWindow is exceeded, the BTS transmits an OAM PDU Event Notification message for that event.
The maximum value of efpEventThreshold equals "32 bit value".
efpEventThreshold.fullName: Errored Frame Period Event counting threshold

efpEventWindow.description: This parameter specifies the measurement interval for counting the Errored Frames. If the number of received errored frames within the measurement interval exceeds the threshold number specified in parameter efpEventThreshold, the BTS transmits an OAM PDU Event Notification message for that event.
efpEventWindow.fullName: Errored Frame Period Event counting interval

efssEventThreshold.description:
This parameter specifies the threshold value for counting the Errored Frame Seconds Summary Event. If the number of errored frame seconds that occurred during the specified measurement interval specified by efssEventWindow is exceeded, the BTS transmits an OAM PDU Event Notification message for that event.
The maximum value of efssEventThreshold equals "16 bit value".
efssEventThreshold.fullName: Errored Frame Seconds Summary Event counting threshold

efssEventWindow.description: This parameter specifies the measurement interval for counting the Errored Frame Seconds Summary Event. If the number of errored frame seconds that occurred during the specified measurement interval exceeds the threshold number specified in parameter efssEventThreshold, the BTS transmits an OAM PDU Event Notification message for that event.
efssEventWindow.fullName: Errored Frame Seconds Summary Event counting interval

eventRepetition.description: This parameter specifies how often the BTS repeats the transmission of OAM Events Notifications to its remote peer to increase the probability that they are received by the remote peer. The parameter specifies the total number of repetitive transmissions of such messages.

eventSupport.description: This parameter specifies if the BTS supports Link OAM events.

linkOAMProfileName.description: This parameter describes a unique configurable name for each link OAM profile.

loopBackTime.description: This parameter specifies the duration of a loopback operation initiated by the BTS or by the remote peer.

loopbackSupported.description:
If set to "true", the FTM enables the discovery process for Link OAM loopback requests initiated by a remote network element. If set to "false", loopback initiated from the remote network are not accepted by the FTM.  BTS allows to start only one loopback.
NOTE: By default, the parameter is set to 'false'

profileId.description: This parameter identifies a Link OAM profile.

testFrameRate.description:
This parameter specifies the number of frames / second to be sent during loopback operation for Link OAM.
Value 0 switched the test frame generator off.
testFrameRate.fullName: Link OAM loopback test message rate

testFrameSize.description: This parameter specifies the ethernet  frame size of test messages sent during loopback operation for Link OAM.
testFrameSize.fullName: Link OAM loopback test message frame size

acfcTarget.description:
This parameter defines if the Address and Control Field (ACF) is used.
If in use, the Address and Control Field (ACF) is compressed.

frliDN.description:
This parameter defines which fractional link (FRLI) shall be used for the PPP link.
The fractional link is defined by giving a distinguished name (DN) of the managed object FRLI.
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/FRLI-17

lcpEchoEnabled.description: This parameter defines whether the Link Control Protocol (LCP) echo is used or not.

lcpEchoInterval.description: This parameter defines the Link Control Protocol (LCP) echo interval in seconds.

localMruTarget.description: This parameter defines the MRU of the local peer in bytes. The local peer will try to negotiate this value with the remote peer. The MRU defines the maximum number of bytes in the Information fields of a PPP packet.

magicNumberUsage.description:
The attribute defines whether magic numbers are used.
The usage of magic numbers provides a way to detect looped-back links and other data link layer anomalies by sending a number that is otherwise unlikely to happen.

p3lpId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the PPP link object. It uniquely identifies the object.

pfcTarget.description:
This parameter defines if protocol field compression is used or not. 
The Protocol Field (PCF) in LCP packets, by default, has 2 octets. 
If the PCF option is used, it is compressed to 1 octet.

acfcResult.description:
This parameter indicates whether access control field compression is in use.
The value is the result of the ACFC negotiation.

localMruResult.description: This parameter indicates the result of the LCP negotiation of the local Maximum Receive Unit (MRU) in bytes. The remote peer normally acknowledges the localMruTarget value, and the localMruResult will be equal to the localMruTarget.

operationalState.description: This parameter indicates the operational state of the PPP link.

p3lpRId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only PPP link object. It uniquely identifies the object.
p3lpRId.fullName: Read only PPP link object identifier

pfcResult.description: This parameter indicates whether protocol field compression is used.

remoteMru.description:
This parameter indicates the MRU of the remote peer in bytes. 
The local peer normally acknowledges all MRU values which the remote peer sends.
The effective interface maximum transmission unit (MTU) of the PPP interface depends on the remote MRU. 
It is calculated as the minimum value of
1.) the local configured MTU of that interface,
2.) the negotiated remote MRU (i.e. the MRU of the peer) of that interface.

administrativeState.description: The administrative state allows to start and stop the ML-PPP interface. A value of "locked" means the ML-PPP interface is administratively prohibited from use. A value of "unlocked" means the ML-PPP interface is not administratively prohibited from use.

endPointDiscriminatorUsageEnabled.description: This parameter enables dynamic connection to an existing multi-link interface in the peer, or creation of a new multi-link interface in the peer.

ipHeaderCompressionUsage.description:
This parameter enables the IP header compression (IPHC) negotiation on the ML-PPP interface.
When "IN_USE", the local peer will try to negotiate the IPHC with the remote peer, with a set of IPHC parameters that is acceptable for both peers. 
When "NOT_IN_USE", the local peer will not try to negotiate the IPHC with
the remote peer. 
The IPHC negotiation must be enabled also on the remote peer to succeed, otherwise, both peers might negotiate an ML-PPP interface without the IPHC. 
The IP header compression result parameter shows the actual outcome of the IPHC negotiation.

ipcpEncapsulation.description:
The parameter defines whether IPCP packets are sent with or without ML-PPP headers on the ML-PPP interface.
This way, the local peer can be adapted to restrictions of the remote peer which may support only one method.

localMrruTarget.description:
The parameter defines the MRRU (Multi-link Maximum Received Reconstructed Unit) of the local peer. The local peer will try to negotiate this value with the remote peer.
Furthermore the MRRU defines the maximum number of octets in the Information fields of the reassembled PPP packet.

mpFragmentSize.description:
This parameter defines, in octets, the PPP multi-link protocol fragment size in the egress direction.
In addition an automatic mode is provided.
The automatic mode selects the fragment size based on the ML-PPP interface.

multiClassTarget.description:
The parameter defines the number of classes for multi-class ML-PPP.
Supported values are:
1.) MC4: multi-class ML-PPP with four classes
2.) MC2: multi-class ML-PPP with two classes
3.) MC0: No multi-class (i.e. ML-PPP without classes or PPP, depending on MRRU configuration)
With MC4 and MC2 configured, the local peer will send the multi-link header format option. MC4 and MC2 require always a MRRU configuration for enabling multi-link PPP.

p3LpDN.description:
This parameter defines which PPP link(s) (P3LP) shall be used for a ML-PPP interface.
At maximum 8 links can be configured for one ML-PPP interface.
The PPP link is defined by giving the related distinguished name (DN) of the managed object P3LP.
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/P3LP-5

p3mlId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the PPP multi-link object. It uniquely identifies the object.

shortSeqNbrFormatUsageEnabled.description:
This parameter enables the Short Sequence-Number Format (SSNF) usage on the ML-PPP interface. 
When "true", the local peer will try to negotiate the SSFN with the remote peer. 
When "false", the local peer will not try to negotiate the SSFN with the remote peer.
shortSeqNbrFormatUsageEnabled.fullName: Short sequence number format usage enabled

endpointDiscriminatorResult.description:
This parameter indicates whether the endpoint discriminators are enabled on the ML-PPP interface.
"IN_USE" means that endpoint discriminators are used on the ML-PPP interface (i.e. endpoint discriminators were enabled with the Endpoint Discriminator Usage parameter, and could be negotiated successfully).
"NOT_IN_USE" means that endpoint discriminators are not used on the ML-PPP interface (i.e. endpoint discriminators were not enabled at all with the Endpoint Discriminator Usage parameter, or could not be negotiated successfully)

fMaxPeriodPeer.description: This parameter indicates the largest number of compressed non-TCP headers that may be sent by the peer without sending a full header.

fMaxTimePeer.description: This parameter indicates the maximum time interval in seconds between full headers supported by the remote peer.

ipHeaderCompressionResult.description:
This parameter indicates whether IP header compression (IPHC) is used on the ML-PPP interface. 
When "IN_USE", the IPHC has been enabled with IP header compression usage parameter and has been negotiated successfully. 
When "NOT_IN_USE", the IPHC has not been enabled with IP header compression usage parameter, or the negotiation has failed.
The result value depends on whether IPHC was enabled/disabled with the IP Header Compression Usage parameter.

localMrruResult.description:
This parameter indicates the result in bytes of the LCP negotiation of the local Maximum Received Reconstructed Unit (MRRU).
When Multi-Link is enabled in the remote peer, the remote normally simply acknowledges the local MRRU value, and the local MRRU Result will be equal to the Local MRRU Target. If multi-link is however not enabled in the remote peer, the peer will reject multi-link, and then local and remote peer will negotiate single-Link PPP interfaces on all designated member links. 
In this case the Local MRRU Result will be 0.

maxHeaderPeer.description: This parameter indicates the maximum header size in bytes which the remote peer can compress and decompress. The value is the result of the negotiation procedure with the remote peer.

multiClassResult.description:
The parameter indicates the multi-class negotiation result.
The negotiation result depends on the configured value for multiClassTarget.

nonTcpSpacePeer.description:
This parameter indicates the maximum value of a context identifier in the space of context
identifiers allocated for non-TCP packets and supported by the remote peer.

operationalState.description:
The operational state indicates whether the ML-PPP/PPP interface is physically existing
and working. 
When "disabled", the ML-PPP/PPP interface is totally inoperable.
When "enabled", the ML-PPP/PP interface is partially or fully operable.

p3mlRId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only PPP multi-link object. It uniquely identifies the object.
p3mlRId.fullName: Read only PPP multi-link object identifier

remoteMrru.description:
This parameter indicates the MRRU of the remote peer. The local peer simply acknowledges all MRRU values which the remote peer sends.
Note: The effective interface  MTU of the ML-PPP interface depends on the remote MRRU. It is calculated as the minimum value of
- the local configured MTU of that interface,
- the negotiated remote MRRU (i.e. the MRRU of the peer) of that interface.

shortSeqNbrFormatResult.description:
This parameter indicates whether SSNF is enabled on the ML-PPP interface. 

When "IN_USE", the SSFN has been enabled with short sequence number format usage enabled parameter and has been negotiated successfully. 
When "NOT_IN_USE", the SSFN has not been enabled with short sequence number format usage enabled parameter, or the negotiation has failed.

administrativeState.description: The administrative state allows to start and stop the SL-PPP interface. A value of "locked" means the SL-PPP interface is administratively prohibited from use. A value of "unlocked" means the SL-PPP interface is not administratively prohibited from use.

ipHeaderCompressionUsage.description:
This parameter enables the IP header compression (IPHC) negotiation on the SL-PPP interface.
When "IN_USE", the local peer will try to negotiate the IPHC with the remote peer, with a set of IPHC parameters that are acceptable for both peers. 
When "NOT_IN_USE", the local peer will not try to negotiate the IPHC with the remote peer. 
The IPHC negotiation must be enabled also on the remote peer to succeed, otherwise, both peers might negotiate an ML-PPP interface without the IPHC. 
The IP header compression result parameter shows the actual outcome of the IPHC negotiation.

p3LpDN.description:
This parameter defines which PPP link (P3LP) shall be used for a SL-PPP interface.
At maximum 1 link can be configured for one SL-PPP interface.
The PPP link is defined by giving the related distinguished name (DN) of the managed object P3LP.
Example:
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/P3LP-10

p3slId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the PPP single-link object. It uniquely identifies the object.

fMaxPeriodPeer.description: This parameter indicates the largest number of compressed non-TCP headers that may be sent by the peer without sending a full header.

fMaxTimePeer.description: This parameter indicates the maximum time interval in seconds between full headers supported by the remote peer.

ipHeaderCompressionResult.description:
This parameter indicates whether IP header compression (IPHC) is used on the SL-PPP interface. 
When "IN_USE", the IPHC has been enabled with IP header compression usage parameter and has been negotiated successfully. 
When "NOT_IN_USE", the IPHC has not been enabled with IP header compression usage parameter, or the negotiation has failed.
The resulting value depends on whether IPHC was enabled/disabled with the ipHeaderCompressionUsage parameter.

maxHeaderPeer.description: This parameter indicates the maximum header size in bytes which the remote peer can compress and decompress. The value is the result of the negotiation procedure with the remote peer.

nonTcpSpacePeer.description:
This parameter indicates the maximum value of a context identifier in the space of context
identifiers allocated for non-TCP packets and supported by the remote peer.

operationalState.description:
The operational state indicates whether the SL-PPP/PPP interface is physically existing and working. 
When "disabled", the SL-PPP/PPP interface is totally inoperable.
When "enabled", the SL-PPP/PPP interface is partially or fully operable.

p3slRId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the read only PPP single-link object. It uniquely identifies the object.

configurationType.description:
With this parameter defines the way how to define  the source.
The possible values are: 
SINGLE: a single IP address is defined.
RANGE: a range of IP addresses given by an IP address and the prefix length.
WILDCARD: any IP adress is allowed. No IP address and no prefix length is to be given.

sourceIpAddr.description:
This parameter is only meaningful if parameter configurationType has value SINGLE or RANGE.

If configurationType is set to the value SINGLE, this parameter defines the only IP address from / towards which traffic is allowed.
If configurationType is set to the value RANGE, this parameter defines the upper limit of a range of IP addresses from / towards which traffic is allowed.
Format: 
 IPv4:  IP address in dotted decimal notation
 IPv6:  IP address according to RFC4291.

sourcePrefixLength.description:
This parameter is meaningful only if parameter configurationType is defined as RANGE, in all other cases it is ignored.
This parameter defines a prefix length which, when applied to the sourceIpAddr, proviedes the allowed range of IP addresses for the source.
The value range depends on the IP address version. 
Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-31
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-127
sourcePrefixLength.fullName: Prefix length for the sorce IP address

rTPmCollEntityIpAddr.description:
This parameter contains the IP address of the Collection Entity that receives the PM Counter data, i.e. TNES IP address.

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the address 0.0.0.0, the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).
rTPmCollEntityIpAddr.fullName: Real Time Performance Monitoring Collection Entity IP Address

sdlPrimaryDestIp.description:

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:

cfgARPRange.description:
This parameter sets the ARP values in each PMQAP Profile. 
The allowed formats are:
 - a single ARP value. Example: 1 for ARP priority 1.
 - a list of ARP values and ranges of ARPs specified by the lowest and highest values of the range with a hyphen delimiter. No whitespaces or punctuation other than the comma and the hyphen range designator are allowed. Example: 1,3-5,12

cfgMCC.description: This parameter sets the MCC of the pLMNID structure.

cfgMNC.description: This parameter sets the MNC of the pLMNID structure.

cfgMNCLength.description: This parameter sets the MNC Length of the pLMNID structure.

cfgPRI.description: This parameter sets the Priority in each PMQAP Profile, used in the Radio Link Failure (RLF) related counters.  There shall be unique priority defined for each profile.

cfgQCIRange.description:
This parameter sets the QCI values in each PMQAP Profile. 
The allowed formats are:
 - a single QCI value. Example: 1 for QCI1.
 - a list of QCI values and ranges of QCIs specified by the lowest and highest values of the range with a hyphen delimiter. No whitespaces or punctuation other than the comma and the hyphen range designator are allowed. Example: 1,3-7,66,98-100,128-131

ethLinkPoEPtr.description:
This is a reference to the Ethernet link interface that the PoE is connected to.
Format: "FTM-1/ETHLK-<slot>-<phy I/F>"
where
FTM-1: = a parent instance of object class ETHLK, This is always 1 (static MO)
ETHLK-<slot>-<phy I/F>:  = an instance of object class ETHLK
For HW variant FWHX, FWHR, FWHU, FWHV the following value is allowed: 
FTM-1/ETHLK-1-2: refers to the physical Ethernet interface EIF2 (port B)

For HW variant FWHC, FW2CA, FWEB, FWHM, FWHT,  FWHY, FWHZ, FWCB, FWIF the following value is allowed: 
FTM-1/ETHLK-1-3: refers to the physical Ethernet interface EIF3 (port C)

For HW variants with 4 ports (e.g. FW2EHB, FW2QC, etc.) the following value is allowed:
FTM-1/ETHLK-1-3: refers to  the physical Ethernet interface EIF3 (port C)
Note: The default value is dependent on FZM HW variant used.
For HW variants with 3 ports (e.g. FWCB, FWHC, FWHR, FWHT, etc.): "FTM-1/ETHLK-1-3"
For HW variants with 4 ports (e.g. FW2EHB, FW2QC, etc.): "FTM-1/ETHLK-1-3"

Determines if special preemption rules shall be applied for emergency sessions.

'Other PLMNs' means either PLMNs of the cell or of cells in the same baseband pool with the same preemption profile assigned which are not in the list of preferred preemption candidates.

applyRulesForRegularUsers :

searchRestPreempCand.description:

No

Yes

lbpsCSONCtlEnabled.description:
Flag which indicates whether the cSON Solution is enabled to control the power group's cell membership and cell switch off priority order.
If lbpsCSONCtlEnabled is set to true, the cSON Solution application can create, delete and modify the power group cell list entries as well as set the power group cell switch off order and determine whether to enable the last cell to be switched off. 
If lbpsCSONCtlEnabled is set to false, the cSON Solution cannot add cells to, or remove cells from, the power group and the cSON Solution cannot change the power group cell switch off order or change the last cell switch off enabled value..
lbpsCSONCtlEnabled.fullName: Load-based power saving cSON control enabled

lbpsCellSOOrder.description:
The load-based power saving cell switch off order parameter defines the relative number within a sequence in which a cell has resources switched off if the capacity of the enabled cells in the Power Group can support the current load.
Cells have resources switched off according to Cell resource switch off order from 1 to N.

lbpsCellSOOrder value of 100 has a special meaning based on lbpsLastCellSOEnable value:
- If lbpsLastCellSOEnable is true, the cell has the lowest cell resource switch off order value.
- If lbpsLastCellSOEnable is false, the cell resources cannot be switched off.

Each cell within a power group must be assigned to a unique cell switch off order value with the exception that multiple cells may be assigned to the special value of 100.
lbpsCellSOOrder.fullName: Load-based power saving cell switch off order

lbpsDayOfWeek.description: The load-based power saving day of week parameter identifies the day of the week for which the power saving period is defined.
lbpsDayOfWeek.fullName: Load-based power saving day of week
lbpsDayOfWeek.officialRange:
0: Sun 
1: Mon 
2: Tue 
3: Wed 
4: Thu 
5: Fri 
6: Sat

lbpsDuration.description: The load-based power saving duration parameter identifies the end time of the power saving period. The power saving period begins at the lbpsStartTime and continues for lbpsDuration number of minutes.

lbpsLastCellMinLoad.description:
Defines the low-watermark for the load of the last enabled cell of a power group.

If the power group load is below the last cell low-water mark (lbpsLastCellMinLoad), the eNB will switch off a cell if the last cell switch off enabled flag (lbpsLastCellSOEnabled) is ‘true’. If there are no enabled power group cells, there is no power group load. All switched off power group cells will be switched on when not in a power saving period.
lbpsLastCellMinLoad.fullName: Load-based power saving last cell minimum load

lbpsLastCellRTXMinLoad.description:
Defines the low-watermark for the load of the last enabled cell of a power group for reduced TX power saving.
If the aggregate power group load of the enabled power group last cells* is below the last cell low-water mark for reduced TX power saving (lbpsLastCellRTXMinLoad) for a minimum duration, the eNB will switch off TX paths at the enabled power group last cells if the last cell switch off enabled flag (lbpsLastCellSOEnabled) is ‘true’. 

All switched off TX paths will be switched on at all power group cells when not in a power saving period.

* The power group last cells are either all power group cells with switch off order set to the last cell special value (lbpsCellSOOrder = 100) or if no power group cell is assigned the last cell special value, then the single enabled power group cell full TX paths with the greatest lbpsCellSOOrder value.
lbpsLastCellRTXMinLoad.fullName: Load-based power saving last cell reduced TX min load

lbpsLastCellSOEnabled.description:
Flag which determines whether the last enabled power group cell may have resources switched off and whether power group cells with the special handling cell switch off order value may have resources switched off.
If lbpsLastCellSOEnabled is true, the last enabled cell and the cells with the special handling cell switch off order value may have resources switched off.
If lbpsLastCellSOEnabled is false, neither the last enabled cell nor the cells with the special handling cell switch off order value may have resources switched off.
lbpsLastCellSOEnabled.fullName: Load-based power saving last cell switch off enabled

lbpsMaxLoad.description:
Defines the high-watermark for the aggregate load of a power group.
Two or more enabled power group cells: 
·	The eNb will not switch off a cell if the expected aggregate power group load of the remaining enabled power group cells will be above the high-water mark value of lbpsMaxLoad. 
·	If needed, the eNB will switch on power group cells in the reverse cell switch off order to increase the aggregate power group capacity until the expected power group load is below the high-water mark value of lbpsMaxLoad. 

Last enabled power group cell: 
·	If the power group load is below the last cell low-water mark (lbpsLastCellMinLoad), the eNB will switch off a cell if the last cell switch off enabled flag (lbpsLastCellSOEnabled) is ‘true’. The high-water mark is not considered as there is no expected aggregate power group load.
·	If there are no enabled power group cells, there is no power group load. All switched off power group cells will be switched on when not in a power saving period.

It is recommended that lbpsMaxLoad be less than the following load-balancing threshold parameters to reduce the chance that load-balancing will be initiated for one of the remaining enabled power group cells:

LNCEL:: intraFreqLbLoadThresholds parameters:
highLoadGbrDl,
highLoadNonGbrDl, and
highLoadPdcchDl.

LNCEL::iFLBLoadThresholds parameters:
iFLBHighLoadGBRDL,
iFLBHighLoadNonGBRDL, and
iFLBHighLoadPdcch.

It is recommended to set lbpsMaxLoad > 2*lbpsMinLoad to avoid a situation where a cell is switched off due to the power group load being below lbpsMinLoad and within a few minutes is switched on due to the power group load increasing above lbpsMaxLoad.

lbpsMinLoad.description:
Defines the low-watermark for the aggregate load of a power group.
The eNB will switch off a power group cell in cell switch off order if the aggregate power group load is less than the low-watermark value of lbpsMinLoad and the expected aggregate power group load for the reduced aggregate power group capacity is less than the high-water mark value of lbpsMaxLoad.

lbpsMinLoad is used except when determining whether the last enabled cell in the Power Group may be switched off (see lbpsLastCellMinLoad).

It is recommended to set lbpsMinLoad < lbpsMaxLoad/2 to avoid a situation where a cell is switched off due to the power group load being below lbpsMinLoad and within a few minutes is switched on due to the power group load increasing above lbpsMaxLoad.

lbpsPdcchLoadOffset.description:
Offset subtracted from the sum of normalized PDCCH load of each enabled power group cell.

The power group PDCCH load average may be greater than the power group GBR and non-GBR load averages. Load-based power saving PDCCH load offset (lbpsPdcchLoadOffset) is applied to align the power group PDCCH load average with the power group GBR and non-GBR load averages.

If the power group PDCCH load average is less than lbpsPdcchLoadOffset, then the power group PDCCH load average is set to 0%.
lbpsPdcchLoadOffset.fullName: Load-based power saving PDCCH load offset

lbpsRTXCellCapOffset.description:
Defines the percent cell throughput at a reduced TX path cell relative to the full TX path cell throughput expected due to the change in supported transmission mode due to reduction in cell TX paths.
The cell throughput is expected to be decrease due to the change in supported transmission mode by the cell with reduced TX paths.
lbpsRTXCellCapOffset.fullName: Load-based power saving reduced TX cell capacity offset

lbpsRTXMaxLoad.description:
Defines the high-watermark for the aggregate load of a power group for reduced TX power saving.
One or more enabled power group cells with all TX paths enabled: 
- The eNb will not switch off TX paths at a cell if the expected aggregate power group load of the enabled power group cells will be above the high-water mark for reduced TX value of lbpsRTXMaxLoad. 
- If the aggregate power group load is at or above the high-water mark for a minimum duration, the eNB will switch on TX paths of power group cells in the reverse cell switch off order to increase the aggregate power group capacity until the expected power group load is below the high-water mark for reduced TX value of lbpsRTXMaxLoad. 

All switched off TX paths will be switched on at all power group cells when not in a power saving period.

It is recommended that lbpsRTXMaxLoad be less than the following load-balancing threshold parameters to reduce the chance that load-balancing will be initiated for one of the enabled power group cells with reduced TX paths:

LNCEL:: intraFreqLbLoadThresholds parameters:
highLoadGbrDl,
highLoadNonGbrDl, and
highLoadPdcchDl.

LNCEL::iFLBLoadThresholds parameters:
iFLBHighLoadGBRDL,
iFLBHighLoadNonGBRDL, and
iFLBHighLoadPdcch.

It is recommended to activate load-equalization (LNBTS:actAmle) to further reduce the chance that load-balancing will be initiated for one of the enabled power group cells with reduced TX paths.

Note: lbpsRTXMaxLoad is for the average load across the set of power group cells while the referenced load-balancing load parameters are for a single cell. Hence, these recommendation reduce the chance that load-balancing will be initiated at a power group cell and do not eliminate the chance.

It is recommended to set lbpsMaxLoad > 2*lbpsMinLoad to avoid a situation where a cell is switched off due to the power group load being below lbpsMinLoad and within a few minutes is switched on due to the power group load increasing above lbpsMaxLoad.
lbpsRTXMaxLoad.fullName: Load-based power saving reduced TX maximum load

lbpsRTXMinLoad.description:
Defines the low-watermark for the aggregate load of a power group for reduced TX power saving.
The eNB will switch off TX paths of a power group cell in cell switch off order if the aggregate power group load is less than the low-watermark for reduced TX power saving value of lbpsRTXMinLoad for a minimum duration and the expected aggregate power group load for the reduced aggregate power group capacity is less than the high-water mark for reduced TX power saving value of lbpsRTXMaxLoad.

lbpsRTXMinLoad is used except when determining whether the last enabled cell in the Power Group with all TX paths enabled may have its TX paths switched off (see lbpsLastCellRTXMinLoad).

All switched off TX paths will be switched on at all power group cells when not in a power saving period.

It is recommended to set lbpsRTXMinLoad < lbpsRTXMaxLoad/2 to avoid a situation where a cell has its TX paths switched off due to the power group load being below lbpsRTXMinLoad and within a few minutes is switched on due to the power group load increasing above lbpsRTXMaxLoad.
lbpsRTXMinLoad.fullName: Load-based power saving reduced TX minimum load

pHB.description:
This parameter designates a per hop behaviour wird drop precedence within the PHB class group for Assured Forwarding (AF) or the PHB classes Best Effort (BE) or Expedited Forwarding (EF).
4 PHB classes are defined within the Assured Forwarding group (AF1 to AF4) and three drop precedences within each class. Within each class the drop precedence is as follows: 1 (e.g. AF41) = low drop precedence, 2 (e.g. AF42) = medium drop precedence and 3 ( e.g. AF43) = high drop precedence.

trafficType.description:
This parameter specifies a traffic type.
Allowed values are:
CPLANE: Signalling transport (C-plane) between eNB and MME (S1AP protocol) and signalling transport between eNB nodes (X2AP protocol).
ICMP: ICMP traffic with high and low priority.
IKE: IPSec IKE traffic.
MPLANE: Transport of O&M data  between eNB and the OPS System with high and low priority.
SPLANE: Synchronization plane traffic (Timing over Packet)
BFD(BFD1 to BFD16): Bidirectional Forwarding Detection
SSE: Site Support Equipment
HighPrioICMPv6: ICMPv6 traffic with high and low priority.

addGsmSIToRedirMsg.description:
The parameter selects the kinds of UE redirections (CS fallback, UE redirection with context release, both) for which GSM system information is included in the RRC Connection Release message.
GSM system information (SI) will be added for up to 16 cells. SI for further GSM cells will be omitted even if configured via LNLRELG settings.
addGsmSIToRedirMsg.fullName: Add GSM system information to redirection message

addUtranSIToRedirMsg.description:
The parameter selects the kinds of UE redirections (CS fallback, UE redirection with context release, both) for which UTRAN system information shall be included in the RRC Connection Release message.
UTRAN system information (SI) will be added for up to 16 cells. SI for further UTRAN cells will be omitted even if configured via LNRELW settings.
addUtranSIToRedirMsg.fullName: Add UTRAN system information to redirection message

csFallBPrio.description:
This parameter defines priority for target RAT in selection of redirection target during CS Fallback with redirection procedure.
Value 1 means highest priority and value 6 lowest.
csFallBPrio.fullName: Redirection priority for CS fallback with redirection

emerCallPrio.description:
This parameter defines priority for target RAT in selection of redirection target during Emergency Call handling procedure.
Value 1 means highest priority and value 6 lowest.

redirBandCdma.description:
This parameter must be configured if redirRAT=cdma2000-HRPD or redirRAT=cdma2000-1xRTT.
Specifies the cdma2000 band class.

redirFreqCdma.description:
Specifies the cdma2000 ARFCN.
The parameter value is based on the absolute radio-frequency channel number “ARFCN”.

This parameter must be configured if redirRAT=cdma2000-HRPD or redirRAT=cdma2000-1xRTT.

redirFreqEutra.description:
Specifies the eUTRA frequency (max value ref to 36.331)
The parameter value is based on the absolute radio-frequency channel number “ARFCN”.

This parameter must be configured if redirRAT=eutra.

redirFreqUtra.description:
This parameter specifies the UTRA frequency. It must be configured if redirRAT=utraFDD.
The parameter value is based on the absolute radio-frequency channel number “ARFCN”.

redirFreqUtraTDDL.description:
This parameter specifies a list of UTRA TDD frequency.
The parameter value is based on the absolute radio-frequency channel number “ARFCN”.

This parameter must be configured if redirRAT=utraTDD.

redirGeranArfcnPrio.description:
The parameter specifies a priority order for GERAN ARFCN value according to which eNB shall built list of GERAN targets (CarrierFreqsGERAN IE of RedirectedCarrierInfo IE) in RRCConnectionRelease message with CSFB to GERAN via redirection.
GERAN ARFCN carriers will be placed in explicitListOfARFCNs IE as a choice of CarrierFreqsGERAN IE of RedirectedCarrierInfo IE in order of 'GERAN ARFCN priority order' value  starting from lowest value to highest configured by operator. GERAN ARFCN values without configured 'GERAN ARFCN priority order' will be placed at the end of list.

redirGeranArfcnValue.description: The parameter specifies a  GERAN ARFCN value.

redirGeranBandIndicator.description:
Indicator to distinguish the GERAN frequency band in case of ARFCN values associated with either GSM 1800 or GSM 1900 carriers.
For ARFCN values not associated with one of those bands, the indicator has no meaning.
This parameter must always be configured if redirRAT=geran.

angle.description: The elevation angle between the direction orthogonal to the antenna element axis and the maximum of its main beam in the elevation plane. A positive electrical tilt angle means that the antenna beam is directed below the direction orthogonal to the antenna axis. The user sets the parameter value at least once according to the configuration/network plan. Otherwise, the present value (factory or old setting) exists. Setting tilt angle of a RET device might take up to 2 minutes according to 3GPP stardards. A typical time for the calibration is approximately 15-30 seconds. According to 3GPP standards, setting tilt of several devices connected onto one antenna line is done as a series of consecutive operation by the system. In addition, set tilt and calibration (for more details of calibration, see calibrate parameter documentation) are done as consecutive operations. When such a situation occurs, accumulative time for the operations may be increased long enough as to not be feasible to be activated in one plan. Thus, in such case, time consuming operations should be devided into the 2 or more plans.

fwdTestDisp.description:
Indicates if the forward tests passed or failed based on comparison to the RF diagnostic threshold values
Pass means that all forward measured values were within the range of the configured threshold values for the forward measurements.
Fail means that one or more of forward measured values were not with in the range of the configured threshold values.
Forward measurement values of zero (the measurement was not available) are not used in calculalting the test disposition.

result.description: Value defines result of the RF Test command.

rtwp.description:
Received Total Wideband Power value.
Unit for the parameter is  dBm. When the measurement is not available for the current test the value is set to zero.
The value of this parameter is expected to be in the range -180...0 with step of 0.1. However, a value outside this expected range may occur.

rvrsTestDisp.description:
Indicates if the reserve test passed or failed based on comparison to the RF diagnostic threshold values
Pass means that the reverse measured value was within the range of the configured threshold values for the reverse measurement.
Fail means that reverse measured value was not with in the range of the configured threshold value.
Reverse measurement value of zero (the measurement was not available) will cause the test disposition to be set to pass.

testOutcome.description:
The outcome of the Remote RF Diagnostic  test
Inconclusive means that the test could not be completed. There are no detailed results available.

Pass means the test was completed and that both Forward test disposition and Reverse test disposition results have a value of pass.

Failed means the test was completed and but either Forward test disposition or Reverse test disposition results has a value of fail.

allowRITest.description:
This paramter controls whether it is allowed to send Remote Rnterference specific sequence manually for test purpose.
If the parameter is set to "true", the cell will send own RI specific sequence expressing eNB RI specific identity at the last 2 symbols of legacy DwPTS in a period of 163840 GPS seconds .
The detail sequence index and sending time are determined by 'eNB RI specific identity'.
allowRITest.fullName: Allowance of TDD Remote Interference specific sequence sending for test purpose

allowRollDwPts.description:
This paramter controls whether this cell is allowed to rollback DwPTS of special subframe as SSP5 (3:9:2) if it is confirmed as the remote interference source.
If the parameter is set to "true", the cell may be ready to rollback DwPTS as ssp5 once the number of RI sequence detected exceed threshold. It should be known that this action might result in downlink througput loss due to legacy DwPTS symbols are unavailable
allowRollDwPts.fullName: Allowance of rollback DwPTS of special subframe to SSP5 (3:9:2)

lowerThresRIUl.description:
This parameter indicates the lower threshold per RB for Remote Interference detected on UpPTS and the first uplink subframe(dBm).
If detected interference was lower than it, remote interference is deemed as disappearance.
lowerThresRIUl.fullName: The lower threshold per RB for Remote Interference detected on UpPTS and the first uplink subframe(dBm)

lowerThresRIUpPts.description: The lower threshold for Remote Interference detected (dBm).
lowerThresRIUpPts.fullName: The lower threshold for Remote Interference detected

maxPowerDiffJointRISpecSeq.description:
This parameter indicated the threshold of signal power difference for jointing Remote interference specific sequences detected in 1st half-frame and 2nd half-frame.
Only if the signal power difference of two sequences is lower than this threshold, they will be available for joint.
maxPowerDiffJointRISpecSeq.fullName: The threshold of signal power difference for jointing Remote Interference specific sequences detected in 1st half-frame and 2nd half-frame

numHfRIUl.description: This parameter indicates the monitoring window length (in term of number of half-frame) of Remote Interference detection and disappearance in UpPTS or the first uplink subframe.
numHfRIUl.fullName: The monitoring window length (the number of half-frame) of Remote Interference detection and disappearance in UpPTS or the first uplink subframe.

numMinuteRISpecSeqUl.description: This parameter indicates the monitoring window length (minutes) of Remote Interference specific sequence detection and disappearance in UpPTS and the first uplink subframe.
numMinuteRISpecSeqUl.fullName: The monitoring window length (minutes) of Remote Interference specific sequence detection and disappearance in UpPTS and the first uplink subframe.

numSfRIUpPts.description: This parameter indicates the monitoring window length (number of subframe) of Remote Interference detection and disappearance in UpPTS.
numSfRIUpPts.fullName: The monitoring window length (the number of subframe) of Remote Interference detection and disappearance in UpPTS.

numThresRIRecov.description: This parameter indicates the threshold of times(N3) for detecting Remote Interference specific sequence. If the times of external RI specific sequence was detected not exceed this threshold, the cell may trigger to recover DwPTS to legacy configuration and stop sending RI sequence.
numThresRIRecov.fullName: The threshold of times(N3) for detecting Remote Interference specific sequence for recovering DwPTS rollback and stopping sending RI sequence purpose.

numThresRIRoll.description: This parameter indicates the threshold of times(N2) for detecting Remote Interference specific sequence. If the times of external RI specific sequence was detected exceed this threshold, the cell may trigger DwPTS rollback as SSP5
numThresRIRoll.fullName: The threshold of times(N2) for detecting Remote Interference specific sequence for DwPTS rollback purpose.

numThresRISpecSeqSending.description: This parameter indicates the threshold of times(N1) for detecting Remote Interference specific sequence for purpose of own RI specific sequence sending. If the times of external RI specific sequence was detected exceed this threshold, the cell will trigger to broadcast its own RI specific sequence.
numThresRISpecSeqSending.fullName: The threshold of times(N1) for detecting Remote Interference specific sequence for purpose of own RI specific sequence sending.

This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC RIM.
It uniquely identifies a RIM instance.

UTRAN RNC identifier to be blacklisted for RIM
The UTRAN Cell Global Id is built as a 28 bit value. It consists either
- of a 12 bit RNC-ID (range 0..4095) and a 16 bit UTRAN Cell ID (range 0..65535) or
- of a 16 bit Extended RNC-Id (range 4096..65535) and a 12 bit UTRAN Cell ID (range 0..4095).

tRimKaG.description:
This timer is started when eNB receives a valid RAN-INFORMATION/Initial Multiple Report PDU.
This timer is restarted when eNB receives  subsequent RAN-INFORMATION/Multiple Report PDU.
When the timer expires the eNB re-sends the RAN-INFORMATION-REQUEST/Multiple Report PDU.
Refer to [RIM.359].
tRimKaG.fullName: Timer to wait for next RI PDU from GERAN

tRimKaU.description:
This timer is started when eNB receives a valid RAN-INFORMATION/Initial Multiple Report PDU from UTRAN.
This timer is restarted when eNB receives  subsequent RAN-INFORMATION/Multiple Report PDU.
When the timer expires the eNB re-sends the RAN-INFORMATION-REQUEST/Multiple Report PDU.
Refer to [RIM.514].
tRimKaU.fullName: Timer to wait for next RI PDU from UTRAN

tRimPollG.description:
This timer is started when RIM procedure for a GERAN neighbor cell fails or ends.
When the timer expires the eNB re-starts RAN-INFORMATION-REQUEST/Multiple Report procedure for the GERAN neighbor cell. 

Note: If this timer’s length is set to a short value (e.g. 5 minutes), the re-sending RIM PDUs may visibly increase the S1 link traffic.
tRimPollG.fullName: Polling timer to ReStart RIR Procedure to GERAN

tRimPollU.description:
This timer is started when RIM procedure for a UTRAN neighbor cell fails or ends.
When the timer expires the eNB re-starts RAN-INFORMATION-REQUEST/Multiple Report procedure for the UTRAN neighbor cell. 

Note: If this timer’s length is set to a short value (e.g. 5 minutes), the re-sending RIM PDUs may visibly increase the S1 link traffic.
tRimPollU.fullName: Polling timer to ReStart RIR procedure to UTRAN

tRimRirG.description:
This timer is started when eNB sends out a RAN-INFORMATION-REQUEST/Mutiple Report message. 
When the timer expires the eNB  re-sends the RIM message up to nRimRirG(see [CCPM.9031]) times.
tRimRirG.fullName: Timer to wait for RIR Response from GERAN

tRimRirU.description:
This timer is started when eNB sends out a RAN-INFORMATION-REQUEST/Mutiple Report message to UTRAN. 
When the timer expires the eNB  re-sends the RIM message up to nRimRirU(see [CCPM.20156]) times.
tRimRirU.fullName: Timer to wait for RIR response from UTRAN

actParExpansionOff.description: Turns off the radio module's PAR (Peak-to-Average power Ratio) expansion / crest-factor-reduction behavior, which otherwise trades some efficiency for reduced signal peaks.

actPimCancellation.description: This parameter activates feature PIM Cancellation for an RMOD of a type and version that supports passive inter-modulation (PIM) cancellation.

actSharedRUIndControl.description: Activates independent control/indication handling for a Radio Unit that is shared between multiple basebands or operators (RAN/multi-operator sharing scenario).

actSnapshotCollection.description:
When this parameter is set to true, the BTS triggers automatic symptom data collection in the following conditions, 'after' the radio module recovers:
-Unexpected loss of communication with radio, recovered without radio reset
-Autonomous radio reset for fault recovery

When this parameter is set to false,  automatic symptom data collection is not triggered in the above scenarios.

administrativeState.description:
Administrative state of the cell, the value is set by the operator.
Note: This parameter used for NB-IoT standalone cell.

alVoltHighThreshold.description: High-voltage alarm threshold for the radio module's DC power supply; exceeding it raises an alarm.

alVoltLowThreshold.description: Low-voltage alarm threshold for the radio module's DC power supply; dropping below it raises an alarm.

alVoltUnstableThreshold.description: Voltage-fluctuation threshold used to detect an 'unstable' DC power condition on the radio module and raise an alarm.

aldManagementProtocol.description: This parameter indicates the actual ALD (Antenna Line Device) management protocol used when connected to a CPRI-A radio module.

climateControlProfiling.description:
Climate control Profiling parameter.
Fan speed will be controlled according to module temperature and desired BTS fan profile.
- Low Noise: Minimised noise for low and moderate ambient temperatures
- Optimized Cooling: Maximised unit MTBF (long life) by running fans with maximum speed already in
moderate ambient temperatures
- Linear: An intermediate profile which increases fan speed linearly as temperature increase.
 
It is possible to select fan control profiles independently for each module in the BTS.

If user does not want to define fan profiling or module does not support fan profiles, the BTS manager will not set a value to SCF.

Parameter values are: "Optimized Cooling", "Linear" and "Low Noise". Default value is "Optimized Cooling".

cpriARfSharing.description:
This parameter indicates the role of LTE in managing the CPRI-A radio.

STANDALONE - default. There is no sharing of the radio with CDMA. LTE is fully responsible for managing the radio module.
SECONDARY - There is sharing with CDMA and LTE has the secondary role.

digitalCombinerMode.description:
This parameter controls Radio Digital Combiner function when operating in 4T transmit mode. 
• When the parameter is set to 'disable', the digital portion of the combiner is disabled.
• When the parameter is set to 'enable', the digital portion of the combiner is enabled.
• When the parameter is set to 'auto', the following is applied:
Butler Matrix is enabled if following conditions are TRUE 
- If two or more cells are a igned to the radio, or 
- If a cell with 2T configuration is a igned to the radio, or 
- If parameter LNCEL.pMax (max cell power) is le than the internal digital combiner minimum power where UHFA will be set to 41.2 dBm and UHIE will be set to 43.0 dBm. 
Else, 
Butler Matrix will be disabled
• When the parameter is not configured, it is the same as setting it to 'enable'.

energySavingMode.description: Power-saving operating mode of the radio module, e.g. Normal (full power) versus a reduced-power state.

groupName.description:
The user can freely define any site specific information with this parameter. 
Note: The parameter is persistently stored but not used/modified by the BTS.

intPIMLevelMeasurementMajorThreshold.description: The parameter is used to determine when to trigger the ‘PIM Performance Measurement Out-of-Correction Range’ fault. The fault is issued if the level of PIM measurement in the antenna line of RX path exceeds the value of configured internal PIM level measurement major threshold value for a fixed fault raising delay. The fault is cancelled if the level of measured PIM in the antenna line is below or equal to the value of configured internal PIM level measurement major threshold for a fixed fault clearing delay.
intPIMLevelMeasurementMajorThreshold.fullName: Internal PIM level measurement major threshold

intPIMLevelMeasurementMinorThreshold.description: The parameter is used to determine when to trigger the ‘PIM Performance Measurement Threshold 2 Exceeded’ fault. The fault is issued if the level of PIM measurement in the antenna line of RX path exceeds the value of configured internal PIM level measurement minor threshold value for a fixed fault raising delay. The fault is cancelled if the level of measured PIM measurement in the antenna line is below or equal to the value of configured internal PIM level measurement minor threshold for a fixed fault clearing delay.
intPIMLevelMeasurementMinorThreshold.fullName: Internal PIM level measurement minor threshold

moduleLocation.description:
Defines a location of the radio module in free text with maximum 50 characters.  Location can be e.g. place or address of the module.

The range represents the number of bytes to store all the characters of the string. If the string is UTF-8 encoded, each character occupies between 1 to 4 bytes, depending upon the language. If ASCII encoded, each character occupies a single byte. The numbers of characters supported in case of UTF-8 encoding is at least 12.

pimCancellingEnabled.description:
This parameter enables or disables the cancelling of the passive inter-modulation (PIM) interference from the received signal at a radio module that has the PIM Cancellation feature activated.

The PIM cancellation algorithm removes the passive inter-modulation interference which is introduced into the uplink signal. 
PIM performance counters and PIM performance threshold alarms remain active as long as the actPIMCancellation parameter is 'true'.

This parameter is ignored if actPIMCancellation parameter is 'false'.

protocol.description:
This parameter defines the protocol information of the IP packet.
If the parameter has value -1, the policy is valid for all protocols.
The value 0...254 refers to the protocol number in the IP header.
Example: TCP=6 and UDP=17

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.

radioMemAbnormalThreshold.description:
This parameter defines the abnormal memory threshold on the radio module.
When the memory consumption on the radio module exceeds the abnormal threshold, an alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds abnormal threshold’ is  raised. When the memory consumption on the radio module falls below the abnormal threshold, the alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds abnormal threshold’ is cleared.
This parameter is defined as a relative value, where the lower bound value of 0% indicates expected average memory consumption.
When abnormal memory threshold is set to 100%, the alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds abnormal threshold’ is not raised and alarm with fault ‘Radio memory consumption exceeds critical threshold’ is directly raised.

rfmTransmitMode.description:
This parameter configures the transmit mode of a CPRI-A radio that supports transmit switching.

STANDARD - default.  - For 1T/2T switching supported radios, this would result in 2T.  For 2T/4T switching supported radios, this would result in 2T. 
DOUBLEPOWER - For 1T/2T switching supported radios, this would result in 1T.

If this parameter is configured on a radio that does not support transmit mode switching, it is being ignored.

STANDARD - For radio modules supporting 1T/2T switching, the radio is operating in default 2T mode. For radios supporting 2T/4T switching, the radio is operating in default 2T mode.
DOUBLEPOWER - For radio modules supporting 1T/2T switching, the radio is configured to allow 1T.
NOTSUPPORTED - The radio module does not support transmit switching or does not support the transmit switching mode specified by EQM/APEQM/RMOD/rfmTransmitMode.

routingTableDN.description:

routingTablePtr.description:
A reference to a routing table. This is a distinguished name referencing an instance of class IPRT or IPRTV6.
Format: "FTM-1/IPNO-1/IPRT-1" or  "FTM-1/IPNO-1/IPRTV6-1"

where
FTM-1: = a parent instance of object class IPNO, This is always 1 (static MO)
IPNO-1: = a parent instance of object class IPRT, 
IPRT-#: # = an instance of object class IPRT
IPRTV6-#: # = an instance of object class IPRTV6

A policy may refer also to the main routing table.

Example: FTM-1/IPNO-1/IPRT-1

Note: FSMr2 supports only IPRT-1.

assocMaxRetrans.description: This is the number of unanswered heartbeat messages or data acknowledgements (within a time defined by RTO/T3-rtx and calculated internally in SCTP), used for declaring the SCTP association failure.

maxTimeSctpSetup.description:
When an X2 link establishment attempt is triggered for an eNB Controlled X2 link or for an X2 link to gNB, eNB attempts at most for the time 'maxTimeSctpSetup' to establish the respective SCTP association, before assuming that the SCTP association establishment failed.

Note: In case of long maxTimeSctpSetup interval it might happen that SCTP layer has already finished  transmitting SCTP INIT sequence before maxTimeSctpSetup expires. In case of short maxTimeSctpSetup interval, the eNB signalling application will finish SCTP INIT retransmission before SCTP computed time interval expires.
maxTimeSctpSetup.fullName: Maximum time to wait for a new SCTP establishment

pathMaxRetrans.description: This is the number of unanswered heartbeat messages or data acknowledgements (within a time defined by RTO/T3-rtx and calculated internally in SCTP), used for declaring SCTP path failure.

rtoMax.description: This parameter specifies the maximum value for retransmission timer T3-rtx when DATA or heartbeat was sent and no ACK has come back. Used for SCTP calculation range.

rtoMin.description: This parameter specifies the minimum value for retransmission timer T3-rtx when DATA or heartbeat was sent and no ACK has come back. Used for the SCTP calculation range.

sctpHeartbeatInterval.description: This parameter defines the interval between two SCTP heartbeat messages, counted in seconds.

sctpId.description: This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SCTP.

sctpMaxPayloadSize.description: This parameter defines the maximum number of octets in an SCTP packet available for chunks.

sctpSackDelay.description:
This parameter specifies the maximum time period the SCTP receiver waits before sending a Sack. 
This parameter specifies the time period the SCTP receiver waits before sending a Sack. The SCTP receiver sends a SACK before the timer expires if the number of received frames achieves the value of the parametre selective acknowledge frequeincy (sctpSackFreq).

sctpSackFreq.description:
This parameter specifies the number of SCTP frames that the SCTP receiver is allowed to receive before it sends a SACK.
This parameter specifies the number of SCTP frames that the SCTP receiver is allowed to receive before it sends a SACK. The SCTP receiver shall send a Sack if the waiting time (sctpSackDelay) for receiving this number of frames expires.

sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetry.description:
This parameter defines the wait time the eNB waits until it tries to re-initialize the SCTP association (S1 and X2 OAM controlled)
Case A: after having tried unsucessfully to establish an association to a peer with a SCTP sequence  
Case B: After reception of SCTP SHUTDOWN/ABORT
The value defines a fixed time period. In addition, eNB adds an equally distributed random time period between 0 and 60s to the configured value.

This prevents the eNBs to which the network element that has sent the SCTP shutdown command (e.g. MME) will be overflooded by SCTP intialization from multiple eNBs.
sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetry.fullName: Wait Time before starting SCTP init after shutdown

sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetryM3.description:
This parameter defines the M3 wait time the eNB waits until it tries to re-initialize the SCTP association
Case A: after having tried unsucessfully to establish an association to a peer with a SCTP sequence  
Case B: After reception of SCTP SHUTDOWN/ABORT
The value defines a fixed time period. In addition, eNB adds an equally distributed random time period between 0 and 10s to the configured value.

This prevents the eNBs to which the network element that has sent the SCTP shutdown command (e.g. MME) will be overflooded by SCTP intialization from multiple eNBs.
sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetryM3.fullName: M3 wait Time before starting SCTP init

sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetryS1.description:
This parameter defines the S1 wait time the eNB waits until it tries to re-initialize the SCTP association
Case A: after having tried unsucessfully to establish an association to a peer with a SCTP sequence  
Case B: After reception of SCTP SHUTDOWN/ABORT
The value defines a fixed time period. In addition, eNB adds an equally distributed random time period between 0 and 10s to the configured value.

This prevents the eNBs to which the network element that has sent the SCTP shutdown command (e.g. MME) will be overflooded by SCTP intialization from multiple eNBs.
sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetryS1.fullName: S1 wait Time before starting SCTP init

sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetryX2.description:
This parameter defines the X2 wait time the eNB waits until it tries to re-initialize the SCTP association (X2 OAM controlled)
Case A: after having tried unsucessfully to establish an association to a peer with a SCTP sequence  
Case B: After reception of SCTP SHUTDOWN/ABORT
The value defines a fixed time period. In addition, eNB adds an equally distributed random time period between 0 and 60s to the configured value.

This prevents the eNBs to which the network element that has sent the SCTP shutdown command (e.g. MME) will be overflooded by SCTP intialization from multiple eNBs.
sctpWaitTimeInitSeqRetryX2.fullName: X2 wait Time before starting SCTP init

drxInactivityT.description:
Configures the Inactivity Timer for DRX.
The Inactivity Timer determines the number of consecutive PDCCH-subframes for which the UE monitors the PDCCH after decoding an UL or DL resource assignment on PDCCH for an initial data transmission.

Note: It is not recommended to set this timer to shorter values than the default value to allow for sufficient scheduling flexibility.

drxLongCycle.description:
Configures the long DRX cycle. 
The long DRX cycle determines the periodic repetition of the DRX On Duration.

drxOnDuratT.description:
Configures the On Duration Timer for DRX.
The On Duration determines the number of consecutive PDCCH-subframes at the beginning of a DRX cycle during which the UE monitors the PDCCH.

Note: It is not recommended to set this timer to shorter values than the default value to allow for sufficient scheduling flexibility.

drxProfileIndex.description:
Smart DRX profile index.
Uniquely identifies a DRX profile.

drxProfilePriority.description:
Smart DRX profile priority.

Applied to identify the Smart DRX profile to be used if a UE has multiple bearers established.
Note: Modification of Smart DRX profile priority is not recommended; preparation for future use.

drxRetransT.description:
Configures the Retransmission Timer for DRX.
The Retransmission Timer determines the maximum number of PDCCH-subframes a UE monitors the PDCCH as soon as a retransmission in DL is expected by the UE.

Note: It is not recommended to set this timer to shorter values than the recommended default value to allow for sufficient scheduling flexibility.

drxShortCycle.description:
Configures the short DRX cycle. 
It is recommended to set this parameter equal to the drxLongCycle in order to optimize battery consumption during VoLTE calls.

drxShortCycleT.description:
Configures the short DRX cycle timer. 
Integer value multiplied with drxShortCycle to determine the run time of short DRX cycle.

sDrxId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SDRX.
It uniquely identifies a SDRX instance.

smartStInactFactor.description:
Factor is used for the calculation of the Short Term Inactivity Timer (STIS) when Smart DRX is used.
smartStInactFactor is multiplied to the short DRX cycle duration to provide STIT value for smart DRX profile.
smartStInactFactor.fullName: Short term inactivity factor for smart DRX

keyContinuation.description:

“on”: the ssh keys defined in the "Service user public keys " parameter are also re-used to escalate to  toor4nsn.

“off”: the ssh keys defined in the "Service user public keys " parameter are not re-used to escalate to  toor4nsn. Keys for the toor4nsn account are maintained separately.

keyDescription.description:

The parameter value should start with the string 'ssh', and cannot have line breaks. Operator is responsible to enter correct value.
