ikePDN.description:
This parameter defines which IKE profile shall be used for this policy.

It can be a direct reference to an instance of an IKE profile or 
a reference to an IKE protection group.
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN):

Examples:
 - MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPAPP-1/IPSECC-1/IKEP-1
 - MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPAPP-1/IPSECC-1/IKEPROTGRP-1

ipSecAction.description:
This parameter defines the basic treatment of a traffic data packet that applies to the selection criteria of this policy.
The following are the allowed values for this parameter and their description:
"DISCARD": The packet is discarded without any further action or notification, that is, it is prevented from passing to its designated destination.
"BYPASS": The packet is delivered to its destination without any other processing, in particular, without any further IPsec-related processing.
"PROTECT": The packet will be made subject to the settings of its security policy.

ipSecPDN.description:
This parameter defines which IPSec profile shall be used for this policy.

The IPSec profile is defined by giving the distinguished name (DN).
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPAPP-1/IPSECC-1/IPSECP-1

localIpAddress.description:
This parameter defines the local IP address of the data traffic packet for this policy as seen by the NE.
IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported.
IPv4 address format: Dot-decimal notation (x.x.x.x). Example: 10.10.10.10.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers and protocol are feasible:
- a single IP address (Any/AnyIPv4/AnyIPv6), no particular protocol/port 
- a single IP address, selected protocol/port
- an IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- an IP subnet, selected protocol/port.

Note: In order to define any IP address (wildcard) the following value has to be given.
- IPv4: 0.0.0.0
- IPv6: 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0

localIpPort.description:
This parameter defines the port number of the local IP address. If value -1 is defined, the IPsec policy is valid in the same way to and from all ports of the local IP address.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address, no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.
localIpPort.fullName: Port number of the local IP address

localIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter defines the prefix length.
Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-32
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-128

policyOrderNumber.description:
This parameter defines the order number of the security policy. Only the lowest number of several equally matching policies will be executed on a specific traffic data packet.
The policy order number must be defined with a unique value across all SECPOL instances.
The BTS supports the dynamic creation of security policies. For each autonomously created security policy the BTS will always use the lowest currently available value (the highest priority) of the policyOrderNumber. For manually created security policies it is recommended to use policyOrderNumber values higher than 1000 (so that automatically created security policies will take precedence over manually configured policies). This ensures that there will be no unintended behavior or conflict between manually created security policies and autonomously  created security policies.

protocol.description:
This parameter defines the protocol information of the IP packet.
If the parameter has value -1, the policy is valid for all protocols.
The value 0...254 refers to the protocol number in the IP header.
Example: TCP=6 and UDP=17

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.

remoteIpAddress.description:
This parameter defines the remote IP address of the data traffic packet for this policy as seen by the NE. 
IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported.
IPv4 address format: Dot-decimal notation (x.x.x.x). Example: 10.10.10.10.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

Note: In order to define any IP address (wildcard) the following value has to be given.
- IPv4: 0.0.0.0
- IPv6: 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:0

remoteIpPort.description:
This parameter defines the port number of the remote IP address. If value -1 is configured, the IPsec policy is valid in the same way to and from all ports of the remote IP address.

The following combinations of local and remote IP addresses, local and remote port numbers  and protocol are feasible:
- single IP address (equivalent to netmask /32 in IPv4), no particular protocol/port 
- single IP address, selected protocol/port
- IP subnet, no particular protocol/port
- IP subnet, selected protocol/port.
remoteIpPort.fullName: Port of the remote IP address

remoteIpPrefixLength.description:
This parameter defines the prefix length.
Prefix length for IPV4 : 0-32
Prefix length for IPV6 : 0-128

secPolId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the security policy object. It uniquely identifies the object.
It is highly recommended to use for object creation the lowest free secPolId value within all SECPOL instances of the BTS.
This will ensure that there will be no conflicts between manually configured SECPOL instances and autonomously created SECPOL instances by the BTS.
If enabled, the BTS can support the autonomous creation of SECPOL instances. For this the BTS will always use the highest free secPolId value.

NOTE: IPSec is not supported on FSMFA (473585A) and ASIAB (474587A).

triggerDN.description:
This parameter defines the Trigger that shall activate this policy. The parameter value shall match one of the object instance identifiers of the Trigger managed object class.
An empty value means the policy is not linked to any Trigger, while a trigger state of "TRUE" will activate this policy. Otherwise, this policy will be not applied.
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example: 
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/TRIGGER-1

acbECTimer.description:
When emergency call barring timer expires emergency calls will be barred automatically if configured so by the ACBPR-eCallAcBarredAuto parameter. 
If the previous ACB level (Max threshold and ACB Skip IEs are deactivated) lasts for at least acbEcTimer, emergency calls may be barred if configured so by ACBPR-eCallAcbarredAuto.
The timer is configured in counter mode as multiplicity of acbUpdateTimer.

Note: If the timer is not configured that means that SIB2 ac-barringForEmergency will be set to FALSE or TRUE according to ACBPR-eCallAcBarredAuto settings.

acbImmediateMax.description: This parameter defines change in step-wise AC Barring algorithm behavior and allows to immediately go to the most stringent Max AC Barring threshold.
acbImmediateMax.fullName: RACH load immediate Max AC barring

acbNumRrcConnCellStart.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the upper threshold of RRC CONNECTED UEs which can trigger ACTIVE RRC_ACB event on the cell level.
RRC_ACB event becomes ACTIVE if #RRC_Connected UEs in the cell >=  ROUND(acbNumRrcConnCellStart * maxNumRRC.Cell / 100) AND acbRrcConnCellStartTimer expires.

ACTIVE RRC_ACB event shall start step-wise upgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if dynamic ACB ACTIVE state not started yet.

Note: maxNumRRC.Cell - indicates that this is Cell related maxNumRRC RAC limit.
acbNumRrcConnCellStart.fullName: Cell RRC connection AC Barring start threshold

acbNumRrcConnCellStop.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the lower threshold of RRC CONNECTED UEs which can trigger INACTIVE RRC_ACB event on the cell level.  
RRC_ACB event becomes INACTIVE if #RRC_Connected UEs in the cell <  ROUND(acbNumRrcConnCellStop * maxNumRRC.Cell / 100) AND acbRrcConnCellStopTimer expires.

INACTIVE RRC_ACB event shall start step-wise downgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if there's no other ACTIVE ACB trigger.

Note: maxNumRRC.Cell - indicates that this is Cell related maxNumRRC RAC limit.
acbNumRrcConnCellStop.fullName: Cell RRC connection AC Barring stop threshold

acbNumRrcReqCFRStart.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the upper threshold of RRC Connection Requests per 1 second which is the one of required two conditions to trigger ACTIVE CFR_ACB event on cell level. CFR_ACB is ACTIVE:
1. When the connection failure rate is above acbRacRejCFRStart 
AND 
2. the number of RRC attempts is above acbNumRrcReqCFRStart. 

The connection failure rate is defined by the ratio between RRC connection setup rejections due to RAC at cell level and total RRC attempts. Both connection failure rate and number of RRC attempts are determined during a time window. Duration of the time window = ROUND(acbRrcReqFactor * acbUpdateTimer)
The real value of upper threshold of RRC Connection Requests per 1 second is the product of acbNumRrcReqStart and maxNumActUe and is calculated by the formula: 
ROUNDUP(acbNumRrcReqCFRStart * maxNumActUE / 100) * duration_of_the_time_window.
ACTIVE CFR_ACB event shall start step-wise upgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if dynamic ACB ACTIVE state not started yet.
The upper and lower thresholds are introduced to prevent repeatedly starting and stopping LTE2823 step-wise ACB algorithm.
acbNumRrcReqCFRStart.fullName: RRC connection attempts AC barring start threshold

acbNumRrcReqCFRStop.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the lower threshold of RRC Connection Requests per 1 second which is the one of two conditions that can trigger INACTIVE CFR_ACB - event on cell level. CFR_ACB is INACTIVE:
1. When the connection failure rate is below acbRacRejCFRStop 
OR
2. the number of RRC attempts is below acbNumRrcReqCFRStop. 

The connection failure rate is defined by the ratio between RRC connection setup rejections due to RAC at cell level and total RRC attempts. Both connection failure rate and number of RRC attempts are determined during a time window. Duration of the time window = ROUND(acbRrcReqFactor * acbUpdateTimer)
The real value of lower threshold of RRC Connection Requests per 1 second is the product of acbNumRrcReqStart and maxNumActUe and is calculated by the formula: 
ROUNDUP(acbNumRrcReqCFRStop * maxNumActUE / 100) * duration_of_the_time_window.
INACTIVE CFR_ACB event shall start step-wise downgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if dynamic ACB ACTIVE state already started.
The upper and lower thresholds are introduced to prevent repeatedly starting and stopping LTE2823 step-wise ACB algorithm.
acbNumRrcReqCFRStop.fullName: RRC connection attempts AC barring stop threshold

acbNumRrcReqStart.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the upper threshold of RRC Connection Requests per 1 second which can trigger ACTIVE RACH_ACB event on the cell level.
The real value of upper threshold is the product of acbNumRrcReqStart and  maxNumActUe.
acbNumRrcReqStart.fullName: RACH load AC Barring start threshold

acbNumRrcReqStop.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the lower threshold of RRC Connection Requests per 1 second which can trigger INACTIVE RACH_ACB event on the cell level.
The real value of lower threshold is the product of acbNumRrcReqStop and  maxNumActUe.
acbNumRrcReqStop.fullName: RACH load AC Barring stop threshold

acbNumSteps.description:
This parameter defines absolute number of ACB thresholds used by the algorithm,including: Min, Max and intermediate ACB thresholds.  
Operator configures ACB Min and Max thresholds for ACB parameters as well as number of steps (inclination of access class barring changes) in which Max ACB threshold settings are reached.

If acbNumSteps=0 that is equal to disabling automatic AC barring in that specific cell.

If acbNumSteps=1 that means that ACB Max threshold is broadcasted.

acbPlmnNumSteps.description:

Operator configures ACB Min and Max thresholds parameters as well as number of steps (inclination of access class barring changes) in which Max ACB threshold settings are reached.

If acbPlmnNumSteps=0 that is equal to disabling access class barring per PLMN in that specific cell.

If acbPlmnNumSteps=1 that means that Max threshold of ACB per PLMN  is broadcasted.
acbPlmnNumSteps.fullName: Steps of adaptive access class barring per PLMN

acbProfileId.description: Instance ID of the assigned Access Class Barring profile.

acbRacRejCFRStart.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the upper threshold of the connection failure rate per sliding window duration time which is the one of required two conditions to trigger ACTIVE CFR_ACB event on the cell level. CFR_ACB is ACTIVE:
1. When the connection failure rate (CFR) is above acbRacRejCFRStart 
AND 
2. the number of RRC attempts is above acbNumRrcReqCFRStart. 

The connection failure rate is defined by the ratio between RRC connection setup rejections due to RAC at cell level and total RRC attempts. Both connection failure rate and number of RRC attempts are determined during a time window. Duration of the time window = ROUND(acbRrcReqFactor * acbUpdateTimer)
Every second eNB performs calculation considering data aggregated per sliding window period:
A - aggregated Number of RRC Connection Requests per sliding window period
B - aggregated RRC Connection Rejects due to RAC per sliding window period

Every second eNB calculates new CFR:
CFR = roundup( B * 100 / A )  
ACTIVE CFR_ACB event shall start step-wise upgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if dynamic ACB ACTIVE state not started yet.
The upper and lower thresholds are introduced to prevent repeatedly starting and stopping LTE2823 step-wise ACB algorithm.

acbRacRejCFRStop.description:
This parameter defines in percentage the lower threshold of the connection failure rate per sliding window duration time which is the one of two conditions that can trigger INACTIVE CFR_ACB event on cell level. CFR_ACB is INACTIVE:
1. When the connection failure rate (CFR) is below acbRacRejCFRStop 
OR 
2. the number of RRC attempts is below acbNumRrcReqCFRStop. 

The connection failure rate is defined by the ratio between RRC connection setup rejections due to RAC at cell level and total RRC attempts. Both connection failure rate and number of RRC attempts are determined during a time window. Duration of the time window = ROUND(acbRrcReqFactor * acbUpdateTimer)
Every second eNB performs calculation considering data aggregated per sliding window period:
A - aggregated Number of RRC Connection Requests per sliding window period
B - aggregated RRC Connection Rejects due to RAC per sliding window period

Every second eNB calculates new CFR:
CFR = roundup( B * 100 / A )  
INACTIVE CFR_ACB event shall start step-wise downgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if dynamic ACB ACTIVE state already started.
The upper and lower thresholds are introduced to prevent repeatedly starting and stopping LTE2823 step-wise ACB algorithm.

RRC_ACB event becomes ACTIVE if #RRC_Connected UEs in the cell >=  ROUND(acbNumRrcConnCellStart * maxNumRRC.Cell / 100) AND acbRrcConnCellStartTimer expires.

ACTIVE RRC_ACB event shall start step-wise upgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if dynamic ACB ACTIVE state not started yet.

Note: maxNumRRC.Cell - indicates that this is Cell related maxNumRRC RAC limit.
acbRrcConnCellStartTimer.fullName: Cell RRC triggered AC Barring start timer

acbRrcConnCellStopTimer.description:
This parameter defines the guard timer before triggering INACTIVE RRC_ACB event on the cell level.   
RRC_ACB event becomes INACTIVE if #RRC_Connected UEs in the cell <  ROUND(acbNumRrcConnCellStop * maxNumRRC.Cell / 100) AND acbRrcConnCellStopTimer expires.

INACTIVE RRC_ACB event shall start step-wise downgrade of AC barring settings and their broadcast in SIB2 message if there's no other ACTIVE ACB trigger.

Note: maxNumRRC.Cell - indicates that this is Cell related maxNumRRC RAC limit.
acbRrcConnCellStopTimer.fullName: Cell RRC triggered AC Barring stop timer

acbRrcReqFactor.description: This parameter defines the multiplication factor which together with acbUpdateTimer determines RACH load sliding window period over which number of received RRC Connection Requests are aggregated. And when LTE4175 is activated the the parameter determines the sliding window period over which number of RRC Connection Requests and number of RRC Connection Rejections are aggregated. acbSkipTimer.description:
When ACB Skip timer expires and any ACB Skip IEs is configured to 'true' (LTE2505) and broadcasted in the SIB2 then ACB Skip IEs will be automatically deactivated it means NOT broadcasted till all ACB triggers are INACTIVE.
If any ACB Skip IEs is configured to 'true'  then the acb Skip IEs may automatically be deactivated which means not broadcasted in SIB2, only in case the maximum ACB level is already reached and remains active for acbSkipTimer time. 
The timer is configured in counter mode as multiplicity of acbUpdateTimer.

Note: If the timer is not configured that means that Skip IEs shall not be removed from the SIB2 if they are configured to 'true'.

acbUpdateTimer.description:
This parameter defines when ACB settings step-wise  upgrade or downgrade and their modification in the SIB2 is allowed.  
The RRC connection triggered ACB parameters changes are executed in the operator configurable update intervals controlled by ACB update timer.
The exception is ACB triggered by the C-Plane OVL2 which is executed immediately up to the ACB Max threshold.

autoAcBarringStartTimer.description:
This parameter defines the guard timer before starting automatic AC barring broadcast of overload specific parameter value in SIB messages when BTS C-Plane get in overload. 
As per TS36.331, systemInfoValueTag changes should be no more than 31 times within 3 hours. Otherwise, UE with a complete set of system information of the cell stored that has left the cell and has come back within three hours might not recognize that there was a system information change.

To avoid systemInfoValueTag overflow solely due to frequent automatic AC barring on/off, it is recommended that the sum of autoAcBarringStartTimer and autoAcbPlmnRmvlStopTimer is  equal to or greater than 900 seconds (i.e. 15 minutes).

autoAcbPlmnRmvlStopTimer.description:
This parameter defines the guard timer before stopping both automatic AC barring broadcast of overload specific parameter value and further PLMN autonomous removal in SIB messages when BTS C-Plane gets out from overload. 
As per TS36.331, systemInfoValueTag changes should be no more than 31 times within 3 hours. otherwise, UE with a complete set of system information of the cell stored that has left the cell and has come back within three hours might not recognize that there was a system information change.

To avoid systemInfoValueTag overflow solely due to frequent automatic AC barring on/off, it is recommended that the sum of autoAcBarringStartTimer and autoAcbPlmnRmvlStopTimer is  equal to or greater than 900 seconds (i.e. 15 minutes).
autoAcbPlmnRmvlStopTimer.fullName: Automatic AC barring and PLMN removal stop timer

autoPlmnRmvlStartTimer.description:
This parameter defines the guard timer before starting autonomous further PLMN removal from SIB1 message when BTS C-Plane gets in overload. 
After starting automatic AC barring broadcast of oveload specific parameter value in SIB messages when BTS C-Plane get in overload, if BTS C-plane overload level 2 keeps active for time defined by this parameter consecutively, the specified subset of further PLMNs is removed from SIB1 autonomously by eNB in the overload cell.
autoPlmnRmvlStartTimer.fullName: Autonomous further PLMN removal start timer

celResTiFHM.description: The cell reselection timer (t-ReselectionEUTRAN) is multiplied by this factor if the UE is in the medium high mobility state.
celResTiFHM.fullName: Cell reselection timer factor high mobility

celResTiFMM.description: The cell reselection timer (t-ReselectionEUTRAN) is multiplied by this factor if the UE is in the medium mobility state.
celResTiFMM.fullName: Cell reselection timer factor medium mobility

cellBarred.description:
The cell barred flag indicates if the cell status is barred or not. A barred cell is a cell that a UE is not allowed to camp on, not even for emergency calls. If a cell on which a UE is currently camped becomes barred, a cell reselection is triggered.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

cellReSelPrio.description:
Defines the absolute priority of the serving layer.
The cell reselection priority parameter defines the absolute priority of the serving layer. 0 means the lowest priority.

cellReSelSubPrio.description: This parameter indicates a fractional value to be added to the value of cellReSelPrio to obtain the absolute priority of the serving layer.

csgId.description:
This parameter defines the Closed Subscriber Identifier for the cell.
This parameter is only used if csgType is set to CSG.

The highest value allowed by 3GPP (134217727) is reserved.

dayLt.description:
Defines the Daylight Savings Time (DST) offset that is used by the BTS to calculate its local time.

This parameter value, derived from TIME-timeZone,  indicates if and how daylight saving time (DST) is applied to obtain the local time.
0    No adjustment for Daylight Saving Time
1   +1 hour adjustment for Daylight Saving Time
2   +2 hours adjustment for Daylight Saving Time

It is broadcast in SIB16 and is sent in the Mobility Parameters CDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in the RRC_CONNECTED mode only when the dayLtIncluded parameter is set to TRUE.

deltaFPucchF1bCSr10.description:
The parameter defines the transport format dependent offset in power control for PUCCH format 1bCS.
This parameter is used only when the Cell is configured as PCell in Carrier Aggregation.
deltaFPucchF1bCSr10.fullName: UL power offset for PUCCH format 1bCS

deltaFPucchF3r10.description:
The parameter defines the transport format dependent offset in power control for PUCCH format 3.
This parameter is used only when the Cell is configured as PCell in Carrier Aggregation.
deltaFPucchF3r10.fullName: UL power offset for PUCCH format 3
deltaFPucchF3r10.officialRange:
-1: deltaF-1 
0: deltaF0 
1: deltaF1 
2: deltaF2 
3: deltaF3 
4: deltaF4 
5: deltaF5 
6: deltaF6

heNBName.description:
This parameter defines the Home eNB Name that may be broadcasted by a Closed Subscriber Group cell coded in UTF-8 with variable number of bytes per character, see TS 22.011 [10].
If this parameter is configured the cell shall broadcast a SIB9 message with hnb-Name IE set to this parameter.

intrFrqCelRes.description:
Used to control cell reselection on intra-frequency cells when the highest ranked cell is barred, or is considered as barred by the UE, as specified in TS 36.304.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE/NB-IoT UE.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

intraPresAntP.description:
Indicates whether all the neighboring cells use Antenna Port 1.
When set to TRUE, the UE may assume that at least two cell-specific antenna ports are used in all neighboring cells.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

ltmOff.description:
Defines the offset between UTC and local time that is used by the BTS to calculate its local time. This parameter value is derived from TIME-timeZone.

Local time offset is broadcast in SIB16 and is also sent in the Mobility Parameters CDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode when the ltmOffIncluded parameter is set to TRUE.   Tthe LTM_OFF field value (6 bits), encoded in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE), if present,  shall have a two’s complement arithmetic representation with a granulatiry of 30 minutes (refer 3GPP2  C.S0005 Section 3.7.2.3.2.26).

mbmsNeighCellConfigIntraF.description:
Provides information related to MBSFN configuration of neighbour cells of this frequency.
Provides information related to MBSFN configuration of neighbour cells of this frequency
00: Not all neighbour cells have the same MBSFN subframe allocation as serving cell
01: No MBSFN subframes are present in all neighbour cells
10: The MBSFN subframe allocations of all neighbour cells are identical to or subsets of that in the serving cell
11: Different UL/DL allocation in neighbouring cells for TDD compared to the serving cell

Notes:
Value of '11' is not applicable for FDD.
For TDD, 00, 10 and 01 are only used for same UL/DL allocation in neighbouring cells compared to the serving cell.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

modPeriodCoeff.description:
The parameter defines the length of the modification period.
Modification period = modificationPeriodCoeff * defaultPagingCycle / 10 ms.
Modification period is equal or lower than 1024.
(n2 corresponds to value 2, n4 corresponds to value 4 and n8 corresponds to value 8.)

n310.description:
This is the maximum number of consecutive "out of sync" indications received from lower layers.
n1 corresponds to 1 and so on.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

n311.description:
Maximum number of consecutive "in-sync" indications received from lower layers.
n1 corresponds to 1 and so on.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

nCellChgHigh.description: The parameter defines the number of cell changes to enter the high mobility state. For the idle mode, it corresponds to NCR_H in TS 36.304.

nCellChgMed.description: The parameter defines the number of cell changes to enter the medium mobility state. For idle mode, it corresponds to NCR_M in TS 36.304.

pMaxIntraF.description:
Pmax to be used for the intra-frequency neighboring EUTRA cells. If pmax is absent, the maximum power according to the UE capability is used.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE/NB-IoT UE.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

pMaxOwnCell.description:
The IE P-Max is used to limit the UE's uplink transmission power on a carrier frequency; it is also used to calculate the parameter P-compensation defined in TS 36.304 .
Corresponds to parameter PEMAX in TS 36.101.
The UE transmit power should not exceed the minimum of this value (in dBm), if provided, and the maximum UE power for the UE power class, PUMAX, as specified in TS 36.101.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.
pMaxOwnCell.fullName: Max. uplink transmission power own cell

prachPwrRamp.description:
The power ramping step size parameter defines the power increment step size for Random Access preamble transmission, including PRACH and NPRACH.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

preambTxMax.description:
The preamble transmission maximum defines the maximum number of Random Access transmissions. 
Note: The values n50, n100 and n200 should not be used.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

primPlmnCellres.description:
Indicates if the cell/PLMN combination is reserved for operator use.
Cells reserved for operator use are treated as barred by 'normal' UEs without a USIM with AC 11 or 15 inserted. UEs with AC 11 or 15 USIM inserted are specific operator UEs and thus allowed to camp on and access such cells. The default value is not reserved.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.
The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

primPlmnCellresAcbMax.description: Indicates if the cell/PLMN combination is reserved for operator use and incoming handovers for the combination are blocked when ACB max step is reached as a result of step-wise ACB. Note that this functionality only applies for the primary PLMN.
primPlmnCellresAcbMax.fullName: Primary PLMN set to cell reserved for operator use

primPlmnUpperLayerIndicationR15.description: Indication of the cell/primary PLMN supports EN-DC in SIB2.
primPlmnUpperLayerIndicationR15.fullName: Cell PLMN indicator for supporting EN-DC.

qHyst.description:
The Qhyst parameter provides the hysteresis value in dB for ranking criteria in the cell reselection procedure. The parameter is used to minimize pingpong.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE/NB-IoT UE.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

qHystSfHigh.description:
The parameter defines an additional hysteresis value to be applied in the high mobility state to the cell reselection procedure hysteresis value (q-Hyst).
Value db-6 corresponds to -6dB, db-4 corresponds to -4dB and so on.

qHystSfMed.description:
The parameter defines an additional hysteresis value to be applied in the medium mobility state to the cell reselection procedure hysteresis value (q-Hyst).
Value db-6 corresponds to -6dB, db-4 corresponds to -4dB and so on.

qQualMinOffsetR9.description:
Offset to the signaled qQualMinR9 taken into account in the Squal evaluation as a result of a periodic search for a higher priority PLMN while camped normally in a VPLMN.
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9.
qQualMinOffsetR9.fullName: Offset for minimum required RSRQ in cell (Rel9)

qQualMinR9.description:
Minimum required quality level in the LTE and NB-IoT cell.
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

qRxLevMinOffset.description:
Affects the minimum required RX level in the cell.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

qrxlevmin.description:
Specifies the minimum required RX RSRP level in the cell.
(Qrxlevmin in 36.304)
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.
qrxlevmin.fullName: Minimum required RX level in cell

qrxlevminintraF.description:
Indicates the minimum required RX level in the cell (dBm) for intra-frequency.
Specifies the minimum required RX RSRP level for the intra-frequency neighbouring E-UTRA cells.
(Qrxlevmin in 36.304)
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.
qrxlevminintraF.fullName: Min. required RX level for intra-freq neighboring cells

sIntraSearchPR9.description:
Power threshold
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

sIntraSearchQR9.description:
Quality threshold
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE.

sIntrasearch.description:
The Sintrasearch parameter defines the threshold (in dB) for intra-frequency measurements. 
The UE can omit measurements of intra-frequency neighbor cells if the serving cell is above a certain threshold.

The setting is commonly valid for all legacy category UE and Cat-M UE/NB-IoT UE.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

sNonIntraSearchPR9.description:
Power threshold
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9
sNonIntraSearchPR9.fullName: Inter-freq and inter-RAT power meas threshold (Rel9)

sNonIntraSearchQR9.description:
Quality treshold
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9
sNonIntraSearchQR9.fullName: Inter-freq and inter-RAT quality meas threshold (Rel9)

sNonIntrsearch.description:
The sNonintrsearch parameter defines the threshold (in dB) for inter-RAT and inter-frequency measurements.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

saiListIntraFreqNeighbors.description:
List of MBMS service area identities (SAI) for intra-frequency neighbor cells

Please note that the sum of SAIs configured in the lists saiListIntraFreqNeighbors and saiListIntraFreq of the optionally assigned SIB15 profile is maximum 63.
If saiListIntraFreqNeighbors is not configured the maximum number of SAIs in saiListIntraFreq is 64. eNB will omit SAIs if one of the above limits is exceeded!
saiListIntraFreqNeighbors.fullName: SAI list of intra-frequency neighbor cells

siMessagePeriodicity.description:
Indicates the periodicity of the SI-2 message.
The parameter System Information 2 Periodicity indicates the repetition period of the SI-2 message.

siMessageRepetition.description: Indicates the repetition of the SI-2 message within the SI window.

siMessageSibType.description:
Indicates which System Information Block is contained in the SI-2 message.
The parameter System Information 2 Mapping Information indicates which System Information Blocks is contained in the SI-2 message.

siWindowLen.description:
Defines the common System Information scheduling window.
The parameter SI Window Length defines the common System Information scheduling window for all SIs.

Note: All Cat-M UEs in RRC Connected mode will be released when this parameter is online modified.

sib15ProfileId.description:
Instance ID of the assigned SIB15 profile.

SIB15 contains MBMS Service Area Identities (SAI) of the current and/ or
neighboring carrier frequencies

sib2xTransmit.description:
As per basic system behavior, a SIB message (SIB2 and higher) is transmitted one time per each SI window, and further transmissions might be added if the message is too big (code rate is too high) for cell-edge UEs to decode it from fewer transmissions. If siWindowLen is greater than or equal to 20 ms, this parameter can be used to add another mandatory transmission per SI window for SIB2 and higher. 
Up to four transmissions can be done in a SIB window. Any further transmission is done as “best effort” and may or may not happen.

Setting sib2xTransmit=true in a system with 5 MHz or below is possible but not recommended for reasons of DL performance.

Even without sib2xTransmit set to 'true', SIB repetitions will be sent if this is required by message size and the code rate defined for SIB messages.
If siMessageRepetition is set to a value of 2 or higher, eNB tries (on best-effort basis only) to send SIB repetitions on top of the minimum number of transmissions defined by message size and code rade. In contrast to this, setting sib2xTransmit to 'true' adds a mandatory SIB repetition.
sib2xTransmit.fullName: Twofold transmission of SIBs per SI window

sibId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SIB.
It uniquely identifies a SIB instance.

t300.description:
Timer T300 supervises the RRC connection establishment procedure. 
Start: Transmission of RRCConnectionRequest
Stop: Reception of RRCConnectionSetup or RRCConnectionReject message, cell re-selection and upon abortion of connection establishment by upper layers

At expiry: Perform the actions as specified in 36.331, 5.3.3.6

In case LNBTS-actContextPreemption is activated, the minimum recommended value is 600ms. If both LNBTS-actContextPreemption and LNBTS-actSatBackhaul are activated the minimum recommended value is further increased to 1500ms.

t301.description:
Timer T301 supervises the RRC connection re-establishment procedure. 
Start: Transmission of RRCConnectionReestabilshmentRequest
Stop: Reception of RRCConnectionReestablishment or RRCConnectionReestablishmentReject message as well as when the selected cell becomes unsuitable

At expiry: Go to RRC_IDLE

t310.description: Timer T310 supervises the recovery from physical layer problems.

t311.description: Timer T311 supervises the RRC connection re-establishment.

tEvaluation.description: Timer TCRmax defines the duration for evaluating the criteria to enter mobility states. For idle mode, it corresponds to TCRmax in TS 36.304.

tHystNormal.description: Timer TCRmaxHyst defines the additional duration for evaluating the criteria to enter normal mobility state. For idle mode, it corresponds to TCRmaxHyst in TS 36.304.

tReselEutr.description: The Treselection parameter defines the cell reselection timer value. It allows averaging of the target cell quality before cell reselection is performed.

threshServingLowQR9.description:
This specifies the Squal threshold used by the UE on the serving cell when reselecting towards a lower priority RAT/ frequency.
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9
threshServingLowQR9.fullName: Q-threshold for reselection towards lower prio RAT/freq

threshSrvLow.description: Specifies the threshold for the serving frequency used in reselection evaluation towards lower priority EUTRAN frequency or RAT.

ulpcIniPrePwr.description:
The parameter defines the initial power for Random Access preamble transmission.
Note: This parameter is used in NB-IoT cell also.

saiListIntraFreq.description:
List of service area identities (SAI) that are supported by cells having the frequency of the cell, which references the SIB15 profile

Please note that the sum of SAIs configured in the lists saiListIntraFreq and saiListIntraFreqNeighbors of a referencing cell is maximum 63.
If saiListIntraFreqNeighbors is not configured in any referencing cell the maximum number of SAIs in saiListIntraFreq is 64.
eNB will omit SAIs if one of the above limits is exceeded!
saiListIntraFreq.fullName: MBMS service area identity list of the cell

sib15PrId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SIB15PR.
It uniquely identifies a SIB15PR instance.

name.description:
This is the name of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The content is filled by the BTS and cannot be changed.

The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

sib15PrSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SIB15PRSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an SIB15PRSPARE instance.

value.description:
This is the value of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The allowed parameter values are defined in the feature specification.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.

maxNumSlCellRecActForBbuPerDay.description: Likely sets the maximum allowed value for "number of Sl cell Rec activate/enable For Bbu Per Day" on the SLCELLDRCONF object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

maxNumSlCellRecActForBtsPerDay.description: Likely sets the maximum allowed value for "number of Sl cell Rec activate/enable For Base Transceiver Station Per Day" on the SLCELLDRCONF object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

maxNumSlCellRecActForCellPerDay.description:
This parameter defines maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for cell per day.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
maxNumSlCellRecActForCellPerDay.fullName: Maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for cell per day

maxNumSlCellRecActForRfmPerDay.description:
This parameter defines maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for RF Module per day.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
maxNumSlCellRecActForRfmPerDay.fullName: Maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for RFM per day

slCommProfId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SLCOMMPROF.
It uniquely identifies a SLCOMMPROF instance.

slEarfcnUL.description:
E-UTRA Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number in uplink
If the feature 'ProSe sidelink communication' is activated it applies implicitly to all cells with earfcnUL and ulChBw equal to slEarfcnUL and slUlChBw of the SLCOMMPROF instance.

slUlChBw.description:
Uplink channel bandwidth defines the UL bandwidth for the eNode-B transmission in a cell. 
This is not the bandwidth reserved for sidelink.

Uplink channel bandwidth defines the UL bandwidth for the eNB transmission in a cell, and also defines the number of available Physical Resource Blocks.

The uplink channel bandwidth mapping to number of Physical Resource Blocks is: 
10.0 MHz = 50 UL PRBS 

If the feature 'ProSe sidelink communication' is activated it applies implicitly to all cells with earfcnUL and ulChBw equal to slEarfcnUL and slUlChBw of the SLCOMMPROF instance.

dataTFResConfSubfrBitMap.description:
Indicates the subframe bitmap in time indicating resources used for sidelink Data

Changing this parameter to a non-default configuration has to be done carefully, as it may lead to suboptimal performance

The octets have to be defined as per TS36.331
The parameter must be added as character string in hexadecimal notation with leading '0x', where for each octet representing two character must be configured. 
4 bits per character representing a total of 40 bits.

dataTFResConfigOffSetInd.description: Indicates the offset used by PSSCH resource configuration. it indicates the start of the data with respect to the start of associated slScPeriod
dataTFResConfigOffSetInd.fullName: Offset indicator for sidelink data short

dataTFResConfigPrbEnd.description:
Specifies the PRB from which resources used for Sidelink Data ends

The PRB allocation for sidelink should not overlap with PRACH resources.

dataTFResConfigPrbNum.description: Specifies a set of PRB resources used for Sidelink Data

dataTFResConfigPrbStart.description:
Specifies the PRB from which resources used for Sidelink Data begins

The PRB allocation for sidelink should not overlap with PUCCH resources.

scTFResConfigOffSetInd.description: Indicates the offset of the first period of pool of resources within a SFN cycle
scTFResConfigOffSetInd.fullName: Offset indicator for sidelink control short

scTFResConfigPrbEnd.description:
Specifies the PRB from which  resources used for Sidelink Control ends

The PRB allocation for sidelink should not overlap with PRACH resources.

scTFResConfigPrbNum.description: Specifies a set of PRB resources used for Sidelink Control

scTFResConfigPrbStart.description:
Specifies the PRB from which resources used for Sidelink Control begins

The PRB allocation for sidelink should not overlap with PUCCH resources.

scTFResConfigSubfrBitMap.description:
Indicates the subframe bitmap in time indicating resources used for sidelink Control.

Changing this parameter to a non-default configuration has to be done carefully, as it may lead to suboptimal performance

The octets have to be defined as per TS36.331

The parameter must be added as character string in hexadecimal notation with leading '0x', where for each octet representing two character must be configured. 
4 bits per character representing a total of 40 bits.

slCommResId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SLCOMMRES.
It uniquely identifies a SLCOMMRES instance.

slDataCpLen.description: Sidelink Cyclic prefix length for Physical SL Data Channel (PSBCH)

slHoppingConfigNumSubBand.description: Indicates the number of subands for hopping configuration used in sidelink
slHoppingConfigNumSubBand.fullName: Number of subbands for sidelink hopping configuration

slHoppingConfigParam.description:
indicates the hopping configuration parameter used for sidelink
Setting this parameter to 0 disables hopping.

slHoppingConfigRbOffset.description: Indicates the offset in resource blocks for hopping configuration used in sidelink

slScCpLen.description: Sidelink Cyclic prefix length for Physical SL Control Channel (PSCCH)

slScPeriod.description: Indicates the period over which the all the resources are allocated in a cell for both Sidelink Control and Data for which the transmission occur.

name.description:
This is the name of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The content is filled by the BTS and cannot be changed.

The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

slCommResSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SLCOMMRESSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an SLCOMMRESSPARE instance.

value.description:
This is the value of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The allowed parameter values are defined in the feature specification.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.

slCommSyncId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SLCOMMSYNC.
It uniquely identifies a SLCOMMSYNC instance.

slSyncCpLen.description: Sidelink Cyclic prefix length for sidelink Sync

slSyncOffsetInd.description: Sidelink Sync Offset Indicator. This value must match the pre-configured value in the SIM card of the UEs.

syncTxParametersAlpha.description: Alpha value for Sidelink Sync transmission

slCommTxId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SLCOMMTX.
It uniquely identifies a SLCOMMTX instance.

slDataTxParametersAlpha.description: Alpha value for Sidelink Data transmission

slScTxParametersAlpha.description: Alpha value for Sidelink Control transmission

a2TimeToTriggerActSL.description:
Time to trigger for A2 measurement when UE has indicated interest in sidelink direct communication
Duration for which the event A2 must be valid at the UE such that the measurement report is sent by UE
a2TimeToTriggerActSL.fullName: Time to trigger for A2 measurement during sidelink

hysThreshold2Sidelink.description:
Related Hysteresis of RSRP Threshold Th2 for event A2 when UE is interested in sidelink direct communication

Parameter is used within the entry and leave condition of the A2 triggered reporting condition. The IE value is multiplied by 2.
hysThreshold2Sidelink.fullName: Related hysteresis of Th2 For RSRP during sidelink

slMeasId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC SLMEAS.
It uniquely identifies a SLMEAS instance.

threshold2Sidelink.description:
RSRP threshold for A2 measurement of serving cell for start of inter frequency and inter-RAT measurements when UE has indicated interest in sidelink direct communication.
Defines the threshold for serving cell RSRP of A2 event, as a trigger to start Inter-Frequency and Inter-RAT handovers when UE is interested in sidelink communication. If RSRP value reported is below threshold2xxx of corresponding mobility type (inter-frequency, inter-RAT) then those mobility measurements are started.

The dBm value is mapped to the 3GPP IE value according to TS 36.133:
* -140 dBm means a threshold lower than -140 dBm
* values between -139 dBm and -44 dBm mean a threshold lower than the configured value but higher than or equal to the (value - 1 dB)
* -43 dBm means a threshold higher than or equal to -44 dBm
threshold2Sidelink.fullName: Threshold th2 for RSRP during sidelink

btsHotelMemberId.description:
Defines unique member identifier of the system module in the BTS hotel.
Note: The btsHotelMemberId assigned to system modules located of the left side of the AirScale Subrack shall be odd number, while btsHotelMemberId assigned to system modules located on the right side shall be even number.
In dual core operation, relation between btsHotelMemberId assigned to SMOD on the left side and SMOD on the right side of the AirScale Subrack shall follow “m = n + 1” rule, where n represents btsHotelMemberId of SMOD on the left side and m represents btsHotelMemberId of SMOD on the right side.
Detailed instructions of usage btsHotelMemberId parameter will be provided to operators in feature documentation.

climateControlOcxoTemperatureLearning.description: This parameter determines whether System Module fan speed is varied during normal phase sync tuning mode in order to generate temperature variation (true) or whether the fan speed is subject to the configured climate control profile only, reducing by this the noise level (false).

climateControlProfiling.description:
Climate control Profiling parameter.
Fan speed will be controlled according to module temperature and desired BTS fan profile.
- Low Noise: Minimised noise for low and moderate ambient temperatures
- Optimized Cooling: Maximised unit MTBF (long life) by running fans with maximum speed already in
moderate ambient temperatures
- Linear: An intermediate profile which increases fan speed linearly as temperature increase.
 
It is possible to select fan control profiles independently for each module in the BTS.

If user does not want to define fan profiling or module does not support fan profiles, the BTS manager will not set a value to SCF.

Parameter values are: "Optimized Cooling", "Linear" and "Low Noise". Default value is "Optimized Cooling".

distRefPoint.description:
This parameter allows to switch off automatic determination of the reference point for antenna line delay calculations and to set the distance to the reference point manually.
This parameter is optional. If required, the parameter should be set to the maximum expected distance  for any RF module or Remote Radio Head served by this SMOD. 
System behavior is different for OBSAI radios and CPRI radios that support different CPRI dialects (e.g. different behavior between Nokia CPRI radios and other flavors of CPRI).
If this parameter is omitted or set to zero, the SMOD will be grouped together with other BBMODs or SMODs that have no settings and an automatic reference point calculation for the group will be performed. 
Detailed instructions how to use parameter distRefPoint will be provided to operators in a release note.

When there is only system module in AirScale, this parameter is informative only and is optional. However, when there are two system modules, the position is enforced and reset will occur when changes are made.

radioProtSearchOrder.description:
This parameter allows the operator to define the starting protocol for radio detection between OBSAI and CPRI variants.  

When this parameter is set, the FHS will start the radio protocol detection algorithm with the specified protocol on first startup or following upgrade activation of that module.  The use of this parameter can reduce the radio detection time in configurations where the Operator knows the type of radio deployment. If this parameter is not specified, the FHS will still be able to automatically detect the type of radio protocols in use, although the time to detect the radios may be increased for certain exceptional cases.  In this scenario, the FHS will attempt to use prior radio detection information to select the starting point for protocol searches.

Since this parameter defines the starting point for the search algorithm, it can only decrease the detection time for radios that are attached to the FHS when the algorithm is started. If no radios are attached to the module, the time to detect to the radios will be dependent upon the radio protocol type and the current protocol being probed by the FHS.

Note that if the Operator sets this parameter incorrectly, the radio detection time can be increased following a BTS restart or upgrade activation.

In all scenarios, the BTS will be able to detect the radio protocol with or without the Operator’s use of this parameter.

syncMaster.description:
The parameter enables a BTS to be the RP3-01 Synchronization Master in a RF Sharing configuration.

The BTS on which this parameter is enabled will be used to drive the RP3-01 interface clock in an RF Sharing Configuration. When enabled this BTS is referred as the "Sync Master".

The BTS on which this parameter is disabled will receive RP3-01 interface clock as a synchronization input reference source for the whole BTS from the "Sync Master" BTS, thereby ignoring all other synchronization input reference sources such as 1pps. When disabled in an RF Sharing configuration, the BTS is referred to as the "Sync Slave".

If own SMOD is configured as synchronization slave, it will get synchronized via the partner SMOD, and other sync sources, such as Timing over Packet (TOPF/TOPB objects) should not be configured, in order to avoid unnecessary alarms.

btsSyncMode.description:
This parameter defines the synchronization mode of the SBTS.

In frequency synchronized mode, the frequency of the radio interface signal is synchronized to the reference source and the phase of the frames on the radio interface is random. The frequency sync mode can be used in FDD systems when no features are used which require phase synchronization.

In phase synchronized mode (this mode is always used in TDD), the radio interface signal is frequency synchronized, and in addition, the start of the frames in the radio interface is phase synchronized to a time reference source. In FDD systems, phase sync mode must be configured when the features which require phase synchronization (for example: OTDOA, MBMS) are used. The phase synchronization requires that the reference source (valid for FDD and TDD) is either GNSSE (1pps/ToD from external GNSS receiver) or internal GNSS receiver (FSIH only) or 1pps/Tod from Sync Hub Master or ToPP,  and in case of hybrid synchronisation, additional SyncE sources are allowed.

In loose phase and time synchronized mode (FDD only), the radio interface signal is frequency synchronized, however the phase of the radio frames is synchronized to the time reference source with a certain accuracy. The BTS time contained in the BTS frame counter is loosely synchronized to the time reference source configured  (NTP, GNSS, BSC) (i.e. with relatively low accuracy).

enableUTCOutOfSyncFault.description: Enables raising a fault/alarm when the system's UTC time reference is detected to be out of synchronization.

manualFrameTimingAdjustment.description:
Different systems could have differences in the frame synchronization to the PPS timing pulse. 
This parameter gives the possiblity to adjust freely an air interface timing as for 1PPS synchronization pulse. 

Note: This parameter is needed only for TD-LTE, and so it will be valid only in SBTS when TD-LTE is supported.

This parameter is aimed for post-processing of measurement reports only. It is not used in any report configuration to the UE.
The dB values are mapped to 3GPP IE values according to TS 36.133:
- -20 dB means a threshold lower than -19.5 dB
- values between -19.5 dB and -3.5 dB mean a threshold higher than or equal to the configured value but lower than (value + 0.5 dB)
- -3 dB means a threshold higher than or equal to -3 dB

distRefPoint.description: This parameter is optional. The parameter controls how the BTS determines the reference point for a timing group. If distRefPoint is not specified (value=0), the alignment within the timing group is performed by the BTS to the radio with the longest path delay. If distRefPoint is specified, the value is converted to a path delay and is used as the alignment point for the timing group.

sPlaneIpAddressDN.description:

It is recommended to exclude the synchronization plane ToP traffic from encryption.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-1/IPADDRESSV4-1 (or MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-1/IPADDRESSV6-1)

topDomainNumber.description:
This parameter selects the ToP domain number the BTS integrated slave clock belongs to.

The recommended values depend on the selected value in parameter ieeeTelecomProfile (TOPF) or topStandardProfile (TOPP) 
 When TOP with frequency synchronization is used the recommended values are: 
 - IEEE1588 telecom profile: 0 
 - ITU telecom profile: 4 
When TOP with phase synchronization is used, the default value is 0
Note:
For compliance with the CCSA YD/T 2375, the ToP domain number must be configured to 0
For compliance with the ITU-T G.8275.1, the ToP domain number must be configured within the range: 24...43
For compliance with the ITU-T G.8275.2, the ToP domain number must be configured within the range: 44...63

topId.description: This is the instance identifier of the TOP object. The TOP contains ToP-synchronization-specific base station parameters.

actTopBoundaryClock.description:
This parameter activates/deactivates the feature "Timing over Packet (ToP) Boundary Clock". 
The parameter activates support for an IEEE1588-2008 Boundary Clock within the eNodeB. The Boundary Clock when enabled allows for IEEE1588-2008 synchronization through daisy-chained backhaul connections.
The feature is disabled by default.
Note: This parameter is applicable to FZM only.
actTopBoundaryClock.fullName: Feature Activation Flag ToP Boundary Clock

actTopMasterClock.description: Likely a true/false switch that enables or disables a behavior related to "activate/enable Top Master Clock" on the TOPB object. This description was auto-generated from the parameter's name and usage context (not individually verified against Nokia's official parameter dictionary), because this parameter did not appear frequently enough in the sample files to be hand-researched.

reqClntIpAddr.description: This parameter shows the IP address of the downstream client providing Request_Unicast_Transmission TLV's.

reqClntSyncMsgRateReq.description: This parameter shows the requested Sync messaging rate received from the downstream client Request_Unicast_Transmission TLV message.
reqClntSyncMsgRateReq.fullName: Requesting Client Sync Message Rate Request
reqClntSyncMsgRateReq.officialRange:
0: Not configured 
-3: 8 msg/sec 
-4: 16 msg/sec 
-5: 32 msg/sec 
-6: 64 msg/sec 
-7: 128 msg/sec

topClntUcastReqState.description: This parameter shows whether IEEE1588-2008 Unicast Transmission TLV requests are being periodically received from the downstream client.

topbId.description: This parameter identifies the Time Over Packet common configuration. The value is always 1.
topbId.fullName: Time over Packet common configuration identifier

acceptedClockClass.description:
This parameter defines the accepted clock classes. The supported and recommanded values are linked to the ieeeTelecomProfile :
 - IEEE1588: 6, 7, 13, 14, 
 - ITU_TELECOM_OPT1: 84, 90, 96 
 - ITU_TELECOM_OPT2: 80, 86

acceptedClockQuality.description: This parameter represents the accepted clock quality levels.

actTopFreqSynch.description:
This parameter activates/deactivates the feature "ToP with frequency synchronization".
ToP frequency synchronization (TOPF) is not supported for TDD release and therefore it cannot be activated.
actTopFreqSynch.fullName: Feature Activation Flag ToP with freq synchronization

announceRequestMode.description:
This parameter defines if the announce messages are requested from all configured ToP masters, or only from active and higher priority masters.
Supported values are:
1.) ANNOUNCE_ALL: Standard mode
2.) ANNOUNCE_ACTIVE_AND_HIGHER_PRIORITY: Nokia mode

Note: A change of the mode causes a restart of the ToP resilience functionality.

ieeeTelecomProfile.description:
This parameter defines the profile for selecting the active master:  
IEEE1588-2008 or ITU-T telecom profile (G.8265.1 (10/2010). 
The supported clock quality level are dependant on this parameter value.

lockState.description: This parameter shows if the ToP master is currently used as synchronization source. The value "locked" means the ToP master is currently used synchronization source. Please note that only one master can be in "locked" state at a time. This parameter shows if the ToP slave in the BTS is locked to this master. The value "locked" means that accurate reference clock is available and can be used as the timing source for the BTS. At most one master can be in “locked” state at a time.

logMeanSyncValue.description: This indicates how often a ToP sync message shall be send by the ToP master within the transmission duration request period (of 300 seconds).

masterClockState.description: This parameter shows if Timing over Packet master is working or not. The value "NOT_OK" means this master is not in a condition to be considered as synchronization source. “topMasterState”  will be set to OK if the ToP Master is sending Announce Message replies to FTM and the delivered clock quality is acceptable.

masterIpAddr.description:
This parameter defines the IP address of the ToP master. 
For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.
For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC2460.

The value for an IPv4 address must be outside the value range below:
        1.) IP address 0.0.0.0 
        2.) IP addresses 0.0.0.1 - 0.255.255.255.
	3.) Multicast addresses 224.0.0.0 - 239.255.255.255.
	4.) Class E addresses 240.0.0.0 - 255.255.255.254.
	5.) IP address 255.255.255.255.
	6.) Private addresses 192.168.253.0 - 192.168.255.255.
	7.) Loopback addresses 127.0.0.0 - 127.255.255.255.
        8.) Link Local  169.254.0.1 - 169.254.255.254

The value for an IPv6 address must be inside the range below:
        1.) global unicast only from 2000::/3
        2.) unique local unicast (FC00::/7)
masterIpAddr.fullName: IP Address of the ToP master

masterVisibility.description:
This parameter  indicates that the announce messages are received from master x.

This parameter is applicable ONLY for the ToP variant with Frequency sync.

priority_1.description:
This parameter defines the configured "priority 1" for this ToP master. 
Lower values mean higher preference for selecting the ToP master as the provider of the ToP clock signal.
The value range depends on the defined announceRequestMode and ieeeTelecomProfile.

If the ieeeTelecomProfile is set to IEEE1588 and the announceRequestMode is set to ANNOUNCE_ALL (Standard mode), 
the value range is 0..255, 
else the value range is 1..255.

priority_2.description:
This parameter defines the configured "priority 2" for this ToP master. 
Lower values mean higher preference for selecting the ToP master as the provider of the ToP clock signal.
The value range depends on the defined announceRequestMode and ieeeTelecomProfile.

receivedClockQuality.description: Received clock quality level from master
receivedClockQuality.fullName: Received clock quality level from master

receivedPriority_1.description:
This parameter holds the priority 1 as received from this Timing over Packet master. In case the configured priority 1 value equals 0, the received priority 1 is used for selecting the ToP master that shall be selected to provide the Timing over Packet clock signal.
Lower values mean higher preference.

receivedPriority_2.description:
This parameter holds the priority 2 as received from this Timing over Packet master. In case the configured priority 2 value equals 0, the received priority 2 is used for selecting the ToP master that shall be selected to provide the Timing over Packet clock signal.
Lower values mean higher preference.

receivedPriority_2.description:

This parameter is used only for Macro Bts.

syncMessageRate.description:
This parameter defines how often the ToP synchronisation message shall be sent by the ToP master within one second. The grant interval is fixed at 300 seconds.
The parameter is applicable only in unicast mode (profile Telecom2008 and G.8275.2)

topComMode.description:
This parameter defines the communication mode of ToP to be either "IP Unicast" or "Ethernet Multicast".
"IP Unicast" is applicable for network topologies with partial on-path support.

"Ethernet Multicast" is applicable for timing network topologies with full on-path support,
relating to the full on-path profile as defined at ITU-T G.8275.1.
"Ethernet Multicast" uses the ITU-T G.8275.1 defined multicast address for ToP.

topDomainNumber.description:
This parameter selects the ToP domain number the BTS integrated slave clock belongs to.

The recommended values depend on the selected value in parameter ieeeTelecomProfile (TOPF) or topStandardProfile (TOPP) 
 When TOP with frequency synchronization is used the recommended values are: 
 - IEEE1588 telecom profile: 0 
 - ITU telecom profile: 4 
When TOP with phase synchronization is used, the default value is 0
Note:
For compliance with the CCSA YD/T 2375, the ToP domain number must be configured to 0
For compliance with the ITU-T G.8275.1, the ToP domain number must be configured within the range: 24...43
For compliance with the ITU-T G.8275.2, the ToP domain number must be configured within the range: 44...63

topEthMulticastAddress.description: This parameter configures the Ethernet MAC address to be used as destination address in Timing over Packet Ethernet frames sent by the BTS.The recommended values is : 01-80-C2-00-00-0E

topMasterUsed.description:
This parameter shows if this master has been selected by ToP best master clock algorithm (BMCA) as the provider of the Timing over Packet clock signal.
This parameter is used only for Macro Bts.

topStandardProfile.description: This parameter is used to select the profile to be used for phase synchronization (Telecom2008, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, CCSA YD/T 2375). The selection of the profile determines if unicast (Telecom2008 and G.8275.2) or multicast (G.8275.1 and CCSA YD/T 2375) communication mode is used, and also determines the range of configurable values for the acceptedClockClass parameter.

toppId.description: This is the instance identifier of the TOPP object. The TOPP contains ToP  phase synchronization specific base station parameters.

tuningProfile.description: This parameter allows to select alternative tuning profiles within the ToP slave clock which are optimized for specific network conditions.

waitingTime.description:
This parameter defines the time in seconds the ToP slave has to wait, before switching over to another ToP master.
This parameter is used only for Macro Bts.

freqTraceable.description: This parameter indicates whether the current grandmaster clock in the timing network is traceable to a PRC clock.

lockState.description: This parameter shows if the slave clock is synchronizing (Locked) or not (Out of Lock) to the ToP Master

receivedPriority_2.description: This parameter holds the priority 2 assigned to the Grandmaster, as received from this ToP master.

targetDN.description: The Distinguished name of the associated target, defined in targetDNType.This parameter is set only when targetDNType is set to RAP. The associated MOC is APEQM.

timeTraceable.description: This parameter denotes whether the current Grandmaster clock in the timing network is traceable to a PRTC clock.

actCoreDumpFileCollection.description: Defines if core dump file collection is activated. Coredumpfile collection is activated by default. If some process crash happens a core dump file will be generated to analyze the root cause of the system failure.

actDccSupport.description: A Nokia-internal transport/board-administration feature toggle whose exact scope is not fully clear from its name; based on the class (transport board admin) it likely enables a data/control-channel related support capability on the transport board.

actDefaultFaultSnapTriggers.description: Activates the default set of fault conditions that automatically trigger a diagnostic snapshot capture.

actInternalTrace.description: Enables internal protocol/signalling tracing used for troubleshooting by field/support engineers.

actRemoteSyslogTransmission.description:
This parameter defines the operator’s selection of syslog transmission to a remote server.
The operator sets this flag to true to request the BTS to begin syslog transmission to the remote syslog server. The operator sets this flag to false to request the BTS to stop syslog transmission to the remote syslog server. The BTS also stops syslog transmission automatically after the specified Remote syslog transmission duration.

It is not useful to set this parameter for FSME based BTS as remote syslog transmission is not supported on this BTS type.
When actRemoteSyslogTransmission parameter is set to true but remoteSyslogTransmissionStatus (set by system) is false then false->true sequence is needed from NMS/BTSSM.

autRrcBasedSlCellDetHCheckFreq.description:
This parameter defines health check frequency used in automatic sleeping cell detection feature. RRC Success Rate factor is calculated with this period.
Parameter changed by Operator will be taken into use in next Healt Check period.
autRrcBasedSlCellDetHCheckFreq.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell detection health check frequency

autRrcBasedSlCellDetRrcSuccRateThr.description:
This parameter defines RRC Success Rate Threshold used in automatic sleeping cell detection feature, in percent.
If the calculated RRC Success Rate for the measurement period is less than this parameter, eNB/BTS will detect that the RRC Success Rate is degraded.
Value 100% shall be used only for test purposes.
Parameter changed by Operator will be taken into use in next Healt Check period.
autRrcBasedSlCellDetRrcSuccRateThr.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell detection RRC success rate threshold

autRrcBasedSlCellDetRrcVolThr.description:
This parameter defines RRC Volume Threshold per measurement period used in automatic sleeping cell detection feature.
Degraded RRC success rate health check and related recovery actions are enabled only when configured RRC attempts number in cell during the measurement period is above this value.
If the RRC attempts number in cell during the measurement period is less than this parameter, eNB/BTS will cancel all timers and clear alarms related to this health check and will resume monitoring once the RRC attempts number in cell is above the threshold.

Parameter changed by Operator will be taken into use in next Healt Check period.
autRrcBasedSlCellDetRrcVolThr.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell detection RRC volume threshold

autRrcBasedSlCellRecPh1Timer.description:
This parameter defines automatic sleeping cell recovery phase 1 timer.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
autRrcBasedSlCellRecPh1Timer.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell recovery phase 1 timer

autRrcBasedSlCellRecPh2Timer.description:
This parameter defines automatic sleeping cell recovery phase 2 timer.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
autRrcBasedSlCellRecPh2Timer.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell recovery phase 2 timer

autRrcBasedSlCellRecPh3Timer.description:

autRrcBasedSlCellRecPh3Timer.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell recovery phase 3 timer

autRrcBasedSlCellRecPhase1Act.description:

Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
autRrcBasedSlCellRecPhase1Act.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell recovery phase 1 activation

autRrcBasedSlCellRecPhase2Act.description:
This is activation flag to enable or disable automatic sleeping cell recovery phase 2.
Activation of this phase has impact to automatic cell locking/unlocking execution. This flag is by deafult disabled.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
autRrcBasedSlCellRecPhase2Act.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell recovery phase 2 activation

autRrcBasedSlCellRecPhase3Act.description:
This is activation flag to enable or disable automatic sleeping cell recovery phase 3.
Activation of this phase has impact to automatic RF Module reset execution. This flag is by deafult disabled.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
autRrcBasedSlCellRecPhase3Act.fullName: Automatic RRC based sleeping cell recovery phase 3 activation
