certTypeForTlsAuth.description: The certificate/key algorithm type (e.g. RSA) used for TLS mutual authentication on the management-plane connection.

diagSnapDestination.description:
This parameter defines the operator’s selection of the default diagnostic snapshot upload destination server.
The diagnostic snapshot is sent to the selected location ("netact", "lss") unless the operator overrides the selection by creating the DIAGSNAPREQ-diagSnapServerConfig structure with an IP Address and Port Number.
If the parameter is not configured, system will take the value of "netact" by default.

faultNumber.description:
Defines the fault number which shall trigger automatic symptom data collection
Fault numbers are defined for purely informatory purpose and may change between versions. Operator shall not base any automated processing on fault numbers.
Operator should modify this parameter only on explicit request by technical support.

lssIPaddress.description: This parameter holds the IP address of the local symptom server (LSS). The IPv4 is in dotted decimal format  or IPv6 in format defined in RFC4291.

lssPortNo.description: This parameter holds the port number of the diagnostic snapshot data server. 6514 for TLS and 514 for UDP are the standard ports used.
lssPortNo.fullName: Local symptoms server IP port number

maxNumSlCellRecActForCellPerDay.description:
This parameter defines maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for cell per day.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
maxNumSlCellRecActForCellPerDay.fullName: Maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for cell per day

maxNumSlCellRecActForRfmPerDay.description:
This parameter defines maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for RF Module per day.
Parameter changed by Operator during recovery action will be taken into use after recovery is completed.
maxNumSlCellRecActForRfmPerDay.fullName: Maximum number sleeping cell recovery actions for RFM per day

maxNumSnapByFaultTrigPerDay.description: Maximum number of fault-triggered diagnostic snapshots the system is allowed to capture per day, rate-limiting snapshot generation.

remoteSyslogDSCP.description:
This parameter specifies the DSCP value that will be used by the BTS for remote syslog transmission. 

The value of this parameter when changed from default could interfere with other traffic types. Caution should be exercised when changing this parameter.

remoteSyslogFormat.description: This parameter specifies whether the BTS should send syslogs to the remote syslog server in RFC 5424 format or NSN proprietary format. When the remote syslog server is either the OMS or the customer’s syslog server, RFC5424 format should be chosen. When the remote syslog server  is a NSN tool, proprietary format can be chosen.

remoteSyslogServerIPaddress.description:
This parameter holds the IP address of the remote syslog server.

The interface is disabled by setting the IP address to ""0.0.0.0"".

For IPv4, the parameter has to be entered in dotted decimal format.

For IPv6, the parameter has to be entered according to formats specified in RFC4291. 

IPv4 address ranges:
It is not allowed to configure the broadcast address 255.255.255.255 or an address within the range of multicast addresses
(224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) or loop-back addresses (127.0.0.0-127.255.255.255).

IPv6 address ranges:
It is recommended to configure only an address within the range of Unique Local Unicast addresses (FC00::/7) or Global Unicast addresses (2000::/3).

remoteSyslogServerPortNo.description: This parameter holds the port number of the remote syslog server. 6514 for TLS and 514 for UDP are the standard ports used. When the remote syslog server is chosen to be the OMS, only standard ports should be chosen.
remoteSyslogServerPortNo.fullName: Remote syslog server IP port number

remoteSyslogTransmitDuration.description:
This parameter defines the duration in minutes for remote syslog transmission.
This parameter specifies the duration in minutes for which the BTS should send syslogs to the remote syslog server. When the BTS is transmitting syslogs to a remote syslog server, the operator can override this parameter by setting the Remote syslog transmission parameter to OFF, even before the transmission for the duration specified by this parameter was completed.

remoteSyslogTransportProtocol.description:
This parameter defines the remote syslog transport protocol for remote syslog transmission.
When the remote syslog server is a NSN tool, UDP protocol must be chosen.
When syslogs are to be sent by the BTS to the remote syslog server, using UDP in an IPsec tunnel, this parameter must be set to UDP.

snapshotUploadDelayForFault6450.description:
Alarm with fault: 6450 EFaultId_TechnicalLogUploadRecommended is reported to inform that DSP memory dumps or baseband module /system module core dumps have been collected after DSP/baseband module/system module crash. To upload the dumps from the BTS, the snapshot files (technical log files) upload from the BTS is necessary.
This parameter defines the delay after which the BTS shall automatically collect and upload snapshot files on fault 6450 detection. 

If this parameter is changed after an alarm with fault 6450 is reported, the active alarm with fault 6450 will be processed based on value of the parameter before this change. Alarms with fault 6450 reported after the parameter change will be processed based on the changed parameter value.

snapshotUploadDestinationForFault6450.description: Destination to which the diagnostic snapshot captured for fault code 6450 is uploaded, e.g. a local storage server or NetAct.

syslogSubstringTrigger.description:
This parameter defines the syslog string that will trigger automated snapshot collection.
When LTE2250 is activated, operator must set trigger substring that will be searched in syslog and if found, will cause snapshot collection.
String must have at least 10 characters.
Operator should modify this parameter only on explicit request by technical support.

trblCAdmId.description: This is an instance identifier of object Troubleshooting Common Administration.

triggerType.description:
Defines if fault symptom data collection is triggered at fault detection or only when alarm is sent
Operator should modify this parameter only on explicit request by technical support.

diagSnapAddInfo.description: This parameter includes valuable detailed information about the diagnostic snapshot collection process. For example, what triggered the diagnostic snapshot collection.

diagSnapFilename.description: This parameter reports the name of the diagnostic snapshot file. The diagnostic snapshot file is created as a zip file.

diagSnapState.description:
This parameter reports the state of the latest diagnostic snapshot collection and upload triggered by NetAct, WebEM, or an external application.

The following values are valid for diagnostic snapshot collection to be uploaded to NetAct or WebEM.

1) Collection requested
2) Collection ongoing
3) Collection ready
4) Collection failed
5) Upload completed
6) Upload failed

The following values are valid for diagnostic snapshot collection to be uploaded to an external server (e.g., Local Symptoms Server, or PC).
1) Collection requested
2) Collection ongoing
3) Collection completed
4) Collection failed
diagSnapState.fullName: Diagnostic snapshot collection and upload state

remoteSyslogTransmissionStatus.description:
This parameter defines whether syslog transmission to remote server is currently ON or OFF at the BTS.
The BTS sets this flag to true before it begins syslog transmission to the remote syslog server and sets it to false after it stops syslog transmission to the remote syslog server

trblCAdmRId.description: This is an instance identifier of the read only TRBLCADM object.
trblCAdmRId.fullName: Troubleshooting Common Administration read only instance identifier

false2TrueDelay.description:
This parameter defines the time, in seconds, by which the state change from FALSE to TRUE shall be delayed. 
If the logical result changes from FALSE to TRUE, the effective change of the state will be delayed by the timer value defined in this parameter.

This can be applied (Eg. Fast IP Re-Routing) :
- Route Re-installation Delay of Primary Path routes into the kernel routing table.
- Switch from Alternative Path back to Primary Path.

itemDN.description:
This parameter defines the object which shall be considered as a trigger item. This object will be logically combined to the defined trigger Logic. For example, TriggerItem will be a BFD object - the BFD object will use the state of the corresponding BFD Session. "UP" will be used as TRUE while all others will be used as FALSE. 
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example:
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPAPP-1/BFD-10

itemId.description: This parameter uniquely identifies an entry within the list.

logic.description: This parameter defines the logical behavior of the listed trigger items.

triggerId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier for the TRIGGER object.

true2FalseDelay.description:
This parameter defines the time, in seconds, by which the state change from TRUE to FALSE shall be delayed. 
If the logical result changes from TRUE to FALSE, the effective change of the state will be delayed by the timer value defined in this parameter.

This can be applied (Eg. Fast IP Re-Routing) :
- Route Removal Delay of Primary Path routes out of the kernel routing table.
- Switch from Primary Path to Alternative Path.

itemId.description: This parameter identifies an entry within the list.

state.description: This parameter indicates the state of the trigger. States are "false" and "true". The meaning of the state will be defined at the objects using the triggger states.

triggerRId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier for the read only TRIGGER object.

prodCodePlanned.description:
Defines the planned product code for the unit and it is used by planning tools before BTS is commissioned. After BTS is commissioned, product code parameter (productCode) from autodetected runtime unit is used by BTS SW.
This is the product code entered at commissioning to indicate the planned unit to be installed.

availabilityStatus.officialRange:
0: in test 
1: failed 
2: power off 
3: off line 
4: off duty 
5: dependency 
6: degraded 
7: not installed 
8: log full

configDN.description: This parameter contains distinguished name (DN) of respective configuration managed object.
configDN.fullName: Distinguished name of paired configured managed object.

operationalState.description: This parameter describes operability state of the Managed Object.

productCode.description: Indicates the product code of the unit.

productName.description: This parameter indicates the name of the module as used in Feature Descriptions, Customer communication etc., e.g. FSMF for a System Module.

serialNumber.description: Indicates the serial number of the unit.

trModRId.description: Defines the transport module runtime identifier.

The related read only object will provide the actually assigned IP address.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-1

ipV4AddressDN2.description:

The related runtime object will provide the actually assigned IP address.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-2

ipV6AddressDN1.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the IPADDRESSV6 object instance which holds the IPv6 address to be used for the first C-Plane.
The related read only object will provide the actually assigned IP address.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-6/IPADDRESSV6-1.
The parameter cPlane-ipV6AddressDN1 can be configured always. It will be taken into operational use only when actDualStackIpV4V6ForS1X2=TRUE

transportNwId.description: This parameter defines the identifier of the transport network.

transportNwInUse.description:
This parameter defines whether the configuration related to the transport network shall be enabled.
The configuration of the main transport network must be always enabled.

trsNwId.description: This parameter is the instance identifier of the TRSNW object. It uniquely identifies the object.

administrativeState.description:
Administrative state of the cell, the value is set by the operator.
Note: This parameter used for NB-IoT standalone cell.
administrativeState.fullName: Administrative State of the TWAMP measurement session

destIpAddress.description:
This parameter defines the destination IP address of the TWAMP session.
IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported.
IPv4 address format: Dot-decimal notation (x.x.x.x). Example: 10.10.10.10.
IPv6 address format: x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. Example: ABCD:EF01:2345:6789:ABCD:EF01:2345:6789.
The IPv6 address has to be defined always in full length. Short formats are not supported.

destPort.description: This parameter defines the UDP destination port for the TWAMP test messages.

dscp.description: This parameter defines the DSCP value which will be put in the outgoing ICMP echo request packet.
dscp.fullName: DSCP value for TWAMP message transmission

messageSize.description: This parameter defines the size, in octets, of the TWAMP messages sent by the TWAMP initiator on this session.

plrAlarmThreshold.description:
This parameter defines the threshold, in %, for raising the TWAMP session alarm for reasons of excessive packet loss ratio (PLR).
The alarm is raised if the packet loss ratio observed over a 15-minute evaluation period equals or exceeds the threshold value. The alarm will be cleared if the packet loss ratio drops below the threshold value for two consecutive 15-minute observation periods.
Setting PLR Threshold to the maximum value (100%) is valid but not recommended. An alarm would be triggered only in extreme cases, e.g. when "the line is cut" or "the reflector at peer end is gone".

rttAlarmThreshold.description:
This parameter defines the threshold, in microseconds, for raising the TWAMP session alarm for reasons of excessive round-trip-time (RTT).
The alarm is raised if the average round-trip-time of the TWAMP messages, calculated during a 1-minute evaluation period, equals or exceeds the configured threshold. The alarm will be cleared if, during 5 consecutive 1-minute periods, the average value of the RTT remains below the threshold.
Setting the value of this parameter to 1 000 000 microseconds means that the alarm will never be raised.

sourceIpAddress.description:
This parameter specifies the source IP address of TWAMP initiator messages. The TWAMP session must be locked, before its source IP address can be changed.

Both IP address formats can be used.
Format: IPv4 address parameter in dotted decimals or IPv6 address parameter acc. to RFC 4291.
sourceIpAddress.fullName: TWAMP initiator messages source IP address

sourceIpAddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the IPADDRESSV4 or IPADDRESSV6 object instance which holds the IPv4 or IPv6 address to be used as source IP address for TWAMP initiator messages.
The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example:
MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-1
sourceIpAddressDN.fullName: Source IP address of the TWAMP initiator

twampDscp.description: This parameter defines the DSCP value to be used for transmission of the TWAMP messages over the session.
twampDscp.fullName: DSCP value for TWAMP message transmission

twampId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the TWAMP object. It uniquely identifies the object.

twampReflectorEnabled.description: This parameter enables/disables the TWAMP reflector functionality on the corresponding local IP address.

twampReflectorLocalIpAddressDN.description:

The value has to be given as distinguished name (DN).
Example:

twampReflectorLocalIpAddressDN.fullName: TWAMP reflector local IP address reference

twampReflectorUdpEchoEnabled.description: This parameter enables/disables the UDP echo server functionality on the corresponding local IP address.

twampStatReqId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the TWAMP statistics request object. It uniquely identifies the object.

twampStatisticsRequest.description: This parameter allows to request the current statistics of an active TWAMP session.

avgRTT_15Min.description: This parameter holds the average round trip time in microseconds for TWAMP messages during the last quarter of an hour.
avgRTT_15Min.fullName: Average TWAMP round-trip-time for the last 15 minutes

avgRTT_1Min.description: This parameter holds the average round trip time in microseconds for TWAMP messages during the last minute.
avgRTT_1Min.fullName: Average TWAMP round-trip-time during the last minute

lostTwampMessages.description: This parameter holds the total number of lost TWAMP messages since the start or re-start of the TWAMP session.
lostTwampMessages.fullName: Total number of lost TWAMP messages

maxRTT_15Min.description: This parameter holds the maximum round trip time in microseconds detected for TWAMP messages during the last quarter of an hour.
maxRTT_15Min.fullName: Maximum TWAMP round-trip-time for the last 15 minutes

maxRTT_1Min.description: This parameter holds the maximum round trip time in microseconds detected for TWAMP messages during the last minute.
maxRTT_1Min.fullName: Maximum TWAMP round-trip-time during the last minute

minRTT_15Min.description: This parameter holds the minimum round trip time in microseconds detected for TWAMP messages during the last quarter of an hour.
minRTT_15Min.fullName: Minimum TWAMP round-trip-time for the last 15 minutes

minRTT_1Min.description: This parameter holds the minimum round trip time in microseconds detected for TWAMP messages during the last minute.
minRTT_1Min.fullName: Minimum TWAMP round-trip-time during the last minute

twampStatResId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the TWAMP statistics response object. It uniquely identifies the object.

twampStatisticsResult.description: This parameter returns the result of the TWAMP statistics request.
twampStatisticsResult.fullName: Result of the TWAMP statistics request

txTwampMessages.description: This parameter holds the total number of transmitted TWAMP messages since the start or re-start of the TWAMP session.
txTwampMessages.fullName: Total number of transmitted TWAMP messages

UFFIM.officialFullName: Utran FDD frequency Idle Mode parameters

dlCarFrqUtra.description: Contains the Downlink Frequency (Nd) as ARFCN value

idleLBUtranFddCelResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the UTRAN FDD carrier frequency used for idle mode load balancing.
For this parameter, 6 is the highest priority and 0 the lowest.

Note:
According to 3GPP 36.304, carriers in different RATs must have different Cell Reselection Priorities.
idleLBUtranFddCelResPrio.fullName: UTRA-FDD carrier freq prio for idle mode load balancing

idleLBUtranFddCelResWeight.description:
Weight factor of UTRA-FDD carrier frequency used by round robin algorithm for idle mode load balancing.
When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in selecting main target for IdleModeMobilityControlInfo for load balancing. Weighted round robin algorithm shall select always one target frequency for idle mode load balancing, which is matching UE capabilities, to be used as main target for idle mode load balancing and this target will have always highest  priority assigned in RRC Release message.  All other target frequency for idle mode load balancing matching UE capabilities and configured in LNCEL, IRFIM, UFFIM, CDFIM and GNFL will be added as well, but with lowered priorities as configured for SIB with kept hierarchy of priorities.  The algorithm shall calculate proportional weights corresponding to configured values. There is no check about the sum of weights configured by the user.
idleLBUtranFddCelResWeight.fullName: UTRA-FDD carrier weight factor idle mode load balancing

idleLBUtranTddCelResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the UTRAN TDD carrier frequency used for idle mode load balancing.
For this parameter, 6 is the highest prio and 0 the lowest.
When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in IdleModeMobilityControlInfofor load balancing.

Note:
According to 3GPP 36.304, carriers in different RATs must have different Cell Reselection Priorities.
idleLBUtranTddCelResPrio.fullName: UTRA-TDD carrier freq prio for idle mode load balancing

idleLBUtranTddCelResWeight.description:
Weight factor of UTRA-TDD carrier frequency used by round robin algorithm for idle mode load balancing.
When the parameter is not defined, the corresponding carrier is not used in selecting main target for IdleModeMobilityControlInfo for load balancing. Weighted round robin algorithm shall select always one target frequency for idle mode load balancing, which is matching UE capabilities, to be used as main target for idle mode load balancing and this target will have always highest  priority assigned in RRC Release message.  All other target frequency for idle mode load balancing matching UE capabilities and configured in LNCEL, IRFIM, UFFIM, CDFIM and GNFL will be added as well, but with lowered priorities as configured for SIB with kept hierarchy of priorities.  The algorithm shall calculate proportional weights corresponding to configured values. There is no check about the sum of weights configured by the user.
idleLBUtranTddCelResWeight.fullName: UTRA-TDD carrier weight factor idle mode load balancing

qQualMinUtra.description: This specifies the minimum required quality level in the cell in dB. It is not applicable to TDD cells or GSM cells or E-UTRA cells.

qRxLevMinUtra.description: This specifies the minimum required RX level in the cell in dBm

uCelResPrio.description:
Absolute priority of the UTRA carrier frequency

Equal priorities between RATs are not supported according to [3GPP 36.304].

uffimId.description: This parameter uniquely identifies an UFFIM (UTRAN Frequency Idle Mode configuration) managed object.
uffimId.fullName: Utran FDD idle mode configuration identifier

utrResTiFHM.description: The field t-ReselectionUTRA is multiplied by this factor if the UE is in the high mobility state as defined in 36.304.
utrResTiFHM.fullName: UTRA cell reselection timer factor high mobility

utrResTiFMM.description: The field t-ReselectionUTRA is multiplied by this factor if the UE is in the medium mobility state as defined in 36.304.
utrResTiFMM.fullName: UTRA cell reselection timer factor medium mobility

utraFrqQThrHighR9.description:
This specifies the  quality threshold used by the UE when reselecting towards a higher priority UTRA RAT 
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9

utraFrqQThrLowR9.description:
This specifies the  quality threshold used by the UE when reselecting towards a lower priority UTRA RAT 
Not recognized by UEs < Rel9

utraFrqThrH.description: This specifies the threshold used by the UE when reselecting towards a higher priority frequency X than the current serving frequency

utraFrqThrL.description: This specifies the threshold used in reselection towards the frequency X priority from a higher priority frequency

a3OffsetCoMp.description:
Margin for intra-frequency better cell UL CoMP.
Used in UL CoMP measurement event type A3 where the event is triggered when the neighbor cell becomes better than the serving cell by the value of the A3 offset. The IE value is multiplied by 2.

a3ReportIntervalCoMp.description:
Defines the interval with which measurement reports are sent as long as the specific criteria for the UL CoMP measurement event A3 are met (Intra-Frequency).
This parameter defines the interval with which measurement reports are repeatedly sent as long as the specific criteria for the UL CoMP measurement event A3 are met. Value definitions as stated in 3GPP TS36.331: value MS120 corresponds to 120 ms, MS240 to 240 ms and so on, while value MIN1 corresponds to 1 min, MIN6 to 6 min and so on.
a3ReportIntervalCoMp.fullName: A3 report interval for UL CoMP

a3TimeToTriggerCoMp.description:
Time for which the specific criteria for the UL CoMP measurement event A3 must be met in order to trigger a measurement report (Intra-Frequency).

Value definitions as stated in 3GPP TS36.331: value MS0 corresponds to 0 ms, MS40 to 40 ms and so on.
a3TimeToTriggerCoMp.fullName: A3 time to trigger for UL CoMP

hysA3OffsetCoMp.description:
Related hysteresis margin for UL CoMP better cell of intra-frequency RSRP.
Parameter is used within the entry and leave condition of the A3 triggered reporting condition. The IE value is multiplied by 2.
hysA3OffsetCoMp.fullName: Hysteresis A3 offset RSRP intra-frequency for UL CoMP

ulCoMpCellList.description:
List of cells belonging to the same uplink comp set  (UL CoMP).

Configuration rule for a TDD UL CoMP set:
For 4 Rx UL-CoMP (LTE1691), only cells with 15 MHz and 20 MHz bandwidth are supported.
For 2 Rx, 4 Rx and 8 Rx UL-CoMP (LTE1402, LTE2104 and LTE2128) cells with 10 MHz, 15 MHz and 20 MHz bandwidth are supported.

ulCoMpId.description:
This parameter uniquely identifies a ULCOMP instance.
eNB will dynamically decide dependent on the current and newly required DSP deployment if eNB restart or dropping of all cells is needed.

ulCoMpMode.description:
This parameter defines the mode of UL coordinated multipoint (CoMP) reception. It is applicable only for a UL CoMP group of TDD cell instances.

IQ_Combining: uses IQ combining algorithm
SoftBit_Combining: shall be used for 4 RX / 8 RX UL CoMP reception with softbit combining.

eNB will dynamically decide dependent on the current and newly required DSP deployment if eNB restart or dropping of all cells is needed.

ulCoMpSinrThreshold.description:
Signal-Interference-Noise Ratio to be use for uplink CoMP operation.
The received uplink signal from a neighbor cell is combined to the serving cell signal if its SINR is less than ulCoMPSinrThreshold below the SINR of the serving cell signal.
The recommended default value is for:
- 2RX CoMP: 10 dB
- 4RX CoMP: 15 dB

Note:
For 4-RX / 8-RX CoMP with Softbit combination, the parameter is not used. A3 measurement configuration is done in a3UlCoMpConfig.

ulCoMpSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC ULCOMPSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an ULCOMPSPARE instance.

value.description:
This is the value of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The allowed parameter values are defined in the feature specification.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.

lnCelId.description: Instance identifier of MOC LNCEL in own eNB.

uMbsfnId.description: This parameter uniquely identifies a UMBSFN instance.

uMbsfnShareMax.description:
Defines the maximum Unicast MBSFN subframe pattern share based on the proportion of the system capacity that shall be reserved for Unicast PDSCH over MBSFN.
The uMbsfnShareMax should be at least 30%, i.e. this is a "strong" recommendation.
E.g. a value of 50 represents the operator desire that at most 50% of subframes are reserved for Unicast PDSCH over MBSFN and 50% is left for normal subframe (nsf) PDSCH.
This parameter impacts the calculation of the value of subframeAllocation(fourFrames) defined in TS36.331 and sent in SIB2, i.e. corresponding to uMbsfnShareUsed.
The eNB automatically selects a MBSFN subframe configuration pattern which is both: 
- consistent with other enabled features (ETWS/CMAS, OTDOA), and other factors e.g. related to CSI-RS,  and 
- will be less than or equal to uMbsfnShareMax
uMbsfnShareMax.fullName: Max DL unicast MBSFN subframe pattern share

uMbsfnShareUsed.description:
This is a read only parameter that models (i.e. reflects) exactly what share of DL subframes are used by Unicast MBSFN within a 40ms time window.
Indicates the Unicast MBSFN subframe share which was selected by the eNB and is currently in use. 
A value of 50 indicates 50% of subframes are reserved for Unicast MBSFN and 50% is left for non-MBSFN (i.e. nsf or normal subframes).
This parameter determines the following SIB2 values that configures MBSFN (commonSF-Alloc, FourFrame) as defined in TS36.331.
uMbsfnShareUsed.fullName: TM MBSFN sf pattern share used

enableRP301Interface.description:
Configure and designate EIF2(Outdoor)/EIF5(Indoor) in the BTS as an RP3-01 interface.
NOTE: This parameter should be "false" by default for FSM and FSI. This parameter should be "true" by default for FSIH.
By default the shared RP3-01/EIF port shall be used as Transport interface for FSM and FSI.The default is RF for FSIH.

Note: This is not relevant for FlexiZone Micro product.

unitTypeExpectedString.description: This parameter allows to manually define hardware unit type product code. Valid only if 'Set by UNIT-unitTypeExpectedString' is selected from expected hardware unit type's list. Entered string shall contain only product code of expected hardware unit type (i.e. 471234A).

queue.description: This parameter defines the queue which shall be used for a defined VLAN ID or VLAN ID range.
queue.officialRange:
0: EF 
1: AF4 
2: AF3 
3: AF2 
4: AF1 
5: BE

vlanIdHighValue.description:
This parameter defines the upper value of a contiguous range of VLAN identifiers.
The lower value is defined by parameter 'vlanIdLowValue'.

For a single VLAN identifier value, the values for vlanIdLowValue and vlanIdHighValue must be equal.
vlanIdHighValue.fullName: Upper value of VLAN identifier range

vlanIdLowValue.description:
This parameter defines the lower value of a contiguous range of VLAN identifiers.
The upper value is defined by parameter 'vlanIdHighValue'.
For a single VLAN identifier value, the values for vlanIdLowValue and vlanIdHighValue must be equal.
vlanIdLowValue.fullName: Low value of VLAN identifier range

vlanIdToQMapId.description:
This parameter defines the instance identifier of the VLAN ID to queue mapping object. It uniquely identifies the object.
This managed object defines the enqueuing of Ethernet frames with a corresponding VLAN ID value or range.
At least one managed object instance must be defined when qosClassificationCriteria is set to VLAN-ID.
At most 16 instances of the managed object can be defined.
vlanIdToQMapId.fullName: DSCP to queue mapping object identifier

userLabel.description: The label that can be used for a usage description of the BFD session.

vlanId.description: This parameter defines the VLAN ID to be used at this VLAN interface.

vlanIfId.description: This parameter defines the instance identifier of the VLAN interface object. It uniquely identifies the object.

availabilityStatus.description: Defines the availability status of the virtual machine.
availabilityStatus.officialRange:
0: in test 
1: failed 
2: power off 
3: off line 
4: off duty 
5: dependency 
6: degraded 
7: not installed 
8: log full 
10: on line

operationalState.description: Defines the  operational status (disable,enable) of the virtual machine.

swVersion.description: Defines the software of the virtual machine.

usageState.description: Defines the Usage state (idle, active) of the virtual machine.

vmName.description: Defines the hostname of the virtual machine.

vmRId.description: Defines the virtual machine runtime identifier.

badQualityDLGapThres.description:
Time duration with consecutive QCI1 DL PDCP packet losses or discards in order to consider voice quality as bad.

If the parameter is not configured then DL voice gap is not considered as voice quality criterion.
badQualityDLGapThres.fullName: Bad quality DL voice gap threshold

badQualityRBlerThres.description:
Final residual BLER threshold for bad voice quality. The parameter applies for TTI- and non-TTI mode.

If the parameter is not configured then final residual BLER is not considered as voice quality criterion.

If harqMaxTrUl = 1, the final residual BLER equals the BLER (target value 10%) and badQualityRBlerThres should be set to > 10% .

badQualityULGapThres.description:
Time duration with consecutive QCI1 UL PDCP packet losses or discards in order to consider voice quality as bad.

If the parameter is not configured then UL voice gap is not considered as voice quality criterion.
badQualityULGapThres.fullName: Bad quality UL voice gap threshold

goodQualityGapThres.description: DL/UL time duration with consecutive successful transmissions/receptions to consider voice quality as good
goodQualityGapThres.fullName: Good quality UL DL voice gap threshold

goodQualityRBlerThres.description:
Final residual BLER threshold for good voice quality. The parameter applies for TTI- and non-TTI mode.

If harqMaxTrUl = 1, the final residual BLER equals the BLER (target value 10%) and goodQualityRBlerThres should be set to > 10% .

rBlerCondTimeToTrigger.description: Time for which the final residual BLER condition must be met in order to consider voice quality as bad or good.
rBlerCondTimeToTrigger.fullName: Residual BLER condition time to trigger

voLteQualPrId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of the MOC VOLTEQUALPR.
It uniquely identifies an instance of the VoLTE quality profile (VOLTEQUALPR).

name.description:
This is the name of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The content is filled by the BTS and cannot be changed.

The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

value.description:
This is the value of the parameter and the class it belongs to. The allowed parameter values are defined in the feature specification.

The value of this spare parameter must be according to the provided information. It need to be case sensitive. In case the specified value doesn't match the supported values for this spare parameter, the BTS will reject the configuration.

voLteQualPrSpareId.description:
This parameter is the naming attribute of MOC VOLTEQUALPRSPARE.
It uniquely identifies an VOLTEQUALPRSPARE instance.

name.description:
This is the name of the read only parameter and the class it belongs to.
The mapping of the parameter to the particular feature is defined in the documentation.

acceptableFrameTypes.description:
If the value of this parameter is "AdmitTagged", the device will discard untagged and Priority-tagged frames received on this interface. If the value is “AdmitAll”, tagged, untagged, and Priority-tagged frames received on this interface will be accepted. Untagged and Priority-tagged frames are assigned to the VLAN defined by the portDefaultVlanId parameter for this interface.
Notes:
1) Priority tagged" frames (IEEE 802.1Q tagged frames with VLAN ID=0) can be configured via the VLAN filter list of parameter l2VlanIdList.
2) Ethernet management frames (i.e. Synchronous Ethernet and Ethernet OAM frames) are always allowed to ingress and egress the Ethernet interface of the layer 2 switch independent of the status of the value of the discardUntagged parameter.

actWiFi.description: Enable or disable WiFi. Only applicable to hardware variants with integrated WiFi.

factoryResetWiFi.description: This is an action parameter to trigger WiFi Access Point to reboot and come up with factory setting.

l2VlanIdList.description:
This parameter specifies the VLANs that are supported over this Ethernet/WiFi interface. The parameter is a list of up to 2 entries where each entry represents  single VLAN identifier.

For Flexi Zone Micro there are limits on the total number of VLANs that can be configured - maximum of 2 VLANs can be configured.

Note: If hardware type is FWHC  this parameter is not used.
l2VlanIdList.fullName: Layer 2 switch member VLAN identifier list

portDefaultPriority.description:
Default VLAN priority for untagged frames.

Every untagged ingress Ethernet frame at this interface gets assigned this Port Default Priority. If QoS classification mode is configured to VLAN-PCP, this priority is used for enqueing decision of the frame. If the frame egresses the switch tagged, this priority shall be used in the VLAN tag header.

rebootWiFi.description: This is an action parameter to trigger reboot of WiFi.

wiFiUplinkRateLimiter.description:
This parameter limits the amount of uplink traffic in Mbps originated from WiFi Access Point, in order to prevent starvation of the shared backhaul due to large amount of WiFi traffic.

The default value is 300 Mbps.
Note: This parameter is applicable for Flexi Zone Outdoor Micro Enhanced variants with integrated WiFi and Flexi Zone Multi-Band Outdoor (MBO) variants with integrated WiFi.

wificnfId.description: This parameter identifies WiFi configuration object.

activityBasedULPowCtrlEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if the activity-based UL power control for Rel99 feature is activated or not in the BTS. When the feature is activated, it allows to reduce the UL interference coming from Rel99 UE L1 control channel when there is no data to send (DTX).
activityBasedULPowCtrlEnabled.fullName: Activity based UL power control for Rel99 DCH enabled

advHSUPATimeDivSchedEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if the advanced HSUPA Time Division Scheduling feature is activated or not in the BTS. When the feature is activated, it allows higher bit rate in one HARQ for the 2ms UEs. Otherwise, the bit rate is limited to the avarage bitrate of 40 kbps in one HARQ.
advHSUPATimeDivSchedEnabled.fullName: Advanced HSUPA time division scheduling enabled

antRxLevelMonitoringEnabled.description:
This parameter defines if the RX Level Monitoring feature is enabled or disabled.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

cPlaneDscp.description: This parameter defines the differentiated services code point (DSCP) value assigned to the WCDMA control plane traffic.

cacMode.description:
This parameter defines whether a common committed bit rate or dedicated committed bit rate shall be used per configured WCDMA user plane.
1.) If set to "dedicatedCac" the defined committedBitRate for each individual user plane will be taken into account for connection admission control.
2.) If set to "commonCac" the defined committedBitRateCommon will be taken into account for all WCDMA user planes.

carrierAggregationEnabled.description:
This parameter indicates if the Carrier Aggregation Optimized Frequency Based BB Pooling feature is activated in the BTS or not. When the feature is activated, it is allowed to enable large carrier aggregation configurations without the need for sector-based pooling in FSM-r3 configurations. The carrier aggregation between multiple MAC-hs instances will be supported so that carrier aggregation between LCGs is possible. There is an allowed carrier aggregation for Dual Cell or Dual Band HSDPA user. 
Note: This parameter is valid only for FSM-r3 or newer.

ccPolicy.description:
This parameter affects how GBR and NBR connections are treated in Iub interface congestion situation. The SPI classes with GBR connections should be set to "1", while SPI classes with operator-configured NBR values (or no NBRs at all) shoule be set to "0". When congestion is detected, the Iub capacity is provided first to GBR connections and then to active NBR connections. The excess is distributed to best effort users according to the operator-configured QoS weighting.
Setting the value to "2" disables congestion control from this SPI class (for example, if streaming is mapped to separate transport path).

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.
ccPolicy.fullName: HSDPA congestion control policy for SPI

cchicEnabled.description: The parameter indicates if the Control Channel Interference Cancellation feature is activated in the BTS or not.

committedBitRate.description: This parameter denotes the committed bit rate for WCDMA user plane connection admission control.

committedBitRateCommon.description: This parameter defines the common committed bit rate to be used for all WCDMA user planes.

cqiDefaultHsCellFach.description:
This parameter defines the default CQI value for the HS Cell_FACH state.

The default CQI value is used when the CQI feedback is disabled (in Rel7), or when the CQI has not yet been received (in Rel8). This parameter is valid for RAN1913 High Speed Cell_FACH feature and applicable only to enhance the Cell_FACH state.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.
cqiDefaultHsCellFach.fullName: Default CQI value for HS Cell_FACH state

currentSctpIpAddress.description: This is the far end SCTP tunnel IP address that is used at the current moment.
currentSctpIpAddress.fullName: Currently used far end SCTP tunnel IP address

dynamicBasebandHsRachEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if the Dynamic Baseband for High Speed RACH feature is activated in the BTS or not. When the feature is activated, it allows dynamic allocation of baseband HW resources for active HS RACH users based on the utilization (traffic) in the LCG for optimal baseband resource usage in BTS.
dynamicBasebandHsRachEnabled.fullName: Dynamic Baseband for High Speed RACH enabled

epicEnabled.description: The parameter indicates whether the Enhanced Parallel Interference Cancellation (ePIC) feature is activated in the BTS.
epicEnabled.fullName: Enhanced parallel interference cancellation in use

fdeEnabled.description:
This parameter indicates whether the Frequency Domain Equalizer (FDE) feature is activated in the BTS.

Note: The FDE feature should not be enabled in a BTS configuration having 4-way RX diversity cells.

highBitrateTDSchedEnabled.description: The parameter indicates if the HSUPA High Bitrate Time Division Scheduling feature is activated in the BTS or not.
highBitrateTDSchedEnabled.fullName: HSUPA High Bitrate Time Division Scheduling enabled

hsdpaFairPacketSched.description: This parameter enables the high-speed downlink packet access (HSDPA) Proportional Fair Resource Packet scheduler feature.
hsdpaFairPacketSched.fullName: HSDPA proportional fair resource packet scheduler

id.description:
This parameter denotes HSDPA Quality of Service Scheduling Priority Indicator (SPI) class identifier (0-15). This is standard defined identification of a priority class with zero being the lowest priority and 15 being the highest.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.
id.fullName: QoS scheduling for SPI class identification

identifier.description: This parameter identifies the entry within the C-plane configurations list.

ipV4AddressDN.description:
This parameter defines the reference to the IPADDRESSV4 object instance which holds the IPv4 address to be used for WCDMA C-Plane.
The related read-only object will provide the actually allocated IP address.
Example: MRBTS-1/TNLSVC-1/TNL-1/IPNO-1/IPIF-17/IPADDRESSV4-1

ircReceiverEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if the IRC (Interference Rejection Combining) Receiver is activated or not in the BTS. If the feature is activated, the IRC algorithm will provide protection against intra-cell, inter-cell, and external interference. The IRC Receiver setting is valid only in BTS configurations having 2RX or 4RX cells.

maxIubDelayThreshold.description:
The Iub congestion control begins rate control actions when the average delay is above the minimum delay threshold (ThMin). The aggressiveness of the rate control increases linearly as the average delay nears the maximum delay threshold (ThMax). The operator can configure a middle threshold between the minimum and maximum thresholds for delay monitoring purposes. The rate control actions are recorded to counter M5000C176 when the average delay is between ThMin and ThMid, and to M5000C177 when the average delay is above ThMid.

The delay thresholds are properly configured when the following condition is true:
Thmin <= Thmid <= Thmax

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

midIubDelayThreshold.description:
The Iub congestion control begins rate control actions when the average delay is above the minimum delay threshold (ThMin). The aggressiveness of the rate control increases linearly as the average delay nears the maximum delay threshold (ThMax). The operator can configure a middle threshold between the minimum and maximum thresholds for delay monitoring purposes. The rate control actions are recorded to counter M5000C176 when the average delay is between ThMin and ThMid, and to M5000C177 when the average delay is above ThMid.

The delay thresholds are properly configured when the following condition is true:
Thmin <= Thmid <= Thmax

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

minIubDelayThreshold.description:
The Iub congestion control begins rate control actions when the average delay is above the minimum delay threshold (ThMin). The aggressiveness of the rate control increases linearly as the average delay nears the maximum delay threshold (ThMax). The operator can configure a middle threshold between the minimum and maximum thresholds for delay monitoring purposes. The rate control actions are recorded to counter M5000C176 when the average delay is between ThMin and ThMid, and to M5000C177 when the average delay is above ThMid.

The delay thresholds are properly configured when the following condition is true:
Thmin <= Thmid <= Thmax

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

numberOfBlindRepetitionHsCellFach.description:
This parameter defines the number of blind repetitions of the MAC-ehs PDUs in the HS Cell_FACH state.

The number of blind repetitions of the MAC-ehs PDUs occurs in the absence of ACK/NACK value from the UE (in Rel7), or when ACK/NACK has not yet been received (in Rel8). This parameter is valid for RAN1913 High Speed Cell_FACH feature and applicable only to enhance the Cell_FACH state.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.
numberOfBlindRepetitionHsCellFach.fullName: Number of blind repetition HS Cell_FACH state

numberOfCCCHSet.description:
This parameter defines the CCCH processing set capacity that is allowed to be used by the BTS SW.

The end-user should be able to select how many CCCH processing sets are allowed to be used by the BTS SW.

numberOfR99ChannelElements.description:
This parameter defines the R99 CE capacity that is allowed to be used by the BTS SW.

The end-user should be able to select how many R99 Channel Elements are allowed to be used by the BTS SW.

powerCtrlEnhancementsEnabled.description: This parameter indicates whether the Power Control Enhancements in BTS sub-feature is activated in the BTS. License is controlled by RNC.
powerCtrlEnhancementsEnabled.fullName: Power Control Enhancements in BTS enabled

premiumVoiceQualityEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if the Premium Voice Quality feature is activated in the BTS or not.

reservationPercentage.description:
This parameter can be used to define the percentage of resources (air interface scheduling time and Iub throughput capacity) that cannot be used by the Nominal Bit Rate (NBR) connections in case of Uu or Iub congestion. The defined resource is then shared with the commissioned air interface scheduling weights to all the active connections (including GBR/NBR/non-NBR). This ensures that the best effort (non-NBR) users are not neglected as they get the least weight defined portion of this parameter value. The parameter does not limit the resources used by the GBR connections.

Example: If all scheduling resources are described as 100%, then setting this parameter to 10 reserves 10% of resources. In congestion, NBR connections cannot take all the remaining resources, but must leave the defined 10% for weighed sharing of resources. If Guaranteed Bit Rate (GBR) connections experience congestion, they are allowed to use all resources despite this parameter. The operator can define with CCPolicy parameter if the SPI class is treated as a GBR (CCPolicy: Control Data over GBR) or NBR class (CCPolicy: Control All Data).

This parameter is applicable only for the resource reservation in HSDPA.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

sctpAssocMaxRetrans.description:
This parameter defines the association's maximum retransmissions (1-15 attempts, default is 5). This SCTP parameter is used only in IP Iub configuration.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

sctpFarEndSubnetIpAddress.description: This parameter denotes the IP address to be used in the transport network at the far end of the SCTP tunnel of the RNC. The address is the SCTP tunnel subnet address, that is, all its host bits must be set to "0". It must be entered in dotted decimal format.
sctpFarEndSubnetIpAddress.fullName: Far end SCTP subnet IP address

sctpFarEndSubnetPrefixLength.description:
This parameter defines the subnet prefix length of the far end of the SCTP subnet.

The prefix length for IPV4 is 0..32.
sctpFarEndSubnetPrefixLength.fullName: Far end SCTP subnet prefix length

sctpMaxPayloadSize.description: This parameter defines the maximum number of octets in an SCTP packet available for chunks.

sctpPathMaxRetrans.description:
This parameter defines the path's maximum retransmissions (1-15 attempts, default is 5). This SCTP parameter is used only in IP Iub configuration.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

sctpPortMin.description: This is the minimum value of the port number to be used for SCTP.

sctpValidCookieLife.description:
This parameter defines the maximum lifespan of the cookie sent in an INIT/INIT ACK chunk (SCTP). When the Interface Control and Signalling Unit (ICSU) switchover in RNC does not work with the Satellite Iub, the SCTP links fail and the cells go down. The operator might increase the value of the parameter validCookieLife to solve this problem.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

singleCellInUse.description: The license parameter to enable single cell solution for dual RF sector.
singleCellInUse.fullName: Single Cell Solution for Dual RF Sector in Use

smoothPCHighUlRateEnabled.description: The parameter indicates if the Smooth Power Control for High Uplink Data Rates feature is activated in the BTS or not.
smoothPCHighUlRateEnabled.fullName: Smooth Power Control for High Uplink Data Rates enabled

tti2msNonFdpchUserIncEnabled.description:
This parameter indicates if the Baseband Capacity increase for 2ms TTI non-FDPCH users feature is activated in the BTS or not. 

When the feature is activated, it improves the Baseband Capacity for 2ms non-FDPCH users (~40% increase per DCD). 

Cell throughput gain is also expected for the same amount of HW when the cell has more 2ms non-FDPCH users and is in normal cell load conditions.

udpPortMax.description: This parameter defines the maximum value of the WCDMA port number to be used for UDP connections.

udpPortMin.description: This parameter defines the minimum value of the WCDMA port number to be used for UDP connections.

uplinkCoMPEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if the uplink CoMP feature is activated in the BTS or not. When the feature is activated, it increases the UL throughput at cell boundaries and reduces interference to neighboring cells by increasing the UL Softer HO area.

vhsEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if VHS Receiver for High Speed Train is activated or not in the BTS. If the feature is activated and the license is on, good receiving performance can be up to 350km/h; otherwise, good receiving performance is only up to 250km/h.
vhsEnabled.fullName: VHS receiver for high speed train enabled

wbtsId.description: This is the WBTS identifier received in NBAP signalling.

wcdmaSupportForDemEnabled.description: This parameter indicates if the WCDMA support for DEM feature is activated in the BTS or not. When the feature is activated, it provides the framework and DEM functionality support for the Nokia-DEM end-to-end solution to work.

weight.description:
This parameter defines a scheduling weight for priority queues with specific SPI value. When there are no services with Guaranteed Bit Rate (GBR) in a cell, the weights are used to define the proportion in which the queues in a cell are scheduled in proportion to each other (the proportion is roughly the weight of queue divided by the sum of the weights of all the queues). When there are priority queues with GBR service in a cell, the weights are used to divide in a similar manner the possibly remaining scheduling capacity that is left after the GBR requirements of the queues are met.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

wnbtsId.description: This is the instance identifier of the WNBTS object. The WNBTS contains WBTS-specific base station parameters.

defaultCarrier.description:
This parameter defines the default carrier used in the tests for the local cells. The UARFCN values used are operator-specific and are defined by the 3GPP. For example, for the 2100 MHz frequency, the allowed values are 10562-10838.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

filterCenterTx.description:
This parameter defines the absolute Tx frequency, in kHz, for overriding the normal Filter center frequency tuning. 

This parameter can be used to override the normal filter tuning to minimize noise to the neighboring frequency band. If the parameter value is not defined, the Tx filter frequency is evaluated as an average of the configured center frequencies.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

lCelwDN.description:
This parameter defines a distinguished name to the LCELW class instance, by classname and identifier. Example: MRBTS-1/MNL-1/MNLENT-1/CELLMAPPING-1/LCELW-1.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

maxCarrierPower.description:
This parameter defines the maximum output power of the cell per antenna carrier in dBm. The maximum output power is the maximum value for the linear sum of the power of all the downlink physical channels that is allowed to be used in a cell. The reference point is the antenna connector.

The most commonly used dBm values correspond to following in Watt unit:
10.0 dBm = 10 mW
30.0 dBm = 1 W
37.0 dBm = 5 W
39.0 dBm = 8 W
40.0 dBm = 10 W
40.8 dBm = 12 W
41.8 dBm = 15 W
43.0 dBm = 20 W
44.0 dBm = 25 W
44.3 dBm = 27 W
44.8 dBm = 30 W
45.4 dBm = 35 W
46.0 dBm = 40 W
46.5 dBm = 45 W
47.0 dBm = 50 W
47.4 dBm = 55 W
47.8 dBm = 60 W
48.1 dBm = 65 W
48.5 dBm = 70 W
48.8 dBm = 75 W
49.0 dBm = 80 W

For low power RRH, the carrier power value is used for repeater(s) connected to the low power RRH, where the carrier power value in RRH is fixed. For example, FHCB output power is fixed to 10 mW (10 dBm), and FHEC output power is fixed to 1 mW (0 dBm).

Note: The allowed cell power values, which are allowed to be configured, depend on the used hardware variant. Please refer to the documentation where, per variant, the supported power values are specified.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

maxRxLevelDifference.description:
This parameter is used in Rx diversity reception to check the difference (dB) between the Rx branches of the same LCR. 
This parameter is created to allow customer to flexibly change the threshold of the Rx signal level difference. 
In case of exceeding the defined value, a fault is to be raised.

mimoType.description:
This parameter is used to select the static DL mimo type. The parameter value is defined for the first time when the local cell is created. When a cell is created for a single TX transmission, the parameter value is "0". For an MIMO-enabled cell, the parameter value is to be "1" (2 x TX transmission).

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

picPool.description: The operator is able to commission PIC pools in use with this parameter; updates and complete removal of PIC pool are possible online.

rxBandwidth.description:
This parameter is used for setting the optional RX BW level during commissioning. It allows the operator to narrow the Rx bandwidth. This parameter is valid for RF, which supports configurable Rx bandwdith.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

txBandwidth.description:
This parameter is used for setting optional TX BW level during commissioning. It allows the operator to narrow the Tx bandwidth. The parameter is valid for RF which supports configurable Tx bandwidth.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

vamEnabled.description:
This parameter indicates whether the Virtual Antenna Mapping is enabled or not in the BTS. The VAM can be enabled with or without the MIMO.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

wncelId.description:
This is the instance identifier of the WCDMA local cell resource object (WNCEL).  A local cell resource consists of the HW required by one cell for transmission and receiving. The local cell resource is associated with the cell identifier (C-ID) in the radio interface. If the configuration is initialized at the BTS, the signalling related to a cell is addressed using C-ID instead of the local cell resource identifier.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

accessBbCapacity.description:
This parameter defines the access to the Baseband HW capacity for each local cell group.

When there is more than one local cell group assigned to the same SMOD, then the Access baseband capacity must get a value between 1...99 for each local cell group assigned to the same SMOD, and the sum of the Access baseband capacity in LCGs assigned to the same SMOD must be "100". When there is only one local cell group assigned to an SMOD, then the Access baseband capacity must get value of "100".

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

cAGroupId.description:
This parameter defines Carrier Aggregation Group Identifier to which the Local Cell Group is assigned. 

A non-zero value enables Carrier Aggregation for the Local Cell Group, while a zero value disables Carrier Aggregation for the Locall Cell Group. 

Carrier Aggregation cannot be enabled for an LCG whose HW resources are allocated on pure FSMr2.

cellGroupName.description: This parameter denotes user-definable name for the Cell Group. The length is 1..20 characters.

dedicatedBbCapacity.description:
This parameter defines the guaranteed Baseband capacity for each local cell group (optional).

When there is more than one local cell group and the dedicated baseband capacity differs from the value of "0" at least for one local cell group, then the dedicated baseband capacity must get a value between 1...99 for each local cell group, and the sum of the dedicated baseband capacity in the LCGs must not exceed "100". The baseband capacity which is not assigned to any local cell groups is the common capacity for all the local cell groups. When there is only one local cell group, then the dedicated baseband capacity must get a value of "0".

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

hspaSetting.description:
The operator can set different HSPA configuration option with this parameter. In addition, there is a ""Rel99 only"" option that can be set when there is a need to use the whole LCG capacity for Rel99 traffic. 
The following required DSP resources are checked by the BTS SW towards the used BTS profile if more than one LCG is commissioned. HSPA configuration is not allowed if the configuration does not have enough DSP resources. 
The required DSP resources per HSPA configuration type per LCG are:
- ""Rel99 only""  - 1 DSP 
- ""Normal HSPA"" - 2 DSP
- ""Small HSPA"" - 2 DSP

Note: 
1. In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.
2. For FSM-r3, this parameter is Mandatory. For AirScale, this parameter is not applicable.
hspaSetting.officialRange:
0: Rel99 only 
1: Normal HSPA 
2: Small HSPA

maxNumOfHsRachResourceStepsRes.description:
This parameter allows to reserve maximum baseband capacity for HS-RACH use. With this parameter, an operator can reserve baseband capacity from 1 to 8 HSUPA resource step for HS-RACH use per Local Cell Group. 
1 HSUPA resource step means 12CE resource block supporting 10 simultaneous active HS-RACH users. So the operator can reserve baseband resources with commissioning parameter in steps 10 HS-RACH users, 20 HS-RACH users, 30 HS-RACH users, 40 HS-RACH users, 50 HS-RACH users, 60 HS-RACH users, 70 HS-RACH users and 80 HS-RACH users per LCG. This parameter is LCG-specific and can be commissioned for every used LCG.
maxNumOfHsRachResourceStepsRes.fullName: Max number of HSUPA resource steps for HS-RACH users
maxNumOfHsRachResourceStepsRes.officialRange: 1...8 HSUPA res. step, step 1 HSUPA res. step

minNumOfHsRachResourceStepsRes.description:
This parameter allows to reserve minimum baseband capacity for HS-RACH use. With this parameter, an operator can reserve baseband capacity from 0 to 8 HSUPA resource step for HS-RACH use per Local Cell Group. 
1 HSUPA resource step means 12CE resource block supporting 10 simultaneous active HS-RACH users. So the operator can reserve baseband resources with commissioning parameter in steps 10 HS-RACH users, 20 HS-RACH users, 30 HS-RACH users, 40 HS-RACH users, 50 HS-RACH users, 60 HS-RACH users, 70 HS-RACH users and 80 HS-RACH users per LCG. This parameter is LCG-specific and can be commissioned for every used LCG. 
If the parameter is commissioned with a value of "0", then the BTS is to reserve a maximum of one HSUPA resource step for HS-RACH use in case HS-RACH is activated for some of the cells in the LCG.
minNumOfHsRachResourceStepsRes.fullName: Min number of HSUPA resource steps for HS-RACH users
minNumOfHsRachResourceStepsRes.officialRange: 0...8 HSUPA res. step, step 1 HSUPA res. step

nbicEnabled.description:
The parameter indicates if the Narrowband Interference Cancellation feature is activated for a cell group or not.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

numOfHsupaResourceStepsRes.description:
This parameter defines the minimum amount of HSUPA resource steps reserved on the baseband for HSUPA.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.
numOfHsupaResourceStepsRes.fullName: Number of HSUPA resource steps reserved for HSUPA users

shareOfHSDPAUser.description:
This parameter defines how the maximum available HSDPA user capacity of the commissioned HSDPA processing sets is shared between the LCGs.

The sum of LCG shares should not exceed 100%, but can be less than 100%. If sum is less than 100%, then the remaining part is called the "common pool". The granularity is one user.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

shareOfHSUPACapacity.description:
This parameter defines how the maximum commissioned HSUPA processing set capacity is shared between the LCGs.

The sum of LCG shares must be always 100% with common pool. The granularity is one processing set. If there is a 50%/50% share and, for example, 5 processing sets, then one LCG gets 3 processing sets and another gets 2.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

smodDN.description:
This parameter identifies the system module SMOD where the HW resources are allocated for the local cell group.
It has to be defined in the format: MRBTS-/EQM-/APEQM-/CABINET-/SMOD-.
Example: MRBTS-1/EQM-1/APEQM-1/CABINET-1/SMOD-1.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

wncelIdList.description:
This parameter defines the list of WCDMA local cells in the local cell group.

The total number of RX resources should be 24 per LCG.

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

wncelgId.description:
This is the instance identifier of the WNCELG object. This parameter appears only in the distinguished name (DN) in the plan file and is used for O&M purpose. 

Note: In SBTS, changing this parameter will require only WCDMA RAT restart.

cacMeasurementInterval.description: This parameter defines the measurement interval for the WBTS call admission control measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" and 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.
cacMeasurementInterval.fullName: WBTS call admission control measurement interval

mtCellThrWBTS.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS cell throughput measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.

mtFrameProtWBTS.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS Frame protocol measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.

mtHSPASchedMon.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the HSPA scheduler monitoring measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.
mtHSPASchedMon.fullName: WBTS HSPA scheduler monitoring measurement interval

mtHSPAWBTS.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS HSPA measurement interval in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.

mtHSPAWBTSExt.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS HSPA extension measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.

mtOperSpecStat.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS Operator specific statistics measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.
mtOperSpecStat.fullName: WBTS operator specific statistics measurement iterval

mtPICPoolWBTS.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS PIC pool measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.

mtSIMonWBTS.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WCDMA SI Monitoring measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is 60 minutes.  No possibility to disable this measurement.

mtSignLoadWBTS.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS signaling load measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.

mtWBTSLevelMon.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS level monitoring measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is 60 minutes. No possibility do disable this measurement.

mtWBTSR99Res.description: This parameter denotes the measurement interval for the WBTS R99 HW resource measurement in minutes. The acceptable range is "disabled" or 60 minutes. The value of "disabled" means that there are no measurement values reported towards the management system.
mtWBTSR99Res.fullName: WBTS R99 HW resource measurement interval

wnpmrnlId.description: This parameter identifies the performance management's measurement configuration within the WCDMA BTS. The value of this parameter is always "1".

auth.description: Defines the authentication mode. This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in the RRC_CONNECTED mode only when the authIncluded parameter is set to TRUE.

authIncluded.description: Defines the authentication mode included indicator. This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

bandClass.description: Defines the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (CDMA2000 1xRTT) band class number associated with this cell.

homeRegIncluded.description: Defines whether the homeReg parameter is included in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

imsi11and12.description:
Defines the 11th and 12th digits of an International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI).
- When an IMSI has 12 or more digits, IMSI_11_12 is equal to the 11th and 12th digits of the IMSI. 
- When an IMSI has fewer than 12 digits, digits with a value equal to zero are added to the most significant side to obtain a total of 12 digits and the IMSI_11_12 is equal to the 11th and 12th digits of the resulting number. 
This field is sent as a 7-bit binary representation in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.
Set this parameter to the integer obtained by encoding the 12th and 11th digits of the IMSI using the formula 10 x D12 + D11 - 11.
Where:
D11 is the 11th digit
D12 is the 12th digit
If the digit is equal to zero, then 10 is used
For example, for an IMSI_11_12 of '04', the derived value 93 (= 10 x 10 + 4 - 11) should be set for this parameter.
The decimal value 127 corresponds to the escape code of all 1's: '1111111'.

imsiTSupported.description:
Defines whether 15-digit IMSI_T addressing is supported. 
This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

ltmOffIncluded.description: Defines whether the ltmOff parameter is included in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

maxNumAltSo.description:
Defines the maximum number of alternative service options that the UE is allowed to include in the CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) Origination message or in the CDMA2000 1xRTT Page Response message.
This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.
maxNumAltSo.fullName: CDMA2000 1xRTT max number of alt SO

mcc.description: Mobile Country Code of the PLMN

minPRev.description:
Defines the minimum protocol revision level. This field is set to prevent UEs which cannot be supported by the Inter-Working Solution (IWS) from accessing the system. The eNodeB shall set this field to the minimum protocol revision level that the IWS supports.
This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

pRev.description:
Defines the Protocol Revision level of the CDMA2000 1xRTT network.
This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

pilotInc.description:
Defines the pilot Pseudo-Random Noise (PN) sequence offset index increment. A UE searches for Remaining Set pilots at pilot PN sequence index values that are multiples of this value.
Set this field to the pilot PN sequence increment, in units of 64 PN chips, which UEs use for searching the remaining set. Set this field to the largest increment such that the pilot PN sequence offsets of all neighboring CDMA2000 1x Radio Transmission Technology (1xRTT) base stations are integer multiples of that increment. 
This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode only when the pilotIncIncuded parameter is set to TRUE.

pilotIncIncluded.description: Defines whether the pilotInc parameter is included in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

prefMSIDType.description:
Defines the Preferred Access Channel Mobile Station Identifier Type.
This parameter is sent in the MobilityParametersCDMA2000 Information Element (IE) in RRC_CONNECTED mode.

xparamId.description:
